children.text: caitanyadevaṃ bhagavantam āśraye śrīvaiṣṇavānāṃ pramude'ñjasā likhan
children.translated_text: I take refuge in the blessed <s>Caitanyadeva</s>, as I write straightforwardly for the delight of the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s>,

children.text: āvaśyakaṃ karma vicārya sādhubhiḥ sārdhaṃ samāhṛtya samastaśāstrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having considered, together with the good, the necessary rite and having gathered it from all the śāstras.

children.text: bhakter vilāsāṃś cinute prabodhānandasya śiṣyo bhagavatpriyasya
children.translated_text: The disciple of <s>Prabodhānanda</s>, who is dear to the Lord, gathers the vilāsas (sections) of devotion,
<s>Gopālabhaṭṭa</s>, while satisfying <s>Raghunāthadāsa</s> and also <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>.
From the vilāsa of love-devotion to the lotus feet of <s>Mathurānātha</s>
has arisen this work named <s>Bhaktivilāsa</s>; let his devotees practice it.
May the <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavas</s>, fixed in ultimate devotion, flourish here in the district of <s>Mathurā</s>;

children.text: kāśīśvaraḥ kṛṣṇavane cakāstu śrīkṛṣṇadāsaś ca salokanāthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Kāśīśvara</s> shine in <s>Kṛṣṇavana</s>, and also <s>Śrīkṛṣṇadāsa</s> together with <s>Lokanātha</s>.
First, taking refuge in the revered guru, with its reasons, is to be written; then

children.text: guruḥ śiṣyaḥ parīkṣādir bhagavān manavo 'sya ca ||
children.translated_text: the guru, the disciple, examination and the rest, the Lord, and his mantras.
Eligibility for mantra, purification for accomplishment and so on, and the consecratory rites of mantra;
<s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation); the daily auspicious rising at the brāhma time, and purity;

children.text: prātaḥ smṛtyādi kṛṣṇasya vādyādaiś ca prabodhanam ||
children.translated_text: morning remembrance and so forth, and the awakening of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with musical instruments and the like.
The removal of offered remnants and the like, and then the auspicious ārātrika;
bodily duties beginning with evacuation, purification, sipping water, and cleaning the teeth.
Bathing, the tantric twilight rite and so forth, and the preparations connected with the god's house.
Bringing <s>Tulasī</s> and other materials, household bathing, hot water, and the like;
garments, seat, the upright sectarian mark, revered <s>Gopīcandana</s>, and so on.
The cakra and other seals, the rosary, the household twilight rite, and worship of the guru;
then the greatness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and worship at the doorway and within the shrine.
The seat for worship, the placement of arghya and other offerings, and the warding off of obstacles;
obeisance to the revered guru and the rest, <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (purification of the elements), and purification of the vital breath.
Nyāsa, the set of five mudrās, and meditation on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the inner worship;
the stages of worship, sacred images, and <s>Śālagrāma</s> stones.
Disks originating from <s>Dvārakā</s>, purifications, and worship of the pīṭha;
invocation and the other acts, their mudrās, and the offering of a seat and other items.
Bathing the deity, the sounding of conch, bell, and other instruments, and the thousand names;
recitation of the Purāṇas, garments, sacred thread, and ornaments.
Fragrance, sandal paste of revered <s>Tulasī</s> wood, and flowers;
leaves, <s>Tulasī</s>, and worship of the limbs, subsidiary limbs, and coverings.

children.text: dhūpo dīpaś ca naivedyaṃ pānaṃ homo balikriyā
children.translated_text: Incense and lamp, <s>naivedya</s> (food offering), drinking water, oblation, and the bali offering;
mouth-rinsing and the other mouth services, and again divine fragrance and the like.
Royal services, song and the rest, and also the great nīrājana;
the sounding of the conch and other instruments, nīrājana with a water-filled conch, and praise.
Bowing, circumambulation, the offering of one's acts and so forth, and requests during recitation;
asking pardon for offense, various offenses, and the wearing of offered remnants.
The sanctified water from the conch, worship of <s>Tulasī</s>, her clay and the like;
the time when the <s>Dhātrī</s>-bath is forbidden, and the gaining of livelihood.
At midday, the vaiśvadeva and other rites and the śrāddha, and what should not be offered to <s>Acyuta</s>;
the faults in eating without worship and likewise in eating food not offered to him.
Eating the <s>naivedya</s>, the saints, good association, and bad company;
the bad destiny of the wicked and the evil fruit of mocking and reviling Vaiṣṇavas.
Devotion to the good, the Viṣṇu-śāstra, and the revered <s>Bhāgavata</s>;
accounts of divine play, the dharmas of the Lord, and one's own evening rites.
Avoidance of lapses in ritual acts, and worship three times a day, especially;
night duties, and then the exposition of the attainment of the fruit of worship and so on.
Gifts for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, various services, and making up what is deficient;
putting the deity to sleep, the greatness of worship, and the wondrous greatness of the blessed Name.
Offenses against the Name, devotion and then love, taking refuge and the rest;
in the fortnights, <s>Ekādaśī</s> with its subsidiary rites, and the great set of eight revered <s>Dvādaśī</s> observances.
Duties in the twelve months beginning with <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>;
the rites of puraścaraṇa, and the marks of a mantra that has been perfected.
The manifestation of an image, installation of an image, and a temple of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
restoration of what is old, the marriage of revered <s>Tulasī</s>, and exclusive religious action.
By the grace of the god <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and through the association of his devotees,

children.text: bhakter māhātmyam ākarṇya tām icchan sadguruṃ bhajet ||
children.translated_text: having heard the greatness of devotion, one who desires it should serve a true guru.
Here a succession of sufferings is experienced constantly, and in the next world too

children.text: duḥsahā śrūyate śāstrāt titīrṣed api tāṃ sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: it is heard from śāstra to be unbearable; therefore a wise person should wish to cross over it.

children.text: tathā coktam ekādaśaskandhe labdhvā sudurlabham idaṃ bahusambhavānte mānuṣyam arthadam anityam apīha dhīraḥ
children.translated_text: And so it is said in the Eleventh Book: Having obtained this very rare human birth after many births, useful for one's goal though impermanent here, the wise person

children.text: tūrṇaṃ yateta na pated anumṛtyu yāvan niḥśreyasāya viṣayaḥ khalu sarvataḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: should strive quickly for the highest good before he falls, while death follows him; for sense-objects are available everywhere.

children.text: svayaṃ śrībhagavatā ca nṛdeham ādyaṃ sulabhaṃ sudurlabhaṃ plavaṃ sukalpaṃ gurukarṇadhāram
children.translated_text: And by the revered Lord himself: The human body, the first means, is easy to obtain yet very hard to obtain, a well-made boat with the guru as helmsman,

children.text: mayānukūlena nabhasvateritaṃ pumān bhavābdhiṃ na taret sa ātmahā ||
children.translated_text: driven by the favorable wind sent by me; the person who does not cross the ocean of becoming is a killer of himself.

children.text: tatraiva śrīprabuddhayogeśvaroktau tasmād guruṃ prapadyeta jijñāsuḥ śreya uttamam
children.translated_text: There too, in the statement of the revered <s>Prabuddha Yogīśvara</s>: Therefore one who desires the highest good should surrender to a guru,

children.text: śābde pare ca niṣṇātaṃ brahmaṇy upaśamāśrayam ||
children.translated_text: one who is deeply versed in the verbal revelation and in the supreme reality, established in Brahman and grounded in tranquility.

children.text: svayaṃ śrībhagavaduktau madabhijñaṃ guruṃ śāntam upāsīta madātmakam ||
children.translated_text: In the revered Lord's own words: One should attend upon a guru who knows me, who is peaceful, and whose self is in me.
And in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>:

children.text: vipraṃ pradhvastakāmaprabhṛtiripughaṭaṃ nirmalāṅgaṃ gariṣṭhāṃ bhaktiṃ kṛṣṇāṅghripaṅkeruhayugalarajorāgiṇīm udvahantam
children.translated_text: a brāhmin who has destroyed the host of enemies beginning with desire, whose body is pure, and who bears the most venerable devotion, colored by the dust of the pair of lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: vettāraṃ vedaśāstrāgamavimalapathāṃ saṃmataṃ satsu dāntaṃ vidyāṃ yaḥ saṃvivitsuḥ pravaṇatanumanā deśikaṃ saṃśrayeta ||
children.translated_text: One who wishes to understand this vidyā should take refuge in a <s>deśika</s> (spiritual preceptor): one who knows the stainless paths of Veda, śāstra, and āgama, is approved among the good, is self-controlled, and is reverently inclined in body and mind.
Also in the śruti:

children.text: tadvijñānārthaṃ sa gurum evābhigacchet samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭham
children.translated_text: For the sake of knowing that reality, he should approach only a <s>guru</s>, with firewood in hand, one learned in revelation and steadfast in Brahman.
A person who has an <s>ācārya</s> knows.

children.text: śrībhāgavate daśamaskandhe śrutistutau vijitahṛṣīkavāyubhir adāntamanasturagaṃ ya iha yatanti yantum atilolam upāyakhidaḥ
children.translated_text: In the praise of the Vedas in the Tenth Skandha of the <s>Śrībhāgavata</s>: those who, with conquered senses and breath, strive here to restrain the untamed horse of the mind, which is exceedingly restless, become worn out by expedients;

children.text: vyasanaśatānvitāḥ samavahāya guroś caraṇaṃ vaṇija ivāja santy akṛtakarṇadharā jaladhau ||
children.translated_text: beset by hundreds of calamities, they abandon the feet of the <s>guru</s>, like merchants in the ocean, O Unborn One, who have not taken on a helmsman.
And in the śruti:

children.text: naiṣā tarkeṇa matir āpaneyā proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha ||
children.translated_text: This understanding cannot be obtained by reasoning; when taught by another alone, dear one, it becomes true knowledge.
In the <s>Mantramuktāvalī</s>:
He should be of pure lineage, clean, intent on conduct proper to himself,
belonging to an āśrama, free from anger, knowing the Veda, and knowing all the śāstras.
He should have faith, be free from envy, pleasant in speech and pleasing to behold,
pure, well dressed, youthful, and devoted to the welfare of all beings.
He should be intelligent, not arrogant in mind, complete, and reflective about egoity,
endowed with virtues, firmly minded in image-worship, grateful, and affectionate toward disciples.
He should be capable in restraint and favor, and devoted to oblations and mantras,
knowing the methods of reasoning for and against, pure in self, and an abode of compassion.
Endowed with such characteristics and others, a <s>guru</s> should be a treasury of gravity and dignity.
And in the <s>Agastyasaṃhitā</s>:
He should be a worshipper of the deity, peaceful, and without longing even amid sense objects,
a knower of the inner self, a speaker of Brahman, and skilled in the meaning of Veda and śāstra.
He should be capable both of raising up and of restraining, the best of brāhmaṇas,
a knower of the principles of yantras and mantras, one who penetrates their vital points and knows their secrets.
He should have performed puraścaraṇa, be accomplished in homa and mantra, and know their practical application,

children.text: tapasvī satyavādī ca gṛhastho gurur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: be ascetic and truthful; such a householder is called a <s>guru</s>.
In the <s>Viṣṇusmṛti</s>:
A <s>guru</s> is not one who desires service, fame, and gain from a disciple.
He is an ocean of compassion, fully accomplished, and a benefactor of all beings.
He is free from craving, accomplished in every respect, and expert in every vidyā,
a cutter-off of all doubts and not lazy: such a one is called a <s>guru</s>.
In the dialogue of the Blessed Lord and <s>Nārada</s> in the <s>Śrīnāradapañcarātra</s>:
A brāhmaṇa who knows all times should bestow grace upon all people.
In his absence, the best of twice-born men, peaceful in self and filled with the Blessed Lord,
with a cultivated self, all-knowing, learned in śāstra, and devoted to good rites,
endowed with the three accomplishments, should be consecrated for the office of <s>ācārya</s>.
For those born as kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, a kṣatriya is capable of bestowing grace.

children.text: kṣatriyasyāpi ca guror bhāvād īdṛśo yadi ||
children.translated_text: And if such a <s>guru</s> is absent even among kṣatriyas,

children.text: vaiśyaḥ syāt tena kāryaś ca dvaye nityam anugrahaḥ
children.translated_text: there may be a vaiśya; by him grace should always be performed for the two classes.
By a śūdra of the same class, O great-minded one, who is of that same kind,
grace and consecration should always be performed for a śūdra.
Moreover:

children.text: varṇottam'tha ca gurau sati yā viśrute'pi ca
children.translated_text: When a <s>guru</s> of a higher varṇa exists, even if another is famous,
whether in one's own country or elsewhere, this should not be done by one who seeks auspiciousness.

children.text: vidyamāne tu yaḥ kuryāt yatra tatra viparyayam
children.translated_text: But if, while such a one exists, someone creates an inversion here or there,
there will be ruin for him both here and hereafter; therefore one should follow what is stated in the śāstra.
One born among kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras should not initiate in reverse order.
And in the <s>Padma</s>:

children.text: mahābhāgavataḥ śreṣṭho brāhmaṇo vai gurur nṛṇām
children.translated_text: A brāhmaṇa who is a supreme great devotee is indeed the <s>guru</s> of human beings;

children.text: sarveṣām eva lokānām asau pūjyo yathā hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is worthy of worship by all worlds, just like <s>Hari</s>.
Even if born in a great family and initiated in all sacrifices,

children.text: sahasraśākhādhyāyī ca na guruḥ syād avaiṣṇavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and even if he has studied a thousand branches, a non-Vaiṣṇava should not be a <s>guru</s>.
A man who has received <s>Viṣṇu</s>-dīkṣā and is devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>-worship
is called a Vaiṣṇava by those who know; one other than this is a non-Vaiṣṇava.
In the <s>Tattvasāgara</s>:
One who eats too much, procrastinates, and is greedy for sense objects and the like,
who delights in contentious reasoning, is wicked, speaks improper words, and reviles virtues,
who is hairless or excessively hairy, and who resorts to a censured āśrama,
who has blackened teeth and dark lips and carries foul-smelling breath,
who is endowed with bad marks, even if he himself were a lord,
and who is attached to receiving many gifts: such an <s>ācārya</s> brings about the loss of prosperity.
In the <s>Mantramuktāvalī</s>:
A disciple should be of pure lineage, prosperous, humble, and pleasing to behold,
truthful in speech, virtuous in conduct, very intelligent, and free from hypocrisy.
He should have abandoned lust and anger and be devoted to the feet of the <s>guru</s>,
inclined toward the deity with body, mind, and speech day and night.
He should be free from illness, have conquered all sin, and be endowed with faith,
always devoted to the worship of twice-born men, gods, and ancestors.
He should be youthful, with all his faculties restrained, and an abode of compassion.
Endowed with such characteristics and others, a disciple is qualified for dīkṣā.
And in the Eleventh Skandha:
He should not crave honor, should be free from jealousy, skillful, without possessiveness, and firm in friendship,
not hasty, desirous of understanding the true purpose, not fault-finding, and not speaking vainly.
In the <s>Agastyasaṃhitā</s>:

children.text: alasā malināḥ kliṣṭā dāmbhikāḥ kṛpaṇās tathā
children.translated_text: The lazy, the impure, the afflicted, the hypocritical, and likewise the miserly,
the poor, the diseased, the angry, the passionate, and those eager for enjoyment,
those seized by envy and jealousy, deceitful people, and those who speak harshly,
those whose wealth has been acquired unjustly, and those attached to others' wives,
enemies of the learned, the ignorant who think themselves learned,

children.text: bhraṣṭavratāś ca ye kaṣṭavṛttayaḥ piśunāḥ khalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those whose vows have lapsed, those of harsh livelihood, slanderers, and wicked people,
those who eat too much, act cruelly, are wicked-souled, and are censured...
Others of this sort too are the most sinful, the lowest of men.
They cannot be restrained from improper acts and cannot endure the instruction of a guru.
Such people are to be abandoned; they are not fit to be accepted as disciples.
For if these people were accepted, they would become objects of the deity's anger.
Here they become poor and bereft of sons and wives.

children.text: nārakāś caiva dehānte tiryañcaḥ prabhavanti te ||
children.translated_text: And after the end of the body they become hell-beings and animals.
In the <s>Hayaśīrṣapañcarātra</s>:

children.text: jaiminiḥ sugataś caiva nāstiko nagna eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Jaimini</s>, <s>Sugata</s>, the atheist, the naked ascetic,

children.text: kapilaś cākṣapādaś ca ṣaḍ ete hetuvādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Akṣapāda</s>: these six are reasoners.
Those lowest of men who act in accordance with these doctrines

children.text: te hetuvādinaḥ proktās tebhyas tantraṃ na dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: are called reasoners; to them one should not impart the <s>tantra</s>.
The examination of the two, one by the other, through dwelling together for one year,
arises only through experience of conduct and character.
In the <s>Mantramuktāvalī</s>:
When the two have come to know one another's character by living for a year,
then there is the status of guru and the status of disciple; not otherwise, this is certain.
And the <s>śruti</s> says:
One should not give it to one who has not lived there for a year.
Also in the <s>Sārasaṃgraha</s>:

children.text: sadguruḥ svāśritaṃ śiṣyaṃ varṣam ekaṃ parīkṣayet ||
children.translated_text: A true guru should examine the disciple who has taken refuge in him for one year.
Faults born from ministers fall upon the king, and a wife's sin upon her husband;

children.text: tathā śiṣyārjitaṃ pāpaṃ guruḥ prāpnoti niścitam ||
children.translated_text: likewise the sin acquired by a disciple certainly falls upon the guru.
But in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>:

children.text: saṃtoṣayed akuṭilādretarāntarātmā taṃ svair dhanaiś ca vapuṣāpy anukūlavāṇyā
children.translated_text: With an inner nature that is not crooked, reverent, and sincere, he should satisfy him with his own wealth, with his body, and also with agreeable speech.

children.text: abdatrayaṃ kamalanābhadhiyātidhīras tuṣṭe vivakṣatu gurāv atha mantradīkṣām ||
children.translated_text: For three years, very steadfast and regarding him as <s>Kamalanābha</s>; when the guru is pleased, he may then ask for <s>mantra-dīkṣā</s>.
In the <s>Kaurma</s>, in the <s>Śrīvyāsagītā</s>:
He should always bring him a water-pot, kuśa grass, flowers, and fuel-sticks.

children.text: mārjanaṃ lepanaṃ nityam aṅgānāṃ vāsasāṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: He should daily perform cleaning and plastering, and attend to the limbs and garments.
He should never step over his used offerings, bed, sandals, or shoes,

children.text: ākrāmed āsanaṃ chāyām āsandīṃ vā kadācana ||
children.translated_text: nor over his seat, shadow, or chair, at any time.
He should procure tooth-sticks and the like, and should report the required task to him.

children.text: anāpṛcchya na gantavyaṃ bhavet priyahite rasaḥ
children.translated_text: One must not go away without asking permission; one should take delight in what is pleasing and beneficial to him.

children.text: na pādau sārayed asya sannidhāne kadācana ||
children.translated_text: One should never stretch out one's feet in his presence.
Yawning, laughter and the like, and covering the throat,

children.text: varjayet sannidhau nityam athāsphoṭanam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: as well as snapping the fingers, should always be avoided in his presence.
Moreover:

children.text: śreyas tu guruvad vṛttir nityam eva samācaret
children.translated_text: One should always conduct oneself toward him just as toward the guru,
toward the guru's sons, wives, and also the guru's own kinsmen.
Rubbing the limbs, bathing, eating the leavings,

children.text: na kuryād guruputrasya pādayoḥ śaucam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and washing the feet of the guru's son one should not do.
The wives of the guru who are of the same varṇa are to be honored like the guru;
those of a different varṇa are to be honored by rising and salutation.

children.text: abhyañjanaṃ snāpanaṃ ca gātrotsādanam eva ca
children.translated_text: Anointing, bathing, rubbing the limbs,

children.text: gurupatnyā ca kāryāṇi keśānāṃ ca prasādhanam ||
children.translated_text: and arranging the hair are not to be done for the guru's wife.
In the <s>Devyāgama</s>, in the statement of <s>Śrīśiva</s>:
The guru's bed, seat, vehicle, sandals, and footstool,

children.text: snānodakaṃ tathā chāyāṃ laṅghayen na kadācana ||
children.translated_text: as well as his bathing water and shadow, one should never cross over.

children.text: guror agre pṛthakpūjām advaitaṃ ca parityajet
children.translated_text: In front of the guru one should abandon separate worship and the claim of nonduality.

children.text: dīkṣāṃ vyākhyāṃ prabhutvaṃ ca guror agre vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: In front of the guru one should avoid giving initiation, exposition, and exercising authority.
In the statement of <s>Śrīnārada</s>:

children.text: yatra yatra guruṃ paśyet tatra tatra kṛtāñjali
children.translated_text: Wherever and whenever one sees the guru, there, with folded hands,

children.text: praṇamet daṇḍavad bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should bow flat upon the ground like a tree whose root has been cut.
The disciple should never step over the guru's word, seat, vehicle, sandals, shoes,

children.text: vastraṃ chāyāṃ tathā śiṣyo laṅghayen na kadācana ||
children.translated_text: garment, or shadow at any time.
In the <s>Śrīmanusmṛti</s>:

children.text: nodāhared guror nāma parokṣam api kevalam
children.translated_text: One should not utter the guru's name alone, even when he is absent.
Nor should one imitate his gait, speech, or gestures.

children.text: guror gurau saṃnihite guruvad dhṛtim ācaret
children.translated_text: When the guru's guru is present, one should maintain conduct as toward the guru.

children.text: na cāvisṛṣṭo guruṇā svān gurūn abhivādayet ||
children.translated_text: And unless permitted by the guru, one should not salute one's own gurus.
In the <s>Śrīnāradapañcarātra</s>:

children.text: yathā tathā yatra tatra na gṛhṇīyāc ca kevalam
children.translated_text: One should not casually take it, in whatever way or wherever, merely by itself.

children.text: abhaktyā na guror nāma gṛhṇīyāc ca yatātmavān ||
children.translated_text: Self-controlled, one should not take the guru's name without devotion.

children.text: praṇavaḥ śrīs tato nāma viṣṇuśabdād anantaram
children.translated_text: With the praṇava, then 'śrī', then the name, after the word <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
together with the word 'pāda', with head bowed and hands joined.
Moreover:

children.text: na tam ājñāpayen mohāt tasyājñāṃ na ca laṅghayet
children.translated_text: Out of delusion one should not command him, nor should one transgress his command.

children.text: nānivedya guroḥ kiṃcid bhoktavyaṃ vā guros tathā ||
children.translated_text: Nothing should be eaten without first offering it to the guru, and likewise what belongs to the guru.
And elsewhere:

children.text: āyāntam agrato gacched gacchantaṃ tam anuvrajet
children.translated_text: When he approaches, one should go before him; when he goes, one should follow him.

children.text: āsane śayane vāpi na tiṣṭhed agrato guroḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should not remain in front of the guru on a seat or on a bed.

children.text: yat kiṃcid annapānādi priyaṃ dravyaṃ manoramam
children.translated_text: Whatever food, drink, or other pleasing and delightful substance there may be,

children.text: samarpya gurave paścāt svayaṃ bhuñjīta pratyaham ||
children.translated_text: having first offered it to the guru, one should oneself eat every day afterward.
In the <s>Śrīviṣṇusmṛti</s>:

children.text: na guror apriyaṃ kuryāt tāḍitaḥ pīḍito 'pi vā
children.translated_text: One should not do what is displeasing to the guru, even if beaten or afflicted.
One should not disregard his word, nor should one do what is displeasing.

children.text: ācāryasya priyaṃ kuryāt prāṇair api dhanair api
children.translated_text: One should do what is dear to the teacher, even with one's life and wealth,

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: by deed, mind, and speech; such a person reaches the supreme goal.
In the <s>Śrīnāradapañcarātra</s>:

children.text: yo vakti nyāyarahitam anyāyena śṛṇoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: The one who speaks what is devoid of propriety, and the one who listens unjustly,

children.text: tāv ubhau narakaṃ ghoraṃ vrajataḥ kālam akṣayam ||
children.translated_text: both go to terrible hell for endless time.
In the <s>Vaiṣṇavatantra</s>:
Protect me, O lord of the universe, O guru, from the fire of worldly existence.

children.text: dagdhaṃ māṃ kāladaṣṭaṃ ca tvām ahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Burned and bitten by Time, I have come to you for refuge.
There, from glorious <s>Vāsudeva</s>, crest-jewel of all the gods,
the wise should receive <s>dīkṣā</s>, which belongs solely to his lotus feet.
In the First Skandha:

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tama iti prakṛter guṇās tair yuktaḥ paramapuruṣa eka ihāsya dhatte
children.translated_text: The qualities of material nature are <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>; joined with them, the one supreme person here assumes, for this world,

children.text: sthityādaye hariviriñcihareti saṃjñāḥ śreyāṃsi tatra khalu sattvatanor nṝṇāṃ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the names <s>Hari</s>, <s>Viriñci</s>, and <s>Hara</s>, for maintenance and the other functions. Among them, surely, auspicious benefits for human beings come from the form grounded in <s>sattva</s>.
Furthermore:
Even so, whose foot-nail discharged the water fit for worship, offered by <s>Viriñci</s>, for the world,

children.text: seśaṃ punāty anyatamo mukundāt ko nāma loke bhagavatpadārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that water, with <s>Śeṣa</s>, purifies: apart from <s>Mukunda</s>, who indeed in the world is a true referent of the word <s>bhagavat</s>?
In the revered Tenth Skandha:
Then, hearing that, the sages were astonished, freed from doubt,

children.text: bhūyāṃsaṃ śraddadhur viṣṇuṃ yataḥ śāntir yato 'bhayam ||
children.translated_text: and placed still greater faith in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, from whom comes peace and from whom comes fearlessness.
In the Vaiśākha-māhātmya of the <s>Padma</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Yama</s> and the Brahmin:

children.text: vyāmohāya carācarasya jagatas te te purāṇāgamās tāṃ tām eva hi devatāṃ paramikāṃ jalpantu kalpāvadhi
children.translated_text: For the bewilderment of the moving and unmoving world, let those many <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s> proclaim this or that deity alone as supreme until the end of the aeon.

children.text: siddhānte punar eka eva bhagavān viṣṇuḥ samastāgamavyāpāreṣu vivecanavyatikaraṃ nīteṣu niścīyate ||
children.translated_text: But in the final doctrine, when the operations of all the scriptures have been brought under discriminating analysis, the one lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is ascertained.
In the <s>Nārasiṃha</s>:

children.text: satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyam utkṣipya bhujam ucyate
children.translated_text: Truth, truth, and again truth is spoken, with the arm raised high:

children.text: vedācchāstraṃ paraṃ nāsti na devaḥ keśavāt paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is no scripture higher than the <s>Veda</s>, and no god higher than <s>Keśava</s>.
For in the <s>Padma</s>:

children.text: arir mitraṃ viṣṃ pathyam adharmo dharmatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: An enemy may become a friend, poison may become wholesome, and <s>adharma</s> may turn into <s>dharma</s>,
when <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> is well pleased; when he is displeased, the opposite becomes the reverse.
There too, the revered Lord's statement:

children.text: mannimittaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpam api dharmāya kalpate
children.translated_text: Even a sin committed for my sake is fit to become <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: mām anādṛtya dharmo 'pi pāpaṃ syān matprabhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: But even <s>dharma</s>, if it disregards me, becomes sin through my power.
Therefore it is said in the <s>Skanda</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>:
One who abandons <s>Vāsudeva</s> and worships another god

children.text: svamātaraṃ parityajya śvapacīṃ vandate hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: is just like one who abandons his own mother and bows to a dog-cooking outcaste woman.
There too, elsewhere:
One who abandons <s>Vāsudeva</s> and worships another god,

children.text: tyaktvāmṛtaṃ sa mūḍhātmā bhuṅkte halāhalaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: that deluded person, having given up nectar, consumes the poison <s>hālāhala</s>.
In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:

children.text: yas tu viṣṇuṃ parityajya mohād anyam upāsate
children.translated_text: But one who abandons <s>Viṣṇu</s> and, through delusion, worships another,
wishes to grasp a heap of dust after casting away a heap of gold.

children.text: anādṛtya tu yo viṣṇum anyadevaṃ samāśrayet
children.translated_text: And one who disregards <s>Viṣṇu</s> and takes refuge in another god
runs after a mirage while thirsty, though the water of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is there.
In the <s>Pañcarātra</s>:

children.text: yo mohād viṣṇum anyena hīnadevena durmatiḥ
children.translated_text: One who, out of delusion and with corrupt understanding, says even once that <s>Viṣṇu</s> is common with another, inferior god
is an outcaste; he is not merely an outcaste, but an outcaste indeed.
In the <s>Vaiṣṇava Tantra</s>:

children.text: na labheyuḥ punar bhaktiṃ harer aikāntikīṃ janāḥ
children.translated_text: People who, even with one-pointed minds, view <s>Viṣṇu</s> as equal to others
will not again obtain exclusive devotion to <s>Hari</s>.
And elsewhere:
One who looks upon the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as exactly equal with deities such as <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s>

children.text: samatvenaiva vīkṣeta sa pāṣaṇḍī bhaved dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: would certainly be a heretic.
In the <s>Sahasranāma-stotra</s> and similar works there are floods of such verses.

children.text: viśeṣataḥ sattvaniṣṭhaiḥ sevyo viṣṇur na cāparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In particular, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and no other, is to be served by those established in <s>sattva</s>.
And likewise in the revered <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, the statement of <s>Śiva</s>:
<s>Hari</s> alone is always to be worshipped by you who are established in <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: viṣṇumantraṃ sadā viprāḥ paṭhadhvaṃ dhyāta keśavam ||
children.translated_text: O Brahmins, constantly recite the <s>Viṣṇu</s> mantra; meditate on <s>Keśava</s>.
If statements of such greatness were collected from everywhere,
there would be the fault of making the book too large; therefore only the needed ones are written here.
In an <s>Āgama</s>:
Having obtained from the grace of the guru Vaiṣṇava mantras, beginning with the glorious king of mantras,

children.text: sarvaiśvaryaṃ japan prāpya yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: one who recites them, gaining all lordly powers, goes to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: puṇyaṃ varṣasahasrair yaiḥ kṛtaṃ suvipulaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Those men who have performed abundant austerity, meritorious through thousands of years,

children.text: japanti vaiṣṇavān mantrān narās te lokapāvanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: recite Vaiṣṇava mantras; they are purifiers of the worlds.
And in the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>:

children.text: prajapan vaiṣṇavān mantrān yaṃ yaṃ paśyati cakṣuṣā
children.translated_text: While reciting Vaiṣṇava mantras, whomever he sees with his eye,

children.text: padā vā saṃspṛśet sadyo mucyate'sau mahābhayāt ||
children.translated_text: or touches with his foot, that person is at once released from great danger.
Now the greatness of the <s>Viṣṇu</s> mantras is written in particular,
with the intention of strengthening the greatness of the revered <s>Gopāla</s> mantra.
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the dialogue of the divine messenger and <s>Vikuṇḍala</s>:
The twelve-syllable mantra, together with its limbs, its ocean, its renunciation, and with its seers and deities,
together with the rite of initiation, with meditation, and with its yantra,

children.text: aṣṭākṣaraṃ ca mantreśaṃ ye japanti narottamāḥ
children.translated_text: and the eight-syllable lord of mantras: the best of men who recite these

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā brahmahā śudhyete yato viṣṇavaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: purify even a Brahmin-killer when seen by him, because they themselves are Vaiṣṇavas.
Having become bearers of conch and discus, long-lived as <s>Brahmā</s>, and wearing forest garlands,

children.text: vasanti vaiṣṇave loke viṣṇurūpeṇa te narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those men dwell in the Vaiṣṇava world in the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
There too, concerning the twelve-syllable mantra, in the Fourth Skandha:

children.text: japaś ca paramo guhyaḥ śrūyatāṃ me nṛpātmaja
children.translated_text: Hear from me, O prince, this recitation, which is supremely secret.

children.text: yaṃ saptarātraṃ prapaṭhan pumān paśyati khecarān ||
children.translated_text: A man who recites it for seven nights sees sky-going beings.
In the revered <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:
The moon, the sun, and the other planets go and go, and return again;
but even now those who meditate on the twelve-syllable mantra do not return.
Concerning the eight-syllable mantra, as in the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>:

children.text: trayo vedāḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni chandāṃsi vividhāḥ surāḥ
children.translated_text: The three <s>Vedas</s>, the six ancillary sciences, the metres, and the various gods,

children.text: sarvam aṣṭākṣarāntaḥsthaṃ yac cānyad api vāṅmayam ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other sacred speech there is, all are contained within the eight-syllable mantra.
The eight-syllable mantra is the essential meaning of all <s>Vedānta</s>, the crossing of the ocean of transmigration,

children.text: gatir aṣṭākṣaro nṝṇāṃ na punar bhavakāṅkṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: and the goal of human beings who do not desire rebirth.
Where a greatly fortunate person perfected in the eight-syllable mantra is honored,
disease, famine, and thieves will not move about there.
Gods, demons, <s>Gandharvas</s>, Siddhas, Vidyādharas, and others
bow down to the great-souled man who knows the eight-syllable mantra.

children.text: vyaktaṃ hi bhagavān eva sākṣān nārāyaṇaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: For clearly the Lord himself, directly <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself,
turns about on mouths in the form of the eight-syllable mantra.
In the Uttarakhanda of the <s>Padma</s>:
Thus the eight-syllabled mantra should be known as accomplishing every aim.
It removes all suffering, is auspicious and glorious, and has the nature of all mantras.
In the <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: kim anyair bahubhir mantraiḥ kim anyair bahubhir vrataiḥ
children.translated_text: What need is there of many other mantras? What need is there of many other vows?
The mantra "namo <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>" accomplishes every aim.

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu namo nārāyaṇeti yaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, at all times, whoever repeats "namo <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>",

children.text: japet sa yāti viprendra viṣṇulokaṃ sabāndhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O best of brāhmins, goes with his relatives to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Bhaviṣyapurāṇa</s>:
The great eight-syllabled mantra is supreme and removes all sins;
it is proclaimed as holding kingship among all the mantras of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And in the dialogue of <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Vyāsa</s>:
The mantra "namo <s>Nārāyaṇāya</s>" accomplishes every aim;
for devotees who repeat it, dear one, it grants the fruit of heaven and liberation.

children.text: eṣa eva paro mokṣa eṣa svarga udāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: This alone is the highest liberation; this is declared to be heaven.
This essence has been extracted from all the secrets of the Vedas.

children.text: viṣṇunā vaiṣṇavānāṃ tu hitāya manunā purā
children.translated_text: Long ago by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, for the welfare of the Vaiṣṇavas, through the Manu
it was proclaimed as destroying all sins and granting every desire.

children.text: nārāyaṇāya nama ity ayam eva satyaṃ saṃsāraghoraviṣasaṃharaṇāya mantraḥ
children.translated_text: "Nārāyaṇāya namaḥ" alone is the true mantra for removing the terrible poison of saṃsāra.

children.text: śṛṇvantu satyamatayo muditās tarāgā uccaistarām upadiśāmy aham ūrdhvabāhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let those whose minds are true, joyful, and free from passion hear; with my arm raised I teach it very loudly.
Standing today with my arm raised, I speak to you in truth:

children.text: he putraśiṣyāḥ śṛṇuta na mantro 'ṣṭākṣarāt paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: O sons and disciples, listen: there is no mantra higher than the eight-syllabled one.
For this very reason it is said in the <s>Gāruḍa</s>:

children.text: āsīno vā śayāno vā tiṣṭhāno yatra tatra vā
children.translated_text: Whether sitting, lying down, or standing, wherever he may be,
one should have the single refuge of the mantra "namo <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>".
In the <s>Tāpanī</s> revelations:

children.text: devā ha vai prajāpatim abruvann ānuṣṭubhasya mantrarājasya nārasiṃhasya phalaṃ no brūhi bhagava iti sa hovāca prajāpatirya etaṃ mantrarājaṃ nārasiṃham ānuṣṭubhaṃ nityam adhīte so 'gnipūto bhavati sa vāyupūto bhavati sa ādityapūto bhavati sa somapūto bhavati sa satyapūto bhavati sa brahmapūto bhavati sa viṣṇupūto bhavati sa rudrapūto bhavati sa sarvapūto bhavati sa sarvapūto bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The gods said to <s>Prajāpati</s>, "Blessed one, tell us the fruit of the Anuṣṭubh king of mantras, the <s>Nārasiṃha</s>." <s>Prajāpati</s> said: "Whoever daily recites this Anuṣṭubh <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, the king of mantras, becomes purified by fire, purified by wind, purified by the sun, purified by the moon, purified by truth, purified by Brahman, purified by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, purified by <s>Rudra</s>, purified by all; he becomes purified by all."
At the end there also:
One hundred uninitiated persons are equal to one initiated person.
One hundred initiated persons are equal to one householder.

children.text: gṛhasthaśatam ekam ekena vānaprasthena tat samaṃ
children.translated_text: One hundred householders are equal to one forest-dweller.

children.text: vānaprasthaśatam ekam ekena yatinā tat samaṃ
children.translated_text: One hundred forest-dwellers are equal to one renunciant.

children.text: yatīnāṃ tu śataṃ pūrṇam ekam ekena rudrajāpakena tatsamam
children.translated_text: A full hundred renunciants are equal to one reciter of the <s>Rudra</s>.
One hundred reciters of the <s>Rudra</s> are equal to one teacher of the <s>Atharvaśiras</s> and <s>Śikhā</s>.

children.text: tad vā etat paramaṃ dhāma mantrarājādhyāpakasya yatra na sūryas tapati yatra na vāyur vāti yatra na candramā bhāti yatra na nakṣatrāṇi bhānti yatra nāgnir dahati yatra na mṛtyuḥ praviśati yatra na duḥkhaṃ sadānandaṃ paramānandaṃ śāntaṃ śāśvataṃ sadāśivaṃ brahmādivanditaṃ yogidhyeyaṃ paramaṃ padaṃ yatra gatvā na nivartante yoginaḥ
children.translated_text: That indeed is the supreme abode of the teacher of the king of mantras: there the sun does not shine, there the wind does not blow, there the moon does not gleam, there the stars do not shine, there fire does not burn, there death does not enter; it is free from sorrow, eternal bliss, supreme bliss, peaceful, everlasting, ever-auspicious, honored by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, meditated upon by yogins, the supreme state, where yogins go and do not return.
This is expressed in a Ṛc:

children.text: tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: The seers always behold that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
like an eye extended in heaven.
The inspired brāhmins, awake and praising, kindle
that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Agastyasaṃhitā</s>:
Among all classes of mantras, the Vaiṣṇava mantra is said to be the best,
granting what is desired among the Gāṇapatya, Śaiva, Śākta, and Saura mantras.
Even among Vaiṣṇava mantras, the <s>Rāma</s> mantras have greater fruit;
they are many millions of times greater than the Gāṇapatya and other mantras.

children.text: vinaiva dīkṣāṃ viprendra puraścaryāṃ vinaiva hi
children.translated_text: Without dīkṣā, O best of brāhmins, and indeed without puraścaryā,
and without the rule of nyāsa, they bestow siddhi by mere repetition.
Among the eight mantras, this six-syllabled one easily grants fruit;
this six-syllabled mantra wards off a great flood of sin.
It is called the king of mantras, the best of the best among all.
Daily evil, and that born of a fortnight, a month, a season, or a year,
it burns up entirely, like fire burning a mountain of cotton.
Thousands of acts of killing a brāhmin, done knowingly or unknowingly,
together with stealing gold, drinking liquor, and violating the guru's bed,
and whatever minor sins there may be by tens of millions and thousands,
all of them perish through the chanting of the <s>Rāma</s> mantra.
And in the <s>Tāpanī</s> revelations:

children.text: ya etattārakaṃ brāhmaṇo nityam adhīte sa pāpmānaṃ tarati sa mṛtyuṃ tarati sa bhrūhatyāṃ tarati sa sarvahatyāṃ tarati sa saṃsāraṃ tarati sa sarvaṃ tarati sa vimuktāśrito bhavati so 'mṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: The brāhmin who daily recites this tāraka mantra crosses over sin, crosses over death, crosses over the killing of an embryo, crosses over every killing, crosses over saṃsāra, crosses over everything; he becomes one who has taken refuge in liberation and attains immortality.

children.text: mantrās tu kṛṣṇadevasya sākṣād bhagavato hareḥ
children.translated_text: The mantras of <s>Kṛṣṇadeva</s>, directly of the blessed Lord <s>Hari</s>,
of him who is the seed of all avatāras, are the most powerful in every way.
And likewise in the <s>Bṛhadgautamīya</s> called <s>Śrīgovindavṛndāvana</s>:
Of all the foremost mantras, the Vaiṣṇava is said to be the best;
especially the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> mantras are the one means to enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: yasya yasya ca mantrasya yo yo devas tathā punaḥ
children.translated_text: And whatever deity belongs to any particular mantra,

children.text: abhedāt tanmanūnāṃ ca devatā saiva bhāṣyate ||
children.translated_text: because of the non-difference of those mantras, that same deity is taught.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is the supreme Brahman, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss.
By the mere recollection of them indeed, he grants the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.
There too, when he manifests his own divinity through cowherd play,

children.text: tasya śreṣṭhatamā mantrās teṣv apy aṣṭādaśākṣaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: his mantras are the very best; among them too, the eighteen-syllabled one is best.
In the <s>Tāpanī</s> śrutis:

children.text: oṃ munayo ha vai brahmāṇam ūcuḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ. The sages indeed said to <s>Brahmā</s>:
Who is the supreme deity?
From whom does death fear?
By knowledge of whom does everything become known?
By whom does this universe move through saṃsāra?

children.text: tān u hovāca brāhmaṇaḥ kṛṣṇo vai paramaṃ daivatam
children.translated_text: He said to them: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> indeed is the supreme deity.
Death fears <s>Govinda</s>.
By knowledge of <s>Gopījanavallabha</s>, everything becomes known.
Through svāhā this universe moves through saṃsāra.
They said to him:

children.text: kaḥ kṛṣṇo govindaḥ ko 'sau gopījanavallabhaḥ kaḥ kā svāheti
children.translated_text: Who is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Who is <s>Govinda</s>? Who is that <s>Gopījanavallabha</s>? What is svāhā?

children.text: tān uvāca brāhmaṇaḥ pāpakarṣaṇo gobhūmivedavidito veditā gopījanāvidyākalāprerakas tanmāyā ceti
children.translated_text: He said to them: He draws away sin; he is known through cows, earth, and the Veda; he is the knower; he impels the kalā of ignorance belonging to the gopī-folk; and that is his māyā.
That is wholly the supreme Brahman alone.

children.text: yo dhyāyati rasati bhajati so 'mṛto bhavati so 'mṛto bhavatīti
children.translated_text: One who meditates on it, savors it, and worships it becomes immortal, becomes immortal indeed.

children.text: te hocuḥ kiṃ tadrūpaṃ kiṃ rasanaṃ kathaṃ vāho tadbhajanaṃ
children.translated_text: They said: What is its form? What is the savoring? And how, indeed, is its worship?
Tell all that to us, who desire to know it.

children.text: tad u hovāca hairaṇyaḥ gopaveśam abhrābhaṃ taruṇaṃ kalpadrumāśritam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hairaṇya</s> said: He is in cowherd dress, cloud-colored, young, and standing beneath a wish-fulfilling tree.
And further on there itself:
Devotion to him is bhajana (worshipful service).
It is the placing of the mind on him alone, here and hereafter, through rejection of limiting adjuncts.
And this itself is naiṣkarmya (freedom from action).

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ taṃ viprā bahudhā yajanti govindaṃ santaṃ bahudhārādhayanti
children.translated_text: The learned worship him in many ways as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; they revere him in many ways as <s>Govinda</s>, the existent one.

children.text: gopījanavallabho bhuvanāni dadhre svāhāśrito jagad ejayjat svaretāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gopījanavallabha</s> upheld the worlds; resting on svāhā, self-seeded, he sets the world in motion.

children.text: vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo janye janye pañcarūpo babhūva
children.translated_text: Just as the one wind, having entered the world, became fivefold in each living being,

children.text: kṛṣṇas tathaiko 'pi jagaddhitārthaṃ śabdenāsau pañcapado vibhāti ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though one, for the welfare of the world, shines through sound as five-worded.
And further, in that same text, after the statement of the procedure for worship:

children.text: eko vaśī sarvagaḥ kṛṣṇa īḍya eko 'pi san bahudhā yo vibhāti
children.translated_text: The one controller, all-pervading <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worthy of praise, who, though one, manifests in many ways,

children.text: taṃ pīṭhasthaṃ ye 'nubhajanti dhīrās teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ||
children.translated_text: those wise ones who worship him seated on the pīṭha have eternal happiness, not others.

children.text: nityo nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān
children.translated_text: The eternal among the eternal, the conscious among the conscious, the one who grants desires to the many,

children.text: taṃ pīṭhagaṃ ye 'nubhajanti dhīrās teṣāṃ siddhiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ||
children.translated_text: those wise ones who worship him established on the pīṭha have eternal perfection, not others.

children.text: etad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ ye nityamuktāḥ saṃyajante na kāmān
children.translated_text: Those ever-liberated ones who always worship this supreme station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not desires,

children.text: teṣām asau goparūpaḥ prayatnāt prakāśayed ātmapadaṃ tadaiva ||
children.translated_text: to them he, in cowherd form, when they strive, reveals the station of the self at that very time.

children.text: yo brahmāṇaṃ vidadhāti pūrvaṃ yo vidyās tasmai gopāyati sma kṛṣṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who fashioned <s>Brahmā</s> in the beginning, who guarded the knowledges for him,

children.text: taṃ ha daivam ātmabuddhiprakāśaṃ mumukṣur vai śaraṇam anuvrajeta ||
children.translated_text: a seeker of liberation should indeed follow that deity, the illumination of self-understanding, as refuge.

children.text: oṃkāreṇāntaritaṃ ye japanti govindasya pañcapadaṃ manum
children.translated_text: Those who recite <s>Govinda</s>'s five-word mantra with the oṃkāra placed between,

children.text: teṣām asau darśayed ātmarūpaṃ tasmān mumukṣur abhyasen nityaśāntyai ||
children.translated_text: to them he shows his own form; therefore a seeker of liberation should practice it for eternal peace.

children.text: tasmād anye pañcapadād abhūvan govindasya manavo mānavānām
children.translated_text: Therefore other mantras of <s>Govinda</s> for human beings arose from the five-word mantra,

children.text: daśārṇādyās te'pi saṅkrandanādyair abhyasyante bhūtikāmair yathāvat ||
children.translated_text: beginning with the ten-syllabled and the rest; they too are properly practiced by <s>Saṅkrandana</s> and others who desire prosperity.
And further, there itself:

children.text: tad u hovāca brāhmaṇo 'sāv anavarataṃ me dhyātaḥ stutaḥ parārdhānte so 'budhyata
children.translated_text: There the Brāhmaṇa said: That one was constantly meditated on and praised by me; at the end of the parārdha he awoke.
A person in cowherd dress appeared before me.

children.text: tataḥ praṇatena mayānukūlena hṛdā mahyam aṣṭādaśārṇaṃ svarūpaṃ sṛṣṭaye dattvāntarhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when I had bowed with a favorable heart, he gave me his eighteen-syllabled form for creation and disappeared.
Again the desire to create arose in me.
Among those syllables he revealed the form of the future world.
Here, from ka came water;
from la, earth;
from ī, fire;
from bindu, the moon;
from its nāda, the sun. Thus from the syllable klīṃ I created.

children.text: kṛṣṇād ākāśaṃ yad vāyur ity uttarāt surabhiṃ vidyāṃ prādurakārṣam
children.translated_text: From kṛṣṇa came space, and from the following syllable ya came wind; thus I brought forth the <s>Surabhī</s> Vidyā.

children.text: taduttarāt taduttarāt strīpumādi cedaṃ sakalam idaṃ iti ||
children.translated_text: From what followed that, and what followed that, came female and male and all this.
And likewise in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>:

children.text: klīṃkārād asṛjad viśvam iti prāha śruteḥ śiraḥ
children.translated_text: The head of śruti declared: From the syllable klīṃ he created the universe.
From the letter la earth was born; from the letter ka came the origin of water.

children.text: īkārād vahnir utpanno nādād āyur ajāyata
children.translated_text: From the letter ī fire arose; from nāda air was born.
From bindu came the arising of space; thus the mantra consists of the elements.

children.text: svāśabdena ca kṣetrajño heti citprakṛtiḥ parā
children.translated_text: By the word svā is meant the kṣetrajña; by ha, the supreme conscious prakṛti.
From the arising of the union of the two comes the syllable that encloses the mouth.

children.text: ata eva hi viśvasya layaḥ svāhārṇake bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore indeed the dissolution of the universe takes place in the syllable svāhā.
And again that śruti says:

children.text: etasyaiva yajanena candradhvajo gatamoham ātmānaṃ vedayitvā oṃkārāntarālakaṃ manum āvartayat saṅgarahito 'bhyānayat
children.translated_text: By worship of this alone, <s>Candradhvaja</s>, having made himself free of delusion and having known the self, repeated the mantra with the oṃkāra inside and, free from attachment, attained it.

children.text: tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti sūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: The seers always behold that supreme station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
spread out like an eye in heaven.
Therefore one should practice this constantly.
Further on there itself:
From whose first word came earth; from the second, water arose;
from the third light arose; from the fourth, the carrier of fragrance;
from the fifth came the arising of sky. One should practice that one alone.
<s>Candradhvaja</s> reached the supreme, imperishable station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Then that pure, stainless, sorrowless state, free from attachment to all greed and the like,

children.text: yat tat padaṃ pañcapadaṃ tad eva sa vāsudevo na yato 'nyad asti ||
children.translated_text: that station which is five-worded is that very <s>Vāsudeva</s>; there is no other beyond him.

children.text: tam ekaṃ govindaṃ saccidānandavigraham pañcapadaṃ vṛndāvanasurabhūruhatalāsīnaṃ satataṃ samarudgaṇo 'haṃ paramayā stutyā toṣayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I constantly satisfy with the highest praise that one <s>Govinda</s>, whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss, the five-worded one, seated beneath the wish-giving tree of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, I together with the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.
Moreover, after the praise:

children.text: amuṃ pañcapadaṃ mantram āvartayed yaḥ sa yāty anāyāsataḥ kevalaṃ tat padaṃ tat
children.translated_text: Whoever repeats this five-worded mantra goes effortlessly to that very state, that very abode.

children.text: anejad ekaṃ manaso javīyo naitad devā āpnuvan pūrvam arśāt ||
children.translated_text: Unmoving, one, swifter than the mind: the gods did not reach it, for it had sped ahead before them.

children.text: tasmāt kṛṣṇa eva paro devas taṃ dhyāyet taṃ raset taṃ yajed iti oṃ tat sad iti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is the supreme god; one should meditate on him, relish him, and worship him. Thus: oṃ, tat, sat.
And in the <s>Trailokyasaṃmohana Tantra</s>:
In the very context of the eighteen-syllable mantra spoken by venerable <s>Mahādeva</s> to the goddess:
He is the lord of <s>dharma</s> (religious duty), wealth, desire, and liberation, the lord of the world,
and, O greatly fortunate one, his avatāras exist by the thousands.
Among those avatāras, childhood is exceedingly rare,

children.text: amānuṣāṇi karmāṇi tāni tāni kṛtāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and these and those superhuman deeds were performed.
Since everything is established in him as the maker of curses and blessings,
I shall declare his unsurpassed mantra, together with its limbs and subsidiary limbs.
By the mere knowledge of it a man may come to omniscience.

children.text: putrārthī putram āpnoti dharmārthī labhate dhanam ||
children.translated_text: One desiring a son obtains a son; one desiring wealth obtains wealth.
He certainly becomes one who has crossed to the far shore of the meaning of all śāstras; there is no doubt.
He could bring the three worlds under control and throw the world into agitation.

children.text: mohayet sakalaṃ so 'pi mārayet sakalān ripūn
children.translated_text: He could bewilder everything, and he could kill all enemies.

children.text: bahunā kim ihoktena mumukṣur mokṣam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Why say much here? One who seeks liberation obtains liberation.

children.text: yathā cintāmaṇiḥ śreṣṭho yathā gauś ca yathā satī
children.translated_text: As the wish-fulfilling jewel is supreme, as the cow is, and as a faithful wife is,

children.text: yathā dvijo yathā gaṅgā tathāsau mantra uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as a twice-born man is and as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is, so this mantra is supreme.

children.text: yathāvad akhilaśreṣṭhaṃ yathā śāstraṃ tu vaiṣṇavam
children.translated_text: As, according to rule, everything most excellent is, and as Vaiṣṇava scripture is,

children.text: yathā susaṃskṛtā vāṇī tathāsau mantra uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well-refined speech is, so this mantra is supreme.
Moreover:

children.text: ato mayā sureśāni pratyahaṃ japyate manuḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, O queen of the gods, this mantra is recited by me every day.

children.text: naitena sadṛśaḥ kaścid jagaty asmin carācare ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing equal to it in this world, among moving and unmoving beings.
Also in the <s>Sanatkumāra Kalpa</s>:
Mantras concerning <s>Gopāla</s> are of thirty-three varieties.

children.text: teṣu sarveṣu mantreṣu mantrarājam imaṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Among all those mantras, hear this king of mantras.
This gracious mantra is in the tantra called <s>Sammohana</s>.
The mantra must be carefully guarded by you, O foremost of sages.
By this king of mantras <s>Purandara</s>, lord of the gods,
readily attained the state of great <s>Indra</s>, given by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Once afflicted with ill fortune because of the curse of <s>Durvāsas</s>,

children.text: sa eva subhagavatvaṃ vai tenaiva punar āptavān ||
children.translated_text: he again recovered prosperity by that very mantra.
Why say much here? Even without the disciplines of <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory rite),
by mere recitation one obtains everything desired.
I bow to that lord <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, the best of gurus,

children.text: kathañcid āśrayād yasya prākṛto 'py uttamo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: by taking shelter of whom in some way even an ordinary person becomes excellent.

children.text: tāntrikeṣu ca mantreṣu dīkṣāyāṃ yoṣitām api
children.translated_text: And with respect to tantric mantras and initiation, even women,
virtuous women and good-minded <s>Śūdras</s> and others, have eligibility.

children.text: tathā ca smṛtyarthasāre pādme ca vaiśākhamāhātmye śrīnāradāmbarīṣasaṃvāde
children.translated_text: And so too in the <s>Smṛtyarthasāra</s>, and in the <s>Vaiśākha-māhātmya</s> of the <s>Padma</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Ambarīṣa</s>:
According to the path taught in the <s>Āgamas</s>, worship

children.text: kartavyaṃ śraddhayā viṣṇoś cintayitvā patiṃ hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: of <s>Viṣṇu</s> should be performed with faith even by women and <s>Śūdras</s>, after contemplating the husband in the heart.

children.text: śūdrāṇāṃ caiva bhavati nāmnā vai devatārcanam
children.translated_text: And for <s>Śūdras</s> too the worship of the deity is by means of the name.
All should act according to the Āgamic path that conforms to the <s>Veda</s>.
Women too have eligibility in the worship and related rites of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and this is the eternal revelation for those devoted to pleasing their husbands.
In the <s>Agastya Saṃhitā</s>, with reference to the king of <s>Rāma</s> mantras:
Very pure in vow, <s>Śūdras</s> who are righteous and serve the twice-born,
women who are devoted to their husbands, and others born in reverse or regular mixed unions,
people down to <s>Cāṇḍālas</s>: all are eligible here.
And the guru should examine, in giving mantras classed as siddha, sādhya, and so on,

children.text: svakulāny akulatvaṃ ca bālaprauḍhatvam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: whether they belong to one's own family or another family, and whether they are childlike or mature.
He should also examine femaleness, maleness, and neuterness, and the matching of zodiacal signs and lunar mansions,
the time of sleeping and awakening, and likewise debt, wealth, and the like.
In the <s>Śāradātilaka</s>:

children.text: prāk pratyag agrā rekhāḥ syuḥ pañca yāmyottarāgragāḥ
children.translated_text: First there should be five lines with their tips toward the west and east, and as many running from south to north.
Thus there should be a maṇḍala made of four groups of four compartments.
In the directions, in the compartments marked by moon, fire, Rudra, nine, a pair of eyes, the seasons, eight, sixteen, fourteen, the elements,

children.text: pātālapañcadaśavahnihimāṃśukoṣṭhe varṇāṃl likhel lipibhavān kramaśas tu dhīmān ||
children.translated_text: the underworld, fifteen, fire, and moon, the wise man should write the letters born from the alphabet in order.
From the birth-asterism letter up to the first syllable of the mantra,

children.text: caturbhiḥ koṣṭhakais tv ekam iti koṣṭhacatuṣṭaye ||
children.translated_text: one should count one for every four compartments, in each group of four compartments.
Again, in the compartments of the compartments, moving clockwise from the syllable belonging to the birth constellation,
the discerning should recognize the sequence as siddha, sādhya, susiddha, and ari.

children.text: siddhaḥ sidhyati kālena sādhyas tu japahomataḥ
children.translated_text: A siddha mantra succeeds in time, while a sādhya mantra succeeds through recitation and oblation.
A susiddha mantra succeeds by merely being received; an ari mantra cuts off the root.
When siddha is joined with siddha, success comes as stated; siddha with sādhya requires double practice.
Siddha with susiddha succeeds with half the recitation; siddha with ari kills one's relatives.
Sādhya with siddha requires double; sādhya with sādhya is fruitless.
Sādhya with susiddha requires triple; sādhya with ari kills those of one's lineage.
Susiddha with siddha succeeds with half the recitation; susiddha with sādhya requires additional multiplication.
Susiddha with susiddha succeeds simply by being received; susiddha with ari destroys one's own lineage.

children.text: arisiddhaḥ sutān hanyād arisādhyas tu kanyakāḥ
children.translated_text: If a mantra is ari-siddha, it kills sons; if ari-sādhya, it kills daughters.

children.text: tatsusiddhas tu patnīghnas tadarir hanti sādhakam ||
children.translated_text: If it is tat-susiddha, it kills the wife; if it is tad-ari, it kills the practitioner.

children.text: tathā ca tantre asya ca mantraviśeṣe'pavādaḥ
children.translated_text: And likewise in the tantra there is an exception for this particular mantra:
For the mantras of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Arka</s>, and <s>Varāha</s>, and for the prāsāda and praṇava,

children.text: vaidikasya ca mantrasya siddhādīn naiva śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: and for a Vedic mantra, one should not examine whether it is siddha and so forth.

children.text: svapnalabdhe striyā datte mālāmantre ca tryakṣare
children.translated_text: For a mantra obtained in a dream, one given by a woman, a mālā-mantra, and a three-syllabled mantra,

children.text: ekākṣare tathā mantre siddhādīn naiva śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: and likewise for a one-syllabled mantra, one should not examine whether it is siddha and so forth.
What belongs to one's own lineage, what is outside the lineage, and so on should be understood from another āgama.

children.text: na vistarabhayād atra vyarthatvād api likhyate ||
children.translated_text: It is not written here from fear of excessive detail, and also because it would be useless.
In the mantras of glorious <s>Gopāladeva</s>, who displays every lordly power,
nothing at all is to be considered with regard to such powers.
And likewise in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>:

children.text: sarveṣu varṇeṣu tathāśrameṣu nārīṣu nānāhvayajanmabheṣu dātā phalānām abhivāñchitānāṃ drāg eva gopālakamantra eṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among all classes, likewise among the āśramas, among women, and among those born under various names and constellations, this <s>Gopālaka</s> mantra quickly grants the desired fruits.
And in the <s>Trailokyasaṃmohana-tantra</s>:
With reference to the eighteen-syllabled mantra, it was said by glorious <s>Śiva</s>:
Here, dear one, hostile defects are not to be considered, nor investigation of letters, svā and the like,

children.text: ṛkṣarāśivicāro vā na kartavyo manau priye ||
children.translated_text: nor should investigation of lunar mansion or zodiac sign be made for the mantra.

children.text: kecic chinnāś ca ruddhāś ca kecin madasamuddhatāḥ
children.translated_text: Some mantras are cut off, some obstructed, and some swollen with intoxication;

children.text: malināḥ stambhitāḥ kecit kīlitā dūṣitā api
children.translated_text: some are impure, some paralyzed, and some are nailed down or defiled.

children.text: etair doṣair yuto nāyaṃ yatas tribhunottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This one is not joined with these defects, because it is the best in the three worlds.
And generally, as in the <s>Bṛhadgautamīya</s>:
Now I shall teach the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> mantras, which grant seen and unseen fruits,

children.text: yān vai vijñāya munayo lebhire muktim añjasā ||
children.translated_text: knowing which the sages swiftly attained liberation.
Householders, forest-dwellers, renunciants, and celibate students,
as well as women, śūdras, and others, all have authority for them.
Here there is no need to consider hostile impurity and the like, nor the marks of enemy, friend, and so on,

children.text: na vā prayāsabāhulyaṃ sādhane na pariśramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor is there much exertion in the practice, nor labor.
Like fire to a mass of cotton that is ignorance, in a mere instant,
there is no consideration here of the forms siddha, sādhya, susiddha, and ari.
For the mantra whose syllable is Brahman is siddha among all siddha mantras.
<s>Prajāpati</s> obtained supremacy; <s>Śacīpati</s> obtained the kingdom of the gods;
the thirty gods obtained heaven, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> obtained lordship of speech.
In that same passage, later:

children.text: viṣṇubhaktyā viśeṣeṇa kiṃ na sidhyati bhūtale
children.translated_text: Through devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> in particular, what is not accomplished on earth,
from insects and the like up to <s>Brahmā</s>, by the favor of <s>Govinda</s>, O sage?
They are abodes of every prosperity and everywhere free from fear.

children.text: ityādi kathitaṃ kiṃcin māhātmyaṃ vo munīśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O lords of sages, a little of its greatness has been told.
As there are stars in the sky, or as there is a mass of sand in the ocean,
by the mere knowledge of this one obtains the fourfold liberation.

children.text: etadanyeṣu mantreṣu doṣāḥ santi pare ca ye
children.translated_text: But in other mantras there are these defects and also further ones.
For that purpose, the ten mantra-saṃskāras are written according to the tantra.
In the <s>Śāradātilaka</s>:

children.text: jananaṃ jīvanaṃ ceti tāḍanaṃ rodhanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Generation, enlivening, striking, and likewise obstruction,
then consecration, purification, and again invigoration,
satiation, kindling, and guarding: these are the ten ritual refinements of a mantra.
The extraction of mantras from within the mātṛkā is remembered as generation.
The wise man should place the mantra-syllables between praṇavas and recite them.
Experts in mantra and tantra call this enlivening.
Having written out the letters of the mantra, he should strike them with sandal-water.

children.text: pratyekaṃ vāyunā mantrī tāḍanaṃ tad udāhṛtam
children.translated_text: The mantra-practitioner should strike each one with the vāyu mantra; that is called striking.

children.text: vilikhya mantraṃ taṃ mantrī prasūnaiḥ karavīrajaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having written that mantra, the mantra-practitioner should use flowers born from the oleander,
equal in number to the syllables of that mantra, to strike it; by that there is obstruction.
According to the procedure taught in its own tantra, the mantra-practitioner, according to the number of the mantra's syllables,
should bathe the mantra with aśvattha shoots for purification.

children.text: saṃcintya manasā mantraṃ yotir mantreṇa nirdahet ||
children.translated_text: Having mentally contemplated the mantra, he should burn it with the jyotis-mantra.

children.text: mantre mūlatrayaṃ mantrī vimalīkaraṇaṃ tv idam
children.translated_text: The mantra-practitioner applies the three roots to the mantra; this is purification.
The jyotis-mantra is understood as consisting of tārā, vyoma, agni, manu-yuga, and daṇḍin.
Sprinkling each syllable of the mantra with kuśa-water that has been empowered by recitation

children.text: tena mantreṇa vidhivad etad āpyāyanaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: with that mantra, according to rule, is remembered as invigoration.

children.text: mantreṇa vāriṇā yantre tarpaṇaṃ tarpaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Satiation is remembered as satiation in a yantra with water by means of the mantra.
The union of tārā, māyā, and ramā is called the kindling of the mantra.
The guarding of a mantra being recited is its non-disclosure.
Because the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> mantras are powerful, there is no need for ritual refinement.
Even so, this has been stated merely as a general indication.

children.text: iti śrīgopālabhaṭṭavilikhite śrībhagavadbhaktivilāse gauravo nāma prathamo vilāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first vilāsa, named Gaurava, in the glorious <s>Bhagavadbhaktivilāsa</s> written by glorious <s>Gopālabhaṭṭa</s>.
I bow to that glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, the teacher of the world,
by whose compassion even a dog may easily cross the great ocean.
Now, the procedure of dīkṣā.
The procedure of dīkṣā is written here following the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>,

children.text: vinā dīkṣāṃ hi pūjāyāṃ nādhikāro 'sti karhicit ||
children.translated_text: for without dīkṣā there is never authority in worship.
In an āgama:
Just as twice-born men who have not undergone initiation here have no authority
in their own rites, study, and the like, but do have it after upanayana,
so too those who are not initiated here have no authority
in mantra, deity-worship, and the like; therefore one should make oneself approved by <s>Śiva</s>.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the Kārttika section, in the dialogue of glorious <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: te narāḥ paśavo loke kiṃ teṣāṃ jīvane phalam
children.translated_text: Those men are beasts in the world; what fruit is there in their life,

children.text: yair na labdhā harer dīkṣā nārcito vā janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who have not received dīkṣā of <s>Hari</s> or have not worshipped <s>Janārdana</s>?
There also, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Rukmāṅgada</s> and <s>Mohinī</s>, and in the <s>Viṣṇuyāmala</s>:
O fair-thighed one, everything done by an uninitiated person is fruitless;
a person devoid of dīkṣā (initiation) obtains an animal womb.
Especially in the <s>Viṣṇuyāmala</s>:

children.text: snehād vā lobhato vāpi yo gṛhṇīyād adīkṣayā
children.translated_text: Whoever, from affection or greed, should receive it without dīkṣā,

children.text: tasmin gurau saśiṣye tu devatāśāpa āpatet ||
children.translated_text: upon that guru, together with his disciple, the curse of the deity would fall.
And in the <s>Viṣṇurahasya</s>:
Without understanding the ritual acts of <s>Hari</s>-worship as stated by rule,
one who performs them with devotion obtains only a hundredth share of the fruit gained according to rule.

children.text: divyaṃ jñānaṃ yato dadyāt kuryāt pāpasya saṅkṣayam
children.translated_text: Because it gives divine knowledge and brings about the destruction of sin,

children.text: tasmād dīkṣeti sā proktā deśikais tattvakovidaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore that is called dīkṣā by teachers who know the truth.

children.text: ato guruṃ praṇamyaivaṃ sarvasvaṃ vinivedya ca
children.translated_text: Therefore, bowing thus to the guru and offering all one's possessions,
one should receive the Vaiṣṇava mantra, preceded by dīkṣā, according to rule.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, there also, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: tapasvinaḥ karmaniṣṭhāḥ śreṣṭhās te vai narā bhuvi
children.translated_text: Ascetics and those steadfast in rites, those men are the best on earth,

children.text: prāptā yais tu harer dīkṣā sarvaduḥkhavimocinī ||
children.translated_text: by whom the dīkṣā of <s>Hari</s>, freeing one from all suffering, has been obtained.
And in the <s>Tantrasāgara</s>:
As bronze becomes gold through the prescribed mercurial treatment,
so through the procedure of dīkṣā dvija-hood arises for human beings.
In an āgama:
Receiving a mantra in Caitra gives the fruit of much suffering;

children.text: vaiśākhe ratnalābhaḥ syāj jyaiṣṭhe tu maraṇaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: in Vaiśākha there is gain of jewels, but in Jyaiṣṭha death is certain.
In Āṣāḍha it leads to loss of relatives; in Śrāvaṇa it brings fear;
in Bhādrapada there is loss of offspring; in Āśvina there is auspiciousness everywhere.
In Kārttika there is increase of wealth; in Mārgaśīrṣa it bestows auspiciousness;

children.text: pauṣe tu jñānahāniḥ syān māghe medhāvivardhanam
children.translated_text: in Pauṣa there is loss of knowledge, and in Māgha increase of intelligence;
in Phālguna mastery over all is proclaimed by the ācāryas.
And in some texts:

children.text: samṛddhiḥ śrāvaṇe nūnaṃ jñānaṃ syāt kārttike tathā
children.translated_text: In Śrāvaṇa there is surely prosperity, and likewise knowledge in Kārttika;
in Phālguna too there is prosperity; one should avoid an intercalary month.
In the <s>Gautamīya</s>:
Beginning a mantra in Caitra grants all the aims of human life;

children.text: vaiśākhe ratnalābhaḥ syāt jyaiṣṭhe tu maraṇaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: in Vaiśākha there is gain of jewels, but in Jyaiṣṭha death is certain.

children.text: āṣāḍhe bandhunāśaḥ syāt pūrṇāyuḥ śrāvaṇe bhavet
children.translated_text: In Āṣāḍha there is loss of relatives; in Śrāvaṇa there will be a full lifespan;
in Bhādra loss of offspring occurs; in Āśvina there is accumulation of jewels.

children.text: kārttike mantrasiddhiḥ syāt mārgaśīrṣe tathā bhavet
children.translated_text: In Kārttika there is mantra-siddhi; likewise it comes about in Mārgaśīrṣa;

children.text: pauṣe tu śatrupīḍā syāt māghe medhāvivardhanam
children.translated_text: in Pauṣa there is harassment by enemies, and in Māgha increase of intelligence;
in Phālguna all desires are obtained; one should avoid an intercalary month.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, there also, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Rukmāṅgada</s> and <s>Mohinī</s>:

children.text: kārttike tu kṛtā dīkṣā nṝṇāṃ janmanikṛntanī
children.translated_text: Dīkṣā performed in Kārttika cuts off the births of human beings;
therefore by every effort one should perform dīkṣā in Kārttika.
But in the dīkṣā of the revered <s>Gopāla</s> mantras,

children.text: caitramāse yad uktā tad dīkṣā tatraiva deśikaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: what is prescribed by teachers for the month of Caitra is not faulty there.

children.text: ravau gurau tathā some kartavyaṃ budhaśukrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be performed on Sunday, Thursday, Monday, Wednesday, or Friday.
In the <s>Nāradatantra</s>:
Rohiṇī, Śravaṇa, Ārdrā, Dhaniṣṭhā, and the three Uttarās,
Puṣya and Śatabhiṣaj are called the nakṣatras for dīkṣā.
And in some texts:
In the lunar mansions Aśvinī, Rohiṇī, Svātī, Viśākhā, and Hasta,
and likewise in Jyeṣṭhā and the three Uttarās, one should perform the mantra-consecration.
In the <s>Sārasaṅgraha</s>:

children.text: dvitīyā pañcamī caiva ṣaṣṭhī caiva viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: The second, fifth, and sixth lunar days especially,

children.text: dvādaśyām api kartavyaṃ trayodaśyām athāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: and also on the twelfth and then on the thirteenth, it should be done.
And in some texts:

children.text: pūrṇimā pañcamī caiva dvitīyā saptamī tathā
children.translated_text: The full-moon day, the fifth, the second, and likewise the seventh,
the thirteenth and the tenth are praised and grant all desires.
Thus, on a pure day, in the bright fortnight, when Venus and Jupiter have risen,
with a good ascendant and the moon and stars favorable, dīkṣā is praised.
In the <s>Rudrayāmala</s>:
At a good tīrtha, during an eclipse of the sun or moon, and on the festivals of Tantu and Dāmana,
one should perform mantra-dīkṣā; one need not examine the month, lunar mansion, and so forth.
For the strength of a good ascendant, moon, stars, and the like is always present here;
a mantra obtained here increases long life, prosperity, and offspring.
There is no time equal to the time of a solar eclipse;

children.text: yatra yad yat kṛtaṃ sarvam anantaphaladaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: whatever is done there, all of it becomes productive of endless fruit;
at a solar parvan there is no examination of month, tithi, weekday, and the like.
And in the <s>Tattvasāgara</s>:

children.text: durlabhe sadgurūṇāṃ ca sakṛt saṅga upasthite
children.translated_text: When the rare company of true gurus has once presented itself,

children.text: tadanujñā yadā labdhā sa dīkṣāvasaro mahān ||
children.translated_text: and when permission from him has been obtained, that is a great occasion for dīkṣā.

children.text: grāme vā yadi vāraṇye kṣetre vā divase niśi
children.translated_text: Whether in a village, in a forest, at a sacred field, by day or by night,

children.text: āgacchati gurur daivād yadā dīkṣā tadājñayā ||
children.translated_text: when the guru comes by fate, then dīkṣā is to be done by his command.
Whenever he wishes, then dīkṣā is to be done in accordance with the guru's command.

children.text: na tīrthaṃ na vrataṃ homo na snānaṃ na japakriyā
children.translated_text: No tīrtha, no vrata, no homa, no bathing, no act of japa,

children.text: dīkṣāyāḥ karaṇaṃ kintu svecchāprāpte tu sadgurau ||
children.translated_text: is what makes dīkṣā happen; rather, it is when a true guru has come of his own accord.
Dīkṣā is fourfold, according to the distinctions beginning with kriyāvatī;
among them, kriyāvatī dīkṣā is written here only in brief.
Having consecrated the ground and worshiped the vāstu-deities there,
one should make a pavilion measuring seven hastas, with a beautiful altar-platform.
It should have eight flags, four entrances, and gateways made from milk-trees,
be furnished with triple-stranded cords, and be encircled with garlands of kuśa grass.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca diśi kauveryāṃ catuṣkoṇaṃ trimekhalam
children.translated_text: And in its northern direction, the wise man should make a square, three-belted
fire-pit measuring twenty-four aṅgulas.
He should make the excavation to that same extent, together with the height of the three belts,

children.text: tasmāt khātād bahiḥ kuryāt kaṇṭham ekāṅgulaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: and outside that excavation he should make a rim one aṅgula wide, certainly.
There, the height and breadth of the first <s>mekhalā</s> (rim) should be four finger-widths.
For the second they should be three finger-widths, and for the third two finger-widths.
And on the western side, above the set of three <s>mekhalās</s>,

children.text: ṣaḍaṅgulāṃ ca vistāre dairghye ca dvādaśāṅgulām ||
children.translated_text: one should make the <s>yoni</s> six finger-widths broad and twelve finger-widths long.
It should likewise be one finger-width high and furnished with an opening in the middle.
One should make it, according to rule, equipped with the <s>mekhalā</s> and shaped like <s>Gadādhara</s>.
For an oblation of fifty offerings, the <s>kuṇḍa</s> should be measured as an upright fist and hand.
For a hundred offerings it is one <s>aratni</s>; for a thousand it is measured by a hand.

children.text: lakṣe caturbhir hastaiś ca koṭau tair aṣṭabhir mitam
children.translated_text: For a lakh it is measured by four hands, and for a crore by eight such hands.
One should make the excavated <s>kuṇḍa</s> square, and below as well of the same form.

children.text: homas tv adhikasaṅkhyākaḥ kuṇḍe vai nyūnasaṅkhyayā
children.translated_text: A <s>homa</s> with a greater number of offerings may indeed be performed in a <s>kuṇḍa</s> made for a smaller number,

children.text: kṛte kāryo na c anyūnasaṅkhyākaḥ saṅkhyādhike ||
children.translated_text: but not one with a smaller number in a <s>kuṇḍa</s> made for a greater number.

children.text: yathāvidhy eva kartavyaṃ kuṇḍaṃ yatnena dhīmatā
children.translated_text: The wise person should carefully make the <s>kuṇḍa</s> exactly according to rule.
Otherwise many faults arise, bringing much suffering.
This has been stated by the tantric authorities:
A <s>kuṇḍa</s> furnished with such marks grants the desired result.
A <s>kuṇḍa</s> in which there is deficiency or excess gives rise to many faults.

children.text: tasmāt samyak parīkṣyaiva kartavyaṃ śubham icchatā
children.translated_text: Therefore one who desires auspiciousness should make it only after examining it properly.
