Or, in an abbreviated <s>homa</s> rite, there may be a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> measuring one hand.
Also according to <s>Hārīta</s>:
When the breadth is excessive or deficient, short life is surely produced.

children.text: khātādhikye bhaved yogī hīne tu dhanasaṃkṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: When the excavation is excessive one becomes a yogin; when it is deficient there is loss of wealth.

children.text: kuṇḍe vakre ca santāpo maraṇaṃ chinnamekhale ||
children.translated_text: In a crooked <s>kuṇḍa</s> there is distress, and in one with a broken <s>mekhalā</s>, death.
When the <s>mekhalā</s> is low there is grief, and when it is too high there is loss of livestock.
When the <s>yoni</s> is absent there is loss of one's wife; when the neck is absent there is loss of auspiciousness.
The measure of a finger-width is also stated:
Eight barley grains placed crosswise on their bellies, or three rice grains placed upright,
should be known as the measure of a finger-width, according to the middle joint of the middle finger.
Particular details needed elsewhere, such as the procedures for garlands, ladles, and offering spoons,
should be learned from another text; they are not written here for fear of prolixity.
Then, when the pavilion has been sprinkled with the five products of the cow and with scented water,
one should draw the initiation <s>maṇḍala</s> on the altar according to rule.
In its center there should be an eight-petalled lotus, and outside that three circles.
After that the zodiac signs, then the seat furnished with four feet.
Outside that, in the four directions, one should draw four pathways,
provided with auspicious and inauspicious corners, and then four doors.

children.text: prātaḥkṛtyaṃ guruḥ kṛtvā yathāsthānaṃ nyaset tataḥ
children.translated_text: After performing the morning duty, the guru should then place in their proper positions
the conch and the materials for worship, according to the procedure described earlier.

children.text: gurūn gaṇeśaṃ cābhyarcya pīṭhapūjāṃ vidhāya ca
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the gurus and <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and having performed the worship of the seat,

children.text: padmamadhye nyaset śālīṃs taṇḍulāṃś ca kuśāṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: he should place unhusked rice, husked rice, and <s>kuśa</s> grass in the middle of the lotus.
Upon the <s>kuśa</s> grass he should place the ten <s>kalās</s> of fire, beginning with the letters from ya onward,

children.text: nyasyābhyarcya japaṃs tāraṃ nyaset kumbhaṃ yathoditam ||
children.translated_text: worship them, recite the <s>tāra</s>, and place the pot as prescribed.
And these are stated:
<s>Dhūmrārci</s>, <s>Uṣmā</s>, <s>Jvalanī</s>, <s>Jvālinī</s>, <s>Visphuliṅginī</s>,
<s>Suśrī</s>, <s>Surūpā</s>, <s>Kapilā</s>, and also <s>Havyavahā</s> and <s>Kavyavahā</s>.

children.text: kādyaṣṭhāntair yutā bhādyair ḍāntaiś cārṇair vilomagaiḥ
children.translated_text: With the letters from ka to ṭha, and with the letters from bha to ḍa in reverse order,

children.text: sūryasya ca kalāḥ kumbhe dvādaśa nyasya pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: one should place the twelve <s>kalās</s> of the sun in the pot and worship them.

children.text: adhunā tasmin kuṇḍe sūryakalānāṃ nyāsādikaṃ likhati kādyair iti
children.translated_text: Now he writes in this <s>kuṇḍa</s> the placement and related rites of the sun's <s>kalās</s>, beginning with the phrase "with those from ka."

children.text: kakārādyaiṣ ṭhakārāntair arṇair varṇair yutā dvādaśāpi kalāḥ
children.translated_text: All twelve <s>kalās</s> are joined with the letters beginning with ka and ending with ṭha.
The word "and" has the sense of conjunction.
They are also joined with the letters beginning with bha and ending with ḍa.

children.text: nanu bhakārādīnāṃ dvādaśavarṇānāṃ ḍakārāntatā kathaṃ syāt krameṇa kṣakārāntatāprāptes tatrāhavilomagaiḥ vyutkramaprāptaiḥ
children.translated_text: If it is asked how the twelve letters beginning with bha can end with ḍa, since in the regular order they would reach kṣa, he says: "in reverse order," that is, obtained in inverse sequence.

children.text: ayam arthaḥ anulomapaṭhitakakārādyaikaikam akṣaraṃ pratilomapaṭhitabhakārādyekaikākṣareṇa sahitam ādau sūryakalāsu saṃyojya nyāsādikaṃ kuryād iti
children.translated_text: This is the meaning: first one should join each single syllable beginning with ka, read in forward order, with each single syllable beginning with bha, read in reverse order, in the sun's <s>kalās</s>, and then perform the placement and related rites.

children.text: prayogaś ca kaṃ bhaṃ tapanyai nama ityādi ||
children.translated_text: The practical application is: "kaṃ bhaṃ, obeisance to <s>Tapanī</s>," and so on.
And these are stated:

children.text: tapanī tāpanī dhūmrā bhrāmarī jvālinī ruciḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tapanī</s>, <s>Tāpanī</s>, <s>Dhūmrā</s>, <s>Bhrāmarī</s>, <s>Jvālinī</s>, and <s>Ruci</s>,

children.text: suṣumṇā bhogadā viśvā bodhinī dhāriṇī kṣamā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣumṇā</s>, <s>Bhogadā</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Bodhinī</s>, <s>Dhāriṇī</s>, and <s>Kṣamā</s>.
Inside the pot, with the root mantra, he should place a white flower,

children.text: sākṣataṃ sasitaṃ svarṇaṃ saratnaṃ ca kuśāṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: together with unbroken rice, sugar, gold, gems, and also <s>kuśa</s> grass.

children.text: tataś coktaprakāreṇādhārarūpam agniṃ kumbharūpaṃ sūryaṃ ca vicintya kumbhasya tasya antar madhye śuklakusumādikaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Then, in the manner stated, having meditated on fire as the support and on the sun as the form of the pot, he should place the white flower and the other substances in the middle inside that pot.
"With sugar" means together with crystallized sugar.
That has been stated:
Having lifted it up, he should place in its middle a white flower together with sugar,

children.text: svarṇaṃ ratnaṃ ca kūrcaṃ ca mūlenaiva vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: gold, a jewel, and a bundle of <s>kuśa</s> grass, by the root mantra alone.

children.text: yac ca mūlagranthārthād adhikaṃ kiṃcil likhate tat pūrvagatasya yathoditam ity asyānuvartanād iti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever little he writes in addition to the meaning of the root text should be understood from the continuation of the preceding phrase "as prescribed."

children.text: kumbhaṃ ca vidhinā tīrthāmbunā śuddhena pūrayet
children.translated_text: He should fill the pot, according to rule, with pure water from sacred bathing places.
In the water, having placed the moon's <s>kalās</s> together with the vowels, he should worship the sixteen.
And these are stated:

children.text: amṛtā mānadā pūṣā tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭī ratir dhṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Mānadā</s>, <s>Pūṣā</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Rati</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s>,

children.text: śaśinī candrikā kāntir jyotsnā śrīḥ prītir aṅgadā
children.translated_text: <s>Śaśinī</s>, <s>Candrikā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Jyotsnā</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, and <s>Aṅgadā</s>,
and <s>Pūrṇā</s> and <s>Pūrṇāmṛtā</s>.
Into a conch filled with pure water, having placed the eight fragrances and the <s>kalās</s>,

children.text: āvāhya sarvās tāḥ prāṇapratiṣṭhām ācaret kramāt ||
children.translated_text: he should invoke them all and perform the establishment of life-breath in due order.
The eight fragrances are also stated:

children.text: uśīraṃ kuṅkumaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ bālakaṃ cāgurur murā
children.translated_text: Vetiver, saffron, kuṣṭha, bālaka, aguru, and murā,
together with jaṭāmāṃsī and sandalwood: this is the desired gandhāṣṭaka (eight fragrances) for <s>Hari</s>.
By some, sandalwood, camphor, aguru, saffron, and rocanā,
together with kakkola and kapimāṃsī, are considered to be this gandhāṣṭaka (eight fragrances).
Likewise, the ten kalās born from akāra are to be assigned with the ten letters beginning with ka,
those born from ukāra with the eight letters beginning with ṭa, and those born from makāra with the letters beginning with pa.

children.text: catasro bindujāḥ ṣādyaiś caturbhir nādajāḥ kalāḥ
children.translated_text: Four kalās born from bindu are assigned with the four beginning with ṣa, and the kalās born from nāda likewise,

children.text: svaraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhir yuktā nyasecchaṅkhe ca ṣoḍaśa ||
children.translated_text: and, joined with the sixteen vowels, one should place the sixteen on the conch.
They are stated as follows:

children.text: sṛṣṭir ṛddhiḥ smṛtir medhā kāntir lakṣmīr dhṛtiḥ sthirā
children.translated_text: Sṛṣṭi, Ṛddhi, Smṛti, Medhā, Kānti, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, Dhṛti, and Sthirā,

children.text: sthitiḥ siddhir akārotthāḥ kalā daśa samīritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with Sthiti and Siddhi, are declared to be the ten kalās arisen from akāra.

children.text: jarā ca pālinī śāntir aiśvarī ratikāmike
children.translated_text: Jarā, Pālinī, Śānti, Aiśvarī, Rati, and Kāmikā,

children.text: varadā hlādinī prītir dīrghā cokārajāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Varadā, Hlādinī, Prīti, and Dīrghā are the kalās born from ukāra.

children.text: tīkṣṇā raudrā bhayā nidrā tantīḥ kṣut krodhanī kriyā
children.translated_text: Tīkṣṇā, Raudrā, Bhayā, Nidrā, Tantī, Kṣut, Krodhanī, and Kriyā,

children.text: utkārī caiva mṛtyuś ca makārākṣarajāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also Utkārī and Mṛtyu are the kalās born from the syllable makāra.

children.text: nivṛttiś ca pratiṣṭhā ca vidyā śāntis tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, Vidyā, and likewise Śānti,

children.text: indhikā dīpikā caiva recikā mocikā parā ||
children.translated_text: Indhikā, Dīpikā, Recikā, Mocikā, and Parā,

children.text: sūkṣmā sūkṣmāmṛtā jñānājñānā cāpy āyanī tathā
children.translated_text: Sūkṣmā, Sūkṣmāmṛtā, Jñānā, Ajñānā, and also Āyanī,
Vyāpinī, Vyomarūpā, and Anantā are born from nāda.

children.text: nyāsaṃ kalānāṃ sarvāsāṃ kuryād ekaikaśaḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: One should perform the nyāsa (ritual placement) of all the kalās one by one in order,
pronouncing the name in the dative ending and, with the respective letters, ending with namaḥ.
Before the prāṇapratiṣṭhā (installation of life-breath), after invoking those kalās,

children.text: ṛcaḥ pañca yathāsthānaṃ paṭhet tāś cārcayet kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should recite five Ṛgvedic verses in their proper places and worship those kalās.

children.text: haṃśaḥ śuciṣad ityādau pratad viṣṇus tataḥ param
children.translated_text: First comes the verse beginning haṃsaḥ śuciṣad, then, after that, pra tad <s>Viṣṇuḥ</s>,

children.text: tryambakaṃ tat savitur viṣṇur yonim iti kramāt ||
children.translated_text: then tryambakam, tat savitur, and <s>Viṣṇur</s> yonim, in that order.

children.text: tac ca śaṅkhodakaṃ kumbhe mūlamantreṇa nikṣipet
children.translated_text: He should put that conch-water into the pot with the root-mantra,
and cover its mouth with shoots of śakravallī, mango, and the like.
Then, covering it with a shallow dish furnished with flowers and other offerings,

children.text: saṃveṣṭya vastrayugmena tataḥ kumbhaṃ ca maṇḍayet ||
children.translated_text: and wrapping it with a pair of cloths, he should next adorn the pot.

children.text: tasminn āvāhya kalase paraṃ tejo yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Having invoked into that kalaśa (ritual pot) the supreme radiance according to rule,
the ācārya, making it complete with all its parts, should worship it with seats and the other offerings.
And sakalīkaraṇa (making complete with all parts) is explained:
the nyāsa of the six limbs on the body of the deity is sakalīkṛti.
Some say that, apart from the two hand-nyāsas, by all the other nyāsas,
the making of that radiance possessed of its limbs is what is called sakalīkṛta.

children.text: evaṃ ca kumbhe taṃ sāṅgopāṅgaṃ sāvaraṇaṃ prabhum
children.translated_text: Thus, in the pot, he should worship that Lord, with limbs, subsidiary limbs, and enclosing deities,
in front, according to the written prescription, up to the offering of food.
After the offering of naivedya (food), all around the maṇḍala,
he should place flour-made lamps, together with vessels containing seeds and sprouts.
Then, for the homa that forms part of initiation, on all sides of the fire-pit,
he should sweep with a darbha broom and smear it according to rule.

children.text: vikīrya sarṣapāṃs tatra gavyaiḥ samprokṣya pañcabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Scattering mustard seeds there and sprinkling it with the five products of the cow,
he should worship the Vāstupuruṣa in the middle and the lords of the directions in the quarters.
Having performed the drying and other rites of the fire-pit and sprinkled it with kuśa-water,
he should mark it out and draw in it a maṇḍala together with the yoni and the other parts.
Writing the śrībīja in the central yoni, sprinkling it, and worshipping it,
he should place there a spread of flowers and the like and arrange it properly.
There he should invoke and worship <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the intervening compound is textually uncertain.
Having brought the fire in a copper or similar vessel, he should set the pure fire in front.
After worshipping the fire with fragrances and the other offerings, he should meditate on this fire, while <s>Viṣṇu</s> sports with <s>Śrī</s>,
as being in the form of semen, and he should worship the fire-pit with the tāra (oṃ) syllable.
With the mantra beginning vaiśvānara, he should cover that fire with good fuel,
kindle it with the mantra beginning citpiṅgala, and attend upon it with the mantra beginning agnim.

children.text: jihvā nyasyet sapta tasminn apy aṅgeṣv aṅgadevatāḥ
children.translated_text: He should place the seven tongues in it, and the limb-deities on its limbs,

children.text: ṣaṭsu ṣaṭ nyasya mūrtīś ca nyasyāṣṭābhyarcayec ca tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: placing six forms in the six places and eight more, and he should worship them.
The seven tongues are stated:

children.text: hiraṇyā gaganā raktā tathā kṛṣṇā ca suprabhā
children.translated_text: Hiraṇyā, Gaganā, Raktā, and likewise Kṛṣṇā and Suprabhā,

children.text: bahurūpātirūpā ca sapta jihvā vasor imāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Bahurūpā and Atirūpā: these are the seven tongues of <s>Vasu</s>.
Sahasrārciḥ, Svastipūrṇa, and Uttiṣṭhapuruṣa,
Dhūmavyāpī, Saptajihva, and Dhanurdhara are remembered.
Jātavedas, Saptajihva, and Havyavāhana,
one called Aśvodaraja, and another called Vaiśvānara,
and also Kaumāratejas and Viśvadevamukha are so named.
Then, having spread the ritual grass around the fire and prepared the ghee according to rule,

children.text: hutvā ca vyāhṛtīḥ paścāt trīn vārān juhuyāt punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should offer the vyāhṛtis; afterward he should again make three oblations.
Then, for this fire, from garbhadhāna up to marriage, in due order,
he should perform the saṃskāras with the stated mantra and with eight oblations for each.

children.text: itthaṃ hi saṃskṛte vahnau pīṭham abhyarcya tatra ca
children.translated_text: In the fire consecrated in this way, after worshipping the pīṭha there,
and invoking the deity, he should worship it by the procedure beginning with fragrance and ending with lamps.
Conceiving that fire as the tongue of the deity, the wise man should offer one thousand and eight oblations,
with ghee mixed with sugar and milk-rice.
Then, after offering with ghee the great vyāhṛtis according to rule, the competent practitioner
should give bali, as prescribed, to the planets, lunar mansions, karaṇas, and the rest.

children.text: karṣamātraṃ ghṛtaṃ home śuktimātraṃ payaḥ smṛtam
children.translated_text: For the homa, a karṣa-measure of ghee is prescribed, and a śukti-measure of milk is remembered.
The five products of the cow are said by the wise to be equal to that measure.
Honey, milk, and cooked rice are equal to that; an akṣa-measure is stated.

children.text: dadhi prasṛtimātraṃ syāt lājāḥ syuḥ muṣṭisaṃmitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The curd should be only a prasṛti measure, and the parched grains should be measured by the handful.
Then, having bowed, and having given water for drinking and waters for sipping,
he should worship up to the self-offering and perform the rite according to the written procedure.
Then, after bringing in according to rule the disciple who is under vow and restrained in speech,

children.text: taddehe mātṛkāṃ sāṅgāṃ nyasyāthopadiśec ca tām ||
children.translated_text: he should place the <s>mātṛkā</s>, together with its limbs, on that one's body, and then teach it to him.
The guru, remembering the deity together with his enclosure and present in the ritual jar,
should recite one thousand and eight times and then lie down after tasting a little.
Seated on a black-antelope skin over darbha grass, remembering the <s>mātṛkā</s>,

children.text: guruṃ ca śiṣyo nidrāṇaṃ tāṃ śayīta japan vratī ||
children.translated_text: and also the guru, the vowed disciple should lie down, reciting it as he sleeps.

children.text: prātaḥkṛtyaṃ guruḥ kṛtvā kumbhaṃ cābhyarcya pūrvavat
children.translated_text: The guru, having performed the morning duties and having worshipped the jar as before,

children.text: hutvā dattvā baliṃ karmānyat kuryāt svārpaṇāvadhi ||
children.translated_text: should offer oblations, give the bali, and perform the rest of the rite up to the self-dedication.
With the saṃhāra-mudrā he should join the enclosure-deities to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: tam cāmṛtamayaṃ dhyātvā svasmiṃś cāgniṃ vilāpayet ||
children.translated_text: and, having contemplated him as made of nectar, he should dissolve the fire into himself.
The deities presiding over the banner, arches, directional jars, pavilion, and the rest

children.text: sarvā vibhāvya cidrūpāḥ kumbhe saṃyojya pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: he should conceive all as forms of consciousness, join them into the jar, and worship them.

children.text: ato guruṃ gaṇeśaṃ ca viṣvaksenaṃ ca pūjayet
children.translated_text: After this he should worship the guru, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and <s>Viṣvaksena</s>;

children.text: udvāsya kalasaṃ spṛṣṭvā śatam aṣṭottaraṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: having dismissed them and touched the kalaśa, he should recite one hundred and eight times.
Then the disciple, having fasted and having performed the morning duties,

children.text: śuklavastraḥ suveśaḥ san viprān dravyeṇa toṣayet ||
children.translated_text: wearing white garments and well adorned, should satisfy the Brahmins with gifts.

children.text: guruṃ ca bhagavaddṛṣṭyā parikramya praṇamya ca
children.translated_text: Seeing the guru as the Lord, he should circumambulate and bow to him,
and, after giving him the prescribed dakṣiṇā, should offer his own body.
And likewise in the Tenth Skandha:

children.text: iyad eva hi sacchiṣyaiḥ kartavyaṃ guruniṣkṛtam
children.translated_text: This alone is to be done by true disciples as repayment to the guru:
namely, with pure feeling, the offering of all purposes and of oneself to the guru.
In the bathing pavilion to the north of the sacrificial hall,
he should seat that disciple on a pīṭha and have him perform the drying and the other rites.
Having performed in full the nyāsa, up to the pīṭha-nyāsa and preceded by the mātṛkā-nyāsa,
on the disciple's body, he should worship him with the pīṭha-mantra.
He should place rocanā, together with dūrvā grass, unbroken rice, and flowers, on the disciple's head,
and bring the jar near him with music and the like.

children.text: śrīkṛṣṇam atha saṃprārthya guruḥ kumbhasya vāsasā
children.translated_text: Then, after supplicating <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the guru should wave the disciple ceremonially with the cloth of the jar
and place its leaves and other items on his head.
That has been said:
Having lifted the jar in the proper way, and having placed the divine-tree leaves from its mouth

children.text: śiśoḥ śirasi vinyasya mātṛkāṃ manasā japet ||
children.translated_text: on the child's head, he should mentally recite the mātṛkā.

children.text: tataḥ kumbhāmbhasā śiṣyaṃ prokṣya trir mūlamantrataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, with the water from the jar, he should sprinkle the disciple three times by means of the root-mantra;
with Brahmins' blessings and auspicious proclamations, he should consecrate him while reciting mantras.
In the <s>Vaśiṣṭhasaṃhitā</s>:
May the gods consecrate you: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, lord of the world, and also mighty <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: pradyumnaś cāniruddhaś ca bhavantu vibhavāya te
children.translated_text: <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s>; may they be for your prosperity.

children.text: ākhaṇḍalo 'gnir bhagavān yamo vai nirṛtis tathā ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>, divine <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and also <s>Nirṛti</s>,

children.text: varuṇaḥ pavanaś caiva dhanādhyakṣas tathā śivaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Pavana</s>, the lord of wealth, and also <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: brahmaṇā sahitā hy ete dikpālāḥ pāntu vaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: these guardians of the directions together with <s>Brahmā</s>, always protect you.

children.text: kīrtir lakṣmīr dhṛtir medhā puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: May <s>Kīrti</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Gati</s>,

children.text: buddhir lajjā vapuḥ śāntir māyā nidrā ca bhāvanā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Lajjā</s>, <s>Vapus</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Nidrā</s>, and <s>Bhāvanā</s>,

children.text: etās tvām abhiṣiñcantu rāhuḥ ketuś ca pūjitāḥ
children.translated_text: may these consecrate you, and <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Ketu</s>, when honored;
the gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, and serpents,

children.text: ṛṣayo munayo gāvo devamātara eva ca
children.translated_text: the ṛṣis, sages, cows, and the mothers of the gods,

children.text: devapatnyo dhruvā nāgā daityā apsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wives of the gods, the Dhruvas, Nāgas, Daityas, and hosts of Apsarases,
missiles and all weapons, kings and vehicles,

children.text: auṣadhāni ca ratnāni kālasyāvayavāś ca ye ||
children.translated_text: herbs and jewels, and all those that are divisions of time,

children.text: saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailās tīrthāni jaladā nadāḥ
children.translated_text: rivers, oceans, mountains, sacred fords, clouds, and streams,
may these consecrate you for the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
Having put on garments and sipped water, the disciple should go to the sacrificial pavilion,

children.text: gatvā bhaktyā guruṃ natvā guror āsīta dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: bow with devotion to the guru, and sit to the guru's right.
The guru, having offered perfumes and the other offerings, should present to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

children.text: nivedya pāyasaṃ kṛṣṇe kuryāt puṣpāñjaliṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: rice pudding in the measure of a man's meal, and then should make a flower offering.
He should make that disciple, adorned with the mudrās and other marks of the tradition and standing with folded hands,
truly a child of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> by the nyāsas beginning with the five-limbed nyāsa.

children.text: nyasya pāṇitalaṃ mūrdhni tasya karṇe ca dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: Having placed the palm of his hand on the disciple's head and at his right ear,
he should pronounce the mantra three times according to rule, together with its ṛṣi and the rest.

children.text: dīrghamantraṃ ca śiṣyasya yāvad āgrahaṇaṃ paṭhet
children.translated_text: He should recite the long mantra for the disciple until it is grasped,
and the disciple should recite it while contemplating the unity of guru, deity, and mantra.

children.text: sākṣataṃ gurur ādāya vāri śiṣyasya dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: The guru should take water with unbroken rice and place it in the disciple's right

children.text: kare'rpayed vadan mantro 'yaṃ samo 'stv āvayor iti ||
children.translated_text: hand, saying, "May this mantra be the same for us both."

children.text: svasmāj jyotirmayīṃ vidyāṃ gacchantīṃ bhāvayed guruḥ
children.translated_text: The guru should imagine the radiant vidyā going forth from himself,
and the disciple should imagine it as having arrived, thinking especially, "I am blessed."
Having given the disciple mahāprasāda, that rice pudding, the guru

children.text: nidadhyād akṣatān mūrdhni tasya yacchan śubhāśiṣam ||
children.translated_text: should place unbroken rice on his head while bestowing auspicious blessings.

children.text: guruṇā kṛpayā dattaṃ śiṣyaś cāvāpya taṃ manum
children.translated_text: And the disciple, having received that mantra given by the guru through compassion,
should recite it one hundred and eight times and then listen to the observances.
In the <s>Śrīnāradapañcarātra</s>:

children.text: svamantro nopadeṣṭavyo vaktavyaś ca na saṃsadi
children.translated_text: One's own mantra must not be taught, nor should it be spoken in an assembly;
likewise the śāstra is to be kept secret and protected like one's own body.
There should be supreme devotion toward Vaiṣṇavas, especially toward the teachers.

children.text: pūjanaṃ ca yathāśakti tān āpannāṃś ca pālayet ||
children.translated_text: And, according to one's ability, one should worship them and protect them when they have fallen into distress.

children.text: prāptam āyatanād viṣṇoḥ śirasāṃ praṇato vahet
children.translated_text: What has been received from the shrine of <s>Viṣṇu</s> one should carry on the head, bowing down,

children.text: nikṣiped ambhasi tato na pated avanau yathā ||
children.translated_text: and then deposit it in water, so that it does not fall upon the ground.
One should meditate on the deity <s>Viṣṇu</s> as abiding between the moon and the sun, and as present among cows, the aśvattha tree, and fire,
and as dwelling in the bodies of the guru and the learned brāhmaṇa.
Wherever, from envy, slander of the guru is heard,

children.text: tatra tatra na vastavyaṃ niryāyāt saṃsmaran harim ||
children.translated_text: one should not live there; one should depart, remembering <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: yaiḥ kṛtā ca guror nindā vibhoḥ śāstrasya nārada
children.translated_text: Those by whom censure has been made of the guru, of the Lord, or of scripture, O <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: nāpi taiḥ saha vastavyaṃ vaktavyaṃ vā kathañcana ||
children.translated_text: with them one should neither live nor speak in any way at all.

children.text: pradakṣiṇe prayāṇe ca pradāne ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: During circumambulation, when setting out, and especially when making a gift,

children.text: prabhāte ca pravāse ca svamantraṃ bahuśaḥ smaret ||
children.translated_text: and at dawn and while away from home, one should remember one's own mantra many times.
If in a dream, or directly before one's eyes, something wondrous and exceedingly joyous

children.text: akasmād yadi jāyeta na khyātavyaṃ guror vinā ||
children.translated_text: should suddenly arise, it should not be made known except to the guru.
In another <s>Pañcarātra</s> text:
I shall state the observances briefly from the <s>Pañcarātra</s>.
One should not eat fish, meat, turtle, or pig.
One should not eat from a bronze vessel, nor on leaves of the plakṣa or vaṭa trees.

children.text: devāgāre na niṣṭhīvet kṣutaṃ cātra vivarjayet
children.translated_text: One should not spit in a temple, and one should avoid sneezing there.
One should never enter the interior with feet wearing shoes.

children.text: ekādaśyāṃ na cāśnīyāt pakṣayor ubhayor api
children.translated_text: On <s>Ekādaśī</s>, in both fortnights, one should not eat,

children.text: jāgaraṃ niśi kurvīta viśeṣāc cārcayed vibhum ||
children.translated_text: one should keep vigil at night, and one should especially worship the Lord.
And in the <s>Sammohana-tantra</s>:

children.text: gopayed devatām iṣṭāṃ gopayed gurum ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: One should keep one's chosen deity secret; one should keep one's guru secret.

children.text: gopayec ca nijaṃ mantraṃ gopayen nijamālikām ||
children.translated_text: One should keep one's own mantra secret, and one should keep one's own rosary secret.
Among the observances of the guru, previously numbered at four hundred,
only when they have been accepted by the disciple do some consider there to be <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation).
And likewise in the <s>Viṣṇuyāmala</s>:
The guru should examine the disciple for a year, without negligence,

children.text: niyamān vihitān varjyān śrāvayec ca catuḥśatam ||
children.translated_text: and should cause him to hear the four hundred prescribed and forbidden rules.
Rising in the brāhma moment and awakening <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s>,
the waving of lights with musical instruments, and the morning bath according to rule;
wearing a pair of pure, unspoiled garments and worshipping the deity;
always applying the upward <s>puṇḍra</s> (sectarian mark) with <s>gopīcandana</s> clay;
wearing the five weapons and partaking of the foot-nectar;
wearing ornaments such as a rosary of <s>tulasī</s> beads every day;
worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone and, with devotion, of images;
eating the consecrated <s>tulasī</s> from the remnants, and gathering <s>tulasī</s> according to rule;

children.text: vidhinā tāntrikī sandhyā śikhābandho hi karmaṇi
children.translated_text: the tantric twilight rite according to rule, and tying the hair-tuft during ritual action;
the act of satisfying the ancestors with water from the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
worship of <s>Hari</s>, according to one's ability, with royal services;
daily and occasional rites that do not conflict with devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
performing purification of the elements and the rest, and all <s>nyāsas</s> (ritual placements) according to rule;
offering new fruits, flowers, and the like with devotion;
daily worship of <s>tulasī</s> and worship of the <s>Śrībhāgavata</s>;
worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> three times a day and hearing the <s>Purāṇas</s> every day;

children.text: viṣṇor niveditānāṃ vai vastrādīnāṃ ca dhāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: wearing the garments and other things that have been offered to <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
undertaking all meritorious acts with the vision that they belong to one's Lord;
receiving the guru's command, and faith in what has been spoken by the guru;
forming one's proper mudrās, and singing, dancing, and the like with devotion;
the auspicious sounds of the conch and other instruments, and the enactment of <s>Hari</s>'s sacred play and the like;
the regular performance of the daily fire offering and the giving of bali offerings according to rule;
welcoming and worshipping sādhus, and eating the remainder of the food offering;
taking the remainder of betel, and association with Vaiṣṇavas;
inquiry into special dharmas during the three days beginning with <s>Daśamī</s>;

children.text: vrate niyamataḥ svāsthyaṃ santoṣo yena kena vai ||
children.translated_text: in a vow, maintaining discipline, soundness of condition, and contentment with whatever may come;
performing festival journeys and the like, and the proper rule for the eight days;
and <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s observance for all seasons, with royal forms of service;
the complete observance of all Vaiṣṇava vows;
regarding the guru as the Lord, and always collecting <s>tulasī</s>;
the services beginning with putting to bed, and meditation on <s>Rāma</s> and the others.

children.text: sandhyayoḥ śayanaṃ naiva na śaucaṃ mṛttikāṃ vinā
children.translated_text: One should not sleep at the two twilights, and there is no purification without clay.
One should not sip water while standing, nor, likewise, sit on the guru's seat.
Stretching out the feet before the guru and crossing the guru's shadow;
neglect of bathing when one is able, and omission of deity worship;
failure to rise and the like before deities and gurus;
displaying learning in front of the guru, and arrogant action of the feet likewise;
applying tilaka and sipping water without mantra, and wearing blue-dyed clothing;
friendship and the like with nondevotees, and acceptance of false scripture;
attachment to the pleasure of low company, and consuming liquor and meat;
use of intoxicating medicines, and eating foods such as lentils;
eating vegetables such as bottle gourd and kalañja, and taking food from nondevotees;
undertaking non-Vaiṣṇava vows, and non-Vaiṣṇava recitation;
performing rites of sorcery and the like, and offering only secondary service when one is able;
being overpowered by grief and the like, and observing an improperly mixed <s>Ekādaśī</s> vow;
failure to distinguish the bright and dark fortnights, and improper business during a vow;
eating fruits and the like when one is able to fast, and performing <s>śrāddha</s> on <s>Ekādaśī</s>;
sleeping by day on <s>Dvādaśī</s>, and likewise plucking <s>tulasī</s> then;
daytime bathing of <s>Viṣṇu</s> there, and a <s>śrāddha</s> with things not offered to <s>Hari</s>;
at an auspicious increase-rite, a <s>śrāddha</s> without <s>tulasī</s>, and likewise a non-Vaiṣṇava <s>śrāddha</s>.
performing the rite of <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping) for purification even after drinking the <s>caraṇāmṛta</s> (water from the Lord's feet);
worship of <s>Vāsudeva</s> while seated on a wooden seat;
improper talk at the time of worship, and worship with oleander and similar items;
an iron incense vessel and the like, and a sideways <s>puṇḍra</s> mark through negligence;
and worship with unconsecrated substances, and with a restless mind;
obeisance with one hand and the like, and seeing the Lord at an improper time;
the offering of stale and otherwise spoiled foods and the like;
recitation of the <s>mantra</s> without counting, and also revealing the <s>mantra</s> openly;
when one has the ability, omitting the principal time and adopting a secondary time;
a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> should always avoid failing to accept the <s>prasāda</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: catuḥśataṃ vidhīn etān niṣedhān śrāvayed guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: The guru should teach these four hundred injunctions and prohibitions.
When acceptance has been firmly made, preceded by the rite of waving lights,
having caused the worship of the deity to be performed, he should recite the <s>mantra</s> into the right ear.

children.text: tataś cotthāya pūrṇātmā daṇḍavat praṇamed gurum
children.translated_text: Then, having risen, full in self-possession, he should bow down to the guru like a staff.
The disciple should place the lotus of his feet upon his own head.

children.text: atha nyāsān guruḥ svasmin kṛtvāntaryajanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Then the guru, having performed the <s>nyāsas</s> (ritual placements) on himself and also the inner worship,
should recite that <s>mantra</s> one thousand and eight times, so that his own power is not impaired.

children.text: śiṣyaḥ kumbhādi tat sarvaṃ dravam anyac ca śaktitaḥ
children.translated_text: The disciple, according to his ability, should give the pot and all those things, and whatever other wealth there is,

children.text: dattvābhyarcya guruṃ natvā viprān sampūjya bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: and, having honored and bowed to the guru, he should worship and feed the Brahmins.
Strengthened by the auspicious blessings of the revered guru and of the Brahmins,

children.text: tān anujñāpya gurvādīn bhuñjīta saha bandhubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: after receiving permission from them, beginning with the guru, he should eat together with his kinsmen.

children.text: iti dīkṣāvidhānena yo mantraṃ labhate guroḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, by the rite of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), one who receives a <s>mantra</s> from the guru

children.text: sa bhāgyavān cirañjīvī kṛtakṛtyaś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: becomes fortunate, long-lived, and one who has accomplished what had to be done.
And likewise, in the <s>Saṃmohanatantra</s>, in the dialogue of venerable <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Umā</s>:

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ kurute martyaḥ kare tasya vibhūtayaḥ
children.translated_text: A mortal who acts in this way has powers in his very hand.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ mahābhāge nānyat karmāsti bhūtale
children.translated_text: Therefore, O greatly fortunate one, there is no other act on earth beyond this,
by the mere performance of which <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself is directly pleased.
This tantric procedure has generally been stated in the <s>Prapañcasāra</s> and similar works;
now the divine Purāṇic procedure of <s>dīkṣā</s> is being written.
Now listen to me, O goddess, to the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god of gods,
which destroys the five great sins and bestows sons and wealth.
If in this birth a man on earth is afflicted by poverty, disease, leprosy, and the like,

children.text: alakṣmīvān aputras tu yo bhavet puruṣo bhuvi
children.translated_text: unfortunate and without sons,

children.text: tasya sadyo bhavel lakṣmīr āyur vittaṃ sutāḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: then for him at once there will be prosperity, life span, wealth, sons, and happiness.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu maṇḍale devi devaṃ devyā samanvitam
children.translated_text: When, O goddess, one sees in the <s>maṇḍala</s> the god accompanied by the goddess,

children.text: nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ devaṃ yaḥ paśyati vidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the supreme deity <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, seeing him according to the prescribed rite,
worshiped in the nine-naveled diagram and likewise on the sixteen-petalled lotus,
the deity shown by the ācārya, the <s>mantra</s>-formed, unborn one,

children.text: kārttike māsi śuddhāyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: in the bright fortnight of the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, especially on the twelfth lunar day,

children.text: sarvāsu ca yajed devaṃ dvādaśīṣu vidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and on all twelfth lunar days one should worship the deity according to rule.
At a <s>saṅkrānti</s> (solar transition), O greatly fortunate one, or at an eclipse of the moon or sun,

children.text: yaḥ paśyati hariṃ devaṃ pūjitaṃ guruṇā śubhe
children.translated_text: he who sees the deity <s>Hari</s>, O auspicious one, worshiped by the guru,

children.text: tasya sadyo bhavet tuṣṭiḥ pāpadhvaṃso 'py aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: for him at once there is satisfaction and complete destruction of sin.

children.text: sa sāmānyo hi devānāṃ bhavatīti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He becomes like the gods; of this there is no doubt.
The guru should examine Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras
for a year, by caste, purity, conduct, and the like.
Then, knowing those who have approached him, he should ascertain them in his heart.
They too, recognizing him with devotion as their own supreme lord,

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ guror bhaktiṃ kuryur viṣṇāv ivācalām ||
children.translated_text: should practice unwavering devotion to the guru for a year, as to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: saṃvatsaraṃ tataḥ pūrṇe guruṃ caiva prasādayet ||
children.translated_text: When the year is then complete, he should please the guru.
"O blessed one, by your grace we desire to cross the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: icchāmas tv aihikīṃ lakṣmīṃ viśeṣeṇa tapodhana ||
children.translated_text: and especially worldly prosperity, O treasure of austerity."

children.text: evam abhyarthya medhāvī guruṃ viṣṇum ivāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus entreated the wise guru before him as if he were <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and having worshiped him, then, permitted by him, on the tenth day of <s>Kārttika</s>,
having taken what is produced from a milk-sapped tree and consecrated by the highest one,
he should eat it and sleep on the ground in the presence of the god of gods.

children.text: svapnān dṛṣṭvā guror agre śrāvayeta vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen dreams, the discerning man should report them in the presence of the guru.

children.text: tataḥ śubhāśubhaṃ tadvad ālapet paramo guruḥ
children.translated_text: Then the supreme guru should speak accordingly about whether they are auspicious or inauspicious.
Having fasted on <s>Ekādaśī</s> and then bathed, he should go to the temple.

children.text: guruś ca maṇḍalaṃ bhūmau kalpitāyāṃ tu vartayet
children.translated_text: And the guru should lay out the <s>maṇḍala</s> on prepared ground,
after marking the ground according to rule with various signs.

children.text: ṣoḍaśāraṃ likhec cakraṃ navanābham athāpi vā
children.translated_text: He should draw a sixteen-spoked wheel, or else a nine-naveled one,

children.text: aṣṭapatram atho vāpi likhitvā darśayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or, having drawn an eight-petalled lotus, the wise man should show it.
He should carefully make a blindfold with a white cloth;
he should lead in the disciples, with flowers in their hands, in the order of the social classes.

children.text: navanābhaṃ yadā kuryān maṇḍalaṃ varṇakair budhaḥ
children.translated_text: When the wise man makes the nine-naveled <s>maṇḍala</s> with colored powders,

children.text: tadānīṃ pūrvato devam indram aindryāṃ tu pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: then, from the east, he should worship <s>Indra</s> as the deity in the eastern quarter.
Then in the southeast the twice-born should worship <s>Agni</s>, the guardian of the world;

children.text: yamaṃ tad anu yāmyāyāṃ nairṛtyāṃ nirṛtiṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: after that <s>Yama</s> in the southern quarter; in the southwest he should install <s>Nirṛti</s>.

children.text: vāruṇyāṃ varuṇaṃ caiva vāyavyāṃ pavanaṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: And in the western quarter he should worship <s>Varuṇa</s>; in the northwest he should worship <s>Pavana</s>.
Placing <s>Dhanada</s> in the north and <s>Rudra</s> in the northeast region,
having worshiped in this manner, especially on the directional petals,
on the lower petal he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme lord.

children.text: pūrvapatre balaṃ pūjya pradyumnaṃ dakṣiṇe tathā
children.translated_text: Having worshiped <s>Bala</s> on the eastern petal and <s>Pradyumna</s> likewise on the southern one,

children.text: aniruddhaṃ tathā pūjya paścime cottare tathā
children.translated_text: and having worshiped <s>Aniruddha</s> in the west, and likewise in the north,
he should worship <s>Vāsudeva</s>, who brings peace from all sins.

children.text: aiśānyāṃ vinyasecchaṅkham āgneyyāṃ cakram eva ca
children.translated_text: In the northeast he should place the conch, and in the southeast the discus.

children.text: saumyāyāṃ tu gadā pūjyā vāyavyāṃ padmam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: In the north the mace is to be worshipped, and in the northwest the lotus.

children.text: nairṛtyāṃ muṣalaṃ pūjyaṃ dakṣiṇe garuḍaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: In the southwest the pestle is to be worshipped, and likewise <s>Garuḍa</s> in the south.
A wise man should place <s>Lakṣmī</s> on the left side of the God of gods.

children.text: dhanuś caiva ca khaḍgaṃ ca devasya purato nyaset
children.translated_text: He should set the bow and also the sword in front of the deity.
And he should worship the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and the <s>Kaustubha</s> in front of the deity.
Having thus worshipped, according to rule, the God of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: diṅmaṇḍale ca vinyasya cāṣṭau kumbhān vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: and having placed eight pots in the circle of the directions according to prescription,

children.text: vaiṣṇavaṃ kalasaṃ caiva navamaṃ tatra kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: he should arrange there a ninth pot, the Vaiṣṇava pot.

children.text: snāpayen muktikāmāṃs tu vaiṣṇavena ghaṭena tu
children.translated_text: He should bathe those who desire liberation with the Vaiṣṇava pot.

children.text: śrīkāmān snāpayet tadvad aindreṇātha ghaṭena tu ||
children.translated_text: In the same way he should bathe those who desire prosperity with the Indra pot.
Those who desire victory and power he should consecrate with the southeastern pot.
By the rite for conquering death, bathing is likewise performed with the southern pot.
For the destruction of the wicked, the southwestern pot is prescribed as sufficient.
For appeasement, then, the western pot is used, and for the destruction of sin, the northwestern one.
For one who desires wealth and possessions, the northern pot is prescribed.

children.text: raudreṇa jñānahetus tu lokapālaghaṭās tv ime ||
children.translated_text: The northeastern pot is for the sake of knowledge; these are the pots of the guardians of the worlds.
A man bathed with even one of these becomes free from all sin.

children.text: bhaved avyāhatajñānaḥ śrīmāṃś ca puruṣaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: He becomes a man of unobstructed knowledge and always possessed of prosperity.

children.text: kiṃ punar navabhiḥ snāto naraḥ pātakavarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: How much more, then, does a man bathed with all nine become free from sin?
At once he becomes equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or else a king.
Alternatively, in all the directions, in their proper order, he should worship the guardians of the worlds
by their own names, according to the rule divided into six parts.

children.text: evaṃ sampūjya devāṃs tu lokapālān prasannadhīḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus fully worshipped the gods, the guardians of the worlds, with a clear and pleased mind,
he should afterwards lead in the examined disciples, their eyes bound.
After they have been burned by the fire visualization and then shaken off by the wind,
and afterwards made to flourish by the moon, the wise teacher should make them hear the observances.

children.text: na ninded abrāhmaṇān devān viṣṇuṃ brāhmaṇam eva ca
children.translated_text: He should not disparage non-Brahmins, the gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or a Brahmin.

children.text: rudram ādiyam agniṃ ca lokapālān grahāṃs tathā
children.translated_text: He should revere <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, fire, the guardians of the worlds, and the planets,
and also a Vaiṣṇava man who has received prior initiation.

children.text: evaṃ tu samayān śrāvya paścāddhomaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: After making him hear the covenants in this way, he should then have the homa performed.
Having placed the principles in the bodies of the disciples, he should purify them.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate viṣṇave sarvarūpiṇe huṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: "Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose forms are all forms; huṃ, svāhā."
With the sixteen-syllabled mantra, while the fire is blazing, he should offer oblations.

children.text: garbhādhānādikāś caiva kriyāḥ sarvāś ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should also have all the rites performed, beginning with impregnation.
With three oblations each, in the presence of the God of gods,

children.text: tato 'panīya dṛgbandhaṃ puraḥ śiṣyaṃ niveśya ca
children.translated_text: then, having removed the blindfold and seated the disciple in front,

children.text: prāyaḥ pūrvoktavidhinā mantraṃ tasmai gurur diśet ||
children.translated_text: the guru should teach him the mantra, generally according to the procedure stated before.
At the end of the homa, the initiated person should afterwards cause the guru's fee to be given.
A king should give elephants, horses, jewels, bracelets, gold, villages, and the like.

children.text: dāpayed gurave prājño madhyamo madhyamāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A wise man of middling means should give a middling fee to the guru.
Another should give a pair together with gold, according to rule.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte tu yat puṇyaṃ māhātmyaṃ jāyate dhare
children.translated_text: O Earth, the merit and greatness that arise when this has been done

children.text: tad aśakyaṃ tu gaditum api varṣaśatair api ||
children.translated_text: cannot be fully told, even in hundreds of years.

children.text: dīkṣitātmā guror bhūtvā vārāhaṃ śṛṇuyād yadi
children.translated_text: If, after becoming one whose self is initiated by the guru, a person hears the <s>Vārāha</s>,

children.text: tena vedāḥ purāṇāni sarve mantrāḥ susaṅgrahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then for him the Vedas, the Purāṇas, and all mantras are well gathered together.

children.text: japtāḥ syuḥ puṣkare tīrthe prayāge sindhusāgare
children.translated_text: It is as though they had been recited at the sacred ford of <s>Puṣkara</s>, at <s>Prayāga</s>, at the ocean into which the <s>Sindhu</s> flows,
at <s>Devahūta</s>, at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, and especially at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: graheṇa viṣuve caiva yat phalaṃ japatāṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The result that would belong to those who recite at an eclipse or at an equinox

children.text: tat phalaṃ dviguṇaṃ tasya dīkṣito yaḥ śṛṇoti ca ||
children.translated_text: is twice that result for the initiated person who hears it.

children.text: devā api tapaḥ kṛtvā dhyāyanti ca vadanti ca
children.translated_text: Even the gods, having practiced austerity, meditate and say:

children.text: kadā me bhārate varṣe janma syād bhūtadhāriṇi ||
children.translated_text: "When shall I have birth in the land of <s>Bhārata</s>, O bearer of beings?

children.text: dīkṣitāś ca bhaviṣyāmo vārāhaṃ śṛṇumaḥ kadā
children.translated_text: When shall we become initiated and hear the <s>Vārāha</s>?
When, joined with a body, shall we see the <s>Vārāha</s>, whose self is sixteenfold,

children.text: paśyāmaḥ paramaṃ sthānaṃ yad gatvā na punar bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the supreme place, having gone to which one does not come back?"

children.text: evaṃ jalpanti vibudhā manasā cintayanti ca
children.translated_text: Thus the wise gods speak and ponder in their minds:
"When shall we see the <s>Vārāha</s> sacrifice in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, O Earth?"

children.text: eṣa te vidhir uddiṣṭo mayā te bhūtadhāriṇi
children.translated_text: This procedure has been stated to you by me, O bearer of beings.
It is in every way difficult for gods, Gandharvas, and Yakṣas to obtain.

children.text: evaṃ yo vetti tattvena yaś ca paśyati maṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Thus, whoever knows this truly and whoever sees the <s>maṇḍala</s>,

children.text: yaś cemaṃ śṛṇuyād devi sarve muktā iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whoever hears this, O goddess, all are liberated: so says revelation.

children.text: saṃkṣiptaś cātha dīkṣāyā vidhir eṣa vilikhyate
children.translated_text: Now this abbreviated procedure for initiation is written down

children.text: mukhyakalpe hy aśaktasya janasya syāddhitāya ca ||
children.translated_text: for the benefit of a person who is unable to perform the primary rite.
Then, when a very auspicious moment has arrived, on a <s>sarvatobhadra-maṇḍala</s>,
he should place a new pot adorned with fragrances, flowers, and the like.
It should be covered with cloth, filled with milk, and furnished with five shoots,
containing all herbs, five jewels, and seven kinds of earth.
The seven kinds of earth are stated:
from a horse-stable, from an elephant-stable, from an anthill, and from a crossroads,

children.text: rājadvārāc ca goṣṭhāc ca nadyāḥ kūlān mṛdaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: from a royal gate, from a cow pen, and earth from a river bank are remembered.

children.text: kṛṣṇam abhyarcya taṃ kumbhaṃ kuśakūrcena deśikaḥ
children.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and that pot, the teacher, with a bundle of <s>kuśa</s> grass,
should consecrate it a thousand and eight times with the mantra to be given.
With those waters, having consecrated the disciple as before, he should teach him the mantra.

children.text: śiṣyo 'rcayed guruṃ bhaktyā yathāśakti dvijān api ||
children.translated_text: The disciple should worship the guru with devotion, and the Brahmins too, according to his ability.
Now the instruction in the <s>Tattvasāgara</s>:

children.text: atrāpy aśaktaḥ kaścic ced abjam abhyarcya sākṣatam
children.translated_text: Here too, if someone is unable, having directly worshipped the lotus
Having sprinkled him with that water eight times with the root-mantra...

children.text: nidhāyāmuṃ japet karṇe upadeśeṣv ayaṃ vidhiḥ
children.translated_text: and having placed this in his ear, he should recite it; this is the rule in acts of instruction.
At a lunar or solar eclipse, at a sacred ford, at a siddha-field, or in a temple of <s>Śiva</s>,
the mere declaration of the mantra is called <s>upadeśa</s> (instruction).
In those several cases there is this special rule in the <s>Śrīnāradapañcarātra</s>:
For an embodied person free from greed for wealth, whose resources are small,
who is afraid of saṃsāra and is truly a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: agnāv ājyānvite bījaiḥ salilaiḥ kevalaiś ca vā
children.translated_text: with seeds in a fire supplied with ghee, or with water alone,
for one lacking materials the guru should bestow grace by speech.
One who is equal toward all beings, dispassionate, free of envy,
self-controlled, pure, capable, and complete in all limbs and bodily parts,

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā bhīte cābhayadaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: who always gives fearlessness to the frightened by deed, mind, and speech,
who has reached the state of equal understanding and, even there, is filled with the Lord,
who is devoted to the five daily times and knows the meaning of the <s>Pañcarātra</s>,
having understood the truth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which is one and yet proceeds into many distinctions,

children.text: vīkṣayen medinīṃ sarvāṃ kiṃ punaś copasannatān ||
children.translated_text: should look upon the whole earth in that way; how much more upon those who have approached him.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: iha kīrtiṃ vadānyatvaṃ prajāvṛddhiṃ dhanaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: Here, through the gift of knowledge, a sāttvika person obtains fame, generosity, increase of offspring, wealth, and happiness;
through the gift of knowledge he obtains them; there is no doubt about this.
Just as the supreme Lord is highest among all the gods,
so too the gift of knowledge is remembered as the highest of all gifts.

children.text: yāvac ca pātakaṃ tena kṛtaṃ janmaśatair api
children.translated_text: Whatever sin has been committed by him even through hundreds of births,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ nāśam āpnoti vidyādānena dehinām ||
children.translated_text: all that comes to destruction through giving knowledge to embodied beings.

children.text: vidyādānāt paraṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: No gift higher than the gift of knowledge has existed or will exist,
by the giving of which one attains <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause.

children.text: iti śrīgopālabhaṭṭavilikhite śrībhagavadbhaktivilāse daikṣiko nāma dvitīyo vilāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Śrībhagavadbhaktivilāsa</s> written by <s>Śrī Gopālabhaṭṭa</s>, the second vilāsa, called the initiation section, is complete.
I venerate <s>Śrīcaitanya Mahāprabhu</s>, whose lordly power is endless and wondrous;
by his grace even a lowly person may become a promoter of right conduct.
For a man who has received initiation and intends to worship <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the conduct that is his duty is written down according to śruti and smṛti.

children.text: labdhvā mantraṃ tu yo nityaṃ nārcayen mantradevatām
children.translated_text: But one who, having received a mantra, does not worship the deity of the mantra daily,
for him that deity makes the fruit of all actions inauspicious.

children.text: na kiṃcit kasyacit sidhyet sadācāraṃ vinā yataḥ
children.translated_text: Since nothing succeeds for anyone without <s>sadācāra</s> (right conduct),

children.text: tasmād avaśyaṃ sarvatra sadācāro hy apekṣyate ||
children.translated_text: therefore <s>sadācāra</s> is certainly required everywhere.
In the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>:
The supreme person, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is worshipped by a person who possesses the conduct of varṇa and āśrama;
there is no other path that causes his satisfaction.
In the <s>Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Śrī Madālasā</s> and <s>Alarka</s>:
A householder must always maintain proper conduct;

children.text: na hy ācāravihīnasya sukham atra paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: for one devoid of conduct has no happiness either here or hereafter.
Sacrifices, gifts, and austerities here do not serve the welfare of the person
who acts after having overstepped <s>sadācāra</s>.
And in the <s>Bhaviṣyottara</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>:

children.text: ācārahīnaṃ na punanti vedāḥ yadyapy adhītāḥ saha ṣaḍbhir aṅgaiḥ
children.translated_text: The Vedas do not purify one who lacks conduct, even though they have been studied together with the six ancillary sciences;

children.text: chandāṃsy enaṃ mṛtyukāle tyajanti nīḍaṃ śakuntā iva jātapakṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: at the time of death the meters abandon him, like birds leaving a nest when their wings have grown.

children.text: kapālasthaṃ yathā toyaṃ śvadṛtau vā yathā payaḥ
children.translated_text: As water in a skull, or as milk in a dog's skin,
would be spoiled by the defect of its place, so too there is inauspiciousness in one whose behavior is deficient.
O king, a person without conduct prospers neither here nor hereafter.
By what has been written, the obligatoriness of remembrance and the rest will indeed be established,
and so too the obligatoriness of <s>sadācāra</s>, even when it consists of remembrance and the like.
In the same <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>, in the context of the duties of a householder:

children.text: sadācāravatā puṃsā jitau lokāv ubhāv api ||
children.translated_text: By a man possessed of good conduct, both worlds are conquered.
The good are those whose faults are diminished, and the word sat denotes a good person;

children.text: teṣām ācaraṇaṃ yat tu sadācāraḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the conduct of such people is called <s>sadācāra</s>.
In the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Agastya</s>:
Death afflicts a Brahmin who is habitually without study and who transgresses <s>sadācāra</s>,
who is lazy and eats bad food.
Therefore a twice-born man should always practice <s>sadācāra</s> with effort;
even sacred fords desire association with one of good conduct.
And in the same <s>Bhaviṣyottara</s>:
Dharma arises from conduct, and the good are marked by conduct;

children.text: sādhūnāṃ ca yathā vṛttaṃ sa sadācāra iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: whatever the behavior of good people is, that is accepted as <s>sadācāra</s>.

children.text: tasmāt kuryāt sadācāraṃ ya icched gatim ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore one who desires his own spiritual course should practice <s>sadācāra</s>.
Even if he lacks all marks, O king, a man possessed of proper conduct,
faithful and free from envy, obtains all desires.
Moreover:

children.text: ācāra eva dharmasya mūlaṃ rājan kulasya ca
children.translated_text: Conduct alone, O king, is the root of dharma and of family standing;

children.text: ācārād vicyuto jantur na kulīno na dhārmikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: a being fallen away from conduct is neither noble-born nor righteous.
Moreover:
Conduct produces prosperity; conduct increases fame;

children.text: ācārād vardhate hy āyur ācāro hanty alakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: from conduct life span increases, and conduct destroys inauspicious marks.

children.text: ācāra eva nṛpapuṅgava sevyamāno dharmārthakāmaphalado bhaviteha puṃsām
children.translated_text: O best of kings, conduct, when practiced, here grants people the fruits of dharma, wealth, and desire;

children.text: tasmāt sadaiva viduṣāvahitena rājan śāstrodito hy anudinaṃ paripālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O king, it should always be followed every day by a wise and attentive person, just as taught in scripture.

children.text: brāhme muhūrta utthāya kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti kīrtayan
children.translated_text: Having risen at the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn time) while chanting '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,'
and having washed his hands and feet, he should clean his teeth.

children.text: ācamya vasanaṃ rātres tyaktvānyat paridhāya ca
children.translated_text: Having sipped water, discarded the garment of the night, and put on another,
he should again perform sipping of water according to the rule to be written below.

children.text: athecchan paramāṃ śuddhiṃ mūrdhni dhyātvā guroḥ padau
children.translated_text: Then, desiring supreme purity, having meditated on the guru's feet on his head...

children.text: stutvā ca kīrtayan kṛṣṇaṃ smaraṃś caitad udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: And after praising and extolling <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, remembering him, he should utter this:

children.text: jayati jananivāso devakījanmavādo yaduvarapariṣat svair dorbhir asyann adharmam
children.translated_text: Victorious is he who dwells among his people, whose birth from <s>Devakī</s> is proclaimed, who is surrounded by the foremost <s>Yadus</s>, and who with his own arms casts down <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness),

children.text: sthiracaravṛjinaghnaḥ susmita śrīmukhena vrajapuravanitānāṃ vardhayan kāmadevam ||
children.translated_text: who destroys the affliction of the moving and unmoving, and who, with his smiling, beautiful face, increases the desire of the women of <s>Vraja</s>.
When he is remembered, a person becomes a vessel of every auspicious good;

children.text: puruṣas tam ajaṃ nityaṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ harim ||
children.translated_text: I go for refuge to that unborn, eternal <s>Hari</s>.
I take refuge in the butter-thief, the Brahman whose whole body is marked with the signs of union with the clever cowherd lovers,

children.text: pavitram āmnāyagirām agamyaṃ brahma prapadye navanītacauram ||
children.translated_text: holy and beyond the reach of the words of the revealed tradition.
In the Tenth Skandha:

children.text: udgāyatīnām aravindalocanaṃ vrajāṅganānāṃ divam aspṛśad dhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: The sound of the women of <s>Vraja</s>, singing aloud of the lotus-eyed one, touched the sky,

children.text: dadhnaś ca nirmanthanaśabdamiśrito nirasyate yena diśām amaṅgalam ||
children.translated_text: mixed with the sound of churning curds; by it the inauspiciousness of the directions is driven away.
And again, following the tradition of the good, one should recite
these four verses for the pacification of all faults and for the attainment of good fortune.

children.text: prātaḥ smarāmi bhavabhītimahārtiśāntyai nārāyaṇaṃ garuḍavāhanam abjanābham
children.translated_text: At dawn I remember <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who rides on <s>Garuḍa</s>, whose navel is a lotus, for the pacification of the great pain of fear of worldly existence;
he is the cause of release for the noble lordly elephant of the waters, overpowered by the crocodile; he bears the discus as his weapon, and his eyes are like young lotus petals.

children.text: prātar namāmi manasā vacasā ca mūrdhnā pādāravindayugalaṃ paramasya puṃsaḥ
children.translated_text: At dawn I bow, with mind, speech, and head, to the pair of lotus feet of the Supreme Person,
of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who carries one across the ocean of hell and who is devoted to Brahmins intent on sacred recitation.

children.text: prātar bhajāmi bhajatām abhayaṅkaraṃ taṃ prāk sarvajanmakṛtapāpabhayāvahatyai
children.translated_text: At dawn I worship him who grants fearlessness to those who worship him, for the removal of the fear-bearing sins committed in all former births,
he who, holding uplifted conch and discus, destroyed the terrible grief of <s>Gajendra</s>, whose foot had fallen into the crocodile's mouth.

children.text: ślokatrayam idaṃ puṇyaṃ prātaḥ prātaḥ paṭhet tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever recites these three holy verses morning after morning,
<s>Hari</s>, the teacher of the three worlds, will grant him his own state.

children.text: tad etal likhitaṃ kutra kutracid vyavahārataḥ
children.translated_text: This has been written here and there according to practical usage;
but one should meditate on the desired form and other aspects of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Thus he should perform the Lord's kīrtana (praise), remembrance, and the like,
which are truly bathing in all sacred fords and purification both outward and inward.

children.text: tathā ca skānde skandaṃ prati śrīśivoktau
children.translated_text: And similarly, in the <s>Skanda</s>, in <s>Śrī Śiva</s>'s statement to <s>Skanda</s>:
Having once said '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,' a man, for three hundred kalpas,
has bathed in all sacred fords beginning with the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, my son.
And elsewhere:

children.text: śayanād utthito yas tu kīrtayen madhusūdanam
children.translated_text: But one who, risen from sleep, praises <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: kīrtanāt tasya pāpasya nāśam āyāty aśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: by that praise, his sin comes to complete destruction.
The greatness of kīrtana is to be written later in its main context;

children.text: smaraṇasya tu māhātmyam adhunā likhyate kiyat ||
children.translated_text: but now something of the greatness of remembrance is being written.
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the <s>Bṛhatsahasranāman</s> hymn:

children.text: smartavyaḥ satataṃ viṣṇur vismartavyo na jātucit
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is always to be remembered and is never to be forgotten;

children.text: sarve vidhiniṣedhāḥ syur etayor eva kiṅkarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all injunctions and prohibitions are servants of just these two.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the Kārttika section, in the statement of <s>Śrīmad Agastya</s>:

children.text: sā hānis tan mahac chidraṃ sa mohaḥ sa ca vibhramaḥ
children.translated_text: That is loss; that is a great breach; that is delusion, and that indeed is confusion:

children.text: yanmuhūrtaṃ kṣaṇaṃ vāpi vāsudevo na cintyate ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Vāsudeva</s> is not thought of for a muhūrta or even for a moment.
And in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, in the account of <s>Śrī Dhruva</s>:

children.text: iyam eva parā hānir upasargo 'yam eva ca
children.translated_text: This alone is supreme loss, and this alone is calamity;

children.text: abhāgyaṃ paramaṃ caitad vāsudevaṃ na yat smaret ||
children.translated_text: this is the highest misfortune: that one does not remember <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: ye muhūrtāḥ kṣaṇā ye ca yāḥ kāṣṭhā ye nimeṣakāḥ
children.translated_text: Those muhūrtas, moments, kāṣṭhās, and nimeṣas

children.text: ṛte viṣṇusmṛter yātās teṣu muṣṭo yamena saḥ ||
children.translated_text: that have passed without remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>: in them that person has been robbed by <s>Yama</s>.
Although this is obligatory, its greatness,
because it grants varied results, should be known by the wise as taught in scripture, like the darśa-pūrṇamāsa sacrifices and the like.
And it has also been said by Smārta authorities:

children.text: māntraṃ pārthivam āgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ divyam eva ca
children.translated_text: Mantric, earthy, fiery, airy, heavenly,

children.text: vāruṇaṃ mānasaṃ ceti snānaṃ saptavidhaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: watery, and mental: bathing is remembered as sevenfold.

children.text: śaṃ na āpas tu vai māntraṃ mṛdālambhaṃ tu pārthivam
children.translated_text: The mantric bath is with 'śaṃ no āpaḥ'; the earthy is the touching of the body with clay;
bathing with ash is fiery; bathing with dust raised by cows is airy.

children.text: ātape sati yā vṛṣṭir divyaṃ snānaṃ tad ucyate
children.translated_text: Rain falling while the sun is shining is called heavenly bathing;

children.text: bahir nadyādiṣu snānaṃ vāruṇaṃ procyate budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: external bathing in rivers and the like is called watery by the wise;

children.text: dhyānaṃ yan manasā viṣṇor mānasaṃ tat prakīrtanam ||
children.translated_text: meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the mind is proclaimed as mental bathing.
Moreover:
Because of bodily incapacity or dependence on time, place, and the like,

children.text: tulyaphalāni sarvāṇi syur ity āha parāśaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them may have equal fruit, so <s>Parāśara</s> says.

children.text: snānānāṃ mānasaṃ snānaṃ manvādyaiḥ paramaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Among baths, the mental bath is remembered by <s>Manu</s> and others as supreme;

children.text: kṛtena yena mucyante gṛhasthā api vai dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: by performing it, even twice-born householders are indeed liberated.
In the <s>Garuḍa</s>, in <s>Śrī Nārada</s>'s statement, and in <s>Viṣṇudharma</s>, in <s>Pulastya</s>'s statement:

children.text: apavitraḥ pavitro vā sarvāvasthāṃ gato 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Impure or pure, or even in whatever condition one may be,

children.text: yaḥ smaret puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ sa bāhyābhyantaraḥ śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever remembers <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> is pure both outwardly and inwardly.
Even if one has been afflicted by sins difficult to overcome even by mental effort,

children.text: tathāpi saṃsmaran viṣṇuṃ sa bāhyābhyantaraḥ śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, remembering <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he is pure both outwardly and inwardly.
In the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:
All expiations without remainder that consist of austerity and ritual action,
of all those without remainder, remembrance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is supreme.

children.text: kṛte pāpe'nutāpo vai yasya puṃsaḥ prajāyate
children.translated_text: For the man in whom remorse arises after sin has been committed,
the one supreme expiation for him is remembrance of <s>Hari</s>.
Moreover:
The exceedingly fierce impurity of the Kali age, which gives the torment of hell to people,
immediately goes to dissolution when he is remembered even once.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bali</s>:

children.text: harir harati pāpāni duṣṭacittair api smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> removes sins even when remembered by those with wicked minds;

children.text: anicchayāpi saṃspṛṣṭo dahaty eva hi pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for fire, even when touched unintentionally, certainly burns.
In that same place, at the end of the discussion of expiation:
Even one joined with a great sin, or joined with all sins,

children.text: sa vai vimucyate sadyo yasya viṣṇuparaṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is indeed released at once, if his mind is fixed supremely on <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>:

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā yaḥ kṛtaḥ pāpasañcayaḥ
children.translated_text: The accumulation of sin that has been made by deed, mind, and speech

children.text: so 'py aśeṣaḥ kṣayaṃ yāti smṛtvā kṛṣṇāṅghripaṅkajam ||
children.translated_text: also goes entirely to destruction when one remembers the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Therefore it is said in the <s>Skanda</s>, in the <s>Kārttika</s> section, by <s>Śrīparāśara</s>:

children.text: yamamārgaṃ mahāghoraṃ narakāṃś ca yamaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The dreadful path of <s>Yama</s>, the hells, and <s>Yama</s> himself

children.text: svapne'pi na naraḥ paśyed yaḥ smared garuḍadhvajam ||
children.translated_text: a man does not see even in a dream, if he remembers <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s>.
In the sixth skandha, by <s>Śrīśuka</s>:

children.text: sakṛn manaḥ kṛṣṇapadāravindayor niveśitaṃ tadguṇarāgi yair iha
children.translated_text: Those by whom the mind has once been fixed here on the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, delighting in his qualities,

children.text: na te yamaṃ pāśabhṛtaś ca tadbhaṭān svapne 'pi paśyanti hi cīrṇaniṣkṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not see <s>Yama</s>, nor the noose-bearing servants of his, even in a dream, for they have performed expiation.
In the <s>Śrīviṣṇupurāṇa</s>, in <s>Śrīprahlāda</s>'s statement:

children.text: dantā gajānāṃ kulśāgraniṣṭhurāḥ śīrṇā yad ete na balaṃ mamaitat
children.translated_text: The tusks of the elephants, harsh as thunderbolt tips, were shattered; that this happened is not my strength.
This is the power of remembering <s>Janārdana</s>, which destroys the fall into great calamity.
And in the <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>:
The <s>Viṣṭi</s> periods, <s>Vyatipāta</s> conjunctions, and whatever other afflictions arise from bad conditions,

children.text: te sarve smaraṇād viṣṇor nāśam āyānty upadravāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all those troubles come to destruction through remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the greatness of <s>Māgha</s>, in the praise by <s>Devadyuti</s>:

children.text: yasya smaraṇamātreṇa na moho na ca durgatiḥ
children.translated_text: By the mere remembrance of whom there is no delusion and no bad destiny,

children.text: na rogo na ca duḥkhāni tam anantaṃ namāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: no disease and no sufferings, to that infinite one I bow.
In the twelfth skandha:

children.text: yathā hemni sthito vahnir durvarṇaṃ hanti dhātujam
children.translated_text: As fire situated in gold destroys the bad color born from ore,
so <s>Viṣṇu</s>, present within the self, destroys the inauspicious disposition of yogins.
In the <s>Pāṇḍavagītā</s>:

children.text: lābhas teṣāṃ jayas teṣāṃ kutas teṣāṃ parābhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Theirs is gain, theirs is victory; how could defeat belong to them
in whose hearts stands <s>Janārdana</s>, dark as a blue lotus?
Its giving of the fruit of all good deeds: in the <s>Skanda</s>, in the <s>Kārttika</s> section, in <s>Agastya</s>'s statement:

children.text: deveṣu yajñeṣu tapaḥsu caiva dāneṣu tīrtheṣu vrateṣu caiva
children.translated_text: Among gods, sacrifices, austerities, gifts, sacred fords, and vows,

children.text: iṣṭeṣu pūrteṣu ca yat pradiṣṭaṃ nṝṇāṃ smṛte tatphalam acyute ca ||
children.translated_text: and in sacrificial and public works, whatever fruit is prescribed for men, that fruit comes when <s>Acyuta</s> is remembered.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>:
In the Kali age, deficiency and excess are established in rites enjoined by the Veda.
Here only remembrance of <s>Hari</s> gives the complete fruit.
And in the smṛti:
Whatever falls short in sacrifices for those who perform rites through negligence,

children.text: smaraṇād eva tad viṣṇoḥ sampūrṇaṃ syād iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by the mere remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s> that becomes complete: so says revelation.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>, in the section on Kali:
The fruit of gifts of one's weight in gold, of the <s>Rājasūya</s>, and of the <s>Aśvamedha</s>

children.text: phalaṃ viṣṇoḥ smṛtisamaṃ na jātu dvijasattama ||
children.translated_text: is never equal to remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of twice-born men.
In the twelfth skandha:
By knowledge, austerity, restraint of breath, friendliness, bathing at sacred fords, vows, gifts, and muttered recitation,

children.text: nātyantaśuddhiṃ labhate 'ntarātmā yathā hṛdisthe bhagavaty anante ||
children.translated_text: the inner self does not obtain complete purity as it does when the Blessed <s>Ananta</s> is present in the heart.
In the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>, in <s>Śrīprahlāda</s>'s statement to <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>:

children.text: bhayaṃ bhayānām apahāriṇi sthite manasy anante mama kutra tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: When <s>Ananta</s>, remover of fears, is present in my mind, where can fear remain for me?

children.text: yasmin smṛte janmajarodbhavāni bhayāni sarvāṇy apayānti tāta ||
children.translated_text: When he is remembered, all fears born of birth and old age depart, dear father.
There also, elsewhere:
Through remembrance of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the whole mass of afflictions having been exhausted,
one goes to liberation; the attainment of heaven is considered an obstacle for him.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>:
Having remembered the excellent, most desirable, boon-giving ancient one, who illumines all worlds by his own radiance,

children.text: saṃkalpitārthapradam ādidevaṃ smṛtvā vrajen muktipadaṃ manuṣyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the primordial god who grants what has been resolved, a person should go to the state of liberation.
In the <s>Skanda</s>:
By the mere remembrance of whom one is released from the bondage of birth and transmigration,
obeisance to that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the mighty lord.
There also, in the <s>Kārttika</s> section, in <s>Śrīparāśara</s>'s statement:
At that very moment a person is freed from birth, suffering, old age, and the like,

children.text: bhaktyā tu parayā nūnaṃ yadaiva smarate harim ||
children.translated_text: when indeed he remembers <s>Hari</s> with supreme devotion.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>:
By whatever means imperishable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is remembered,

children.text: api pātakayuktasya prasannaḥ syān na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he becomes gracious even to one joined with sin; there is no doubt.
In the <s>Vāmanapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: anādyanantam ajarāmaraṃ hariṃ ye saṃsmaranty aharahar niyataṃ narā bhuvi
children.translated_text: Those men on earth who constantly remember, day after day, <s>Hari</s>, beginningless and endless, undecaying and deathless,

children.text: tat sarvagaṃ brahma paraṃ purāṇaṃ te yānti vaiṣṇavapadaṃ dhruvam avyayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: go to that all-pervading supreme ancient brahman, the sure and imperishable state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Devadūta</s> and <s>Vikuṇḍala</s>, in <s>Yama</s>'s instruction to his messengers:

children.text: smaranti ye sakṛd bhūtāḥ prasaṅgenāpi keśavam
children.translated_text: Beings who remember <s>Keśava</s> once, even incidentally,

children.text: te vidhvastākhilāghaughā yanti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: their whole flood of sins destroyed, go to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Brahmapurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Viṣṇurahasya</s>:

children.text: śāṭhyenāpi narā nityaṃ ye smaranti janārdanam
children.translated_text: Even through deceit, those people who always remember <s>Janārdana</s>

children.text: te 'pi yānti tanuṃ tyaktvā viṣṇulokam anāmayam ||
children.translated_text: also, after abandoning the body, go to the painless world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>:

children.text: nirāśīr nirmamo yas tu viṣṇor dhyānaparo bhavet
children.translated_text: Whoever is without expectation and without possessiveness, and is devoted to meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: tatpadaṃ samavāpnoti yatra gatvā na śocati ||
children.translated_text: attains that state, having gone to which one does not grieve.
In the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, in the episode of <s>Bindumādhava</s>, in <s>Agnibindu</s>'s praise:

children.text: ye tvāṃ trivikrama sadā hṛdi śīlayanti kādambinīrucir arociṣam ambujākṣa
children.translated_text: O <s>Trivikrama</s>, lotus-eyed one, those who always cultivate you in the heart, whose radiance is beautiful like a raincloud,

children.text: saudāminīvilasitāṃśukavītamūrte te'pi spṛśanti tava kāntim acintyarūpām ||
children.translated_text: whose form is wrapped in a garment flashing like lightning, they too touch your inconceivable radiance.
In the <s>Śrībhagavadgītā</s>:

children.text: antakāle ca mām eva smaran muktvā kalevaram
children.translated_text: And at the final moment, remembering me alone and abandoning the body,

children.text: yaḥ prayāti sa madbhāvaṃ yāti nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever departs attains my state; there is no doubt about this.
In the tenth skandha, in the account of <s>Pṛthu</s>'s anger:
To one who remembers his lotus feet, he gives even himself.
What then of material aims and desires, not greatly cherished, for one who worships him, the teacher of the world?
In the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> text:
For one whose mind is on <s>Vāsudeva</s> in muttering, oblation, worship, and the like,
O <s>Maitreya</s>, lordship over the gods and other excellent results are an obstacle.
In the <s>Gāruḍa</s>:
The root of great austerity, the source of a stream of merit,

children.text: jīvitasya phalaṃ svādu niyataṃ smaraṇaṃ hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the sweet fruit of life is certainly remembrance of <s>Hari</s>.
In the Second Book:
