Through <s>Sāṅkhya</s>, yoga, and steadfast adherence to one's own duty,
this alone is the supreme gain of birth for human beings: remembrance of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at the end.
For this very reason it was requested in the Tenth Book by the group of kings imprisoned by <s>Jarāsandha</s>:

children.text: taṃ naḥ samādiśopāyaṃ yena te caraṇābjayoḥ
children.translated_text: Teach us that means by which, at your two lotus feet,

children.text: smṛtir yathā na viramed api saṃsaratām iha ||
children.translated_text: remembrance may not cease, even for those who wander here in worldly existence.
And also by <s>Śrī Nārada</s>:

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ tavāṅghriyugalaṃ janatāpavargaṃ brahmādibhir hṛdi vicintyam agādhabodhaiḥ
children.translated_text: I have seen your pair of feet, the release of people from suffering, contemplated in the heart by <s>Brahmā</s> and others of unfathomable understanding,

children.text: saṃsārakūpapatitottaraṇāvalambaṃ dhyāyaṃś carāmy anugṛhāṇa yathā smṛtiḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: the support for crossing out for those fallen into the well of worldly existence. Meditating on them I wander; favor me so that remembrance may arise.
The great ocean of the greatness of remembrance of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is hard to cross by the intellect.

children.text: yo yiyāsati tatpāraṃ sa hi caitanyavañcitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to reach its far shore is indeed devoid of true awareness.

children.text: tataḥ pādodakaṃ kiṃcit prāk pītvā tulasīdalaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having first drunk a little foot-water taken with <s>tulasī</s> leaves,
with that water he should perform a sprinkling on his own head.
Next, at the beginning, having bowed to the blessed guru and to the two lotus feet of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>,
making a small petition, he should offer all his own duties and bow.
In the <s>Vāmana Purāṇa</s>:
Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious, the most excellent, the giver of boons, and the gracious one,
he should have all actions performed.
In the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>:

children.text: yadutsavādikaṃ karma tat tvayā prerito hare
children.translated_text: Whatever act there is, a festival or the like, O <s>Hari</s>, impelled by you

children.text: kariṣyāmi tvayā jñeyam iti vijñāpanaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: I shall perform it. Let it be known by you: this is my petition.

children.text: prātaḥ prabodhito viṣṇo hṛṣīkeśena yat tvayā
children.translated_text: O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O Lord, awakened in the morning by you as <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>,

children.text: yad yat kārayasīśāna tat karomi tavājñayā ||
children.translated_text: whatever you cause me to do, that I do by your command.
O primal god filled with the consciousness of the three worlds, O <s>Śrīnātha Viṣṇu</s>, by your command alone,

children.text: prātaḥ samutthāya tava priyārthaṃ saṃsārayātrām anuvartayiṣye ||
children.translated_text: having risen in the morning, I shall continue the journey of worldly life for your pleasure.
As I continue the journey of worldly life by your command, O <s>Śrī Nṛhari</s>, inner self,
may rivalry, contempt, strife, negligence, and fears not overwhelm me, O vast one.

children.text: jānāmi dharmaṃ na ca me pravṛttir jānāmy adharmaṃ na ca me nivṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: I know <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), yet I have no inclination toward it; I know <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), yet I have no turning away from it.

children.text: tvayā hṛṣīkeśa hṛdi sthitena yathā niyukto 'smi tathā karomi ||
children.translated_text: As I am appointed by you, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, dwelling in my heart, so I act.
In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:
Obeisance to the god of the Brahmins and to the benefactor of cows and Brahmins;
again and again obeisance to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Govinda</s>, the benefactor of the world.
In the <s>Garuḍa Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: asuravibudhasiddhair jñāyate yasya nāntaḥ sakalamunibhir antaś cintyate yo viśuddhaḥ
children.translated_text: I bow to that unborn, immortal lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>, whose limit is not known by demons, gods, and siddhas, who is pure and is contemplated inwardly by all sages,

children.text: nikhilahṛdi niviṣṭo vetti yaḥ sarvasākṣī tam ajam amṛtam īśaṃ vāsudevaṃ nato 'smi ||
children.translated_text: who, lodged in every heart, knows all and is the witness of all.
In the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:
I bow to him whom sacrificers call the Sacrificial Person, whom the <s>Sātvatas</s> call <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: vedāntavedibhir viṣṇuḥ procyate yo nato 'smi tam ||
children.translated_text: and whom the knowers of <s>Vedānta</s> call <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: evaṃ vijñāpayan dhyāyan kīrtayaṃś ca yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: Thus petitioning, meditating, and chanting according to rule,
the wise person should perform prostrations according to his ability, not fewer than four in number.
Having made the vertical <s>puṇḍra</s> mark with blessed <s>gopīcandana</s> according to rule,
he should sit facing east, in a pure place, on an auspicious seat.
And so in the <s>Nāradīya Pañcarātra</s>:

children.text: nirgatyācamya vidhivat praviśya ca punaḥ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone out and sipped water according to rule, and having entered again, the intelligent man,

children.text: āsane prāṅmukho bhūtvā vihite copaviśya vai ||
children.translated_text: having become east-facing, should sit down on the prescribed seat.
Having performed <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (purification of the elements) according to his tradition,

children.text: prāṇāyāmāṃś ca vidhivat kṛṣṇaṃ dhyāyet yathoditam ||
children.translated_text: and breath controls according to rule, he should meditate on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as stated.
And so it has been said:
In all minor offenses and in the great sins,
having entered the last quarter of the night, he should undertake meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And in the <s>Vaihāyasa Pañcarātra</s>:
Likewise, during the remaining portion of the night, up to sunrise,

children.text: kartavyaṃ sajapaṃ dhyānaṃ nityam ārādhakena vai ||
children.translated_text: the worshipper should always perform meditation together with mantra-recitation.
Dividing the night into five parts, in the last part, worship of the deity and the like,

children.text: japaṃ homaṃ tathā dhyānaṃ nityaṃ kurvīta sādhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as mantra-recitation, oblation, and meditation, should always be performed by the practitioner.
For this very reason, in the <s>Viṣṇusmṛti</s>:

children.text: rātres tu paścime yāme muhūrto brāhmya ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The last watch of the night is called the brāhma muhūrta.
The procedure and greatness of drinking the foot-water and the other acts

children.text: lekhyo 'dhunā tu dhyānasya sa saṅkṣepeṇa likhyate ||
children.translated_text: are to be written later; now that of meditation is written briefly.
In the <s>Tāpanīya Śrutis</s>:
One should contemplate the Lord whose eyes are like good lotuses, whose color is like a cloud, whose garment is like lightning,
who is two-armed, rich in the gesture of knowledge, and garlanded with forest flowers,
surrounded by cowherds, cowherd women, and cows, and sheltered beneath a divine tree,
adorned with celestial ornaments and situated in the middle of a jewel lotus,
served by a breeze joined with the waves of the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s>.

children.text: cintayaṃś cetasā kṛṣṇaṃ mukto bhavati saṃsṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Contemplating <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with the mind, one becomes free from worldly existence.
And in the <s>Śāradātilaka</s>, stated according to the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya Saṃhitā</s>:
He should remember, in lovely <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, lotus-eyed, incessantly enchanting
thousands of cowherd maidens,
whose bee-like eyes are set in motion by the lotus of his own face,
overpowered by the arrows of love and long eager for embrace,
bent under the weight of their full, high breasts shining with pearl necklaces,
with hair-knots and garments loosened and speech faltering from intoxication,
adorned with trembling lips made bright by the radiance of rows of teeth,
enticing him with various amorous gestures pregnant with feeling.

children.text: phullendīvarakāntim induvadanaṃ barhāvataṃsapriyaṃ śrīvatsāṅkam udārakaustubhadharaṃ pītāmbaraṃ sundaram
children.translated_text: I worship <s>Govinda</s>, beautiful, wearing a yellow garment, with the splendor of a blooming blue lotus, a moon-like face, fond of a peacock-feather ornament, marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, and bearing the noble <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel,

children.text: gopīnāṃ nayanotpalārcitatanuṃ gogopasaṅghāvṛtaṃ govindaṃ kalaveṇuvādanaparaṃ divyāṅgabhūṣaṃ bhaje ||
children.translated_text: whose body is worshipped by the lotus-eyes of the gopīs, who is surrounded by herds of cows and cowherds, who is intent on playing the sweet flute, and whose limbs are adorned with divine ornaments.
In the <s>Śrīgautamīya Tantra</s> and other works, that supreme meditation on him is well known.

children.text: agrato 'trāpi saṃlekhyaṃ yad iṣṭaṃ tatra tad bhajet ||
children.translated_text: It too should be written here beforehand; whatever form is desired, one should worship him there in that form.
In the <s>Bṛhatśātātāpa Smṛti</s>:
The sin of a man that is destroyed by fasting through a fortnight,
and the sin of people that is destroyed by just a hundred <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls),
and the sin of people that is destroyed by a thousand <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>,

children.text: kṣaṇamātreṇa tat pāpaṃ harer dhyānāt praṇaśyati ||
children.translated_text: that sin is destroyed in a mere instant through meditation on <s>Hari</s>.
In the <s>Viṣṇudharma</s>:
Even though attached to all sins, a person who meditates on <s>Acyuta</s> for the blink of an eye,
having become an ascetic, becomes a purifier even of those who purify the dining row.
And in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: dhyāyen nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ snānādiṣu ca karmasu
children.translated_text: One should meditate on the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> during bathing and other rites;
for this is certainly the expiation for every evil deed.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>, in the section on the Kali age:
When the terrible Kali age has arrived, one who meditates on <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: ghore kaliyuge prāpte viṣṇuṃ dhyāyan na sīdati ||
children.translated_text: the support of the entire universe and the embodiment of ultimate reality, does not sink down.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the <s>Kārttika Māhātmya</s>, in the statement of <s>Agastya</s>:

children.text: kintv asya bahubhis tīrthaiḥ kiṃ tasya bahubhir vrataiḥ
children.translated_text: But what need has such a man of many sacred fords? What need has he of many vows,

children.text: yo nityaṃ dhyāyate devaṃ nārāyaṇam ananyadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: who constantly meditates on the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with an undivided mind?
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>, in the section on the Kali age:

children.text: ye mānavā vigatarāgaparāvarajñā nārāyaṇaṃ suraguruṃ satataṃ smaranti
children.translated_text: Those humans who are free from passion, who know higher and lower, and who constantly remember <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the teacher of the gods,

children.text: dhyānena tena hata kilbiṣacetanās te mātuḥ payodhararasaṃ na punaḥ pibanti ||
children.translated_text: with their sinful awareness destroyed by that meditation, do not again drink the milk from their mother's breast.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the statement of holy <s>Brahmā</s>:

children.text: muhūrtam api yo dhyāyen nārāyaṇam atandritaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever meditates on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> even for a moment, without indolence,

children.text: so 'pi sadgatim āpnoti kiṃ punas tatparāyaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: attains the good state; how much more one who is wholly devoted to him?
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the <s>Vaiśākha Māhātmya</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Yama</s> and the Brahmin:

children.text: dhyāyanti puruṣaṃ divyam acyutaṃ ye smaranti ca
children.translated_text: Those who meditate on the divine Person, <s>Acyuta</s>, and remember him
obtain the abode of <s>Acyuta</s>; this is the ancient revelation.
In the Eleventh Book:
Kings such as <s>Śiśupāla</s>, <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, and <s>Śālva</s>, meditating on him through enmity, their minds fixed on his form by his gait, sport, glances, and the like,

children.text: dhyāyanta ākṛtadhiyaḥ śayanāsanādau tatsāmyam āpur anuraktadhiyāṃ punaḥ kim ||
children.translated_text: even while lying down, sitting, and so on, obtained likeness to him; what then of those whose minds are attached to him?
In the Fourth Book, in the statement of holy <s>Pṛthu</s>:

children.text: bhajanty atha tvām ata eva sādhavo vyudastamāyāguṇavibhramodayam
children.translated_text: Therefore the good worship you, whose arising of the bewilderment caused by the qualities of <s>māyā</s> has been cast away;

children.text: bhavatpadānusmaraṇād ṛte satāṃ nimittam anyad bhagavan na vidmahe ||
children.translated_text: apart from remembrance of your feet, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, we know no other motive for the good.
And in the <s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>, in the statement of <s>Brahmā</s>:

children.text: āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having stirred through all the śāstras and considered again and again,

children.text: idam eva suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: this alone is firmly concluded: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is always to be meditated upon.
Therefore it is said in the <s>Hayaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s>, in the <s>Nārāyaṇavyūha Stava</s>:
Those who have abandoned worldly <s>dharma</s> and wealth and have come under the power of devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
who meditate on the supreme self: to them too, here, obeisance again and again.

children.text: smaraṇe yat tan māhātmyaṃ taddhyāne'py akhilaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever greatness belongs to remembering him, they should know all of that to belong to meditating on him as well.
How much difference could be imagined between the two, through the distinction of general and particular?
Then, having gone to the temple, with the ringing of bells and the like first,

children.text: prabodhya stutibhiḥ kṛṣṇaṃ nīrājyaṃ prārthayed idam ||
children.translated_text: having awakened <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with praises and performed the waving of lights, he should make this request:
In the Third Book:

children.text: so 'sāv adabhrakaruṇo bhagavān vivṛddhapremasmitena nayanāmburuhaṃ vijṛmbhan
children.translated_text: May that primeval Person, the blessed one of abundant compassion, opening his lotus eyes with a smile of increased love,

children.text: utthāya viśvavijayāya ca no viṣādaṃ mādhvyā girāpanayatāt puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: arise for the conquest of the universe and remove our sorrow with his honeyed speech.
O <s>Keśava</s>, remover of the distress of those who have sought refuge in the deity, show favor;
by granting your glance, carry me across again, O <s>Acyuta</s>.
Then, having entered the temple while reciting the hymns he desires,
he should remove <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>nirmālya</s> (previous offerings), except for <s>tulasī</s>.
In the <s>Atri Smṛti</s>:
At morning time the wise man should always perform the removal of the <s>nirmālya</s>.

children.text: tṛṣitāḥ paśavo baddhāḥ kanyakā ca rajasvalā
children.translated_text: Thirsty animals that are bound, and a menstruating maiden,

children.text: devatā ca sanirmālyā hanti puṇyaṃ purākṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and a deity together with <s>nirmālya</s> destroy merit earned in the past.
In the <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, in the statement of holy <s>Yama</s>:
Removing the deity's garlands, sweeping in the temple,
and bathing all the gods are remembered as equal to the gift of a cow.
In the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s>:

children.text: yaḥ prātar utthāya vidhāya nityaṃ nirmālyam īśasya nirākaroti
children.translated_text: Whoever, rising in the morning, regularly removes the Lord's <s>nirmālya</s>,

children.text: na tasya duḥkhaṃ na daridratā ca nākālamṛtyur na ca rogamātram ||
children.translated_text: for him there is no suffering, no poverty, no untimely death, and not even the slightest illness.
At the time of dawn the <s>nirmālya</s> becomes a thorn;
in the morning, when only a <s>ghaṭikā</s> has passed, it becomes a great thorn.
After that one should know it as an excessive thorn, like the strike of a thunderbolt;
at the time of dawn <s>Hari</s> tolerates that thorn.
When a <s>ghaṭikā</s> has elapsed, it brings about a minor sin;
when a <s>muhūrta</s> has fully elapsed, it is called a full sin.
When four <s>ghaṭikās</s> have passed, it becomes an excessive sin;
when three <s>muhūrtas</s> are complete, it is called a great sin.
After that it is equal to killing a Brahmin, the five great sins;

children.text: prahare pūrṇatāṃ yāte prāyaścittaṃ tato na hi ||
children.translated_text: when a watch of the day is complete, there is thereafter no expiation.
Now the expiation for delay regarding the <s>nirmālya</s> is stated.
When half a <s>muhūrta</s> has elapsed, he should perform a thousand recitations.

children.text: pūrṇe muhūrte saṃjāte sahasraṃ sārdham ucyate
children.translated_text: When a full <s>muhūrta</s> has occurred, one and a half thousand are prescribed.
One should perform two thousand in the space of four ghaṭikās.
When three muhūrtas have passed, one should perform ten thousand recitations.
When a full watch has elapsed, it is called puraścaraṇa.
When a watch has passed beyond that, there is no expiation.
For the washing of the blessed lotus-like hands, feet, and mouth, in his house,
one should offer mouth-rinsing water and present a tooth-stick.
Having given a tongue-scraper, sandals, pure clay,

children.text: salilaṃ ca punar dadyād vāso 'pi mukhamārjanam ||
children.translated_text: and water, one should again give cloth and also something for wiping the face.
Then one should offer the holy <s>Tulasī</s>, dear to the Lord.
Its greatness is to be written later in the principal context concerning it.
In the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>:
By giving a tooth-stick, one attains the good fortune of fine teeth;
by giving a tongue-scraper, one indeed becomes free from disease.
By the gift of sandals, one obtains the desired path;
from giving a portion of clay to the god, one obtains an unsurpassed land.
Then, after reciting beloved verses, with the sounds of great musical instruments,
one should perform the Lord's nīrājana, called maṅgala, which benefits the world.

children.text: nīrājanaṃ tv idaṃ sarvaiḥ kartavyaṃ śucivigrahaiḥ
children.translated_text: This nīrājana is to be performed by all whose bodies are pure,
and people should always rise and behold it with supreme faith.

children.text: strīṇāṃ puṃsāṃ ca sarveṣām etat sarveṣṭapūrakam
children.translated_text: For women, men, and all people, this fulfills every desire
and brings about the pacification of all wretchedness, poverty, sin, and the like.
After that, at the end of dawn, he should go outside for bathing.
Chanting the names of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he should then go to a sacred ford.
And similarly, in the <s>Śukrasmṛti</s>:

children.text: brāhme muhūrte cotthāya śucir bhūtvā samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having risen in the brāhma muhūrta, become pure and composed,
and assumed a posture such as svastika, he should meditate on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s lotus feet.
Then, going out from his dwelling, he should chant these names:
<s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>,
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, homage to you.
Having gone to a sacred ford or the like and placed there the articles for bathing,
having duly performed the duties beginning with maitrya and having carried out cleansing,

children.text: ācamya khāni saṃmārjya snānaṃ kuryāt yathocitam ||
children.translated_text: he should sip water, wipe the bodily openings, and bathe as is proper.
In the <s>Śrī Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Aurva</s> and <s>Sagara</s>, in the teaching on the dharma of householders:

children.text: tataḥ kalye samutthāya kuryān mūtraṃ nareśvara
children.translated_text: Then, rising early, one should urinate, O king,
in the southwestern direction, beyond the distance of an arrow-shot from the house.
One should discharge urine and feces far from the dwelling;
one should not throw water from washing the feet or leavings into the courtyard of the house.
A wise man should never urinate toward his own shadow, the shadow of a tree, cows, the sun, fire, wind,

children.text: guruṃ dvijādīṃś ca budho na meheta kadācana ||
children.translated_text: nor toward his guru, brahmins, and the like.

children.text: na kṛṣṭe śasyamadhye vā govraje janasaṃsadi
children.translated_text: Not in a ploughed field, nor among crops, nor in a cow pen, nor in a public assembly,
nor on a road, nor at river-banks and other sacred fords, O best of men.

children.text: nāpsu naivāmbhasas tīre na śmaśāne samācaret
children.translated_text: He should not carry out, in water, nor on the bank of water, nor in a cremation ground,

children.text: utsargaṃ vai purīṣasya mūtrasya ca visarjanam ||
children.translated_text: the discharge of feces or the release of urine.
Facing north by day he should discharge feces; facing the opposite direction by night,
and the wise man should also release urine thus when there is no emergency, O king.
Having covered the ground with grass, with his head wrapped in a cloth,

children.text: tiṣṭhen nāticiraṃ tatra naiva kiṃcid udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: he should not remain there too long, and he should not utter anything at all.
Similarly, in the <s>Kūrma</s>, in the <s>Vyāsagītā</s>:
Having placed the brahmasūtra over the right ear, facing north,

children.text: antardhāpya mahīṃ kāṣṭhaiḥ patrair loṣṭrais tṛṇena vā ||
children.translated_text: and having concealed the ground with sticks, leaves, clods, or grass,

children.text: prāvṛtya tu śiraḥ kuryād viṇmūtrasya visarjanam
children.translated_text: with his head covered, he should discharge feces and urine.
And never facing women, the guru, brahmins, or cows,
nor gods, temples, or waters at any time.

children.text: nadīṃ jyotīṃṣi vīkṣitvā na vāyvagnimukho 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Having seen a river or the luminaries, he should not face wind or fire either,
nor toward the sun, toward fire, or toward the moon.
In the <s>Kāśīkāṇḍa</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Skanda</s> and <s>Agastya</s>:

children.text: tataś cāvaśyakaṃ kartuṃ nairṛtīṃ diśam āśrayet
children.translated_text: Then, to do what is necessary, he should resort to the southwestern direction.

children.text: grāmād dhanuḥśataṃ gacchen nagarāc ca caturguṇam ||
children.translated_text: He should go a hundred bows from a village, and four times that from a city.
With the sacred thread placed over the ear, facing north by day and also at the twilights,
he should silently discharge feces and urine; at night, facing south.

children.text: nālokayed diśo bhāgān jyotiś cakraṃ nabho 'malam
children.translated_text: He should not look at the quarters, the parts of the sky, the circle of lights, or the stainless heavens.
Holding the penis with the left hand, he should rise with care.
Just there, further on:

children.text: na mūtraṃ govraje kuryān na valmīke na bhasmani
children.translated_text: One should not urinate in a cow pen, on an anthill, or on ashes,

children.text: na garteṣu sasattveṣu na tiṣṭhan na vrajann api ||
children.translated_text: nor in pits containing living creatures, nor while standing, nor while walking.
At night he may face whatever direction is comfortable; by day, in shadow or darkness,
in situations of fear or danger to life, he may discharge excrement.
In the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>, in the same place:
Clay from an anthill, dug up by mice, or from within water,

children.text: śaucāvaśiṣṭāṃ gehāc ca na dadyāl lepasambhavām ||
children.translated_text: or left over after cleansing, or from a house, or produced by plastering, should not be used.
And clay containing living creatures, or dug up by a plough, O king,
all these clays one should avoid as means of cleansing.

children.text: ekā liṅge gude tisro daśa vāmakare nṛpa
children.translated_text: One application of clay is for the penis, three for the anus, ten for the left hand, O king,
and seven further applications of clay for both hands; these accomplish cleansing.
In the <s>Yamasmṛti</s>:

children.text: tisras tu pādayor deyāḥ śuddhikāmena nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Three should always be applied to the feet by one desiring purity.
Moreover:

children.text: tisras tu mṛttikā deyāḥ kṛtvā tu nakhaśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: Three applications of clay should be given after cleaning the nails.
And in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, in that same place:

children.text: guhye dadyān mṛdaṃ caikāṃ pāyau pañcāmbusāntarāḥ
children.translated_text: He should apply clay once to the private part, and five times to the anus, alternating with water;

children.text: daśa vāmakare cāpi sapta pāṇidvaye mṛdaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also ten applications to the left hand and seven applications of clay to both hands.

children.text: ekaikāṃ pādayor dadyāt tisraḥ pāṇyor mṛdaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: One should apply one clod of clay to each foot; three clods are prescribed for the hands.
Thus a householder should perform purification until the odorous smear has been removed.

children.text: kramād dviguṇam etat tu brahmacaryādiṣu triṣu
children.translated_text: But this is successively doubled for the three āśramas beginning with brahmacarya.

children.text: divā vihitaśaucāc ca rātrāv ardhaṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: At night one should perform half of the purification prescribed for the daytime.

children.text: rujārdhaṃ ca tadardhaṃ ca pathi caurādipīḍite
children.translated_text: In illness, half of that; and when on a road, oppressed by thieves and the like, half of that again.

children.text: tadardhayoṣitāṃ cāpi svāsthye nyūnaṃ na kārayet
children.translated_text: For women too there is half of that; but when they are healthy, one should not make it deficient.
The clods of clay for purification are declared to be the size of a moist dhātrī fruit.
In the <s>Śaṅkha-smṛti</s>:

children.text: mṛttikā tu samuddiṣṭā triparvī pūryate yayā ||
children.translated_text: Clay is specified as the amount by which three finger-joints are filled.
In the <s>Dakṣa-smṛti</s>:
The first clod of clay is remembered as measuring half a prasṛti.

children.text: dvitīyā ca tṛtīyā ca tadardhaṃ parikīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: The second and the third are each proclaimed to be half of that.
<s>Dakṣa</s>:

children.text: ekā liṅge tu savye trir ubhayor mṛddvayaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: For the organ there is one clod; for the left hand, three; for both, two clods of clay are prescribed.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>:
Taking two clods for the feet, and with the hand well washed,

children.text: ācamya tu tataḥ śuddhaḥ smṛtvā viṣṇuṃ sanātanam ||
children.translated_text: then sipping water, he becomes pure, remembering eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Viṣṇupurāṇa</s>, in that same context:
With clear water that is without smell, foam, or bubbles,

children.text: ācāmeta mṛdaṃ bhūyas tathā dadyāt samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should perform <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping); then, composed, he should again apply clay.

children.text: niṣpāditāṅghriśaucas tu pāpāv abhyukṣya vai punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having completed the purification of the feet, he should again sprinkle them,

children.text: triḥ pibet salilaṃ tena tathā dviḥ parimārjayet ||
children.translated_text: and with that water sip three times and then wipe twice.

children.text: śīrṣaṇyāni tataḥ khāni mūrdhānaṃ ca mṛdā labhet
children.translated_text: Then he should touch the openings in the head and the head itself with clay.

children.text: bāhū nābhiṃ ca toyena hṛdayaṃ cāpi saṃspṛśet ||
children.translated_text: He should also touch the arms, the navel, and the heart with water.
And here a particular rule has been stated by <s>Dakṣa</s>:

children.text: prakṣālya hastau pādau ca triḥ pibed ambu vīkṣitam
children.translated_text: Having washed the hands and feet, he should sip water that has been inspected three times.
Then with the base of the thumb closed in, he should wipe the mouth twice.

children.text: saṃhatya tisṛbhiḥ pūrvam āsyam evam upaspṛśet
children.translated_text: First joining the three fingers together, he should touch the mouth in this way.
After that, with the thumb and forefinger, he should touch the nose.
With the thumb and ring finger he should touch the eyes and ears again and again.

children.text: kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhayor nābhiṃ hṛdayaṃ tu talena vai
children.translated_text: With the little finger and thumb he should touch the navel, and with the palm, the heart.

children.text: sarvābhis tu śiraḥ paścād bāhū cāgreṇa saṃspṛśet ||
children.translated_text: Then with all the fingers he should touch the head, and with their tips, the arms.
Likewise in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, in that same context:

children.text: prāgāsya udagāsyo vā sūpaviṣṭaḥ śucau bhuvi
children.translated_text: Facing east or facing north, well seated on clean ground,
one should perform the ritual sipping on ground free from chaff, charcoal, bones, and ash.
With water that is not hot, not foamy, and reaches the heart, without haste,
a brāhmaṇa should sip with the <s>brahmatīrtha</s> (the sacred part of the hand), using water purified by sight.
A king is purified by water reaching the throat, and a vaiśya by water reaching the palate.
Women and śūdras are purified even by mere contact with the mouth.
In the <s>Yājñavalkya-smṛti</s>:
A twice-born man should not perform <s>ācamana</s> with water left over from washing the feet.
If he does perform <s>ācamana</s>, <s>Baudhāyana</s> said, it should be after letting it flow onto the ground.
In the <s>Bharadvāja-smṛti</s>:
One should perform <s>ācamana</s> with the right hand alone, with the fingers joined together.
With the thumb and little finger free, one should reject water touched by the nails.
And in the <s>Kūrma</s> and the <s>Vyāsa-gītā</s>:

children.text: bhuktvā pītvā ca suptvā ca snātvā rathyopasarpaṇe
children.translated_text: After eating, drinking, sleeping, bathing, or entering a road,

children.text: auṣṭhau vilomakau spṛṣṭvā vāso viparidhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: after touching the two lips the wrong way, and after putting on a garment differently,
upon the discharge of semen, urine, or feces, or upon speaking falsehood,
after spitting, at the beginning of study, and when coughing or labored breathing occurs,

children.text: catvaraṃ vā śmaśānaṃ vā samabhyasya dvijottamaḥ
children.translated_text: and after approaching a crossroads or a cremation ground, the best of the twice-born,

children.text: sandhyor ubhayos tadvad ācānto 'py ācamet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise at both twilights, should perform <s>ācamana</s> again, even if he has already performed it.
Moreover:

children.text: śiraḥ prāvṛtya kaṇṭhaṃ vā muktakacchaśikho 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Covering the head or the neck, or with the tucked garment or topknot loosened,

children.text: akṛtvā pādayoḥ śaucam ācānto 'py aśucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and without cleansing the feet, one remains impure even after performing <s>ācamana</s>.

children.text: sopānatkau jalastho vā noṣṇīṣī cācamed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: A wise man should not perform <s>ācamana</s> while wearing footwear, while standing in water, or while wearing a turban.

children.text: na caiva varṣadhārābhir hastocchiṣṭe tathā budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nor should a wise man do so with streams of rainwater, or with water left over in the hand.
Nor with water offered by one hand, nor again without the sacred thread.

children.text: na pādukāsanastho vā bahir jānur athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: Nor should he do so while standing on footwear or a seat, or with the knee outside.

children.text: triḥpāne keśavaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ mādhavam apy atha
children.translated_text: At the three sips he should recite <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Mādhava</s>.

children.text: prakṣālane dvayoḥ pāṇyor govindaṃ viṣṇum apy ubhau ||
children.translated_text: At the washing of the two hands, he should recite <s>Govinda</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, both of them.
For one act of wiping he should recite <s>Madhusūdana</s>, and for the other, <s>Trivikrama</s>.
For wiping the two lower lips he should recite <s>Vāmana</s> and <s>Śrīdhara</s>, both of them.

children.text: prakṣālane punaḥ pāṇyor hṛṣīkeśaṃ ca pādayoḥ
children.translated_text: At the washing of the two hands again he should recite <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, and at the two feet,

children.text: padmanābhaṃ prokṣaṇe tu mūrdhno dāmodaraṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Padmanābha</s>; at sprinkling, and then at the head, <s>Dāmodara</s>.

children.text: vāsudevaṃ mukhe saṅkarṣaṇaṃ pradyumnam ity ubhau
children.translated_text: At the mouth he should recite <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s>, both of them,
at the nostrils and at the pair of eyes: <s>Aniruddha</s> and <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
At the ears he should recite <s>Adhokṣaja</s> and <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, and at the navel, <s>Acyuta</s>.

children.text: janārdanaṃ ca hṛdaye upendraṃ mastake tataḥ
children.translated_text: At the heart he should recite <s>Janārdana</s>, and then at the head, <s>Upendra</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇe tu hariṃ bāhau vāme kṛṣṇaṃ yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: On the right arm he should recite <s>Hari</s>, and on the left, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, according to rule.

children.text: namo 'nantaṃ ca caturthyantam ācāmet kramato japan ||
children.translated_text: Performing <s>ācamana</s> in order, he should recite each name in the dative with namaḥ, including <s>Ananta</s>.

children.text: aśaktaḥ kevalam dakṣaṃ spṛśet karṇaṃ tathā ca vāk
children.translated_text: One who is unable should merely touch the right ear; and there is also this statement:
he may perform even the touching of the right ear.
On this, <s>Kātyāyana</s> says:

children.text: utthāya netraṃ prakṣālya śucir bhūtvā samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having risen, washed the eyes, become pure, and composed himself,
after reciting with the mantra, he should chew the tooth-cleaning stick.
And this is the mantra:

children.text: āyur balaṃ yaśo varcaḥ prajā paśuvasūni ca
children.translated_text: Life, strength, fame, splendor, progeny, cattle, and wealth,

children.text: brahma prajñāṃ ca medhāṃ ca tvaṃ no dhehi vanaspate ||
children.translated_text: sacred knowledge, insight, and intelligence: grant these to us, O tree.
In the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>:
Then, for the purification of the mouth, one should take a tooth-cleaning stick.
For even after <s>ācamana</s> one is impure if tooth-cleaning has not been done.
And in the <s>Varāha</s>:

children.text: dantakāṣṭham akhāditvā yas tu mām upasarpati
children.translated_text: Whoever approaches me without chewing a tooth-stick,
by that one act, every rite performed at any time is destroyed.
<s>Manu</s>:
On the fourteenth day, the eighth day, the new-moon day, the full-moon day, and at the sun's transition,
on these occasions one should avoid women, oil, meat, and tooth-sticks.
<s>Saṃvartaka</s>:

children.text: ādye tithau navamyāṃ ca kṣaye candramasas tathā
children.translated_text: On the first lunar day, on the ninth, and likewise at the waning of the moon,
one should avoid tooth-cleaning on Sunday and on Saturday.
<s>Kātyāyana</s>:
On the first lunar day, on the new-moon day, on the sixth days, and especially on the ninth,

children.text: dantānāṃ kāṣṭhasaṃyogo dahaty ā saptamaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: the contact of wood with the teeth burns one's family up to the seventh generation.
<s>Vṛddha-Vasiṣṭha</s>:
On a fast, and likewise at a <s>śrāddha</s> rite, one should not chew a tooth-cleaning stick.
The contact of wood with the teeth indeed destroys seven generations.
And elsewhere:
On the first lunar day, the new-moon day, the sixth days, the ninth, the eleventh, and Sunday,
the contact of wood with the teeth destroys merit previously acquired.

children.text: dineṣv eteṣu kāṣṭhair hi dantānāṃ dhāvanasya tu
children.translated_text: Because on these days the cleaning of the teeth with sticks

children.text: niṣiddhatvāt tṛṇaiḥ kuryāt tathā kāṣṭhetaraiś ca tat ||
children.translated_text: is forbidden, one should do it with grasses and likewise with things other than wood.
And so <s>Vyāsa</s> says:
On the first lunar day, the new-moon day, the sixth days, and the ninth, tooth-cleaning

children.text: parṇair anyatra kāṣṭhaiś ca jīvollekhaḥ sadaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: should be done with leaves, and elsewhere with sticks; scraping of the tongue is always prescribed.
<s>Paiṭhīnasi</s>:

children.text: alābhe ca niṣedhe vā kāṣṭhānāṃ dantadhāvanam
children.translated_text: When tooth-sticks are unavailable or forbidden, tooth-cleaning
should be done with clean leaves and the like; scraping of the tongue is always prescribed.
That tooth-cleaning with sticks which is forbidden on the first lunar day and other such days,

children.text: tṛṇaparṇais tu tat kuryād amām ekādaśīṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: one should do with grasses and leaves, except on the new-moon day and the eleventh day.
For this very reason there is another statement of <s>Vyāsa</s>:
When tooth-sticks are unavailable, and likewise on a forbidden lunar day,
one should perform tooth-cleaning by means of twelve mouthfuls of water.
In the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, in that same context:

children.text: mukhe paryuṣite yasmād bhaved aśucibhāg naraḥ
children.translated_text: Because a man with a stale mouth becomes a participant in impurity,
therefore he should carefully perform tooth-cleaning for the sake of purity.
Even during a fast, there is no fault in tooth-cleaning, collyrium,
fragrance, ornaments, good garments, flower-garlands, and anointing.
In a <s>smṛti</s>:
All thorny trees are meritorious; milky trees are remembered as life-giving.
Pungent, bitter, and astringent ones bestow strength, health, and happiness.
Moreover:
One should avoid tooth-sticks made from <s>palāśa</s>, and also sandals from it.

children.text: varjayec ca prayatnena vaṭaṃ vāśvattham eva ca ||
children.translated_text: And one should carefully avoid the banyan and the <s>aśvattha</s> as well.
In the <s>Kūrma</s>, in the <s>Śrīvyāsagītā</s>:
A tooth-stick equal in thickness to the middle finger, measuring twelve finger-breadths,

children.text: satvacaṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ yat tadagre na tu dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: and having its bark, is proper; but one should not hold it by the tip.
That which comes from a milky tree, that which comes from jasmine, is auspicious,

children.text: apāmārgaṃ ca bilvaṃ vā karavīraṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>bilva</s>, or especially <s>karavīra</s>.
Having avoided the condemned kinds and taken one as prescribed,

children.text: parihṛtya dinaṃ pāpaṃ bhakṣayed vai vidhānavit ||
children.translated_text: the knower of the rule should chew it, avoiding an inauspicious day.
He should not split the tooth-stick, nor hold it with the tips of the fingers.

children.text: prakṣālya bhuktvā taj jahyāt śucau deśe samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having washed it and chewed it, he should discard it in a clean place, with collected mind.
And in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, in that same context:
With a girth like the tip of the little finger, having bark, unblemished, straight,
measuring twelve finger-breadths, and moist, such should the tooth-cleaning stick be.
Or he should make an auspicious tongue-scraper in the shape of a bow.
And in the <s>Rāmārcanacandrikā</s>:

children.text: dantollekho vitastyā bhavati parimitād annam ity ādimantrāt prātaḥ kṣīryādikāṣṭhād vaṭakhadirapalāśair vinārkāmrabilvaiḥ
children.translated_text: In the morning, tooth-scraping is performed with the mantra beginning with 'annam,' using a stick measured by a span, from milky trees and the like, excluding banyan, khadira, palāśa, arka, mango, and bilva.

children.text: bhuktvā gaṇḍūṣaṣaṭkaṃ dvir api kuśam ṛte deśinīm aṅgulībhir nandābhūtāṣṭaparvaṇy api na khalu navamyarkasaṅkrāntipāte ||
children.translated_text: After eating, one should perform six mouth-rinsings, and again with the fingers apart from the index finger; not, however, on the nandā, bhūta, eighth, and parvan days, nor on the ninth, Sunday, saṅkrānti, or pāta.
Then, having sipped water according to rule and arranged his hair,
the twice-born man should remember the <s>praṇava</s> and the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and bind his <s>śikhā</s>.
And so it has been said:
He should not arrange his hair facing south, nor upward.
Having remembered the <s>oṃkāra</s> and the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he should then bind his <s>śikhā</s>.
In the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s>, in that same context:
For the sake of daily rites one should bathe in rivers, streams, ponds, waters dug for the gods,
and also in mountain springs.
Or, from wells, one should bathe on the ground with water that has been drawn up.
If bathing in those places is impossible, one should bathe with drawn water on the ground.
There <s>Kātyāyana</s> says:

children.text: yathāhani tathā prātar nityaṃ snāyād anāturaḥ
children.translated_text: Every morning, day by day, a person who is not ill should bathe regularly.
The body is extremely impure, furnished with nine apertures,
and it flows day and night; morning bathing is its purifier.
<s>Dakṣa</s>:
For forest-dwellers and householders, bathing is in the morning and at midday.

children.text: yates trisavanaṃ snānaṃ sakṛt tu brahmacāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For an ascetic, bathing is at the three pressings of the day, but for a celibate student only once.

children.text: sarve cāpi sakṛt kuryur aśaktau codakaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: And all should perform it once; when unable, they may do so even without water.
Moreover:

children.text: aśiraskaṃ bhavet snānam aśaktau karmiṇāṃ sadā
children.translated_text: For ritual performers, when they are unable, bathing should always be without washing the head,

children.text: ārdreṇa vāsasā vāpi pāṇinā vāpi mārjanam ||
children.translated_text: or it may be wiping with a wet cloth or even with the hand.
And <s>Śaṅkha</s>:
A man who has not bathed is not fit for recitation and other acts, nor for oblation and the like.
In the <s>Kūrma</s>, in the <s>Vyāsagītā</s>:

children.text: prātaḥsnānaṃ vinā puṃsāṃ pāpitvaṃ karmasu smṛtam
children.translated_text: Without the morning bath, men are regarded as sinful in rites,

children.text: home jape viśeṣeṇa tasmāt snānaṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: especially in oblation and recitation; therefore one should undertake bathing.
In the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>:
Because a man is soiled by sweat, saliva, and the like and is under the sway of sleep,
therefore, through morning bathing, he becomes fit for mantras, hymns, recitation, and the like.
And in the <s>Padma</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Devahūti</s> and <s>Vikuṇḍala</s>:

children.text: snānaṃ vinā tu yo bhuṅkte malāśī sa sadā naraḥ
children.translated_text: But the man who eats without bathing is always an eater of filth.
The ancestors and deities turn away from that unbathed, impure man.
A man without bathing is sinful; a man without bathing is impure.
One who does not bathe experiences hell and is born among worms, insects, and the like.
In the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, in the <s>Udyogaparvan</s>, in the saying of <s>Śrī Vidura</s>:

children.text: guṇā daśa snānaśīlaṃ bhajante balaṃ rūpaṃ svaravarṇapraśuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Ten qualities attend one who is devoted to bathing: strength, beauty, purity of voice and complexion,

children.text: sparśaś ca gandhaś ca viśuddhatā ca śrīḥ saukumāryaṃ pravarāś ca nāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: touch, fragrance, purity, fortune, softness, and excellent women.
And in the <s>Padma</s>, in that same place:

children.text: yāmyaṃ hi yātanāduḥkhaṃ nityasnāyī na paśyati
children.translated_text: One who bathes daily does not see the tormenting pain belonging to <s>Yama</s>.
Even men who have committed sins are purified by daily bathing.
O <s>Vaiśya</s>, morning bathing removes the external and internal dirt.

children.text: prātaḥsnānena niṣpāpo naro na nirayaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Through morning bathing a man becomes free from sin and does not go to hell.

children.text: ye punaḥ srotasi snānam ācarantīha parvaṇi
children.translated_text: Moreover, those who perform bathing in a stream here on a festival day,

children.text: tenaiva narakaṃ yānti na jāyante kuyoniṣu ||
children.translated_text: by that very act do not go to hell and are not born in bad wombs.

children.text: duḥsvapnā duṣṭacintāś ca bandhyā bhavanti sarvadā
children.translated_text: Bad dreams and evil thoughts become forever fruitless
for men purified by morning bathing, O best of the people.
In the <s>Atrismṛti</s>:

children.text: snāne manaḥprasādaḥ syād devā abhimukhāḥ sadā
children.translated_text: In bathing there is serenity of mind, and the gods are always favorable.

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ śrīḥ sukhaṃ puṣṭiḥ puṇyaṃ vidyā yaśo dhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Good fortune, prosperity, happiness, nourishment, merit, learning, fame, and firmness arise.
Morning bathing especially removes great sins, misfortune, evil, and evil thoughts,
as well as grief, suffering, and the rest.
In the <s>Kaurma</s>, in that same place:
They praise morning bathing, for it brings visible and invisible results.
Through morning bathing sins are purified; of this there is no doubt.
And in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>:

children.text: prātaḥsnānāt yataḥ śudhyet kāyo 'yaṃ malinaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Since this body, always impure, is purified by morning bathing,

children.text: chidrito navabhiś chidraiḥ sravaty eva divāniśam ||
children.translated_text: pierced with nine openings, it continually flows day and night.
Morning bathing is praised as promoting energy, intelligence, good fortune, beauty, and wealth,
and as the cause of cheerfulness of mind.

children.text: prātaḥ prātas tu yat snānaṃ saṃjāte cāruṇodaye
children.translated_text: The bathing that is performed every morning when dawn has arisen
is said to be equal to a <s>Prājāpatya</s> penance and destroys great sin.

children.text: prātaḥsnānaṃ haret pāpam alakṣmīṃ glānim eva ca
children.translated_text: Morning bathing removes sin, misfortune, weariness,

children.text: aśucitvaṃ ca duḥsvapnaṃ tuṣṭiṃ puṣṭiṃ prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: impurity, and bad dreams, and grants satisfaction and nourishment.
The wicked never approach a person who bathes in the morning.
Therefore one should perform morning bathing, which has visible and invisible fruit.
Bathing in general and morning bathing are both prescribed here.

children.text: yadyapy anyo 'nyamilite pṛthag jñeye tathāpy amū ||
children.translated_text: Although these two are mixed with one another, they should nevertheless be understood separately.

children.text: atha tīrthagatas tatra dhautavastraṃ kuśāṃs tathā
children.translated_text: Now, having gone to a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred bathing-place), he should place a washed garment, <s>kuśa</s> grasses,

children.text: mṛttikāṃ ca taṭe nyasya snāyāt svasvavidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and earth on the bank, and should bathe according to his own proper rule.
If one performs a daily or occasional rite with an unwashed garment,

children.text: kurvan na phalam āpnoti kṛtā cen niṣphalā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: he does not obtain its fruit; if it has been performed, it becomes fruitless.
Having washed his feet and hands, sipped water, and respectfully made the resolve,
and having remembered <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the other rivers, he should offer an oblation of water to the <s>tīrtha</s>.
O lord whose roar is the sound of the ocean, holding a staff, destroyer of demons,
creator of the world, crusher of the world, lord of the gods, I bow to you.
After uttering this mantra, he should perform bathing at the <s>tīrtha</s>.
Otherwise the lord of the <s>tīrtha</s> himself takes away half of its fruit.

children.text: natvātha tīrthaṃ snānārtham anujñāṃ prārthayed imām
children.translated_text: Then, bowing to the <s>tīrtha</s>, he should ask this permission for the sake of bathing:
O god of gods, lord of the world, bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, grant me your permission to attend upon your <s>tīrtha</s>.

children.text: vidhivan mṛdam ādāya tīrthatoye praviśya ca
children.translated_text: Having taken earth according to rule and entered the water of the <s>tīrtha</s>,
he should face the current in a river, but elsewhere he should face the sun.
Having performed the sealing of the directions according to rule and having ritually imagined the <s>tīrthas</s>,
he should invoke the blessed <s>Gaṅgā</s> from the solar orb.
With <s>darbha</s> grass in hand, having performed breath control,
meditating on the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and chanting his name, he should immerse himself in the meritorious water.
Having sipped water and recited the root mantra together with breath control,

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ dhyāyan jale bhūyo nimajjya snānam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he should immerse himself again in the water and perform the bath.
Having performed the rite ending with <s>aghamarṣaṇa</s> and, with the names beginning with <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: tatra dvādaśadhā toye nimajjya snānam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: having immersed himself twelve times there in the water, he should perform the bath.
In the <s>Śrīnāradapañcarātra</s>:

children.text: prasiddheṣu ca tīrtheṣu yady anyasyābhidhāṃ smaret
children.translated_text: If, at famous <s>tīrthas</s>, one remembers the name of another <s>tīrtha</s>,

children.text: snātakaṃ taṃ tu tat tīrtham abhiśapya kṣaṇād vrajet ||
children.translated_text: that <s>tīrtha</s>, cursing the bather, departs at once.
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the <s>Vaiśākhyamāhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Nārada</s> and <s>Ambarīṣa</s>:

children.text: evam uccārya tattīrthe pādau prakṣālya vāgyataḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and washed his feet at that <s>tīrtha</s>, restrained in speech,

children.text: smaran nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ snānaṃ kuryād vidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: remembering the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he should bathe according to rule.

children.text: tīrthaṃ prakalpayed dhīmān mūlamantram imaṃ paṭhan
children.translated_text: The wise man should ritually establish the <s>tīrtha</s> while reciting this root mantra:
The root mantra is declared to be: <s>auṃ namo nārāyaṇāya</s>.

children.text: darbhapāṇis tu vidhivad ācāntaḥ praṇato bhuvi
children.translated_text: With <s>darbha</s> grass in hand, having duly sipped water and bowed down on the ground,
a man should form, on every side, a square measuring four hands,
and then invoke <s>Gaṅgā</s> with this mantra:
You have arisen from the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; you are <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, whose deity is <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: trāhi nas tvenasas tasmād ā janmamaraṇāntikāt ||
children.translated_text: Therefore protect us from sin, from birth up to death.
With water held in joined hands, after reciting it seven times,

children.text: mūrdhni kṛtvā jalaṃ bhūpaś catur vā pañca sapta vā
children.translated_text: O king, placing the water on his head four, five, or seven times,

children.text: snānaṃ kṛtvā mṛdā tadvad āmantrya tu vidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having bathed with earth in the same way, he should address it according to rule:
O earth, crossed by horses, crossed by chariots, crossed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: mṛttike hara me pāpaṃ yan mayā duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: O clay, remove my sin, whatever misdeed has been done by me.
You were raised up by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of the boar, the hundred-armed one.
Obeisance to you, noble one, source and fire-drill of all worlds.
Then, when the guru is present, with the water from the feet of the parents as well,

children.text: viprāṇāṃ ca padāmbhodhiḥ kuryān mūrdhany abhiṣecanam ||
children.translated_text: and with the foot-water of brahmins, he should perform an ablution upon his head.
And similarly in the <s>Padma</s>:
O son, the water from the guru's feet gives the fruit of ten million sacred fords.
Moreover:
For the one whose head remains moistened by water from a brahmin's feet,
bathing in the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> takes place day after day.
Likewise in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>:

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni tāni tīrthāni sāgare
children.translated_text: Whatever sacred fords are on the earth, those sacred fords are in the ocean;
all those sacred fords, together with the ocean, are in the right foot of a brahmin.

children.text: śaṅkhe vasanti sarvāṇi tīrthāni ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: All sacred fords dwell in the conch, especially;
therefore with the conch and the root mantra he should again perform the ablution.
Likewise, with water from the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone mixed with <s>tulasī</s>,

children.text: abhiṣekaṃ vidadhyāc ca pītvā tat kiṃcid agrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should perform the ablution, after first drinking a little of it.
That is said in the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s>:
Water from the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone, mixed with <s>tulasī</s> and sandal,

children.text: kṛtvā śaṅkhe bhrāmayaṃs triḥ prakṣipen nijamūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: having placed it in a conch and turned it around three times, he should sprinkle it on his own head.
But he who, without drinking the water of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone,
would perform the sprinkling upon the head, is said to be a slayer of a brahmin.
Before <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s foot-water, one should drink the foot-water of a brahmin;

children.text: viruddham ācaran mohād brahmahā sa nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: one who acts in the reverse order through delusion is said to be a slayer of a brahmin.
It removes untimely death and destroys every disease:

children.text: viṣṇoḥ pādodakaṃ pītvā śirasā dhārayāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: having drunk <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s foot-water, I bear it upon my head.
The greatness of bearing and drinking the sacred water of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s lotus feet should be written earlier;
but here the greatness of ablution with that sacred water is being written.
In the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>:
He has bathed in all sacred fords and been consecrated in all sacrifices,
who performs ablution with water from the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: gaṅgā godāvarī revā nadyo muktipradās tu yāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Revā</s>, and the rivers that bestow liberation,
dwell there, together with their sacred fords, in the water of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.
What use is there for thousands of crores of sacred fords that have been resorted to,
if there is the holy sacred ford born from the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone?
In that same place, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Gautama</s> and <s>Ambarīṣa</s>:

children.text: yeṣāṃ dhautāni gātrāṇi hareḥ pādodakena vai
children.translated_text: Those whose limbs have indeed been washed with <s>Hari</s>'s foot-water,

children.text: ambarīṣa kule teṣāṃ dāso 'smi vaśagaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, I am always the servant of those people, obedient to them.

children.text: rājante tāni tāvac ca tīrthāni bhuvanatraye
children.translated_text: Only so long do those sacred fords shine in the three worlds
as the water produced by the ablution of the <s>śālagrāma</s> has not been obtained.
In the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s> of the <s>Skanda</s>:

children.text: gṛhe'pi vasatas tasya gaṅgāsnānaṃ dine dine
children.translated_text: Even while he lives at home, there is bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> for him day after day,
for the man who bathes with water from the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.
There itself, and elsewhere:

children.text: yāni kāni ca tīrthāni brahmādyā devatās tathā
children.translated_text: Whatever sacred fords there are, and likewise the deities beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>,
these are not worth even a sixteenth part of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s foot-water.
The god arising from the <s>śālagrāma</s> and the god arising from <s>Dvāravatī</s>,
by the bathing water of both of them, the sin of killing a brahmin is removed.
Moreover:

children.text: sa vai cāvabhṛtasnātaḥ sa ca gaṅgājalāplutaḥ
children.translated_text: He indeed has bathed at the avabhṛtha rite, and he has been drenched with <s>Gaṅgā</s> water,
the person who, having placed <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s foot-water in a conch, bathes with it.
In the <s>Śrī Nṛsiṃhapurāṇa</s>:
The sacred waters of <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Prayāga</s>, <s>Gayā</s>, <s>Naimiṣa</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, and the holy waters of <s>Kurujāṅgala</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: kālena tīrthasalilāni punanti pāpaṃ pādodakaṃ bhagavataḥ prapunāti sadyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: purify sin over time; the Lord's foot-water purifies it immediately.
And in the Smṛti:
Whatever rivers do not go to the ocean give the fruit of three nights;

children.text: samudragāś ca pakṣasya māsasya saritāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: those that go to the ocean give that of a fortnight, and the lord of rivers gives that of a month.
<s>Godā</s> gives the fruit of six months, and <s>Jāhnavī</s> that of a year;
the Lord's foot-water gives the fruit of twelve years.
In the <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: jalaṃ ca yeṣāṃ tulasīvimiśritaṃ pādodakaṃ cakraśilāsamudbhavam
children.translated_text: Men for whom the water mixed with <s>tulasī</s>, the foot-water arising from the cakra-stone,

children.text: nityaṃ trisandhyaṃ plavate na gātraṃ khagendra te dharmabahiṣkṛtā narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: does not bathe the body daily at the three twilights, O king of birds, are excluded from dharma.

children.text: tato jalāñjalīn kṣiptvā mūrdhni trīn kumbhamudrayā
children.translated_text: Then, having cast three handfuls of water onto the head with the kumbha-mudrā,
with the root mantra, and then without distinction, he should make tarpaṇa for the gods and the rest.
And that is well known among the Vedic rites.

children.text: brahmādayo ye devās tān devān tarpayāmi
children.translated_text: I satisfy those gods, <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods.
I satisfy the gods of the earth-world.
I satisfy the gods of the mid-space.
I satisfy the gods of heaven.
I satisfy the gods of earth, mid-space, and heaven.
Having sipped water, wiped the limbs, and put on bathing garments together with a lower cloth,
and having put on two white cloths, seated, he should perform sipping of water.

children.text: vidhivat tilakaṃ kṛtvā punaś cācamya vaiṣṇavaḥ
children.translated_text: Having made the tilaka according to rule, and having again sipped water, the Vaiṣṇava,
after performing the Vedic sandhyā, should then worship the Tantric one.
There in the <s>Kūrma</s>:
Then, standing on eastward-pointing darbha grasses, well composed,

children.text: prāṇāyāmatrayaṃ kṛtvā dhyāyet sandhyām iti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: having performed three breath-controls, he should meditate on <s>Sandhyā</s>; so says the śruti.
In the <s>Manusmṛti</s>:

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ śāktikāḥ sarve na śaivā na ca vaiṣṇavāḥ
children.translated_text: All brahmins are śāktikas, not Śaivas and not Vaiṣṇavas,
because they worship the goddess <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the mother of the Veda.

children.text: yā ca sandhyā jagatsūtir māyātītā hi niṣkalā
children.translated_text: And <s>Sandhyā</s>, the mother of the world, is beyond māyā and without parts;
she is the sovereign, sole power, arisen from the three principles.
Having meditated on that <s>Sāvitrī</s> located in the disk of the sun, the wise man should recite it;
a brahmin, facing east, should always perform the worship of <s>Sandhyā</s>.
Moreover:
A thousand is supreme, a hundred is middling, and ten is the lowest.

children.text: sāvitrīṃ vai japed vidvān prāṅmukhaḥ prayataḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A learned man should recite <s>Sāvitrī</s>, facing east, standing purified.
Moreover:
One without sandhyā is always impure and unfit for all rites;

children.text: yad anyat kurute kiṃcin na tasya phalam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: whatever else he does, he does not obtain its fruit.
O best of twice-born, one who directs his effort elsewhere in a dharma rite...
Abandoning the salutation at <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship), he goes to ten thousand hells.
Peaceful brahmins, whose minds were fixed on no other, and who had crossed to the far shore of the Veda,

children.text: upāsya vidhivat sandhyāṃ prāptāḥ pūrve parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: having worshiped <s>sandhyā</s> according to rule in former times, attained the supreme goal.
Then, having worshiped in water his own glorious mantra-deity,
he should satisfy it according to rule, and likewise its enclosing deities.
And so it is said in the <s>Bodhāyanasmṛti</s>:

children.text: haviṣāgnau jale puṣpair dhyānena hṛdaye harim
children.translated_text: The wise daily worship <s>Hari</s> with oblation in the fire, with flowers in water, and by meditation in the heart,
and by recitation in the solar disk.
And in the <s>Padma</s>, in that same place:
Worship in the sun is excellent, and in water it is done with water and the like.
Having then uttered the root mantra and meditated on the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: śrīkṛṣṇaṃ tarpayāmīti triḥ samyak tarpayet kṛtī ||
children.translated_text: the capable practitioner should properly offer tarpaṇa three times, saying, "I satisfy <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>."
To <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose form has been indicated by meditation and who abides in the solar disk,
he should thereafter give an arghya (offering) with the <s>Kāmagāyatrī</s>.
In the <s>Śrī Sanatkumārakalpa</s>:
First, after bringing out "manmatha," he should say the word "kāmadeva";
with the ending in "-āya," he should say "vidmahe," then the word "puṣpabāṇāya";
then, after saying "dhīmahi" in the same way, he should say, "May that <s>Anaṅga</s> impel us."
Then, having meditated on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the disk of the sun, he should recite this ten times;

children.text: kṣamasveti tam udvāsya dadyād arghyaṃ vivasvate ||
children.translated_text: dismissing him with "forgive me," he should give an arghya to <s>Vivasvat</s>.
A certain procedure of tantric <s>sandhyā</s> and worship in water,

children.text: yo 'nyo manyeta so 'py atra tadviśeṣāya likhyate ||
children.translated_text: which some others hold, is also written here for its particular details.
First the Vaiṣṇava should take water with the right hand,
and then, with the heart-mantra, place it in the palm of the left hand.
Then, with the right hand, using drops of water issuing from those fingers,
he should sprinkle his head with the eye-mantra.
Taking the remaining water in the right hand with the weapon-mantra,

children.text: adhaḥ kṣipet punaś caivam iti vāracatuṣṭayam ||
children.translated_text: he should cast it downward; and again in this same way, four times.
Again, taking water in the right hand with the heart-mantra,
he should inhale it through the left nostril and expel it through the other.
Then, taking a handful of water, to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who abides in the solar disk,
he should present arghya three times with the <s>Gopālagāyatrī</s>.

children.text: brūyād gopījanaṃ ṅe'ntaṃ vidmahe ity ataḥ param
children.translated_text: He should say "gopījana" with the ending in "ṅe," and after that "vidmahe";

children.text: punar gopījanaṃ tadvad dhīmahīti tataḥ param
children.translated_text: again "gopījana" in the same way, and after that "dhīmahi";

children.text: tan naḥ kṛṣṇa iti prānte prapūrvaṃ codayād iti ||
children.translated_text: at the end, "May that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> impel us," with the prefix "pra-."

children.text: mūrdhni nyaset tadaṅgāni lalāṭe netrayor dvayoḥ
children.translated_text: He should place the limbs of that mantra on the crown of the head, on the forehead, on the two eyes,

children.text: bhujayoḥ pādayoś caiva sarvāṅgeṣu tathā kramāt ||
children.translated_text: on the arms, on the feet, and likewise on all the limbs, in order.
And these are stated:

children.text: pañcabhiś ca tribhiś caiva pañcabhiś ca tribhiḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: With five and with three, then again with five and with three,

children.text: caturbhiś ca caturbhiś ca kuryād aṅgāni varṇakiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and with four and with four, one who knows the syllables should perform the limb-placements.
Meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, absorbed in the rāsa-play, in the solar disk,
with his arms raised toward him, he should recite that <s>Gāyatrī</s> for a moment.
Having performed aṅganyāsa with his own mantra, he should then conceive a lotus in the water,

children.text: saṃcintya pīṭhamantreṇa tarpayec ca sakṛt sakṛt ||
children.translated_text: and, with the seat-mantra, offer tarpaṇa once to each.

children.text: tasmiṃś ca kṛṣṇam āvāhya sakalīkṛtya mānasān
children.translated_text: Having invoked <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> there and mentally made the worship complete,
after giving the five services in the water, he should display the cow-mudrā.
Meditating that this water is nectar and consecrating it with his own mantra,
the capable practitioner should offer tarpaṇa one hundred and eight times upon the crown of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: tataś ca mūlamantreṇa vārān vai pañcaviṃśatim
children.translated_text: Then, with water that has been recited over twenty-five times with the root mantra,
he should perform ācamana according to rule.
In the <s>Padma</s>:

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ tarpayet pūrvaṃ viṣṇuṃ rudraṃ prajāpatīn
children.translated_text: One should first offer tarpaṇa to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and the <s>Prajāpatis</s>,

children.text: devā yakṣās tathā nāgā gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: to the gods, the <s>Yakṣas</s>, the <s>Nāgas</s>, and the hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>;

children.text: krūrāḥ sarpāḥ suparṇāś ca taravo jambhakādayaḥ
children.translated_text: to fierce beings, serpents, <s>Suparṇas</s>, trees, and beings such as <s>Jambhakas</s>,
to <s>Vidyādharas</s>, cloud-bearers, and likewise sky-going beings;

children.text: nirādhārāś ca ye jīvāḥ pāpadharmaratāś ca ye
children.translated_text: and to those unsupported living beings, and those who delight in sinful conduct:
"For their refreshment, this water is given by me."

children.text: kṛtopavīto devebhyo nivītī ca bhavet tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having assumed the upavīta position of the sacred thread for the gods, he should then become nivītin;

children.text: manuṣyāṃs tarpayed bhaktyā ṛṣiputrān ṛṣīṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: with devotion he should offer tarpaṇa to human beings, to the sons of sages, and to the sages.

children.text: sanakaś ca sanandaś ca tṛtīyaś ca sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sananda</s>, and the third, <s>Sanātana</s>,

children.text: kapilaś cāsuriś caiva voḍhuḥ pañcaśikhas tathā
children.translated_text: also <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Āsuri</s>, <s>Voḍhu</s>, and <s>Pañcaśikha</s>;

children.text: sarve te tṛptim āyāntu maddattenāmbunā sadā ||
children.translated_text: may all these always attain satisfaction through the water given by me.
He should offer tarpaṇa with direct waters to <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>,

children.text: pracetasaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca bhṛguṃ nāradam eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Pracetas</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Nārada</s>,
and to all the divine brahmarṣis.

children.text: apasavyaṃ tataḥ kṛtvāsavyaṃ jānu ca bhūtale
children.translated_text: Then, having made the thread apasavya and placed the left knee on the ground,
he should offer tarpaṇa to the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, the <s>Saumyas</s>, the <s>Barhiṣmants</s>, and the <s>Uṣmapās</s>,
to the <s>Kavyas</s>, <s>Analas</s>, the <s>Barhiṣads</s>, and again to the <s>Ājyapās</s>,
with devotion to the ancestors, using water with sesame and sandal.
Obeisance to <s>Yama</s>, to <s>Dharmarāja</s>, to <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and to <s>Antaka</s>,
to <s>Vaivasvata</s>, to <s>Kāla</s>, and to the imperishable lord of all beings;
to <s>Auḍumbara</s>, to <s>Dadhna</s>, to <s>Nīla</s>, and to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
to <s>Vṛkodara</s>, to <s>Citra</s>, and to <s>Citragupta</s>: indeed, obeisance.

children.text: darbhapāṇiḥ suprayataḥ pitṝn svān tarpayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, holding darbha grass in his hand and being very well purified, he should offer tarpaṇa to his own ancestors.
Having fully satisfied his father and the others by name and gotra, and the maternal grandfathers as well,

children.text: saṃtarpya vidhinā sarvān imaṃ mantram udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: all according to rule, he should utter this mantra:
Those who were not relatives, or were relatives, or who were relatives in another birth,

children.text: te tṛptim akhilāṃ yāntu ye cāsmattoyakāṅkṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those who desire water from us: may they all attain complete satisfaction.
Before the worship of <s>sandhyā</s>, some perform tarpaṇa beginning with the gods.
They consider this to be done only once, according to what is stated in the Purāṇas.
And likewise, in the <s>Padma</s>, after taking earth during the bath:

children.text: evaṃ snātvā tataḥ paścād ācamya suvidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: Having bathed in this way, then afterward having sipped water properly,

children.text: utthāya vāsasī śukle śuddhe tu paridhāya vai
children.translated_text: having risen and put on two white, clean garments,

children.text: tatas tu tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt trailokyāpyāyanāya vai ||
children.translated_text: then he should perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) for the refreshment of the three worlds.
For this very reason, in the <s>Śrīrāmārcanacandrikā</s>:

children.text: niṣpīḍayitvā vastraṃ tu paścāt sandhyāṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: Having wrung out the garment, afterward he should perform the twilight rite.

children.text: anyathā kurute yas tu snānaṃ tasyāphalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: But one who does otherwise has his bath become fruitless.
Moreover:

children.text: vastraṃ triguṇitaṃ yas tu niṣpīḍayati mūḍhadhīḥ
children.translated_text: The foolish-minded man who wrings out a garment folded three times

children.text: vṛthā snānaṃ bhavet tasya niṣpīḍayati cāmbuni ||
children.translated_text: has a useless bath, and he wrings it out in the water.
In the <s>Kāśīkāṇḍa</s>:
Even with the waters of all rivers, with heaps of clay, and then with products of the cow,
one may perform outward purification; but one whose disposition is corrupt does not partake of purity.

children.text: naktaṃ dinaṃ nimajjyāpsu kaivartāḥ kimu pāvanāḥ
children.translated_text: Are fishermen, who immerse themselves in water night and day, thereby pure?

children.text: śataśo 'pi tathā snātā na śuddhā bhāvadūṣitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even when bathed hundreds of times in that way, those corrupted in disposition are not pure.
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the <s>Vaiśākhamāhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Nārada</s> and <s>Ambarīṣa</s>:

children.text: puṇyena gāṅgena jalena kāle deśe'pi yaḥ snānaparo 'pi bhūpa
children.translated_text: O king, even one who is intent on bathing at the proper time and place with the meritorious water of <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: ā janmato bhāvahato 'pi dātā na śudhyatīty eva mataṃ mamaitat ||
children.translated_text: if ruined in disposition from birth, is not purified, though he may be a giver; this indeed is my opinion.
Having kindled a fire soaked with ghee and oil, its flame turning clockwise, at the proper time,

children.text: praviśya dagdhaḥ kila bhāvaduṣṭo na svargam āpnoti phalaṃ na cānyat ||
children.translated_text: one corrupted in disposition, entering it and being burned, does not attain heaven, nor any other fruit.
For this very reason, in the <s>Bhaviṣyottara</s>:

children.text: yasya hastau ca pādau ca vāṅ manaś ca susaṃyatam
children.translated_text: He whose hands and feet, speech and mind are well restrained,

children.text: vidyātapaś ca kīrtiś ca sa tīrthaphalam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: and who has knowledge, austerity, and good repute, obtains the fruit of a <s>tīrtha</s>.
The faithless man, the evil-souled man, the atheist, one whose doubt is not cut off,
and one fixed on mere reasoning: these five do not share in the fruit of <s>tīrthas</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgopālabhaṭṭavilikhite śrībhagavadbhaktivilāse śaucīyo nāma tṛtīyo vilāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>vilāsa</s>, named <s>Śaucīya</s>, in the <s>Śrībhagavadbhaktivilāsa</s> written by <s>Śrī Gopālabhaṭṭa</s>.
Having bathed once in the supreme <s>tīrtha</s> of the name of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>,

children.text: nityāśuciḥ śucīndraḥ san svadharmaṃ vaktum arhati ||
children.translated_text: one who is always impure becomes foremost among the pure and is fit to speak of his own <s>dharma</s>.
Then he should return to his own home, first bowing to his chosen deity,
to gurus and elders, and carrying flowers, fuel, <s>kuśa</s> grass, water, and the rest.
And likewise in the <s>Śrīnṛsiṃhapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: jale devaṃ namaskṛtya tato gacched gṛhaṃ pumān
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the deity in the water, then a man should go home,

children.text: pauruṣeṇa tu sūktena tato viṣṇuṃ samarcayet ||
children.translated_text: and then worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the <s>Pauruṣa</s> hymn.
He should sweep the temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having performed sipping of water and the other preliminaries,

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ paśyan kīrtayaṃś ca dāsyenātmānam arpayet ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, singing praise, and offering himself in servitude.

children.text: śuddhaṃ gomayam ādāya tato mṛtsnāṃ jalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Taking pure cow-dung, and then clay and water as well,

children.text: bhaktyā tat parito limped abhyukṣec ca tadaṅganam ||
children.translated_text: he should devoutly smear around it and sprinkle its courtyard.
And likewise in the ninth book, in the story of <s>Śrīmad Ambarīṣa</s>:

children.text: sa vai manaḥ kṛṣṇapadāravindayor vacāṃsi vaikuṇṭhaguṇānuvarṇane karau harer mandiramārjanādiṣu śrutiṃ cakārācyutasatkathodaye ||
children.translated_text: He fixed his mind on the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, his words on recounting the virtues of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, his hands on sweeping the temple of <s>Hari</s> and similar acts, and his hearing on the arising of true stories of <s>Acyuta</s>.
In the eleventh book, in the dialogue of the Blessed Lord and <s>Uddhava</s>, in the teaching of <s>bhagavad-dharma</s>:
By sweeping and smearing, by sprinkling and making <s>maṇḍalas</s>,
there is service to my house, done for me like a servant and without deceit.
In the <s>Śrīnṛsiṃhapurāṇa</s>:
Whoever daily performs sweeping in the house of <s>Narasiṃha</s>,
freed from all sins, rejoices in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Śrīviṣṇudharmottara</s>:

children.text: saṃmārjanaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt puruṣaḥ keśavālaye
children.translated_text: The man who performs sweeping in the shrine of <s>Keśava</s>

children.text: rajastamobhyāṃ nirmuktaḥ sa bhaven nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: becomes free from <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: pāṃśūnāṃ yāvatāṃ rājan kuryāt saṃmārjanaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: O king, for as many particles of dust as a man sweeps away,

children.text: tāvanty abdāni sa sukhī nākam āsādya modate ||
children.translated_text: for that many years, having reached heaven, he rejoices happily.
In the <s>Śrīvārāha</s>:
As many strokes as they make in sweeping the ground,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.
And he is born as my devotee, endowed with every <s>dharma</s>,
pure, a <s>Bhāgavata</s>, purified, and free from offences.
Then, having enjoyed all pleasures and crossed the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
when fallen from <s>Śākadvīpa</s>, he goes to the world of heaven.

children.text: nandanaṃ vanam āśritya modate cāpsaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: Resorting to the <s>Nandana</s> grove, he rejoices with the apsarases;
and when fallen from <s>Nandana</s>, established in my rite,

children.text: sarvasaṅgāt parityajya mama lokaṃ tu gacchati ||
children.translated_text: abandoning all attachment, he goes to my world.
There itself:

children.text: gomayaṃ gṛhya vai bhūmiṃ mama veśmopalepayet
children.translated_text: Taking cow-dung, he should smear the ground of my dwelling;

children.text: yāvatas tu padāṃs tatra samantād upalepayet
children.translated_text: as many steps as he smears there on every side,
for that many thousands of years he likewise is born as my devotee.

children.text: samīpe yadi vā dūre yaś cālayati gomayam
children.translated_text: Whether nearby or far away, whoever carries cow-dung,

children.text: yāvat tasya padāgrāṇi tāvat svarge mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: for as many steps as the fronts of his feet make, for that long he is honored in heaven.
Fallen from there, he becomes a righteous king on <s>Śālmalī</s>,
and he is born as my devotee, learned in all <s>śāstras</s>.
Whoever, firm in vow, has the ground smeared with cow-dung,

children.text: tasya dṛṣṭvānulepaṃ tu mama tuṣṭiḥ prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: when I see that smearing, satisfaction arises in me.

children.text: goś ca yasyāḥ purīṣeṇa kriyate bhūmilepanam
children.translated_text: And the cow with whose dung the smearing of the ground is done
is freed from birth in a cow's womb by a single smearing.

children.text: sthānopalepane bhūme salilaṃ yo dadāti me
children.translated_text: O greatly fortunate one, hear truly and completely the merit

children.text: tasya puṇyaṃ mahābhāge śṛṇu tattvena niṣkalam ||
children.translated_text: of one who gives me water for smearing the ground of the place.
O beautiful one, as many drops of water as there are while it is being smeared,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in the world of heaven.
As many drops whatsoever of water there are, O <s>Vasundharā</s>,
For so many thousands of years he is honored in <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>.
Having fallen away from <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>, devoted to every <s>dharma</s> (religious duty),

children.text: sarvasaṅgān parityajya mama lokaṃ ca gacchati ||
children.translated_text: and abandoning all attachments, he goes to my world.
In the <s>Śrīviṣṇudharmottara</s>:

children.text: kṛtvopalepanaṃ viṣṇor naras tv āyatane sadā
children.translated_text: A man who always performs the plastering of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s shrine

children.text: gomayena śubhān lokān ayatnād eva gacchati ||
children.translated_text: with cow dung goes without effort to auspicious worlds.
O king, after plastering a piece of ground the measure of a hand,
a man continually obtains a hundred divine pleasure-groves in heaven.
In the <s>Nārasiṃha</s>:

children.text: gomayena mṛdā toyair yaḥ kuryād upalepanam
children.translated_text: Whoever performs plastering with cow dung, clay, and water,
obtains the fruit of a <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar vow) and is honored in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world.
There itself, in the instruction of the messengers of <s>Śrīdharmarāja</s>:
Whoever performs sweeping and plastering with cow dung

children.text: karoti bhavane viṣṇos tyājyaṃ teṣāṃ kulatrayam ||
children.translated_text: in the house of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the three generations of those people are to be spared.
In the <s>Śrīviṣṇudharmottara</s>:

children.text: abhyukṣaṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt pānīyena surālaye
