children.translated_text: But whoever performs sprinkling with water in a temple of the gods

children.text: sa śāntatāpo bhavati nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: becomes one whose burning afflictions are pacified; no doubt should be entertained here.

children.text: abhyukṣaṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryād devadevājire naraḥ
children.translated_text: And a man who performs sprinkling in the courtyard of the God of gods
is freed from all sin and enjoys the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
One who knows how should make all-auspicious lotuses and the like, and also svastikas,
fashion them in varied forms, and adorn the temple of <s>Hari</s>.
And likewise in the <s>Nārasiṃha</s>:
With sweeping and plastering, beautified with colored lotuses and the like,
he should joyfully make the place of <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s> bright in every part.
In the <s>Skandapurāṇa</s>, in the section on <s>Kārttika</s>:
The sin in going where one should not go and in eating what should not be eaten,

children.text: sarvaṃ tannāśam āpnoti maṇḍayitvā harer gṛham ||
children.translated_text: all that comes to destruction after one has adorned the house of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: aṇumātraṃ tu yaḥ kuryān maṇḍalaṃ keśavāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever makes even an atom-sized maṇḍala before <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: mṛdā dhātuvikāraiś ca divi kalpaśataṃ vaset ||
children.translated_text: with clay and mineral substances, dwells in heaven for a hundred kalpas.

children.text: śālagrāmaśilāgre tu yaḥ kuryāt svastikaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: And whoever makes an auspicious svastika before the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,

children.text: kārttike tu viśeṣeṇa punāty ā saptamaṃ kulam ||
children.translated_text: especially in <s>Kārttika</s>, purifies his family up to the seventh generation.

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ kurute nityaṃ yā nārī keśavāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: A woman who daily makes a maṇḍala before <s>Keśava</s>
never suffers widowhood for seven births.

children.text: gṛhītvā gomayaṃ yā tu maṇḍalaṃ keśavāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: And a woman who takes cow dung and makes a maṇḍala before <s>Keśava</s>

children.text: bhartur viyogaṃ nāpnoti santateś ca dhanasya ca ||
children.translated_text: does not suffer separation from her husband, her offspring, or her wealth.
Whoever makes the courtyard of the deity furnished with colors

children.text: devasya kurute yas tu krīḍate bhuvanatraye ||
children.translated_text: and provided with svastikas sports throughout the three worlds.
In the <s>Nāradīya</s>:

children.text: mṛdā dhātuvikārair vā varṇakair gomayena vā
children.translated_text: With clay, mineral substances, pigments, or cow dung,

children.text: viṣṇuloke'tha tatra rathaiḥ saspṛhaṃ vīkṣyate sukhī ||
children.translated_text: he is happy in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world, and is gazed at longingly by those there in chariots.
In the <s>Haribhaktisudhodaya</s>:
After plastering the dwelling of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and then painting it with pigments,
he is happy in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world, and is gazed at longingly by those who dwell there.
In the <s>Āgama</s>:
The wise man, after dividing the four sections lying in the intermediate directions into sixteen parts,
should wipe them in the form of a svastika with white, yellow, red, and black colors.
And there is a statement from the <s>Pañcarātra</s>:
He should have powders of five colors prepared for the sake of the maṇḍala:
white from powdered rice-grain, or produced from barley;
red produced from saffron, vermilion, red ocher, and the like;
yellow produced from orpiment, and sometimes produced from turmeric;
black mixed from burnt green and yellow barley.
Then, placing flags, banners, and the like in <s>Hari</s>'s temple,

children.text: vicitraṃ bhūṣayet tac ca bhagavadbhaktimān naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the man devoted to the Lord should adorn it in varied ways.

children.text: dhvajam āropayed yas tu prāsādopari bhaktitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever raises a flag on top of the temple with devotion

children.text: tasya brahmapade vāsaḥ krīḍate brahmaṇā saha ||
children.translated_text: has residence in the station of <s>Brahmā</s> and sports together with <s>Brahmā</s>.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>:
Whoever performs the excellent raising of a flag in the house of <s>Viṣṇu</s>
is worshiped by <s>Viriñci</s> and the others; what need is there for much speech by others?
There itself, also earlier:

children.text: paṭo dhvajasya viprendra yāvac calati vāyunā
children.translated_text: O best of brahmins, as long as the cloth of the flag moves in the wind,

children.text: tāvanti pāpajālāni naśyanty eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so many nets of sins are surely destroyed; there is no doubt.
Even if one is joined with a great sin, or joined with all sins,
by making a flag in the house of <s>Viṣṇu</s> one is released from all sins.
Those righteous people who rejoice on seeing a flag that has been raised
are all also released from tens of millions of great sins.

children.text: evaṃ bṛhannāradīye khyātaṃ yac cānyad adbhutam
children.translated_text: Thus the famous and otherwise wondrous
greatness of raising a flag in the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s> should be consulted here in full.
In the <s>Dvārakāmāhātmya</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇālayaṃ yaḥ kurute patākābhiś ca śobhitam
children.translated_text: Whoever makes the temple of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> beautiful with banners

children.text: sadaiva tasya loke tu vāsas tasya na cānyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: always has his dwelling in that one's world, and not elsewhere.
In the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>:

children.text: patākāṃ ca śubhāṃ dattvā tathā keśavaveśmani
children.translated_text: And, having given an auspicious banner in the house of <s>Keśava</s>,
a twice-born man obtains the world of <s>Vāyu</s> for many groups of years.

children.text: dodhūyate yathā sā tu vāyunā keśavālaye
children.translated_text: Just as that banner is shaken by the wind in the temple of <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: tathā tasyāpi sakalaṃ dehāt pāpaṃ vidhūyate ||
children.translated_text: so all sin is shaken off from his body.
There itself, in the <s>Dvārakāmāhātmya</s>:
O king, whoever makes a festooned garland in the house of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
is served by hundreds of thousands of lords of the gods surrounded by divine maidens.
Whoever makes the house of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> beautiful with plantain pillars
rejoices accompanied by apsarases; the king of the gods welcomes him.

children.text: tatra tāmrādipātraṃ yat prabhor vastrādikaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: There, whatever copper and other vessels belong to the Lord, and whatever cloths and the like,

children.text: pīṭhādikaṃ ca tat sarvaṃ yathoktaṃ ca viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: and whatever seats and so on, he should purify all that as prescribed.
In the <s>Nārasiṃha</s>:
He should scrub <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s footstool with a bilva leaf,
and, after washing it with hot water, he is released from all sins.
In the <s>Mārkaṇḍeyapurāṇa</s>:
Objects of <s>uḍumbara</s> wood are purified with an acid; tin and lead with alkali,

children.text: bhasmāmbubhiś ca kāṃsyānāṃ śuddhiḥ plāvo dravasya ca ||
children.translated_text: bronze vessels with ash and water; and a liquid is purified by flooding.
And in the <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s>:
Jewels, diamonds, corals, pearls, conches, and stones
are purified with a paste of white mustard seeds, or again with sesame paste.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>:
Objects made of gold, silver, conch, stone, mother-of-pearl, or jewels,
and those made of bronze, iron, copper, brass, tin, and lead,
if they are not smeared, are purified with water alone.
If they are polluted by a <s>śūdra</s>'s leavings, they should be cleaned in three ways: with alkali, acid, and water.
A vessel or the like that is greatly defiled should be purified for the rite of hospitality;
one may use it for an exchange of that vessel, or for some other work of the master.
By exchanging it, one should offer another to the lord.

children.text: ity ayaṃ sarvato loke sadācāro virājate ||
children.translated_text: Thus this good custom shines everywhere in the world.
<s>Manu</s>:
For copper, iron, bronze, brass, tin, and lead,
cleaning should be done as appropriate with alkali, acid, water, and the like.
<s>Śaṅkha</s>:
For copper, and likewise for lead and tin, purification is by acidic water;

children.text: kṣāreṇa śuddhiṃ kāṃsyasya lauhasya ca vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: for bronze and iron, one should prescribe purification by alkali.
Moreover:
For a vessel polluted by a woman in childbirth's leavings, or damaged by liquor and the like,
purity comes from rubbing it twenty-one times; but bronze is not to be heated.
And elsewhere:
Copper is purified with acid, if it has not been smeared with meat.

children.text: āmiṣeṇa tu yal liptaṃ punar dāhena śudhyanti ||
children.translated_text: But what has been smeared with meat is purified again by burning.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>:
Things affected by a woman in childbirth, a corpse, feces, urine, or a menstruating woman

children.text: prakṣeptavyāni tāny agnau yac ca yāvat sahed api ||
children.translated_text: should be thrown into fire, to the extent and for as long as they can endure it.
Therefore <s>Devala</s> says:
Metals are purified by burning, or with ash or cow dung;

children.text: dahanāt khananād vāpi śailānām ambhasāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: stones also by burning or burying, or even with water.
Wood is purified by cutting or scraping, and also with clay, cow dung, and water;
but for earthen vessels, purification by burning is accepted.
<s>Manu</s>:

children.text: madyair mūtraiḥ purīṣair vā ṣṭhīvanaiḥ pūyaśoṇitaiḥ
children.translated_text: An earthen object touched by liquors, urine, feces,
spittle, pus, or blood is not purified even by being baked again.
<s>Vṛddhaśātātapa</s>:

children.text: saṃhatānāṃ tu pātrāṇāṃ yad ekam upahanyate
children.translated_text: Among vessels joined together, if one is defiled,
this purification of that one alone is prescribed, effecting the general purity of the substance.
There <s>Śaṅkha</s> says:

children.text: tāntavaṃ malinaṃ pūrvam adbhiḥ kṣāraiś ca śodhayet
children.translated_text: First one should clean a soiled woven cloth with water and alkalis;

children.text: aṃśubhiḥ śoṣayitvā vā vāyunā vā samāharet ||
children.translated_text: after drying it in sunlight or by wind, one should take it up.
For woolen cloth, silk, fine cloth, linen, dukūla cloth, sheep products, and leather,
in cases of slight impurity, purification is by drying, sprinkling, and the like.
Those same things, when smeared with impure matter, one should wash with white mustard,
with grain pastes, leaf pastes, juices, and fruit-barks.
Mattresses and other cushions, flowers, jewels, and garments
should be purified in the sun for a little while, and repeatedly wiped by hand.

children.text: paścāc ca vāriṇā prokṣya śucīty evam udāharet
children.translated_text: Afterwards, having sprinkled them with water, one should declare, "They are clean."
Those too, if very much stained with dirt, should be purified properly.
<s>Śātātapa</s>:
Things colored red with safflower or saffron, and likewise with lac-dye,
are purified by washing, and also when touched by a <s>caṇḍāla</s>.
<s>Yama</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇājinānāṃ vātaiś ca bālānāṃ mṛdbhir ambhasā
children.translated_text: Black antelope skins are purified by winds; hair by clay and water;
bones and teeth by cow urine; linens by white mustard.
<s>Śaṅkha</s>:
Objects made of tooth and horn are purified with a paste of white mustard seeds,
fruit vessels with cow hair, and bones in the same way as horns.
Moreover:

children.text: niryāsānāṃ guḍānāṃ ca lavaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: For resins, molasses, and salts likewise,
and for safflower blossoms, wool, and cotton,

children.text: prokṣaṇāt kathitā śuddhir ity āha bhagavān yamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: purification is said to be by sprinkling; so says the blessed <s>Yama</s>.
<s>Manu</s>:

children.text: adbhis tu prokṣaṇaṃ śaucaṃ bahūnāṃ dhānyavāsasām
children.translated_text: For many grains and garments, cleaning is by sprinkling with water;

children.text: prakṣālanena tv alpānām adbhiḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: but for a few, cleaning with water is prescribed by washing.
Leathers are purified like cloth; objects made of split bamboo are likewise.
Vegetables, roots, and fruits are considered purified like grain.

children.text: prokṣaṇāt tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ ca palālaṃ caiva śudhyati
children.translated_text: Grass, wood, and straw are purified by sprinkling;
a dwelling by sweeping and plastering, and an earthen object by being baked again.
Moreover:

children.text: yāvan nāpaity amedhyāktād gandho lepaś ca tatkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: As long as the odor from something smeared with impurity, and the coating caused by it, do not depart,
so long clay and water must be applied in every purification of substances.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>:
For cloth, objects of split bamboo, leather, and the like, purification is remembered as washing.
For something very defiled, that portion alone should be cut off and discarded for purification.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>:
For clay, leaves, grass, and wood, when there is contact with dogs, bones, <s>caṇḍālas</s>, or crows,
purification is prescribed by the moon's rays, the sun's rays, and wind.
<s>Baudhāyana</s>:

children.text: āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ nāvaḥ panthās tṛṇāni ca
children.translated_text: Seats, beds, vehicles, boats, roads, and grasses,
as well as things made of baked bricks, are purified by wind and sunlight.
There <s>Baudhāyana</s> says:
Rice grains, vegetables, roots, and fruits are purified by sprinkling with water,
or by removing just that portion, or by removing the husk.
<s>Śaṅkha</s>:
Ghee and oil are purified by heating; cow's milk products by flooding.
One should flood vessels with water, and also vegetables, roots, and fruits.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>:
Abundant liquid substances should be thoroughly flooded with water.
Grains and rice, and vegetables, roots, and fruits,

children.text: tyaktvā tu dūṣitaṃ bhāgaṃ plāvyāny atha jalena tu ||
children.translated_text: after the spoiled portion has been discarded, should then be flooded with water.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>:
Ghee and oil are purified by heating; cow's milk products by flooding.

children.text: tanmātram uddhṛtaṃ śudhyet kaṭhinaṃ tu payodadhi ||
children.translated_text: Only that much which has been taken out is purified; but a solid item, yogurt, or milk is purified.

children.text: avilīnaṃ tathā sarpir vilīnaṃ śrapaṇena tu
children.translated_text: Likewise unmelted ghee is purified; melted ghee, however, by boiling.

children.text: ādhāradoṣe tu nayet pātrāt pātrāntaraṃ dravam ||
children.translated_text: But when the fault lies in the container, one should transfer a liquid from that vessel to another vessel.

children.text: ghṛtaṃ ca pāyasaṃ kṣīraṃ tathaikṣavaraso guḍaḥ
children.translated_text: Ghee, pāyasa, milk, sugarcane juice, and jaggery,

children.text: śūdrabhāṇḍasthitaṃ takraṃ tathā madhu na duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: as well as buttermilk, honey, when standing in a Śūdra's vessel, are not defiled.
Moreover, <s>Manu</s> says:
If, in some way, a man holding a substance in his hand has been touched by leavings,

children.text: anidhāyaiva tad dravyam ācāntaḥ śucitām iyāt ||
children.translated_text: without putting that substance down, he attains purity after performing ācamana.
Other rules of purification for substances are also to be known by Vaiṣṇavas from the smṛti-śāstras;
enough with elaborating each of those in detail.
Then, having bowed to <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s> and asked permission, the Vaiṣṇava
should gather sacred tulasī and flowers and the like, as prescribed.
And there is the statement of <s>Hārīta</s>:

children.text: snānaṃ kṛtvā tu ye kecit puṣpaṃ gṛhṇanti vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever twice-born men take flowers after having bathed,

children.text: devatās tan na gṛhṇanti bhasmībhavati kāṣṭhavat ||
children.translated_text: the deities do not accept that; it becomes like wood reduced to ash.

children.text: tac ca madhyāhnasnānaviṣayaṃ yata uktaṃ pādme vaiśākhamāhātmye
children.translated_text: That, however, concerns the midday bath, since it is said in the Vaiśākha-māhātmya of the <s>Padma</s>:
Having cut tulasī without bathing, for the sake of a deity or in ancestral rites,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ niṣphalaṃ yāti pañcagavyena śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: all that becomes fruitless; it is purified with pañcagavya.

children.text: svagṛhe vācaran snānaṃ prakṣālyāṅghrī karau tathā
children.translated_text: Or, while performing the bath in one's own house, after washing the feet and hands,

children.text: ācamyāyamya ca prāṇān kṛtanyāso hariṃ smaret ||
children.translated_text: having performed ācamana, restrained the breaths, and done nyāsa, he should remember <s>Hari</s>.
Then, remembering <s>Gaṇa</s> and the others, with waters mixed with tulasī,

children.text: pūrṇe pātre samastāni tīrthāny āvāhayet kṛtī ||
children.translated_text: the competent man should invoke all the tīrthas in a full vessel.
And this is the invocation mantra:

children.text: gaṅge ca yamune caiva godāvari sarasvati
children.translated_text: O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and O <s>Yamunā</s>, O <s>Godāvarī</s>, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
O <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, and <s>Kāverī</s>, be present in this water.
Or the wise man may invoke only <s>Jāhnavī</s>, who consists of all tīrthas,
into the water-vessel with her twelve names.
The twelve names are:

children.text: nalinī nandinī sītā mālinī ca mahāpagā
children.translated_text: <s>Nalinī</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Sītā</s>, <s>Mālinī</s>, and <s>Mahāpagā</s>,
she who arose from the arghya-water of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, who travels the three paths,
<s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, <s>Bhogavatī</s>, <s>Jāhnavī</s>, and <s>Tridaśeśvarī</s>.
And in the Vaiśākha-māhātmya of the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: nandinīty eva te nāma vedeṣu nalinīti ca
children.translated_text: In the Vedas your name is indeed <s>Nandinī</s>, and also <s>Nalinī</s>;

children.text: dakṣā pṛthvī ca vihagā viśvagāthā śivapriyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dakṣā</s>, <s>Pṛthvī</s>, <s>Vihagā</s>, <s>Viśvagāthā</s>, and <s>Śivapriyā</s>;
<s>Vidyādharī</s>, <s>Mahādevī</s>, and likewise <s>Lokaprasādinī</s>,
<s>Kṣemaṃkarī</s>, <s>Jāhnavī</s>, <s>Śāntā</s>, and <s>Śāntipradāyinī</s>.

children.text: athācamya guruṃ smṛtānujñāṃ prārthya ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Then, having performed ācamana, remembering the guru and asking permission as before,
he should meditate on <s>Gaṅgā</s> falling upon his head from the lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
And so it is said in the <s>Śrīnāradapañcarātra</s>:
He should remember the lotus-eyed lord, abiding in his own place, the embodiment of mantra,
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, four-armed, shining like countless suns,
holding conch, discus, mace, and lotus, clothed in yellow garments,
dark in complexion, with a tranquil face, gracious, with eyes that grant boons,
his limbs anointed with divine sandalwood, his lotus-face bearing a charming smile,
wearing blazing makara-earrings covered with many jewels,
encircled by a forest garland and worshiped by <s>Nārada</s> and others,
adorned with armlets and bracelets, radiant with a golden crown,
the god beautiful in every limb and ornamented with all ornaments.
He should meditate on a stream falling from that lotus of his feet upon his own head,
entering his body through the brahmarandhra,
and with it he should wash away all impurity that has entered the inner body.
At that very moment the mantra-practitioner becomes stainless, like crystal.

children.text: idaṃ snānāntaraṃ māntrāt sahasram adhikaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: This inner bath by mantra is remembered as more than a thousand ordinary baths.
There he should recite the statement beginning, 'Once, Nārāyaṇa,' and so forth,

children.text: snānakāle tu tannāma saṃsmarec ca mahāprabhum ||
children.translated_text: and at the time of bathing he should remember that name and the great lord.
And similarly in the <s>Kūrmapurāṇa</s>:
The waters are born from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; they are his very abode.

children.text: tasmān nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ snānakāle smared budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise man should remember the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at the time of bathing.
He may bathe even with warm water, and, if able, also with āmalakas,

children.text: tilais tailaiś ca saṃvarjya pratiṣiddhadināni tu ||
children.translated_text: but avoiding sesame, oils, and the prohibited days.
In the <s>Ṣaṭtriṃśanmata</s>:
Waters are by nature purifying, and especially so through contact with fire;

children.text: tena santaḥ praśaṃsanti snānam uṣṇena vāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: therefore the good praise bathing with warm water.
And <s>Yama</s> says:

children.text: āpaḥ svayaṃ sadā pūtā vahnitaptā viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Waters are always pure by themselves, especially when heated by fire;

children.text: tasmāt sarveṣu kāleṣu uṣṇāmbhaḥ pāvanaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: therefore warm water is remembered as purifying at all times.
And what was said by <s>Śaṅkha</s>:
For one who has bathed with water heated by fire, and likewise with water warmed by the sun,

children.text: śarīraśuddhir vijñeyā na tu snānaphalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: bodily purity should be understood; but there will not be the fruit of bathing.
That, however, concerns occasional and desire-motivated baths.

children.text: kuryān naimittikaṃ snānaṃ śītādbhiḥ kāmyam eva ca
children.translated_text: One should perform an occasional bath, and also a desire-motivated bath, with cold waters;
but a daily or incidental bath one may perform according to preference.
On that point <s>Yama</s> says:
At the birth of a son, at a solar ingress, at an eclipse of the moon or sun,
and upon touching an untouchable, one should not bathe with warm water.
<s>Vṛddhamanu</s> says:

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ tathā darśe yaḥ snāyād uṣṇavāriṇā
children.translated_text: He who bathes with warm water on the full-moon day or on the new-moon day

children.text: sa gohatyākṛtaṃ pāpaṃ prāpnotīha na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: incurs here the sin committed by killing a cow; there is no doubt.
On that point <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> says:
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is especially pleased by āmalakas on Ekādaśī;
a man desiring prosperity should always bathe with āmalakas.

children.text: saptamyāṃ na spṛśet tailaṃ nīlīvastraṃ na dhārayet
children.translated_text: On the seventh lunar day a man should not touch oil, nor wear blue clothing,

children.text: na cāpy āmalakaṃ snāyān na kuryāt kalahaṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor bathe with an āmalaka, nor engage in quarrel.
<s>Bhṛgu</s> says:

children.text: amāṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ saptamīṃ ca navamīṃ ca trayodaśīm
children.translated_text: The new-moon day, the sixth, the seventh, the ninth, and the thirteenth...
On a <s>saṅkrānti</s> day and on Sunday, one should avoid bathing with āmalaka fruits.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s>:
With dhātrī fruits, on the new-moon day and on the seventh and ninth lunar days,

children.text: yaḥ snāyāt tasya hīyante tejaś cāyurdhanaṃ sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: if one bathes, his brilliance, lifespan, wealth, and sons diminish.
There <s>Bṛhaspati</s> says:

children.text: sarvakālaṃ tilaiḥ snānaṃ punar vyāso 'bravīn muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> declared that bathing with sesame is for all times.
In the <s>Ṣaṭtriṃśanmata</s>:
Likewise on the seventh lunar day, the new-moon day, <s>saṅkrānti</s>, and eclipses,
one who desires wealth, sons, and a wife should not touch what has been touched by sesame.
In that same place:

children.text: ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tailam anāyuṣyaṃ caturthīṣv api ca parvasu ||
children.translated_text: On the sixth lunar day oil is harmful to life, and also on fourth lunar days and festival days.
The yogin <s>Yājñavalkya</s>:

children.text: daśamyāṃ tailam apṛṣṭvā yaḥ snāyād avicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: On the tenth lunar day, the undiscerning man who bathes after contact with oil

children.text: catvāri tasya naśyanti āyuḥ prajñā yaśodhanam ||
children.translated_text: loses four things: lifespan, intelligence, fame, and wealth.

children.text: mohāt pratipadaṃ ṣaṣṭhīṃ kuhūṃ riktātithiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He who, through delusion, anoints himself with oil on the first lunar day, the sixth, the <s>kuhū</s> new moon,
or likewise on a <s>riktā</s> lunar day, is deprived of four things.
On the fifteenth, fourteenth, and seventh lunar days, and at the sun's transition,
on the twelfth, seventh, and sixth lunar days, one should avoid contact with oil.
And another text says:

children.text: saptamyāṃ na spṛśet tailaṃ navamyāṃ pratipady api
children.translated_text: On the seventh lunar day one should not touch oil, nor on the ninth or the first,
nor on the eighth and fourteenth, and especially not on the new-moon day.
Moreover:

children.text: snāne vā yadi vāsnāne pakkatailaṃ na duṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Whether for bathing or not for bathing, prepared oil is not faulty.
Moreover, in the <s>Atrismṛti</s>:
If a twice-born man smeared with oil or smeared with ghee voids feces or urine,
then, after remaining fasting for a day and night, he is purified by <s>pañcagavya</s>.
Then, having removed the dirt from his limbs and bathed, he should perform the rite according to rule,
the <s>aghamarṣaṇa</s> only with a handful of water held to the nose.
Then, after performing the sprinkling as before with water from the feet of the guru and others,
the ablution should be performed with a conch, using waters mixed with tulasī.
In the <s>Gāruḍa</s>:

children.text: mārjayaty abhiṣeke tu tulasyā vaiṣṇavo naraḥ
children.translated_text: At the ablution, the Vaiṣṇava man sprinkles himself with tulasī;
his body at once becomes composed of all sacred bathing places, O twice-born one.
When bathing with water produced from tulasī leaves, especially on the eleventh lunar day,
one is freed from all sins, even if one were a killer of a Brahmin.
Having anointed himself with earth from its root, he bathes day by day;
he obtains the bathing merit of the concluding bath of ten horse-sacrifices.
Water mixed with tulasī leaves is known to be equal to the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: yo vahecchirasā nityaṃ dhṛtā bhavati jāhnavī ||
children.translated_text: he who always bears it on his head bears the <s>Jāhnavī</s> itself.
Having placed foot-water in a copper vessel together with a tulasī leaf,
and having placed it in a conch, one should pour it over one's own head with the root mantra.
And its greatness is stated in the <s>Padma</s>, in the <s>Kārttikamāhātmya</s>:
Water from a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone joined with the <s>Dvārakā</s> discus-mark,

children.text: śaṅkhe kṛtvā tu nikṣiptaṃ snānārthaṃ tāmrabhājane
children.translated_text: placed in a conch and set in a copper vessel for bathing,
when joined with a tulasī leaf, destroys the sin of Brahmin-killing.
With a cloth other than the bathing cloth, he should wipe the water from his limbs,
and then put on the two garments, the lower garment and the upper garment.
There <s>Atri</s> says:

children.text: adhautaṃ kārudhautaṃ vā paredyudhautam eva vā
children.translated_text: An unwashed garment, one washed by a craftsman, or one washed the previous day,

children.text: kāṣāyaṃ malinaṃ vastraṃ kaupīnaṃ ca parityajet ||
children.translated_text: a reddish-brown garment, a dirty garment, and a loincloth should be discarded.

children.text: na cārdram eva vasanaṃ paridadhyāt kadācana ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one ever put on a garment while it is wet.

children.text: nagno malinavastraḥ syāt nagnaś cārdhapaṭas tathā
children.translated_text: One in a soiled garment is naked; naked also is one wearing a half-cloth.

children.text: nagno dviguṇavastraḥ syān nagno raktapaṭas tathā ||
children.translated_text: One wearing a doubled cloth is naked, and so is one wearing a red cloth.

children.text: nagnaś ca syūtavastraḥ syān nagnaḥ snigdhapaṭas tathā
children.translated_text: One wearing a stitched garment is naked, and so is one wearing an oily cloth;

children.text: dvikaccho 'nuttarīyaś ca nagnaś cāvastra eva ca ||
children.translated_text: one with two tucked hems, one without an upper garment, and one without clothing are naked.

children.text: śrautaṃ smārtaṃ tathā karma na nagnaś cintayed api
children.translated_text: A naked man should not even think of a Vedic or remembered rite.

children.text: mohāt kurvann adho gacchet tad bhaved āsuraṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: If through delusion he performs it, he goes downward; that is remembered as demonic.
In recitation, oblation, and fasting, he should wear washed garments,

children.text: alaṃkṛtaḥ śucir maunī śrāddhādau ca jitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: being adorned, pure, silent, and self-controlled, and likewise at śrāddha and other rites.
<s>Gobhila</s>:

children.text: ekavastro na bhuñjīta na kuryād devanārcanam ||
children.translated_text: One wearing a single garment should not eat and should not perform worship of the gods.
In the <s>Trailokyasammohanapañcarātra</s>:

children.text: śuklavāso bhaven nityaṃ raktaṃ caiva vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: One should always wear white clothing and should avoid red.
<s>Aṅgiras</s>:
The purification of things with a thousand hairs is by wind, fire, and the rays of the sun and moon;
a woolen thing touched by semen or touched by a corpse is not defiled.
And elsewhere:

children.text: chinnaṃ vā saṃdhitaṃ dagdham āvikaṃ na praduṣyati
children.translated_text: A woolen garment, whether cut, mended, or burned, is not defiled.

children.text: āvikena tu vastreṇa mānavaḥ śrāddham ācaret
children.translated_text: A man may perform śrāddha in a woolen garment;
what is given to the ancestors is said to be inexhaustible and equal to a <s>Gayā</s> śrāddha.

children.text: na kuryāt saṃdhitaṃ vastraṃ devakarmaṇi bhūmipa
children.translated_text: O king, one should not use a mended garment in a rite for the gods;

children.text: na dagdhaṃ na ca vai chinnaṃ pārakyaṃ na tu dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: one should not wear one that is burned, nor one that is cut, nor one belonging to another.

children.text: kākaviṣṭhāsamaṃ hy uktam avidhautaṃ ca yad bhavet
children.translated_text: Whatever is unwashed is said to be like crow-dung,

children.text: rajakād āhṛtaṃ yac ca na tad vastraṃ bhavecchuci ||
children.translated_text: and what has been brought from a washerman is not a pure garment.

children.text: kīṭaspṛṣṭaṃ tu yad vastraṃ purīṣaṃ yena kāritam
children.translated_text: A garment touched by insects, one on which feces has been deposited,

children.text: mūtraṃ vā maithunaṃ vāpi tad vastraṃ parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: or urine, or sexual intercourse too: one should avoid that garment.

children.text: āvikaṃ tu sadā vastraṃ pavitraṃ rājasattama
children.translated_text: But a woolen garment is always pure, O best of kings,
and is praised in rites for ancestors, gods, and human beings.
Whether washed or unwashed, burned, mended, or brought from a washerman,
and even if smeared with semen, urine, or blood, it is nevertheless supremely pure.

children.text: agnir āvikavastraṃ ca brāhmaṇāś ca tathā kuśāḥ
children.translated_text: Fire, a woolen garment, Brahmins, and <s>kuśa</s> grasses:

children.text: caturṇāṃ na kṛto doṣo brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā ||
children.translated_text: for these four no fault was made by <s>Brahmā Parameṣṭhin</s>.
Moreover elsewhere:
He should wear two pure garments, a lower garment and an upper garment,
uncut, with good fringes, and white; seated on a seat, he should sip water.
In the <s>Bahvṛcapariśiṣṭa</s>:

children.text: yatīnām āsanaṃ śuklaṃ kūrmākāraṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: For ascetics one should make the seat white and shaped like a tortoise,

children.text: anyeṣāṃ tu catuṣpādaṃ caturasraṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: but for others one should make it four-footed and square.
A wise man should avoid a seat made of cow dung, broken, made of <s>palāśa</s> or <s>pippala</s> wood,
bound with iron, or always exposed to the sun.
In the same place:
Giving, sipping water, oblation, eating, worship of the deity,

children.text: prauḍhapādo na kurvīta svādhyāyaṃ caiva tarpaṇam ||
children.translated_text: recitation and libation: one should not perform these with the feet set up high.
A person whose feet are raised on a seat, or on the knees or shanks,

children.text: kṛtāvasakthiko yas tu prauḍhapādaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and who has made such a seat beneath him, is called one with feet set up high.
Then, with his feet placed on the ground, having sat down, sipped water, and taken darbha grass,
he should make the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> and the like with sacred <s>śrīgopīcandana</s> and other substances.
There, first, by an anointing from the lotus feet of the Lord,
with the offered remnants as grace, he should wipe all his limbs.
That was said in the <s>Brāhma</s> by the Blessed Lord:
One should always wear sandal-paste attached to the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone,
on all the limbs, for the attainment of great purity, O <s>Kamalāsana</s>.
Then a Vaiṣṇava should make, with the twelve names beginning with <s>Keśava</s>,
the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> marks on the twelve limbs according to rule.
In the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s>:
On the forehead he should meditate on <s>Keśava</s>, and then on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> on the belly;
on the chest, on <s>Mādhava</s>; on <s>Govinda</s> in the hollow of the throat.

children.text: viṣṇuṃ ca dakṣiṇe kukṣau bāhau ca madhusūdanam
children.translated_text: And on <s>Viṣṇu</s> on the right side of the belly, and on <s>Madhusūdana</s> on the arm;
on <s>Trivikrama</s> on the shoulder, and on <s>Vāmana</s> on the left side.

children.text: śrīdharaṃ vāmabāhau tu hṛṣīkeśaṃ tu kandhare
children.translated_text: On the left arm, on <s>Śrīdhara</s>; on the shoulder, on <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>;

children.text: pṛṣṭhe tu padmanābhaṃ ca kaṭyāṃ dāmodaraṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: on the back, on <s>Padmanābha</s>, and on the waist he should place <s>Dāmodara</s>.
And the water with which that is washed should be placed on the head with the name <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Moreover:

children.text: ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ lalāṭe tu sarveṣāṃ prathamaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: The <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> on the forehead is remembered as the first for everyone;
wearing it is prescribed precisely in order beginning with the forehead.
Having performed the placement in this way, according to his tradition,
he should also place the crown-mantra on the head, for the attainment of every aim.

children.text: oṃ śrīkirīṭakeyūrahāramakarakuṇḍalacakraśaṅkhagadāpadmahastapītāmbaradhara śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣaḥsthala śrībhūmisahitasvātmajyotir dīptikarāya sahasrādityatejase namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage and homage to the one who wears the beautiful crown, armlets, necklace, makara-earrings, discus, conch, mace, lotus in hand, and yellow garment; whose chest is marked with <s>Śrīvatsa</s>; who is joined with <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Bhūmi</s>; who makes his own inner light shine forth; whose splendor is that of a thousand suns.
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the statement of the Blessed Lord:
For the sake of pleasing me, or for auspiciousness, or for protection, O four-faced one,
at the time of my worship and oblation, in the evening and morning, composed in mind,
my devotee should always wear the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, which removes fear.
There also, in the statement of <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: yajño dānaṃ tapo homaḥ svādhyāyaḥ pitṛtarpaṇam
children.translated_text: Sacrifice, gift, austerity, oblation, recitation, and libation to the ancestors:

children.text: vyarthaṃ bhavati tat sarvam ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ vinā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: all that becomes fruitless when performed without the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>.
There also, in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s>:

children.text: ūrdhvapuṇḍrair vihīnas tu kiṃcit karma karoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever rite a person performs while devoid of <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> marks,

children.text: iṣṭāpūrtādikaṃ sarvaṃ niṣphalaṃ syān na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all his acts of sacrifice, public works, and the like become fruitless; there is no doubt.
If one devoid of <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> marks performs twilight rites and the like,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ rākṣasaṃ nityaṃ narakaṃ cādhigacchati ||
children.translated_text: all that is always demonic, and he goes to hell.
And also:
That lowest of men who makes a <s>tripuṇḍra</s> on the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>,

children.text: bhaṅktvā viṣṇugṛhaṃ puṇḍraṃ sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: having broken the mark that is Viṣṇu's house, surely goes to hell.
Therefore, in the <s>Padma</s>, in the statement of <s>Nārada</s>:
The body of human beings that is made without the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ naiva tat tāvat śmaśānasadṛśaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should not even be looked at; it would be like a cremation ground.
In the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ mṛdā saumyaṃ lalāṭe yasya dṛśyate
children.translated_text: He on whose forehead an <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> made with clay is seen, O gentle one,

children.text: sa cāṇḍālo 'pi śuddhātmā pūjya eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if he is a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, he is pure-souled and indeed worthy of honor; there is no doubt.
In the <s>Skanda</s>:

children.text: tiryakpuṇḍraṃ na kurvīta samprāpte maraṇe'pi ca
children.translated_text: One should not make a horizontal mark, even when death has arrived,

children.text: naivānyan nāma ca brūyāt pumān nārāyaṇād ṛte ||
children.translated_text: nor should a man utter any other name except <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
He should wear Viṣṇu's offered remnants, the remainder of incense, and an anointing,
and should make the Vaiṣṇava mark arising from <s>gopīcandana</s>.
There also, in the section on <s>Kārttika</s>:

children.text: yasyordhvapuṇḍraṃ dṛśyeta lalāṭe no narasya hi
children.translated_text: If no <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> is seen on a man's forehead,

children.text: taddarśanaṃ na kartavyaṃ dṛṣṭvā sūryaṃ nirīkṣayet ||
children.translated_text: one should not look at him; having seen him, one should look at the sun.
Elsewhere too:
For Vaiṣṇavas and Brahmins the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> is prescribed;

children.text: anyeṣāṃ tu tripuṇḍraṃ syād iti brahmavido viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: for others there should be the <s>tripuṇḍra</s>: so knowers of Brahman know.

children.text: tripuṇḍraṃ yasya viprasya ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ na dṛśyate
children.translated_text: A Brahmin on whom a <s>tripuṇḍra</s> is seen, and no <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> is seen:

children.text: taṃ spṛṣṭvāpy athavā dṛṣṭvā sacelaṃ snānam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: having touched him, or even having seen him, one should bathe with one's clothes on.
One should not make a <s>tripuṇḍra</s> on the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> of Vaiṣṇavas;
the rite of a mortal who has made a <s>tripuṇḍra</s> is not for the pleasure of <s>Hari</s>.
Therefore, in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s>:
Resembling a leaf of the <s>aśvattha</s>, and also shaped like a bamboo leaf,
and resembling a lotus bud: the three are remembered as enchanting.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the section on <s>Kārttika</s>:

children.text: ūrdhvapuṇḍro mṛdā śubhro lalāṭe yasya dṛśyate
children.translated_text: He on whose forehead a white <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> made with clay is seen,
even if he is a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, purified in soul, goes to the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ūrdhvapuṇḍre sthitā lakṣmīr ūrdhvapuṇḍre sthitaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> dwells <s>Lakṣmī</s>; in the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> dwells fame;

children.text: ūrdhvapuṇḍre sthitā muktir ūrdhvapuṇḍre sthito hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> dwells liberation; in the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> dwells <s>Hari</s>.
In the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ mudā saumyaṃ lalāṭe yasya dṛśyate
children.translated_text: He on whose forehead the auspicious <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> is seen with joy, O gentle one,

children.text: sa cāṇḍālo 'pi śuddhātmā pūjya eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if he is a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, he is pure-souled and indeed worthy of honor; there is no doubt.
There also, in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Umā</s>:
In the middle of the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, broad and very lovely,
the god of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>, is seated together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

children.text: tasmād yasya śarīre tu ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ dhṛto bhavet
children.translated_text: Therefore, on the body of one by whom the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> (vertical sectarian mark) is worn,

children.text: tasya dehaṃ bhagavato vimalaṃ mandiraṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: his body becomes the stainless and auspicious temple of the Lord.
A Brahmin who wears the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> is honored in all worlds;

children.text: vimānavaram āruhya yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: mounting an excellent aerial car, he goes to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
On seeing one who wears the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, one is released from all sins;
or, having bowed to him with devotion, one obtains the fruit of all gifts.
He who feeds at a śrāddha a Brahmin who wears the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>

children.text: ā kalpakoṭipitaras tasya tṛptā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: has his ancestors satisfied for ten million kalpas; there is no doubt.
And he who, wearing the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, performs a śrāddha, O fair-faced one,
obtains for thousands of ten-million kalpas the fruit of a śrāddha at <s>Gayā</s>.
Whatever sacrifice, gift, ascetic practice, recitation, oblation, and the like there is,
if one wearing the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> performs it, his merit is endless.
In the <s>Śrībrahmāṇḍapurāṇa</s>:
Even if impure, or without proper conduct, or committing sin in his mind,

children.text: śucir eva bhaven nityam ūrdhvapuṇḍrāṅkito naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a man marked with the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> becomes ever pure indeed.
There also, a statement of the Blessed Lord:
A mortal who wears the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, wherever he may die,
even if he is a dog-cooker, is honored in my world, stationed in an aerial car.
A mortal wearing the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> eats food in whose house,

children.text: tadā viṃśatkulaṃ tasya narakād uddharāmy ahaṃ ||
children.translated_text: then I lift up twenty generations of that man from hell.
In the <s>Śrībrahmāṇḍapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: vīkṣyādarśe jale vāpi yo vidadhyāt prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: He who, looking in a mirror or in water, carefully applies

children.text: ūrdhvapūṇḍraṃ mahābhāga sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, O greatly fortunate one, goes to the highest goal.
A measure of ten fingers is called the very best;

children.text: navāṅgulaṃ madhyamaṃ syād aṣṭāṅgulam ataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: nine fingers is middling, and eight fingers is the next below that.

children.text: etair aṅgulibhedais tu kārayen na nakhaiḥ spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: With these distinctions of fingers one should make it; one should not touch it with the nails.
In the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s>, in that same place:
The greatly fortunate exclusive devotees, devoted to the welfare of all beings,
should make a <s>puṇḍra</s> with an intervening space, in the form of <s>Hari</s>'s foot.

children.text: śyāmaṃ śāntikaraṃ proktaṃ raktaṃ vaśyakaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Dark is said to be pacifying, red to bring control,

children.text: śrīkaraṃ pītam ity āhuḥ śvetaṃ mokṣakaraṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: yellow, they say, brings prosperity, and white, auspiciously, brings liberation.

children.text: vartulaṃ tiryag acchidraṃ hrasvaṃ dīrghaṃ tataṃ tanum
children.translated_text: Round, horizontal, without a gap, short, long, spread out, thin,
crooked, misshapen, with its tip closed, broken at the root, fallen from its place,
inauspicious, rough, stuck together, and likewise not fashioned by a finger,

children.text: vigandham avasahyaṃ ca puṇḍram āhur anarthakam ||
children.translated_text: without fragrance and unsuitable: such a <s>puṇḍra</s>, they say, is useless.
Beginning at the root of the nose, one should draw with clay up to the end of the forehead;
three parts of the nose are called the root of the nose.
Starting from the middle of the eyebrows, one should form the intervening space.
In that same place:
The lowest of twice-born men who makes the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> without an intervening space

children.text: sa hi tatra sthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ śriyaṃ caiva vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: thereby removes <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Śrī</s> who stand there.

children.text: acchidram ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ tu ye kurvanti dvijādhamāḥ
children.translated_text: Those lowest of twice-born men who make the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> without an opening,

children.text: teṣāṃ lalāṭe satataṃ śunaḥ pādo na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on their forehead there is always a dog's foot; there is no doubt.
Therefore a <s>puṇḍra</s> furnished with an opening, staff-shaped and very beautiful,

children.text: viprāṇāṃ satataṃ kāryaṃ strīṇāṃ ca śubhadarśane ||
children.translated_text: should always be made by Brahmins and by women, O auspicious-looking one.
The very beautiful <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> extends from the nose up to the hair;
one should know that, provided with an opening in the middle, to be the temple of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: vāmapārśve sthito brahmā dakṣiṇe ca sadāśivaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> is stationed on the left side, and <s>Sadāśiva</s> on the right;

children.text: madhye viṣṇuṃ vijānīyāt tasmān madhyaṃ na lepayet ||
children.translated_text: one should know <s>Viṣṇu</s> to be in the middle; therefore one should not smear the middle.
In the section on offenses in worship, in the <s>Vāyupurāṇa</s>:

children.text: adhṛtvā cordhvapuṇḍraṃ ca hareḥ pūjāṃ karoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: He who performs the worship of <s>Hari</s> without wearing the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>,

children.text: tiryakpuṇḍradharo yas tu yajed devaṃ janārdanam ||
children.translated_text: and he who, wearing a horizontal <s>puṇḍra</s>, worships the god <s>Janārdana</s>,
or with an unbroken <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, with ash, with limbs marked horizontally,

children.text: adhṛtvā śaṅkhacakre ca cetyādinā doṣa uktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and without wearing the conch and discus marks, and so on: fault is declared in such matters.
And there is a śruti text of the <s>Yajurveda</s>, in the <s>Hiraṇyakeśa</s> branch:
He who bears on himself the stepping-mark of <s>Hari</s>'s foot

children.text: sa parasya priyo bhavati sa puṇyavān
children.translated_text: becomes dear to the Supreme One; he is meritorious.

children.text: madhye chidram ūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ yo dhārayati sa muktibhāg bhavati ||
children.translated_text: He who wears the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> with an opening in the middle becomes a sharer in liberation.
A smṛti text:
The ring finger is said to grant desire; the middle finger brings long life;
the thumb is said to give nourishment, and the forefinger grants liberation.
In the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>, in that same place:
On a mountaintop, on a riverbank, at the root of a bilva tree, at a reservoir,
on the bank of the ocean, at an anthill, and especially in a sacred field of <s>Hari</s>,
where the bathing water of <s>Viṣṇu</s> constantly flows,
there one should take clay for the purpose of wearing the <s>puṇḍras</s>.

children.text: śrīraṅge veṅkaṭādrau ca śrīkūrme dvārake śubhe
children.translated_text: At <s>Śrīraṅga</s>, on <s>Veṅkaṭādri</s>, at <s>Śrīkūrma</s>, in auspicious <s>Dvārakā</s>,
at <s>Prayāga</s>, on <s>Nārasiṃhādri</s>, at <s>Vārāha</s>, and in a grove of <s>Tulasī</s>,
having taken clay with devotion, together with water from <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s feet,
and having worn the <s>puṇḍras</s> on his limbs, one obtains union with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In that same place:

children.text: yat tu divyaṃ harikṣetre tasyaiva mṛdam āharet ||
children.translated_text: But whatever clay is divine in a sacred field of <s>Hari</s>, one should bring that very clay.
And it is said in the <s>Padma</s> by <s>Śrī Nārada</s>:

children.text: brahmaghno vātha goghno vā haitukaḥ sarvapāpakṛt
children.translated_text: Whether one is a slayer of a Brahmin, a killer of a cow, a rationalist, or one who commits every sin,
through contact with <s>gopīcandana</s> one becomes purified at that very moment.

children.text: gopīcandanakhaṇḍaṃ tu yo dadāti hi vaiṣṇave
children.translated_text: He who gives a piece of <s>gopīcandana</s> to a Vaiṣṇava,

children.text: kulam ekottaraṃ tena sambhavet tāritaṃ śatam ||
children.translated_text: by him a hundred and one generations may be carried across.
In the <s>Skandapurāṇa</s>:
If a person is seen with his body marked by conch and discus, bearing mañjarī on his head,

children.text: gopīcandanaliptāṅgo dṛṣṭaś cet tad aghaṃ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: his limbs smeared with <s>gopīcandana</s>, then whatever sin has been committed is destroyed.
<s>Gopī</s>-clay, <s>Tulasī</s>, a conch, and a <s>Śālagrāma</s> with its discus...

children.text: gṛhe'pi yasya pañcaite tasya pāpabhayaṃ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even in a house where these five are present, whence could there be fear of sin for its owner?
And in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, by <s>Śrī Yama</s>:

children.text: śrīkhaṇḍe kva sa āmodaḥ svarovarṇaḥ kva tādṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: Where is such fragrance in sandalwood, and where is such a beautiful color?

children.text: tat pāvitryaṃ kva vai tīrthe śrīgopīcandane yathā ||
children.translated_text: Where in a sacred ford is there indeed such purity as there is in <s>śrīgopīcandana</s>?
And it is said in the <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>, by <s>Nārada</s>:

children.text: yo mṛttikāṃ dvāravatīsamudbhavāṃ kare samādāya lalāṭapaṭṭake
children.translated_text: He who takes in his hand the clay produced at <s>Dvāravatī</s>

children.text: karoti nityaṃ tv atha cordhvapuṇḍraṃ kriyāphalaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ sadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and daily makes the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> on the strip of his forehead, the fruit of his rites is always multiplied ten million times.

children.text: kriyāvihīnaṃ yadi mantrahīnaṃ śraddhāvihīnaṃ yadi kālavarjitam
children.translated_text: Even if a rite is lacking in ritual action, lacking in mantra, lacking in faith, or devoid of the proper time,

children.text: kṛtvā lalāṭe yadi gopīcandanaṃ prāpnoti tat karmaphalaṃ sadākṣayam ||
children.translated_text: if one has placed <s>gopīcandana</s> on the forehead, he obtains that imperishable fruit of the act.

children.text: gopīcandanasambhavaṃ suruciraṃ puṇḍraṃ lalāṭe dvijo nityaṃ dhārayate yadi dvijapate rātrau divā sarvadā
children.translated_text: O lord of the twice-born, if a twice-born man always wears on his forehead, night and day, a lovely mark produced from <s>gopīcandana</s>,

children.text: yat puṇyaṃ kurujāṅgale ravigrahe mādhyāṃ prayāge tathā tat prāpnoti khagendra viṣṇusadane saṃtiṣṭhate devavat ||
children.translated_text: then, O king of birds, he obtains the merit that is gained in <s>Kurujāṅgala</s>, at an eclipse of the sun, at midday, and at <s>Prayāga</s>, and he dwells like a god in the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: yasmin gṛhe tiṣṭhati gopīcandanaṃ bhaktyā lalāṭe manujo bibharti
children.translated_text: In the house where <s>gopīcandana</s> remains, and where a man devoutly bears it on his forehead,

children.text: tasmin gṛhe tiṣṭhati sarvadā hariḥ śraddhānvitaḥ kaṃsahā vihaṅgama ||
children.translated_text: in that house <s>Hari</s> always remains, full of faith, O bird, the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>.

children.text: yo dhārayet kṛṣṇapurīsamudbhavāṃ sadā pavitrāṃ kalikilbiṣāpahām
children.translated_text: He who always bears on his forehead the clay born in the city of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, ever pure and removing the sins of the Kali age,

children.text: nityaṃ lalāṭe harimantrasaṃyutāṃ yamaṃ na paśyed yadi pāpasaṃvṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: joined with <s>Hari</s>'s mantra, does not see <s>Yama</s>, even if he is covered with sin.

children.text: yasyāntakāle khaga gopīcandanaṃ bāhvor lalāṭe hṛdi mastake ca
children.translated_text: O bird, at whose final hour <s>gopīcandana</s> is on his arms, forehead, heart, and head,

children.text: prayāti lokaṃ kamalālayaṃ prabhor gobālaghātī yadi brahmahā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: he goes to the lotus-abode, the world of the Lord, even if he has killed cows and calves, or has slain a Brahmin.

children.text: grahā na pīḍanti na rakṣasāṃ gaṇāḥ yakṣāḥ piśācoragabhūtadānavāḥ
children.translated_text: The planets do not afflict him, nor do hosts of rākṣasas, yakṣas, piśācas, serpents, bhūtas, and dānavas,

children.text: lalāṭapaṭṭe khaga gopīcandanaṃ saṃtiṣṭhate yasya hareḥ prasādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: on whose forehead-strip, O bird, <s>gopīcandana</s> rests through the grace of <s>Hari</s>.
In the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>, by <s>Śrī Gautama</s>:
O <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, cast your glance for the destruction of great sin
upon those by whom the little <s>gopīcandana</s> mark is made daily on the forehead.
And in the <s>Kāśīkhaṇḍa</s>, by <s>Śrī Yama</s>:
Messengers, listen: the forehead that is marked with <s>gopīcandana</s>,
even that man should carefully be avoided from afar, like blazing fuel.
Then, above that, with the earth from the root of glorious <s>tulasī</s>,
there the Vaiṣṇavas should make a beautiful <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>.

children.text: tanmṛdaṃ gṛhya yaiḥ puṇḍraṃ lalāṭe dhāritaṃ naraiḥ
children.translated_text: The men who have taken that earth and worn the mark on the forehead

children.text: pramāṇakaṃ kṛtaṃ tais tu mokṣāya gamanaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: have thereby made a warrant for their journey toward liberation.
And there also, in the <s>Kārttikamāhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>:
On whose forehead a mark of <s>tulasī</s>-earth is seen,

children.text: dehaṃ na spṛśati pāpaṃ kriyamāṇas tu nārada ||
children.translated_text: sin does not touch his body, even when it is being committed, O <s>Nārada</s>.
In the <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>:
He who makes a mark of <s>tulasī</s>-earth day after day,
from the mere sight of him the sin of men committed over a year departs.
Above that, an anointing with the Lord's <s>nirmālya</s> should be worn in just the same way;

children.text: tathaiva dhāryam evaṃ hi trividhaṃ tilakaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: indeed, in this manner a threefold <s>tilaka</s> is remembered.

children.text: tato nārāyaṇīṃ mudrāṃ dhārayet prītaye hareḥ
children.translated_text: Then, for the pleasure of <s>Hari</s>, one should bear the seal of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>:
the marks of fish, tortoise, and so forth, and the weapons beginning with the discus.
In a smṛti text:
Marked with conch and discus at the roots of both arms,
one should worship <s>Hari</s> daily; otherwise there is no worship.
In the <s>Ādityapurāṇa</s>:
A low Brahmin who lacks conch, discus, <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s>, and the like

children.text: gardabhaṃ tu samāropya rājā rāṣṭrāt pravāsayet ||
children.translated_text: the king should mount on a donkey and banish from the kingdom.
In the <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>, in the blessed Lord's statement:
Authority for all rites is prescribed only for the pure,
and purity should be known from the bearing of my weapons.
And in the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Padmapurāṇa</s>:
A Brahmin devoid of marks such as conch and discus, which are most dear to <s>Hari</s>,
has fallen away from all dharmas and goes to hell.
And in the śruti, in the <s>Yajuḥ-Kaṭha</s> branch:

children.text: dhṛtordhvapuṇḍraḥ kutacakradhārī viṣṇuṃ paraṃ dhyāyati yo mahātmā
children.translated_text: The great-souled man who bears the <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> and is marked with the discus meditates on supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: svareṇa mantreṇa sadā hṛdi sthitaṃ parātparaṃ yan mahato mahāntam ||
children.translated_text: who abides always in the heart through sound and mantra, the highest beyond the highest, greater than the great.
And in the <s>Atharvaṇa</s>:

children.text: ebhir vayam urukramasya cihnair aṅkitā loke subhagā bhavema
children.translated_text: Marked with these signs of <s>Urukrama</s>, may we become fortunate in the world;

children.text: tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ ye gacchanti lāñchitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who are marked go to that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Therefore also in the <s>Brahmapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇāyudhāṅkitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sammānaṃ na karoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, seeing a man marked with the weapons of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, does not show him honor,
goes to the fruitlessness of the merit acquired over twelve years.
In the <s>Skānda</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śrī Sanatkumāra</s> and <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>:
O best of Brahmins, the devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is marked with signs such as conch and discus
goes indeed to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from burning and dissolution.
There, or elsewhere:
For him whose body is always marked with the weapons of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
what can <s>Yama</s> do, even if he is joined with millions of sins?

children.text: śaṅkhoddhāre tu yat proktaṃ vasatāṃ varṣakoṭibhiḥ
children.translated_text: The fruit that is declared at <s>Śaṅkhoddhāra</s> for those dwelling there for ten million years,

children.text: tat phalaṃ likhite śaṅkhe pratyahaṃ dakṣiṇe bhuje ||
children.translated_text: that fruit comes each day when a conch is drawn on the right arm.
The fruit that comes daily at <s>Puṣkara</s> from beholding the lotus-eyed Lord,

children.text: śaṅkhopari kṛte padme tat phalaṃ samavāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: that fruit one fully obtains when a lotus is made above the conch.

children.text: vāme bhuje gadā yasya likhitā dṛśyate kalau
children.translated_text: For the man on whose left arm a mace is seen drawn in the Kali age,
<s>Gadādhara</s> grants him each day the merit of <s>Gayā</s>.
And the fruit that is declared at <s>Ānandapura</s>, near <s>Cakrasvāmin</s>,
that fruit is gained by seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> when a discus is drawn above the mace.
In the blessed Lord's statement:

children.text: yaḥ punaḥ kalikāle tu matpurīsambhavāṃ mṛdam
children.translated_text: But the man who in the age of <s>Kali</s>, taking clay produced in my city
and a mark such as the fish and tortoise, makes it on himself,
know, O best of the thirty gods, that I have entered his body.

children.text: tasya me nāntaraṃ kiṃcit kartavyaṃ śreya icchatā ||
children.translated_text: For one who desires welfare, nothing at all should be regarded as separate from me in him.
He on whose body the marks of my avatāras are seen

children.text: martyair martyo na vijñeyaḥ sa nūnaṃ māmakī tanūḥ ||
children.translated_text: should not be understood by mortals as a mere mortal; he is surely a body belonging to me.

children.text: pāpaṃ sukṛtarūpaṃ tu jāyate tasya dehinaḥ
children.translated_text: For that embodied person, even sin becomes of the nature of merit
when my weapons are inscribed on his limbs in the age of <s>Kali</s>.
He who is marked with both signs, with the fish-seal

children.text: kūrmayāpi svakaṃ tejo nikṣiptaṃ tasya vigrahe ||
children.translated_text: and also with the tortoise, has his own radiance deposited in his body.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ ca padmaṃ ca gadāṃ rathāṅgaṃ matsyaṃ ca kūrmaṃ racitaṃ svadehe
children.translated_text: The conch, the lotus, the mace, the discus, the fish, and the tortoise, fashioned on one's own body,

children.text: karoti nityaṃ sukṛtasya vṛddhiṃ pāpakṣayaṃ janmaśatārjitasya ||
children.translated_text: always produce the increase of merit and the destruction of sin accumulated over a hundred births.
There also, in the dialogue of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>:
The armor marked with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons is hard to pierce for gods and demons,
and invisible to all beings, even to enemies and rākṣasas.
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and <s>Harivallabhā</s>

children.text: nityaṃ tasya vased dehe yasya śaṅkhāṅkitā tanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: always dwell in the body of him whose body is marked with the conch.

children.text: gaṅgā gayā kurukṣetraṃ prayāgaṃ puṣkarādi ca
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Gayā</s>, <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Prayāga</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, and the rest

children.text: nityaṃ tasya sadā tiṣṭhed yasya padāṅkitaṃ vapuḥ ||
children.translated_text: always and constantly remain with him whose body is marked with the lotus.
He whose left arm bears the mark of the <s>Kaumodakī</s>, O lover of <s>Kali</s>,
there the confluence of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the ocean is to be seen every day.

children.text: savye kare gadādhastād rathāṅgaṃ tiṣṭhate yadi
children.translated_text: If the discus stands on the left hand beneath the mace,
then the three worlds, together with the moving and unmoving, are there along with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: trayo 'gnayas trayo devā viṣṇos trīṇi padāni ca
children.translated_text: The three fires, the three gods, and the three steps of <s>Viṣṇu</s>

children.text: nivasanti sadā yasya yasya dehe sudarśanam ||
children.translated_text: dwell always in the body of anyone whose body bears the <s>Sudarśana</s>.
Moreover:
He who has on his hand the <s>Nārāyaṇī</s> seal marked with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons

children.text: ūrdhvalokādhikārī ca sa jñeyas tridaśāṃ patiḥ ||
children.translated_text: is entitled to the higher worlds and should be known as lord of the thirty gods.

children.text: kṛṣṇamudrāprayuktas tu daivaṃ pitryaṃ karoti yaḥ
children.translated_text: When someone furnished with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s seal performs rites for the gods and ancestors,

children.text: nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ pratyahaṃ cākṣayaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: whether daily, occasional, or desire-motivated, each day it becomes imperishable.

children.text: pīḍayanti na tatraiva grahā ṛkṣāṇi rāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Planets, lunar mansions, and zodiacal signs do not afflict him there,
he whose hand bears a metal seal marked with the eight-syllabled mantra.
In the <s>Vārāha</s>, in the statement of <s>Sanatkumāra</s>:
Having marked his body with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons by means of <s>gopīcandana</s> clay,

children.text: prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu sa gatvā kiṃ kariṣyati ||
children.translated_text: what need will he have of going to sacred places such as <s>Prayāga</s>?
Whenever one sees a body marked with signs such as the conch,

children.text: tadā tasya jagatsvāmī tuṣṭo harati pātakam ||
children.translated_text: then the Lord of the world is pleased with him and removes his sin.

children.text: bhavate yasya dehe tu ahorātraṃ dine dine
children.translated_text: For the person on whose body, day and night, day after day,
the conch, discus, mace, and lotus are inscribed, he is <s>Acyuta</s> himself.
In the age of <s>Kali</s>, having made oneself furnished with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s weapons,
the meritorious acts one performs are equal to <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: śaṅkhādināṅkito bhaktyā śrāddhaṃ yaḥ kurute dvija
children.translated_text: O twice-born one, if a man marked with the conch and the rest performs śrāddha with devotion,

children.text: vidhihīnaṃ tu sampūrṇaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu gayāsamam ||
children.translated_text: even if deficient in rule it is complete, and for the ancestors it is equal to <s>Gayā</s>.

children.text: yathāgnir dahate kāṣṭhaṃ vāyunā prerito bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Just as fire, strongly driven by wind, burns wood,

children.text: tathā dahyanti pāpāni dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇāyudhāni vai ||
children.translated_text: so sins are burned away merely by seeing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s>:
The devotee who bears a seal marked with <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s name, joined with the eight-syllabled mantra,
and furnished with weapons such as the conch and the rest, even if made of gold or silver,

children.text: dhatte bhāgavato yas tu kalikāle viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: especially in the age of <s>Kali</s>,
is to be regarded as equal to <s>Prahlāda</s>, and not otherwise, O beloved of <s>Kali</s>.
Moreover:

children.text: śaṅkhāṅkitatanur vipro bhuṅkte yasya ca veśmani
children.translated_text: In the house of one where a Brahmin whose body is marked with the conch eats,

children.text: tadannaṃ svayam aśnāti pitṛbhiḥ saha keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> himself eats that food together with the ancestors.

children.text: kṛṣṇāyudhāṅkito yas tu śmaśāne mriyate yadi
children.translated_text: But if one marked with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons dies in a cremation ground,

children.text: prayāge yā gatiḥ proktā sā gatis tasya nārada ||
children.translated_text: the state declared for <s>Prayāga</s> is his state, O <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇāyudhaiḥ kalau nityaṃ maṇḍitaṃ yasya vigraham
children.translated_text: The person whose body in <s>Kali</s> is always adorned with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons:
the various gods beginning with <s>Vāsava</s> make their dwelling there.

children.text: yaḥ karoti hareḥ pūjāṃ kṛṣṇaśastrāṅkito naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man marked with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons who performs worship of <s>Hari</s>:
<s>Keśava</s> removes thousands of offenses for him every day.

children.text: kṛtvā kāṣṭhamayaṃ bimbaṃ kṛṣṇaśastrais tu cihnitam
children.translated_text: Having made a wooden image marked with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons,

children.text: yo hy aṅkayati cātmānaṃ tatsamo nāsti vaiṣṇavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the person who also marks himself is a Vaiṣṇava without equal.
A man marked with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s weapons is not tainted by heretics, fallen men, uninitiated outcasts,
atheists, the sins of conversation with them, or sins produced by <s>Kali</s>.
Moreover:
He whose metal seal is marked with the eight-syllabled mantra,
and furnished with the conch, lotus, and the rest, is worshiped by gods and demons.

children.text: dhṛtā nārāyaṇī mudrā prahlādena purā kṛte
children.translated_text: The <s>Nārāyaṇī</s> seal was formerly borne in the <s>Kṛta</s> age by <s>Prahlāda</s>,

children.text: vibhīṣaṇena balinā dhruveṇa ca śukena ca ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, and <s>Śuka</s>;
by <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and Brahmins headed by <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.
Having placed weapons marked with signs such as the conch on the body, O beloved of <s>Kali</s>,
they worshiped <s>Keśava</s> and obtained the great desired fruit.
Moreover:
He on whose body there is inscribed with <s>gopīcandana</s> clay
a conch, lotus, discus, or the like: <s>Hari</s> dwells in his body.
There also, in the statement of <s>Sanatkumāra</s>:
He whose body bears the <s>Nārāyaṇī</s> seal and is marked with signs such as the conch,
and a necklace made from dhātrī fruits, produced from tulasī wood,
and whose body has weapons assigned with the twelve-syllabled mantras:

children.text: āyudhāni ca viprasya matsamaḥ sa ca vaiṣṇavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that Brahmin is a Vaiṣṇava equal to me.
Moreover:

children.text: yasya nārāyaṇī mudrā dehe śaṅkhādi cihnitā
children.translated_text: He whose body bears the <s>Nārāyaṇī</s> seal, marked with the conch and the like...
For one whose whole body is marked with weapons born from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: praveśo nāsti pāpasya kavacaṃ tasya vaiṣṇavam ||
children.translated_text: sin has no entry; that is his Vaiṣṇava armor.
And elsewhere:
In the Kali age, by these Bhāgavata marks, twice-born men
become, in the mortal world, capable of cursing and blessing.
In the <s>Gautamīya</s>:

children.text: cakraṃ ca dakṣiṇe bāhau śaṅkhaṃ vāme'pi dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: One should bear the discus on the right arm, and the conch on the left, and also on the right;

children.text: gadāṃ vāme gadādhastāt punaś cakraṃ ca dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: one should bear the mace on the left, and below the mace again the discus.

children.text: śaṅkhopari tathā padmaṃ punaḥ padmaṃ ca dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: Likewise above the conch one should bear a lotus, and again a lotus on the right;

children.text: khaḍgaṃ vakṣasi cāpaṃ ca saśaraṃ śīrṣṇi dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: one should bear a sword on the chest and a bow with an arrow on the head.

children.text: iti pañcāyudhāny ādau dhārayed vaiṣṇavo janaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus at the outset a Vaiṣṇava person should bear the five weapons;

children.text: matsyaṃ ca dakṣiṇe haste kūrmaṃ vāmakare tathā ||
children.translated_text: also the fish on the right hand, and likewise the tortoise on the left hand.
And so it is said:

children.text: dakṣiṇe tu bhuje vipro vibhṛṣād vai sudarśanam
children.translated_text: On the right arm a Brahmin should indeed bear the <s>Sudarśana</s> discus;

children.text: matsyaṃ padmaṃ cāpare'tha śaṅkhaṃ padmaṃ gadās tathā ||
children.translated_text: on the other, the fish and lotus, then the conch, lotus, and maces likewise.
According to the practice of the respected members of the tradition, and according to one's preference,
one should bear the marks of the conch, discus, and so on upon all the limbs.
With devotion one should also bear the emblems of one's own chosen deity.

children.text: cakraśaṅkhau ca dhāryate saṃmiśrāv eva kaiścana ||
children.translated_text: Some people bear the discus and conch together, combined as one.
A wise man should thus bear the discus and the other marks every day with <s>śrīgopīcandana</s>;

children.text: dhārayecchayanādau tu taptāni kila tāni hi ||
children.translated_text: but at lying down and the like, those marks are said to be heated ones.
The discus should have twelve spokes, be six-cornered, joined with three circles,

children.text: cakraṃ syād dakṣiṇāvartaṃ śaṅkhaṃ ca śrīhareḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and turn to the right; the conch is remembered as belonging to <s>Śrīhari</s>.
The mace, lotus, and the rest are regarded by the wise as established in common usage.
Or there may be a seal marked with the Lord's name, or with the eight-syllabled mantra and the like.
Then one should wear a garland offered to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, made with tulasī leaves,

children.text: padmākṣais tulasīkāṣṭhaiḥ phalair dhātryāś ca nirmitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and made of lotus seeds, tulasī wood, and fruits of the dhātrī tree.
A Vaiṣṇava should also wear ornaments of tulasī wood

children.text: mastake karṇayor bāhvoḥ karayoś ca yathāruci ||
children.translated_text: on the head, ears, arms, and hands, according to preference.
In the <s>Skanda</s>:
Having first offered to <s>Hari</s> a garland produced from tulasī wood,

children.text: mālāṃ paścāt svayaṃ dhatte sa vai bhāgavatottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he afterward puts it on himself; he is the highest Bhāgavata.
But the fool who does not offer to <s>Hari</s> a garland produced from tulasī wood

children.text: mālāṃ dhatte svayaṃ mūḍhaḥ sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: and puts it on himself goes surely to hell.
Washed with pañcagavya and consecrated with the root mantra,

children.text: gāyatryā cāṣṭa kṛtvā vai mantritāṃ dhūpayec ca tām
children.translated_text: and consecrated eight times with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he should fumigate it,
and worship it according to rule, with supreme devotion, by the <s>Sadyojāta</s> mantra.
O garland born from tulasī wood, dear to the people of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: bibharmi tvām ahaṃ kaṇṭhe kuru māṃ kṛṣṇavallabham ||
children.translated_text: I wear you on my neck; make me beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: yathā tvaṃ vallabhā viṣṇor nityaṃ viṣṇujanapriyā
children.translated_text: As you are dear to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, always dear to the people of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: tathā māṃ kuru deveśi nityaṃ viṣṇujanapriyam ||
children.translated_text: so, O goddess, make me always dear to the people of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: dāne lādhātur uddiṣṭo lāsi māṃ harivallabhe
children.translated_text: The root lā is specified in the sense of giving; O beloved of <s>Hari</s>, you give me,

children.text: bhaktebhyaś ca samastebhyas tena mālā nigadyase ||
children.translated_text: and all the devotees; therefore you are called a mālā.
Having prayed in this way, according to rule, for the garland offered at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s neck,

children.text: dhārayed vaiṣṇavo yo vai sa gacched vaiṣṇavaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: the Vaiṣṇava who wears it indeed goes to the Vaiṣṇava abode.
There also, in the section on <s>Kārttika</s>:

children.text: dhātrīphalakṛtāṃ mālāṃ kaṇṭhasthāṃ yo vahen na hi
children.translated_text: He who does not wear at his neck a garland made from dhātrī fruits

children.text: vaiṣṇavo na sa vijñeyo viṣṇupūjārato yadi ||
children.translated_text: should not be known as a Vaiṣṇava, even if he is devoted to the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Gāruḍa</s>:

children.text: dhārayanti na ye mālāṃ haitukāḥ pāpabuddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those argumentative men of sinful mind who do not wear a garland

children.text: narakān na nivartante dagdhāḥ kopāgninā hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: do not turn back from hell, burned by the fire of <s>Hari</s>'s anger.
Therefore, in the <s>Skanda</s>:
One should not abandon the tulasī garland, especially the dhātrī garland,
which destroys great sins and grants <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
In the <s>Agastyasaṃhitā</s>:
Whoever worships <s>Hari</s> while wearing a tulasī garland that is an offered remnant,

children.text: yad yat karoti tat sarvam anantaphaladaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: whatever he does, all of that becomes productive of endless fruit.
In the <s>Nāradīya</s>:

children.text: ye kaṇṭhalagnatulasīnalinākṣamālā ye vā lalāṭaphalke lasadūrdhvapuṇḍrāḥ
children.translated_text: Those whose necks bear garlands of tulasī and lotus seeds, whose forehead-plates shine with <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> marks,

children.text: ye bāhumūlaparicihnitaśaṅkhacakrās te vaiṣṇavā bhuvanam āśu pavitrayanti ||
children.translated_text: and whose upper arms are marked with conch and discus: those Vaiṣṇavas quickly purify the world.
Furthermore:

children.text: bhujayugam api cihnair aṅkitaṃ yasya viṣṇoḥ paramapuruṣanāmnāṃ kīrtanaṃ yasya vāci
children.translated_text: He whose pair of arms is marked with the signs of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose speech has the chanting of the names of the Supreme Person,

children.text: ṛjutaram api puṇḍraṃ mastake yasya kaṇṭhe sarasijamaṇimālā yasya tasyāsmi dāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose head bears a very straight <s>puṇḍra</s>, and whose neck has a lotus-seed garland: I am his servant.
In the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>, in the statement of the Blessed Lord:

children.text: tulasīkāṣṭhamālāṃ ca kaṇṭhasthāṃ vahate tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever wears a tulasī-wood garland at his neck,

children.text: apy aśauco 'py anācāro mām evaiti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if impure, even if without proper conduct, comes to me alone; there is no doubt.
In the <s>Skanda</s>:
A garland made from dhātrī fruit or produced from tulasī wood,

children.text: dṛśyate yasya dehe tu sa vai bhāgavatottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: on whose body it is seen: he is the highest Bhāgavata.

children.text: tulasīdalajāṃ mālāṃ kaṇṭhasthāṃ vahate tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever wears at his neck a garland made from tulasī leaves,
especially one offered to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is worthy of homage by the gods.
A garland made from tulasī leaves, and also one made from dhātrī fruit,

children.text: dadāti pāpināṃ muktiṃ kiṃ punar viṣṇusevinām ||
children.translated_text: gives liberation to sinners; how much more, then, to servants of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
There also, in the section on <s>Kārttika</s>:

children.text: yaḥ punas tulasīmālāṃ kṛtvā kaṇṭhe janārdanam
children.translated_text: Whoever, having made a tulasī garland and put it on his neck, worships <s>Janārdana</s>,
obtains merit equal to ten thousand cows for each flower.

children.text: yāval luṭhati kaṇṭhasthā dhātrīmālā narasya hi
children.translated_text: As long as a dhātrī garland rests upon a man's neck,

children.text: tāvat tasya śarīre tu prītyā luṭhati keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so long does <s>Keśava</s> lovingly abide in his body.

children.text: spṛśec ca yāni lomāni dhātrīmālā kalau nṛṇām
children.translated_text: Whatever hairs of men in the Kali age the dhātrī garland touches,
for that many thousands of years he dwells in <s>Keśava</s>'s abode.

children.text: yāvad dināni vahate dhātrīmālāṃ kalau naraḥ
children.translated_text: For as many days as a man in the Kali age wears a dhātrī garland...
For that many thousands of yugas, there would be residence in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.
But the person who wears a pair of garlands produced from <s>dhātrī</s> and <s>tulasī</s>

children.text: vahate kaṇṭhadeśe tu kalpakoṭiṃ divaṃ vaset ||
children.translated_text: and wears them at the region of the neck dwells in heaven for ten million kalpas.
And in the <s>Garuḍa</s>, in the statement of <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>:

children.text: tulasīdalajāṃ mālāṃ kṛṣṇottīrṇā vahet tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever wears a garland made from <s>tulasī</s> leaves and offered to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
on each leaf he obtains the fruit of ten horse sacrifices.
The man who wears a garland produced from <s>tulasī</s> wood,
to him the foe of the demons grants each day the merit arising at <s>Dvārakā</s>.
Having offered to <s>Viṣṇu</s> a garland produced from <s>tulasī</s> wood,

children.text: vahate yo naro bhaktyā tasya vai nāsti pātakam ||
children.translated_text: the man who wears it with devotion has no sin at all.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, son of <s>Devakī</s>, is always pleased in mind with him.
The man who wears a garland produced from <s>tulasī</s> wood

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ na tasyāsti nāśaucaṃ tasya vigrahe ||
children.translated_text: has no need of expiation, and there is no impurity in his body.
For the mortal whose adornment on the head is produced from <s>tulasī</s> wood,

children.text: bāhvoḥ kare ca martyasya dehe tasya sadā hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: and on whose arms and hands it is worn, <s>Hari</s> is always in that body.
If, adorned with garlands of <s>tulasī</s> wood, he performs a meritorious act,

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca kṛtaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ kalau ||
children.translated_text: what is done for the ancestors and for the deities becomes ten-million-fold in the Kali age.
When the messengers of the king of the dead see a garland of <s>tulasī</s> wood,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā naśyanti dūreṇa vātoddhūtaṃ yathā dalam ||
children.translated_text: they perish from afar like a leaf blown away by the wind.
If one wanders adorned with garlands of <s>tulasī</s> wood,

children.text: duḥsvapnaṃ durnimittaṃ ca na bhayaṃ śastrajaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: there is no bad dream, no evil omen, and nowhere any fear born from weapons.
Then he should perform the rite of sandhyā worship and the other duties according to rule,
and there the offering to the gods and others is made only with water from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s feet.
With <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s nirmālya (offering-remnant) on the head and also with his foot-water, the offering

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca vaiṣṇavais tu samaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: to the ancestors and the deities is considered by Vaiṣṇavas to be the same.
And regarding sandhyā worship, the statement of <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: gṛhe tv ekaguṇā sandhyā goṣṭhe daśaguṇā smṛtā
children.translated_text: At home sandhyā is onefold; in a cowshed it is remembered as tenfold;
