at a river it is a hundred-thousandfold, and in the presence of <s>Viṣṇu</s> it is infinite.

children.text: pūjayiṣyaṃs tataḥ kṛṣṇam ādau saṃnihitaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: Then, intending to worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he should first bow to the guru who is present nearby

children.text: praṇamya pūjayed bhaktyā dattvā kiṃcid upāyanam ||
children.translated_text: and worship him with devotion, giving some offering.
In the <s>Smṛtimahārṇava</s>:

children.text: riktapāṇir na paśyeta rājānaṃ bhiṣajaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: One should not see a king, a physician, or a guru empty-handed;
nor, without making an offering, should one look upon a son, a pupil, or a servant.
Moreover, in the statement of the blessed Lord:

children.text: prathamaṃ tu guruṃ pūjya tataś caiva mamārcanam
children.translated_text: First worshipping the guru, and only then worshipping me,

children.text: kurvan siddhim avāpnoti hy anyathā niṣphalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one who acts obtains success; otherwise it becomes fruitless.
And by <s>Śrī Nārada</s>:

children.text: gurau saṃnihite yas tu pūjayed anyam agrataḥ
children.translated_text: If, when the guru is present, someone worships another before him,

children.text: sa durgatim avāpnoti pūjanaṃ tasya niṣphalam ||
children.translated_text: he obtains a bad destiny, and his worship is fruitless.
In the śrutis:

children.text: yasya deve parā bhaktiḥ yathā deve tathā gurau
children.translated_text: For one who has supreme devotion to the deity, and to the guru just as to the deity,

children.text: tasyaite kathitā hy arthāḥ prakāśante mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these meanings that have been taught become manifest for that great-souled one.
In the Eleventh Book, in the statement of the blessed Lord:
One should know the ācārya to be me; one should never despise him,
nor should one envy him with the thought that he is mortal, for the guru consists of all the gods.
And in the Tenth Book:
I, the self of all beings, am not satisfied by sacrifice, progeny,
austerity, or tranquility as I am by service to the guru.
In the Seventh Book:
For one whose intellect regards the guru, who is directly the blessed Lord and giver of the lamp of knowledge,
as an unreal mortal, all that he has heard is like an elephant's bath.
Elsewhere also:
The deities diminish the practitioner's devotion toward the guru,

children.text: yan no 'tītya vrajed viṣṇuṃ śiṣyo bhaktyā gurau dhruvan ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'May the disciple, passing beyond us, not go to <s>Viṣṇu</s> through firm devotion to the guru.'
In the <s>Manusmṛti</s>:

children.text: ajño bhavati vai bālaḥ pitā bhavati mantradaḥ
children.translated_text: One who is ignorant is indeed a child; the giver of the mantra becomes the father.

children.text: ajñaṃ hi bālam ity āhuḥ pitety eva tu mantradam ||
children.translated_text: They call the ignorant person a child, but the giver of the mantra alone is called father.
Moreover:

children.text: gurur brahmā gurur viṣṇur gurur devo maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The guru is <s>Brahmā</s>; the guru is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the guru is the god <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: gurur eva paraṃ brahma tasmāt sampūjayet sadā ||
children.translated_text: The guru alone is the supreme brahman; therefore one should always worship him fully.
In the <s>Vāmanakalpa</s>:

children.text: yo mantraḥ sa guruḥ sākṣāt yo guruḥ sa hariḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The mantra itself is directly the guru; the guru is remembered as <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: gurur yasya bhavet tuṣṭas tasya tuṣṭo hariḥ svayam
children.translated_text: For one whose guru is pleased, <s>Hari</s> himself is pleased.

children.text: guroḥ samāsane naiva na caivoccāsane vaset ||
children.translated_text: One should not sit on the same seat as the guru, nor on a higher seat.
In the <s>Viṣṇurahasya</s>:
Therefore, with every effort and according to rule,

children.text: abhedenārcayet yas tu sa muktiphalam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: whoever worships the guru without difference obtains the fruit of liberation.
In the <s>Viṣṇudharma</s> and the <s>Śrībhāgavata</s>, the statement of <s>Hariścandra</s>:
What is called service to the guru is the very highest of all dharmas.

children.text: tasmād dharmāt paro dharmaḥ pavitraṃ naiva vidyate ||
children.translated_text: No dharma higher than that dharma, and no purity greater than it, is found.
Whatever is the cause of one's own harm, such as desire and anger,

children.text: etat sarvaṃ gurau bhaktyā puruṣo hy añjasā jayet ||
children.translated_text: all this a person easily conquers through devotion to the guru.
In the <s>Padma</s>:
Those who always worship the guru with the sense that he is superior to the father

children.text: bhavanty atithayo loke brahmaṇas te viśāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: become guests of <s>Brahmā</s> in the world, O best of people.
There itself, in <s>Devahūti</s>'s praise:

children.text: bhaktir yathā harau me'sti tadvan niṣṭhā gurau yadi
children.translated_text: If there is steadfastness toward the guru in me just as there is devotion to <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: mamāsti tena satyena svaṃ darśayatu me hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, by that truth, let <s>Hari</s> show me his own form.
In the <s>Ādityapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: avidyo vā savidyo vā gurur eva janārdanaḥ
children.translated_text: Whether ignorant or learned, the guru is <s>Janārdana</s> himself;

children.text: mārgastho vāpy amārgastho gurur eva sadā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether standing on the path or off the path, the guru alone is always the refuge.
And elsewhere:

children.text: harau ruṣṭe gurus trātā gurau ruṣṭe na kaścana
children.translated_text: If <s>Hari</s> is angry, the guru is the protector; if the guru is angry, there is no one at all.
Therefore, with every effort, one should propitiate the guru alone.
In the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>:

children.text: api ghnantaḥ śapanto vā viruddhā api ye kruddhāḥ
children.translated_text: Even if they strike, curse, oppose, or are angry,

children.text: guravaḥ pūjanīyās te gṛhaṃ natvā nayeta tān ||
children.translated_text: those gurus are to be worshipped; one should bow to them and bring them to one's house.

children.text: tat ślāghyaṃ janma dhanyaṃ tat dinaṃ puṇyātha nāḍikā
children.translated_text: That birth is praiseworthy, that day is blessed, and that nāḍikā is holy

children.text: yasyāṃ guruṃ praṇamate samupāsya tu bhaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in which, after duly attending upon the guru, one bows to him with devotion.
Those who reject the teacher who has come down in the sacred tradition,

children.text: tān mṛtān api kravyādāḥ kṛtaghnān nopabhuñjate ||
children.translated_text: those ungrateful men even carrion-eaters do not consume after they are dead.
Knowledge has been defiled by him, and wickedness has been made manifest:

children.text: gurur yena parityaktas tena tyaktaḥ purā hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: the man by whom the guru has been abandoned has already abandoned <s>Hari</s>.
And elsewhere:

children.text: pratipadya guruṃ yas tu mohād vipratipadyate
children.translated_text: But he who accepts a guru and then, through delusion, turns against him,
that lowest of men is cooked in hell for ten million aeons.
In the <s>Pañcarātra</s>:
With a mantra taught by a non-Vaiṣṇava one would go to hell;

children.text: punaś ca vidhinā samyag grāhayed vaiṣṇavād guroḥ ||
children.translated_text: and again one should have it properly received, according to rule, from a Vaiṣṇava guru.
In the <s>Agastyasaṃhitā</s>:

children.text: ye gurvājñāṃ na kurvanti pāpiṣṭhāḥ puruṣādhamāḥ
children.translated_text: Those most sinful and lowest men who do not carry out the guru's command,
for them there is no deliverance from the torments of hell, O best of sages.

children.text: yaiḥ śiṣyaiḥ śaśvad ārādhyā guravo hy avamānitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those disciples by whom gurus, who should always be worshiped, are dishonored
fall away from prosperity in sons, friends, wives, and the like.

children.text: adhikṣipya guruṃ mohāt paruṣaṃ pravadanti ye
children.translated_text: Those who, through delusion, abuse the guru and speak harshly to him

children.text: śūkaratvaṃ bhavaty eva teṣāṃ janmaśateṣv api ||
children.translated_text: are indeed born as pigs even through hundreds of births.
Those foolish betrayers of the guru, always doers of evil,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yāvat sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ syān na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for them whatever merit exists becomes demerit; there is no doubt.

children.text: ataḥ prāg gurum abhyarcya kṛṣṇabhāvena buddhimān
children.translated_text: Therefore, first worshiping the guru with the understanding that he is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the wise man
should make not fewer than three prostrations, falling like a staff.
For this very reason, in the <s>Kaurma</s>, in the <s>Śrī-Vyāsagītā</s>:
The respectful grasping of the guru's feet should be done with the hands crossed;

children.text: savyena savyaḥ spraṣṭavyo dakṣiṇena tu dakṣiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the left foot should be touched with the left hand, and the right with the right.
Then, having obtained permission from the feet of the revered guru, the practitioner,

children.text: prāk saṃskṛtaṃ harer gehaṃ pravekṣyan pāduke tyajet ||
children.translated_text: when about to enter the previously consecrated house of <s>Hari</s>, should remove his sandals.
And so in <s>Āpastamba</s>:
In a fire-room, in a cowshed, in the presence of gods and Brahmins,
during recitation and at the time of eating, one should put aside sandals.
Then, having gone into the courtyard of the temple for worshiping the blessed Lord,

children.text: prakṣālya hastau pādau ca dvirācamanam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: he should wash his hands and feet and perform ācamana twice.
And so in the <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>:
Acts such as worship of the deity, and likewise salutation of the guru,

children.text: kurvīta samyag ācamya tadvad eva bhujikriyām ||
children.translated_text: one should perform after properly doing ācamana, and the act of eating in the same way.

children.text: iti śrīgopālabhaṭṭavilikhite śrībhagavadbhaktivilāse śrīvaiṣṇavālaṅkāro nāma caturtho vilāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth vilāsa, named <s>Śrīvaiṣṇavālaṅkāra</s>, in the <s>Śrībhagavadbhaktivilāsa</s> written by <s>Śrī Gopālabhaṭṭa</s>.
I praise <s>Śrī Caitanya Prabhu</s>, by whose grace even a child
may cross the ocean of worship-procedure, pervaded by the graspers that are many doctrines.
<s>Sanātana</s>:
Obeisance to <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>.
"Child" means ignorant;
alternatively, it means an actual child.
The various kinds of doctrines themselves are the graspers; it is pervaded by them.
The sequence of worship is its order, its rule,
or else the ordered sequence of rules; that itself is the ocean, and he crosses it.
From the eighteen-syllabled yantra of venerable <s>Gopāladeva</s>,
the hidden rite of worship is being written, as seen in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>.
<s>Sanātana</s>:
The rite of worship, that is, the manner of pūjā, with the eighteen-syllabled mantra is being written.

children.text: yadyapi daśākṣarādināpi pūjāvidhau bhedo nāsti tathāpi nyāsādibhedāpekṣayā tathā likhitam
children.translated_text: Although there is no difference in the rite of worship even with the ten-syllabled and other mantras, nevertheless it has been written in that way with regard to differences such as nyāsa.

children.text: gūḍho 'pi kramadīpikayā śrīkeśavācāryaviracitayā īkṣitaḥ darśitaḥ san
children.translated_text: Though hidden, it has been seen, that is, shown, by the <s>Kramadīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Keśavācārya</s>.
Therefore the sense is that it is to be written according to what is stated in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>.
By the path taught in the āgama, the blessed Lord is always to be worshiped even by Brahmins;

children.text: sadaiva pūjyo 'to lekhyaḥ prāya āgamiko vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the mainly āgamic procedure is to be written.
And so in the <s>Viṣṇuyāmala</s>:
In the <s>Kṛta</s> age the path is that taught by śruti; in <s>Tretā</s>, it is shaped by smṛti;
in <s>Dvāpara</s>, it is taught by the purāṇas; in <s>Kali</s>, it arises from āgama.
Brahmins born in <s>Kali</s> are impure, indeed almost like Śūdras;
for them purification comes by the āgamic path, not by the Vedic way.
<s>Sanātana</s>:

children.text: teṣām āgamamārgeṇa śrautavartmanety anena tair api āgamikavidhinaiva pūjā kāryeti bhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: By the words "for them, by the āgamic path, not by the Vedic way," the sense is that pūjā is to be performed by them too only according to the āgamic rule.

children.text: tathā caikādaśaskandhe nānātantravidhānena kalāv api tathā śṛṇu iti
children.translated_text: And so in the Eleventh Book: "Hear how, even in the <s>Kali</s> age, it is likewise by the prescriptions of many tantras."
There the venerable <s>Śrīdhara Svāmin</s> says:

children.text: nānātantravidhāneneti kalau tantramārgasya prādhānyaṃ darśayati iti
children.translated_text: By the phrase "by the prescriptions of many tantras," he shows the predominance of the tantric path in the <s>Kali</s> age.
Having then given pādya and the other offerings to the doorway deities of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>,
one should worship them with fragrant paste and flowers, each in its proper place and proper order.
<s>Sanātana</s>:

children.text: tān śrīkṛṣṇadvāradevān praṇavādicaturthyantaṃ devanāma namo'ntakam ity agre lekhyatvād atraivaṃ prayogaḥ śrīkṛṣṇadvāradevatābhyo namaḥ
children.translated_text: Those doorway deities of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>: since later it will be written that the deity's name is to end in the dative case, be preceded by praṇava and the rest, and end with namaḥ, the application here is, "Obeisance to the doorway deities of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>."

children.text: anena mantreṇa pādyārghyādikaṃ dattvā gandhādibhiḥ punar viśeṣeṇa pūjayed ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is that, after giving pādya, arghya, and the rest with this mantra, one should again worship them especially with fragrant substances and so on.

children.text: evam agre'pi saparivārebhyaḥ śrīkṛṣṇapārṣadebhyo namaḥ ityādi prayogo draṣṭavyaḥ
children.translated_text: In the same way, later applications such as "Obeisance to the attendants of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> together with their retinues" should be understood.
In front of the doorway, on the ground-platform, one should worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s attendants together with their retinues;
in front of them, <s>Garuḍa</s>, and above the doorway, <s>Dvāraśrī</s>.
On both sides of the eastern doorway one should worship <s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>;

children.text: dvāre ca dakṣiṇe dhātṛvidhātārau ca paścime ||
children.translated_text: at the southern doorway, <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, and at the western one,

children.text: jayaṃ ca vijayaṃ caiva balaṃ prabalam uttare
children.translated_text: <s>Jaya</s> and <s>Vijaya</s>; and <s>Bala</s> and <s>Prabala</s> at the northern one.
Having thus worshiped them in pairs, he should worship <s>Vāstupuruṣa</s> on the threshold.
<s>Sanātana</s>:

children.text: evaṃ sāmānyena sarveṣām eva pūjāvidhir likhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the general worship-procedure for all of them has been written.

children.text: idānīṃ yathāsthānaṃ yathākramam iti yal likhitaṃ tad eva vivicya likhati dvārāgra iti dvārābhyām
children.translated_text: Now, as for what was written, "in the proper place and in the proper order," he writes it after distinguishing just that: "at the front of the door" means at the two doorways.

children.text: tatrāpy ādau dvārasyāgre yat bhūrūpaṃ pīṭhaṃ tatra samastaparivārānvitān śrīkṛṣṇapārṣadān yajet pūjayet
children.translated_text: There also, first, on the platform in the form of ground that is in front of the door, one should worship, that is, honor, the attendants of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> together with all their retinues.
After that, in front of that door, one should worship <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: yadyapi dvāraśriyo 'rcanaṃ prabalārcanānantaram eva kramadīpikāyām uktam tathāpi iṣṭveti kṭvāpratyayena caṇḍādipūjātaḥ pūrvakāla eveti bodhitam
children.translated_text: Although the worship of <s>Dvāraśrī</s> is stated in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s> only immediately after the worship of <s>Prabala</s>, nevertheless by the gerund in "having worshipped" it is indicated as taking place before the worship of <s>Caṇḍa</s> and the others.
And the same is known from established practice.

children.text: kiṃca dvandva ity agre likhanāt caṇḍapracaṇḍābhyāṃ namaḥ ity evaṃ yugmatvena prayogo jñeyaḥ
children.translated_text: Moreover, because he writes below "as a pair," the usage should be understood in paired form, thus: "obeisance to <s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>."
Then, on the inner sides of the doorway, he should worship <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.
On their sides he should likewise worship <s>Śaṅkhanidhi</s> and <s>Padmanidhi</s>.
<s>Sanātana</s>:

children.text: dvārasyāntaḥ abhyantare tatpārśvadvaye tayor gaṅgāyamunayoḥ pārśvadvaye
children.translated_text: "Inside the door" means within it; "on their two sides" means on the two sides of those two, <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.
He should worship <s>Gaṇeśa</s> in the fire-corner of the temple and <s>Durgā</s> in the southwest,
<s>Vāṇī</s> in the northwest, and likewise <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> in the northeast.
<s>Sanātana</s>:
In the southeastern corner he should worship <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
And so it is said in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>:
When all the retinues have been completed, then again the attendants of <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>
are to be worshipped on the bali-platform before the door, and the lord of birds before that.
<s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> are in the east, and <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> in the south;

children.text: jayaḥ savijayaḥ paścād balaḥ prabala uttare
children.translated_text: <s>Jaya</s> with <s>Vijaya</s> are in the west, and <s>Bala</s> and <s>Prabala</s> in the north.

children.text: ūrdhve dvāraśriyaṃ ceṣṭvā dvāry etān yugmaśo 'rcayet
children.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Dvāraśrī</s> above, one should worship these at the door in pairs.
There the <s>Vāstupumān</s> is to be worshipped in the middle of the doorway platform.

children.text: dvārāntaḥpārśvayor arcyā gaṅgā ca yamunā nadī
children.translated_text: On the inner sides of the doorway, the rivers <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s> are to be worshipped.

children.text: koṇeṣu vighnaṃ durgāṃ ca vāṇīṃ kṣetre samarcayet
children.translated_text: In the corners one should worship <s>Vighna</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s>, and <s>Kṣetra</s>.
Taking support from the left door-jamb, contracting his limbs, and without touching the threshold,

children.text: aspṛṣṭvā praviśed veśma nyasyan prāg dakṣiṇaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: he should enter the house, placing his right foot first.
<s>Sanātana</s>:

children.text: vāmāṃ svavāmabhāgavartinīṃ dvāraśākhāṃ āśrayan īṣat spṛṣad nijāṅgāni saṃkocya dehalīm aspṛṣṭvā na laṅghayitvety arthaḥ
children.translated_text: "The left" means the door-jamb situated on his own left side; taking support from it means touching it slightly. Having contracted his own limbs, he should not touch the threshold, that is, should not step upon it.
"Placing the right foot first" means setting down the right foot at the beginning.
The meaning is: according to the procedure of setting down the right foot.

children.text: veśma śrībhagavanmandiraṃ harer gehaṃ pravekṣyann iti pūrvalikhanāt
children.translated_text: "The house" means the temple of the blessed Lord, the house of <s>Hari</s>, since it was previously written, "intending to enter."
He should enter: the worshipper should go slowly into its midst.
And similarly, in the <s>Śāradātilaka</s>, there is something on this point:
The guru, touching the left jamb and stepping over the threshold,
should enter inside with his right foot, contracting his body.
<s>Sanātana</s>:
"Guru" means the one mentioned in the prescription for initiation.
And its greatness is stated in the <s>Haribhaktisudhodayā</s>:
The wise man, full of devotion, who enters <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s shrine for the sake of worship

children.text: na bhūyaḥ praviśan mātuḥ kukṣikārāgṛhaṃ sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: does not again enter the prison of his mother's womb.
In the southwest one should worship <s>Vāstupuruṣa</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> as well.

children.text: āsanastho yajet tāṃs tān anyatra bhagavadgṛhāt ||
children.translated_text: Seated on the seat, he should worship each of those, except when in the house of the blessed Lord.
And the mantra for their worship is stated:
Beginning with the praṇava, ending in the dative form of the deity's name, and ending with "namaḥ":
this is declared to be the worship-mantra in every act of worship.

children.text: atha kṛṣṇāgratas tiṣṭhan kṛtvā digbandhanaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Then, standing before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, after making the binding of the quarters, he should throw
flowers and unbroken rice in all the directions, with the mantra stated there.
Then, consecrating and worshipping the seat with the seat-mantra,
he should sit on it in the lotus posture or in the svastika posture.

children.text: tatra kṛṣṇārcakaḥ prāyo divase prāṅmukho bhavet
children.translated_text: There the worshipper of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> should generally face east by day,

children.text: udaṅmukho rajanyāṃ tu sthiramūrtiś ca sammukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but at night face north; and in the case of a fixed image, he should face it directly.
And on this point, in the Eleventh Book:

children.text: āsīnaḥ prāg udagvārcet sthirāyāṃ tv atha sammukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seated, he should worship facing east or north; but when the image is fixed, he should face it.
For the seat-mantra, <s>Merupṛṣṭha</s> is the seer and <s>Sutala</s> is the metre.
<s>Kūrma</s> is the deity; the application is for consecrating the seat.

children.text: pṛthvi tvayā dhṛtā lokā devi tvaṃ viṣṇunā dhṛtā
children.translated_text: O goddess <s>Pṛthivī</s>, the worlds are held by you, and you are held by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ ca dhāraya māṃ nityaṃ pavitraṃ kuru cāsanam ||
children.translated_text: You too should always support me, and make the seat pure.
In the <s>Nāradapañcarātra</s>:
The learned man should avoid a seat made of bamboo, stone, wood, earth, grass, or leaves,
for it gives poverty, disease, and sorrow.

children.text: kṛṣṇājinaṃ kambalaṃ vā nānyad āsanam iṣyate ||
children.translated_text: A black-antelope skin or a blanket is approved as a seat, and no other.
And elsewhere:
He should prepare as a soft seat a black-antelope skin, tiger skin, silk, something made of cane,

children.text: vastrājinaṃ kambalaṃ vā kalpayed āsanaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: cloth, a skin, or a blanket.
In the <s>Nāradapañcarātra</s>:
From bamboo they say there is poverty; on stone, the arising of disease;
on the ground, the arising of sorrow; on a wooden seat, misfortune.
On a grass seat there is loss of fame; on leaves, disturbance of the mind.
On a darbha seat there is destruction of disease; a blanket brings release from sorrow.
Moreover, in the revered <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>:

children.text: śucau deśe pratiṣṭhāpya sthiram āsanam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Having established for oneself a firm seat in a pure place,
not too high and not too low, covered with cloth, skin, and kuśa grass,
then, sitting as prescribed and according to the tradition,
one should place the worship materials, such as the conch and the rest, in their respective places.

children.text: svasya vāmāgrataḥ śaṅkhaṃ sādhāraṃ sthāpayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should place the conch, together with its stand, in front of himself on the left,
and should also set down there the vessels for arghya and the rest, separately at the door.
The vessels for tulasī, sandal paste, flowers, and the like should be on the right,

children.text: vāme ca sthāpayet pārśve kalasaṃ pūrṇam ambhasā ||
children.translated_text: and on the left side he should place a water-pot filled with water.

children.text: dakṣiṇe ghṛtadīpaṃ ca tailadīpaṃ ca vāmataḥ
children.translated_text: He should place a ghee lamp on the right and an oil lamp on the left,
and set the other requisites in a place within the range of his own sight.
For washing the hands, he should also place one vessel behind himself.
In the <s>Devīpurāṇa</s>:
One should arrange vessels of many varied forms, and also ones shaped like lotuses,
and vessels having the appearance of conches and blue lotuses.
They may be fashioned of jewels and other materials, and furnished with golden bases;
one should have the vessels made according to beauty and according to what is available.
Moreover:
With a haṃsa-vessel one obtains all desired things, O sage.

children.text: arghyaṃ dattvā tathā raupyeṇāyurājyaṃ śubhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Having offered <s>arghya</s> in a silver vessel, long life and royal fortune become auspicious.
With a copper vessel there is good fortune; from an earthen one, <s>dharma</s> (religious merit) arises.
In the <s>Vārāha</s>:

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ kāṃsyaṃ yena dīyate bhājanam
children.translated_text: When a vessel of gold, silver, or bronze is offered by someone,

children.text: tān sarvān samparityajya tāmraṃ tu mama rocate ||
children.translated_text: setting all those aside, copper alone pleases me.

children.text: pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ yo maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam
children.translated_text: Copper is the purifier of purifiers and the auspicious thing among auspicious things;
it is the purity of the completely pure, and releases one from worldly existence.
For initiated and purified persons devoted to my rites,

children.text: sadā tāmreṇa kartavyam evaṃ bhūmi mama priyam ||
children.translated_text: the act should always be done with copper; thus, O <s>Bhūmi</s>, it is dear to me.
And some, because of the fault caused by contact of cow products and the like with copper vessels,
desire a vessel other than copper for the <s>madhuparka</s>.
Likewise some desire a conch itself as the <s>arghya</s>-vessel.

children.text: śaṅkhe kṛtvā tu pānīyaṃ sapuṣpaṃ salilākṣatam
children.translated_text: Having placed water in a conch, together with flowers, water, and unbroken rice,
one offers <s>arghya</s> to the deity: so it is stated in the <s>Skānda</s>.
For auspiciousness he should place a water-filled kalaśa, provided with a karaka,
divine and accompanied by fruits and the like, before the Lord.
And likewise in the <s>Skānda</s>:
At the time of worship he should place a divine water-pot with a karaka,
joined with fruits and camphor; it is exceedingly dear to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Moreover:

children.text: sanīraṃ ca sakarpūraṃ kumbhaṃ kṛṣṇāya yo nyaset
children.translated_text: He who places for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> a water-pot containing water and camphor,

children.text: kalpaṃ tasya na pāpekṣāṃ kurvanti prapitāmahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: his great-grandfathers do not turn their regard toward sin for a kalpa.
Into the <s>arghya</s>-vessel the practitioner should put fragrant paste, flowers, unbroken rice, barley,
tips of kuśa grass, sesame, dūrvā grass, and also white mustard seeds.

children.text: kecic cātra jalādīni dravyāṇy aṣṭau vadanti hi ||
children.translated_text: Some indeed say that here the substances beginning with water are eight.
For it is said in the <s>Bhaviṣya</s>:
Water, milk, tips of kuśa grass, curd, unbroken rice, and sesame,
as well as barley and white mustard seeds: <s>arghya</s> is declared to have these eight parts.

children.text: pādyapātre ca kamalaṃ dūrvā śyāmākam eva ca
children.translated_text: In the <s>pādya</s>-vessel he should put a lotus, dūrvā grass, and śyāmāka grain,
and also <s>Viṣṇu</s>-patrī; such is the set of four substances.
Likewise, for the sake of <s>ācamana</s>, the wise man should put three substances into the vessel:

children.text: jātīphalaṃ lavaṅgaṃ ca kakkolam api nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: nutmeg, clove, and also kakkola.

children.text: madhuparkīyapātre ca gavyaṃ dadhi payo ghṛtam
children.translated_text: And in the <s>madhuparka</s> vessel he should put the five substances:
cow products, namely curd, milk, ghee, honey, and khaṇḍa sugar.

children.text: kecit trīṇy eva pātre'smin dravyāṇīcchanti sādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Some good practitioners desire only three substances in this vessel.
For it is said in the <s>Śrīviṣṇudharma</s>:

children.text: ghṛtaṃ dadhi tathā kṣaudraṃ madhuparko vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Ghee, curd, and honey are prescribed as <s>madhuparka</s>.
And in the <s>Ādivārāha</s>:
For me, curd, ghee, and honey in equal measure are to be placed in an udumbara vessel.

children.text: madhunas tu alābhe tu guḍena saha miśrayet ||
children.translated_text: But if honey is unavailable, he should mix it with jaggery.

children.text: ghṛtasyālābhe suśroṇi lājaiś ca saha miśrayet
children.translated_text: If ghee is unavailable, O fair-hipped one, he should mix it with parched grain,

children.text: tathā dadhno 'py alābhe tu kṣīreṇa saha miśrayet ||
children.translated_text: and likewise, if curd is unavailable, he should mix it with milk.
In the absence of these, he should put flowers and the like, with the corresponding thing mentally intended.
But <s>Nārada</s> says: it is filled with pure water alone.
With the root mantra he should consecrate it eight times in a single vessel,

children.text: kuryāc ca teṣāṃ pātrāṇāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ cakramudrayā ||
children.translated_text: and he should protect those vessels by means of the cakra-mudrā.
Beginning the worship, seated on the seat as prescribed,

children.text: paṭhen maṅgalaśāntiṃ tāṃ yārcane saṃmatā satām ||
children.translated_text: he should recite that auspicious peace-invocation which is approved by the good for worship.

children.text: oṃ bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devā bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhir yajatrā
children.translated_text: O gods, may we hear what is auspicious with our ears; O worshipful ones, may we see what is auspicious with our eyes.

children.text: sthirair aṅgais tuṣṭuvāṃsas tanubhir vyaśema devahitaṃ yad āyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Praising you with firm limbs and bodies, may we pass the span of life allotted by the gods.
May <s>Indra</s> of great fame grant well-being to us.
May <s>Pūṣan</s> and the <s>Viśvadevas</s> grant well-being to us.
May <s>Tārkṣya</s> of unharmed wheel grant well-being to us.
May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> bestow well-being on us.

children.text: paṭhan oṃ śāntiḥ śrīkṛṣṇapādapadmārādhaneṣu śāntir bhavatu
children.translated_text: Reciting, "Oṃ, peace; may there be peace in the worships of the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>."

children.text: apasarpantu te bhūtā ye bhūtā bhuvi saṃsthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Let those beings withdraw, those beings that stand upon the earth;

children.text: ye bhūtā vighnakartāras te naśyantu śivājñayā ||
children.translated_text: let those beings who make obstacles perish by the command of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having uttered this, with the astra-mantra and with the heel of the left foot,

children.text: ghātais tribhir budho vighnān bhaumān sarvān nivārayet ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should ward off all earthly obstacles by three blows.
And with that same mantra, by three claps directed higher and higher upward,
the mantra-practitioner should cast out the atmospheric obstacles and drive away the divine ones by divine sight.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtāñjalir vāme śrīguruṃ paramaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: Then, with joined palms, he should bow on the left to the <s>śrīguru</s>, the supreme guru,
and the parameṣṭhi-guru, that is, to the lineage of gurus.

children.text: gaṇeśaṃ dakṣiṇe bhāge durgām agre'tha pṛṣṭhataḥ
children.translated_text: He should bow with devotion to <s>Gaṇeśa</s> on the right side, to <s>Durgā</s> in front, and then behind
to <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>, and in the middle to his own chosen deity.

children.text: tataś cāstreṇa saṃśodhya karau kurvīta tena hi
children.translated_text: Then, after purifying the hands with the astra-mantra, by that same mantra he should perform

children.text: tālatrayaṃ diśāṃ bandham agniprākāram eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the three claps, the binding of the directions, and the enclosure of fire.
The purification of the elements that have taken the form of the body,
through contact with imperishable <s>Brahman</s>, is considered this <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (purification of the elements).
Without <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s>, the agent's rites such as recitation and oblation

children.text: bhavanti niṣphalāḥ sarvā yathāvidhy apy aniṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all become fruitless, even if they have been performed according to rule.
Having made the karakacchapikā mudrā, he should, by his understanding, join his self from the heart-lotus
to the supreme self in the thousand-petalled lotus of the head.
He should contemplate the principles beginning with earth as dissolved in that supreme self.
The left hand is turned upward, with the right hand bound below it;
this is proclaimed as the karakacchapikā mudrā in <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (purification of the elements).
Having dried out this body, burned it, and flooded it with a shower of nectar,
having produced it again and made it firm, he should perform the rite of firm establishment according to rule.
Having purified himself in this way and brought himself to fitness for the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: vātsalyāddhṛdgataṃ kṛṣṇaṃ yaṣṭuṃ hṛt punar ānayet ||
children.translated_text: out of affection he should bring <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who dwells in the heart, back into the heart in order to worship him.
And likewise in the <s>Trailokyasaṃmohana-tantra</s>:
The wise man should purify the body, together with its sin, by the wind situated in the navel;

children.text: vahninā hṛdayasthena dahet tac ca kalevaram ||
children.translated_text: and with the fire situated in the heart he should burn that body.
In the great thousand-spoked lotus, situated at the forehead, he should contemplate the moon,
with its full disk, pure, and made of nectar.
With streams dripping from that moon the wise man should flood what has become ashes;
and with those streams, made of letters, he should flood the body composed of the five elements.
As before, he should visualize the goddess.
And further on:

children.text: tatas tasmāt samākṛṣya praṇavena tu mantravit
children.translated_text: Then, drawing that radiance forth from it with the praṇava, the knower of mantra

children.text: tat tejo hṛdaye nyasya cintayed viṣṇum avyayam ||
children.translated_text: should place that radiance in the heart and contemplate imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: kiṃ vā cintanamātreṇa bhūtaśuddhiṃ vidhāya tām
children.translated_text: Or else, having performed that <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> merely by contemplation,
he should then perform the <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls) according to his tradition.
Exhalation should be with sixteen mātrās, and inhalation should be with thirty-two;

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭyā bhavet kumbha evaṃ syāt prāṇasaṃyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: retention should be with sixty-four. Thus there is control of the breath.
After first exhaling the breath and contracting the anal region,
having inhaled according to rule, he should remain in retention according to his own capacity.

children.text: tatra praṇavam abhyasyan bījaṃ vā mantram ūrdhvagam
children.translated_text: There, practicing the praṇava, or a seed-syllable or mantra that rises upward,
and remembering the seer and the rest, he should perform meditation without weariness.
And that meditation is stated:
I bow to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, adorned with a shining crown, armlets, bracelets, ornaments, necklace, waist, feet, and hips, with the jewel on his chest and great makara earrings touching his cheeks;

children.text: hastodyacchaṅkhacakrāmbujagadam amalaṃ pītakauśeyavāsaṃ vidyotadbhāsam udyaddinakarasadṛśaṃ padmasaṃsthaṃ namāmi ||
children.translated_text: spotless, with hands raised bearing conch, discus, lotus, and mace, clothed in yellow silk, radiant with light, like the rising sun, and seated on a lotus.
And in some places:

children.text: rudras tu recake brahmā pūrake dhyeyadevatā
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> is to be meditated on in exhalation, <s>Brahmā</s> in inhalation, and the chosen deity

children.text: śrīviṣṇuḥ kumbhake jñeyo dhyānasthānaṃ guror mukhāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> should be known in retention; the place of meditation is to be learned from the guru's mouth.
For so it is said:
During inhalation one should contemplate, in the place of the navel, lotus-seated
<s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire, red and fair in body and four-faced.
During retention one should contemplate in the middle of the heart the great-souled one,
four-armed, established there, dark as the petal of a blue lotus.
During exhalation the wise man should perform a pure meditation on <s>Īśvara</s> at the forehead, removing all sins,
clear and resembling pure crystal.
For single-minded devotees, the Lord, the master who consists of all the gods,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, accompanied by his beloved people, is indeed to be contemplated everywhere.
In the <s>Padma</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Devahūti</s> and <s>Vikuṇḍala</s>:
Those devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s> do not see the world of <s>Yama</s>;
even if they have done evil deeds, their sins are destroyed by those very breath-controls.

children.text: divase divase vaiśya prāṇāyāmās tu ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: Day by day, O vaiśya, sixteen <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>,

children.text: api brahmahaṇaṃ sākṣāt punanty aharahaḥ kṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: performed day after day, purify even one who is directly a killer of a Brahmin.

children.text: tapāṃsi yāni tapyante vratāni niyamāś ca ye
children.translated_text: The austerities that are practiced, the vows, and the disciplines,
and the gift of a thousand cows: <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is equal to that.

children.text: ambubinduṃ yaḥ kuśāgreṇa māse māse naraḥ pibet
children.translated_text: If a man drinks a drop of water with the tip of kuśa grass month by month
for a full hundred years and more, <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is equal to that.

children.text: pātakaṃ tu mahad yac ca tathā kṣudropapātakam
children.translated_text: Whatever great sin there is, and likewise whatever small secondary sin,

children.text: prāṇāyāmaiḥ kṣaṇāt sarvaṃ bhasmasāt kurute naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a man makes it all into ashes in an instant by <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.

children.text: nyāsān vinā japaṃ prāhur āsuraṃ viphalaṃ budhāḥ
children.translated_text: The wise declare japa without nyāsas to be demonic and fruitless;
therefore he should perform the nyāsas according to his tradition and according to rule.
Having first remembered the seer, meter, deity, and so on of the mātṛkā-mantra,
and having placed them on the head, mouth, heart, and so forth, he should perform its meditation.
And that is stated:

I take refuge in the goddess of speech, whose face, arms, lotus-hands, middle, and breast-region are divided by the fifty letters, whose shining head bears a crescent moon, and whose breasts are full and high;

children.text: mudrām akṣaguṇaṃ sudhāḍhyakalasaṃ vidyāṃ ca hastāmbujair bibhrāṇāṃ viśadaprabhāṃ trinayanāṃ vāgdevatām āśraye ||
children.translated_text: who bears a mudrā, a rosary, a nectar-filled jar, and knowledge in her lotus hands, who has clear radiance and three eyes.
The wise man should first place the letters, beginning with a and ending with kṣa, by themselves
on the forehead and the other limbs in proper sequence.
And that is explained in detail:
On the forehead, face, round of the face, eyes, ears, nose, and cheeks,
on the lips, teeth, crown, mouth, arms, feet, joints, and tips,
on the sides, back, navel, belly, heart, and shoulders,
and on the nape and mouth, beginning with the heart, then on the pair of hands and feet,
and then on the belly and mouth, he should place the mātṛkā letters in order.
With anusvāra, with visarga, and with both anusvāra and visarga,

children.text: nyased bhūyo 'pi tān vidvān evaṃ vāracatuṣṭayam ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should place those same letters again; thus there are four rounds.
In the throat, heart, navel, genitals, anus, and between the brows,
in the sixteen-petalled lotus situated there, and then, in order, in the twelve-petalled,
the ten-petalled, the six-petalled, the four-petalled, and the two-petalled lotuses,
he should place one letter with bindu at the end of each petal.
Remembering the seer and the rest, the letters together with the forms beginning with <s>Keśava</s>...

children.text: kīrtyādibhiḥ śaktibhiś ca nyaset tān pūrvavat kramāt ||
children.translated_text: And with the powers beginning with <s>Kīrti</s> he should place them in order as before.

children.text: nyasec caturthīn atyantā mūrtīḥ śaktīś ca yādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: He should place the final forms and powers in the fourth case, with the syllables beginning with ya.
He should also place the seven bodily constituents, <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath), <s>jīva</s> (living soul), and wrath, each ending with "ātmane."

children.text: udyatpradyotanaśataruciṃ taptahemāvadānaṃ pārśvadvandve jaladhisutayā viśvadhātryā ca juṣṭam
children.translated_text: I worship him whose brilliance is like hundreds of rising suns, whose complexion is like heated gold, who is attended on his two sides by the daughter of the ocean and by the sustainer of the world,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, shining with many jewels and various ornaments, clad in yellow garments, and holding the conch, lotus, <s>Kaumodakī</s> mace, and discus in his hands.

children.text: prathamaṃ keśavo nārāyaṇaḥ paścāc ca mādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: First is <s>Keśava</s>, then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and afterward <s>Mādhava</s>;

children.text: govindaś ca tathā viṣṇur madhusūdana eva ca ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Madhusūdana</s>.

children.text: trivikramo vāmano 'tha śrīdharaś ca tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Then <s>Trivikrama</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and after that <s>Śrīdhara</s>;
then <s>Ṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Padmanābha</s>, and likewise <s>Dāmodara</s>.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and then <s>Aniruddha</s>;

children.text: cakrī gadī tathā śārṅgī khaḍgī śaṅkhī halī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Cakrī</s>, <s>Gadī</s>, likewise <s>Śārṅgī</s>, <s>Khaḍgī</s>, <s>Śaṅkhī</s>, and likewise <s>Halī</s>;

children.text: musalī ca tathā śūlī pāśī caivāṅkuśī tathā
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Musalī</s>, <s>Śūlī</s>, <s>Pāśī</s>, and also <s>Aṅkuśī</s>;

children.text: mukundo nandajaś caiva tathā nandī naras tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mukunda</s> and <s>Nandaja</s>, and likewise <s>Nandī</s> and <s>Nara</s>;

children.text: narakajiddhariḥ kṛṣṇaḥ satyaḥ sātvata eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Narakajit</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Satya</s>, and <s>Sātvata</s>;

children.text: tataḥ śauris tathā śūras tataḥ paścāj janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Śauri</s>, likewise <s>Śūra</s>, and afterward <s>Janārdana</s>;
<s>Bhūdhara</s>, <s>Viśvamūrti</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, and <s>Puruṣottama</s>;

children.text: balo balānujo bālo vṛṣaghno vṛṣa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bala</s>, <s>Balānuja</s>, <s>Bāla</s>, <s>Vṛṣaghna</s>, and <s>Vṛṣa</s>;

children.text: haṃso varāho vimalo nṛsiṃhaś ceti mūrtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Varāha</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, and <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>: these are the forms.

children.text: kīrtiḥ kāntis tuṣṭipuṣṭī dhṛtiḥ śāntiḥ kriyā dayā
children.translated_text: <s>Kīrti</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, and <s>Dayā</s>;

children.text: medhā harṣā tathā śraddhā lajjā lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Harṣā</s>, likewise <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Lajjā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: prītī ratir jayā durgā prabhā satyā ca caṇḍikā
children.translated_text: <s>Prīti</s>, <s>Rati</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and <s>Caṇḍikā</s>;

children.text: vāṇī vilāsinī caiva vijayā virajā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāṇī</s>, <s>Vilāsinī</s>, and also <s>Vijayā</s> and <s>Virajā</s>;

children.text: viśvā ca vinadā caiva sunandā ca smṛtis tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvā</s> and <s>Vinadā</s>, and also <s>Sunandā</s> and <s>Smṛti</s>;

children.text: ṛddhiḥ samṛddhiḥ śuddhiś ca buddhir mūrtir natiḥ kṣamā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>Samṛddhi</s>, <s>Śuddhi</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Mūrti</s>, <s>Nati</s>, and <s>Kṣamā</s>;

children.text: ramomā kledinī klinnā vasudā vasudhā parā
children.translated_text: <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Umā</s>, <s>Kledinī</s>, <s>Klinnā</s>, <s>Vasudā</s>, <s>Vasudhā</s>, and <s>Parā</s>;

children.text: parāyaṇā ca sūkṣmā ca sandhyā prajñā prabhā niśā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Parāyaṇā</s>, <s>Sūkṣmā</s>, <s>Sandhyā</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, and <s>Niśā</s>;
<s>Amoghā</s> and <s>Vidyut</s>: these are held to be the fifty-one powers.
This Keśavādi-nyāsa grants all prosperity here.
Hereafter, merely by the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement), it leads one to likeness with <s>Acyuta</s>.
That has been stated:

children.text: dhyātvaivaṃ paramapumāṃsam akṣarair yo vinyased dinam anu keśavādiyuktaiḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, having meditated in this way on the supreme person, day after day performs placement with the syllables joined to the names beginning with <s>Keśava</s>,
he becomes long strengthened by intelligence, life-span, memory, firmness, fame, beauty, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and good fortune.
And elsewhere:
This nyāsa beginning with <s>Keśava</s>, by the mere act of nyāsa,

children.text: acyutatvaṃ dadāty eva satyaṃ satyaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: certainly gives the embodied being the state of <s>Acyuta</s>; true, true, there is no doubt.

children.text: yaś ca kuryād imaṃ nyāsaṃ lakṣmībījapuraḥsaram
children.translated_text: And whoever performs this nyāsa preceded by the seed-syllable of <s>Lakṣmī</s>,

children.text: bhaktiṃ muktiṃ ca bhuktiṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ ca labhate'cirāt ||
children.translated_text: quickly obtains devotion, liberation, enjoyment, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
And likewise it has been said:

children.text: amum eva ramāpuraḥsaraṃ prabhajed yo manujo vidhiṃ budhaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man who practices this very rite preceded by <s>Ramā</s>,

children.text: samupetya ramāṃ prathīyasīṃ punar ante haritāṃ vrajaty asau ||
children.translated_text: having attained abundant <s>Ramā</s>, at the end goes on to the state of <s>Hari</s>.
With the letters beginning with ma and ending with ka, joined with bindus,

children.text: namaḥ parāyeti pūrvam ātmane nama ity anu ||
children.translated_text: first with "namaḥ parāya," and afterward with "ātmane namaḥ,"
he should place the names of the principles beginning with <s>jīva</s> in their respective places in order.
By this <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) a person becomes qualified for worship.
There, first, he should place <s>jīva</s> and <s>prāṇa</s> throughout the whole body,
and then the three, intellect, ego, and mind, in the heart.

children.text: śabdaṃ sparśaṃ tato rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ ca mastake
children.translated_text: Then he should place sound, touch, form, taste, and smell on the head,

children.text: mukhe hṛdi ca guhye ca pādayoś ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: on the mouth, in the heart, in the secret place, and on the two feet, respectively.

children.text: śrotraṃ tvacaṃ dṛśaṃ jihvāṃ ghrāṇaṃ svasvapade tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then he should place hearing, skin, sight, tongue, and smell in their own respective places,
and likewise speech, hands, anus, and genitals in their own respective places.
He should place ether, air, fire, water, and earth on the crown of the head,

children.text: vadane hṛdaye liṅge pādayoś ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: on the face, in the heart, on the liṅga, and on the two feet, respectively.
In the heart he should place the heart-lotus, beginning with the twelve, sixteen, and ten-petaled forms,
and, after first saying "pervaded by the kalās," the solar, lunar, and fire circles.

children.text: varṇaiḥ saha sarephaiś ca kramān nyaset sabindukaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Together with the letters, with rephas and bindus, he should place them in order.
He should place <s>Vāsudeva</s> with the syllable ṣa, joined with <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, at ke,
and with the syllable ya he should place <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, endowed with <s>Pumān</s>, in the mouth.
In the heart he should place <s>Pradyumna</s>, joined with <s>Viśva</s>, by means of the syllable la,
and <s>Aniruddha</s>, endowed with <s>Nivṛtti</s>, by means of the syllable va in the secret place,
and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, endowed with all, by the syllable la alone on the two feet.
He should place <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, joined with wrath, by that seed-syllable in the whole self.
This <s>tattvanyāsa</s> (placement of principles) quickly brings about the nearness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
And likewise it has been said:
Because it is the means for attaining him whose form pervades what is beyond the principles,
the wise knowers of the truth of <s>nyāsa</s> call it <s>tattvanyāsa</s>.

children.text: yaḥ kuryāt tattvavinyāsaṃ sa pūto bhavati dhruvam
children.translated_text: Whoever performs the placement of principles certainly becomes purified.
Entering in the form of that self, the Blessed Lord remains here,

children.text: yataḥ sa eva tattvāni sarvaṃ tasmin pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: because he himself is the principles; everything is established in him.

children.text: prāṇāyāmāṃs tataḥ kuryān mūlamantraṃ japan kramāt
children.translated_text: Then he should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s>s, reciting the root mantra in order:

children.text: vārau dvau caturaḥ ṣaṭ ca recapūrakakumbhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: twice, four times, and six times for exhalation, inhalation, and retention respectively.

children.text: athavā recakādīṃs tān kuryād vārāṃs tu ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: Or he should perform those beginning with exhalation sixteen times,

children.text: dvātriṃśac ca catuḥṣaṣṭhiṃ kāmabījaṃ japan kramāt ||
children.translated_text: thirty-two times, and sixty-four times respectively, reciting the desire-seed.
And likewise in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>:

children.text: recayen mārutaṃ dakṣayā dakṣiṇaḥ pūrayed vāmayā madhyanāḍyā punaḥ
children.translated_text: He should exhale the breath through the right nostril; the right one should inhale through the left; then again through the middle channel...
One should hold it; the three beginning with <s>recaka</s> are said to have measures called <s>kalā</s>, <s>danta</s>, and <s>vidyā</s>.
<s>Sanātana</s>:

children.text: tad eva kramadīpikoktyā saṃvādayan tatraiva kiṃcid viśeṣaṃ ca darśayati recayed iti
children.translated_text: Reconciling that very point with the statement of the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>, he also shows there a certain distinction, beginning with "one should exhale."
"By the right" means by the right channel; "right" means the skilled, knowledgeable person.
He should retain by the middle channel, the <s>suṣumṇā</s>.
Thus there is the triad called <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), and <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention).

children.text: recakādiṣu triṣu krameṇāvadhikālam āha kalāḥ ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: For the three beginning with <s>recaka</s>, he states the limiting time in order: sixteen <s>kalās</s>.
<s>Danta</s> means thirty-two.
<s>Vidyā</s> means sixty-four; the sense is that each consists of a measure of that respective number.
A <s>mātrā</s> is the time of contact made by the left thumb with each of the three joints of the left fingers beginning with the little finger.
Or it is the time taken by the left hand to touch the circle of the left knee in a clockwise motion.
Even there, a rule about the fingers has also been stated.
The holding of the nostrils with the little finger, ring finger, and thumb,
without the forefinger and middle finger, is to be understood as <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

children.text: tatra teṣu prāṇāyāmeṣu pūrvaṃ recakādiṣu saṅkhyoktā
children.translated_text: There, among those <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>, the number was previously stated with reference to the <s>recaka</s> and the rest.
Here the distinction is that it is stated with reference to the <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.
There again:

children.text: purato japasya parato 'pi vihitam atha tattrayaṃ budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Before the recitation and also afterward, the wise prescribe that threefold practice.

children.text: ṣoḍaśa ya iha samācared dineśaḥ paripūyate sa khalu māsato 'ṃhasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who performs it sixteen times here each day is indeed purified from sin within a month.
<s>Sanātana</s>:

children.text: japasya purata ādau parataḥ ante ca iti prāṇāyāmeṣu kālaḥ
children.translated_text: "Before the recitation" means at its beginning, and "afterward" means at its end; this is the time for the <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>.
"That threefold practice" means the three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>; this is the number.

children.text: yo jano dinaśaḥ pratyahaṃ ṣoḍaśaprāṇāyāmān ācaret sa māsataḥ māsenaikena aṃhasaḥ pāpāt paripūyate śuddho bhavatīti sāmānyataḥ phalam
children.translated_text: The person who performs sixteen <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> day by day is purified from <s>aṃhas</s>, sin, in a month, that is, in one month; such is the general result.

children.text: paraṃ ca sarvaṃ purvaṃ likhitam eva
children.translated_text: Moreover, everything further has already been written above.
Then he should conceive his own body itself as the worship-seat.
He should install on his own limbs the supports of the seat, beginning with the <s>ādhāraśakti</s>, just as with the <s>tāra</s>.

children.text: ādhāraśaktiṃ prakṛtiṃ kūrmānantau ca tatra tu
children.translated_text: There he should install the <s>ādhāraśakti</s>, <s>prakṛti</s>, the tortoise, and <s>Ananta</s>,

children.text: pṛthivīṃ kṣīrasindhuṃ ca śvetadvīpaṃ ca bhāsvaram ||
children.translated_text: the earth, the milk-ocean, and the radiant <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>;
and likewise the splendid jewel pavilion and the wish-fulfilling tree in the heart.
He should install, in clockwise order, <s>dharma</s> and <s>jñāna</s> next on the shoulders,
<s>vairāgya</s> and <s>aiśvarya</s> on the thighs, and likewise <s>adharma</s> on the face,
<s>ajñāna</s> on the lower back, and <s>avairāgya</s> and <s>anaiśvarya</s> on the sides.
In the lotus of the heart he should install <s>Ananta</s>'s lotus, and also the maṇḍalas of sun, moon, and fire,
in order, with the syllables of the <s>praṇava</s> furnished with bindus.
There indeed he should also install sattva, rajas, tamas, the self, and the inner self,
and the supreme self too, with the letters beginning with the first, each furnished with a bindu.
He should install the knowledge-self joined with the seed-syllable of <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s>,
and in its eight directions, and also in the middle, the nine powers in the order of the directions.
And they are stated as follows:
<s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Jñānā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, and <s>Yogā</s> are powers;
<s>Prahvī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and likewise <s>Īśānā</s> and <s>Anugrahā</s> are remembered as the ninth.
Above that he should install the seat-mantra as prescribed.
Then he should recall the seer and the rest for this eighteen-syllable mantra.
Those devoted to single-minded worship should understand the group of four beginning with the milk-ocean
as, in order, splendid <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, its bower, and the nīpa trees.
And so in the <s>Brahmasaṃhitā</s>, in the hymn called the <s>Ādipuruṣarahasyastotra</s>:

children.text: sa yatra kṣīrābdhiḥ sravati surabhībhyaś ca sumahān nimeṣārdhākhyo vā vrajati na hi yatrāpi samayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where the great milk-ocean flows from the surabhī cows, and where time, called half a blink, does not pass at all,

children.text: bhaje śvetadvīpaṃ tam aham iha golokam iti yaṃ vidantas te santaḥ kṣitiviralacārāḥ katipaye ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> here, which those few saints who rarely move upon the earth know as <s>Goloka</s>, I worship.
In the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>:

children.text: evaṃ hṛdayaṃ bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sarvānvitaś ca bhūtātmā
children.translated_text: Thus: the heart; <s>Bhagavān</s>; <s>Viṣṇu</s>; and <s>Bhūtātman</s>, joined with "all";
the words ending in -ṅe, each with <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and the compound joined with "all-self";

children.text: yogāvadhaś ca padmaṃ pīṭhāt ṅeyuto natiś cānte
children.translated_text: and at the end of "yoga" comes "lotus"; the seat, joined with -ṅe, and obeisance at the end:
the great seat-mantra is made clear; this is sufficient for worships.
<s>Sanātana</s>:
The <s>tāra</s> is the <s>praṇava</s>, oṃ.
Then comes the word "hṛdayam," followed by "namaḥ."

children.text: tataś ca bhagavān iti viṣṇur iti ca
children.translated_text: After that come "bhagavate" and "viṣṇave."
"Joined with all" means joined with the word "sarva"; <s>Bhūtātman</s> means "sarvabhūtātmane."

children.text: ete trayaḥ savāsudevā vāsudevasahitāḥ pratyekaṃ ṅe'ntāś caturthyantāḥ
children.translated_text: These three, each accompanied by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, end in -ṅe, that is, they have the dative ending.

children.text: tataś ca sarvātmanā yutaṃ saṃyogaṃ sarvātmasaṃyogam iti napuṃsakatvam ārṣam
children.translated_text: Then comes the compound joined with "sarvātman," namely "sarvātmasaṃyogam"; the neuter gender is according to sage usage.

children.text: tataś ca yogasyāvadhau ante padmaṃ yogapadmam iti
children.translated_text: Then at the limit, that is, at the end, of "yoga" comes "padma," giving "yogapadma."
At its end comes "pīṭhātmā," joined with -ṅe, that is, in the dative.
And at its end comes <s>nati</s>, the word "namaḥ."

children.text: evaṃ oṃ namo bhagavate viṣṇave sarvabhūtātmane vāsudevāya sarvātmasaṃyogayogapadmapīṭhātmane nama iti siddham
children.translated_text: Thus the established mantra is: "oṃ namo bhagavate viṣṇave sarvabhūtātmane vāsudevāya sarvātmasaṃyogayogapadmapīṭhātmane namaḥ."
And similarly in the <s>Śāradātilaka</s>:

children.text: namo bhagavate brūyād viṣṇave ca padaṃ vadet
children.translated_text: One should say "namo bhagavate," and then pronounce the word "viṣṇave."
Then one should say "sarvabhūtātmane vāsudevāya."
After the word "sarvātmasaṃyoga," again comes the word "yogapadma."
This mantra, ending with "pīṭhātmane" and beginning with the <s>tāra</s>, is said to have "hṛd" at its end.
And in the <s>Sanatkumārakalpa</s>:

children.text: oṃ namaḥ padam ābhāṣya tathā bhagavate padam
children.translated_text: Having uttered the word "oṃ namaḥ," and then the word "bhagavate,"

children.text: vāsudevāya ity uktvā sarvātmeti padaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: and having said "vāsudevāya," likewise the word "sarvātma,"

children.text: saṃyogayogety uktvā ca tathā pīṭhātmane padam
children.translated_text: and having said "saṃyogayoga," and then the word "pīṭhātmane,"
when it is joined with the wife of fire, it is said to be the seat-mantra.

children.text: oṃ aṣṭādaśākṣaramantrasya śrīnārada ṛṣir gāyatrīchandaḥ sakalalokamaṅgalo nandatanayo devatā hrīṃ bījaṃ svāhā śaktiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ prakṛtir durgādhiṣṭhātrī devatā abhimatārthe viniyogaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. For the eighteen-syllable mantra: <s>Śrī Nārada</s> is the seer, <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter, the son of <s>Nanda</s>, auspicious for all worlds, is the deity, hrīṃ is the seed, svāhā is the power, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the nature, <s>Durgā</s> is the presiding deity, and its application is for the desired aim.
And similarly, in the <s>Saṃmohana-tantra</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Umā</s>:

children.text: ṛṣir nārada ity ukto gāyatrīchanda ucyate
children.translated_text: "The seer is said to be <s>Nārada</s>; the meter is called <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wearing the dress of a cowherd, is proclaimed to be the deity.

children.text: bījaṃ manmathasaṃjñaṃ tu priyā śaktir havir bhujaḥ
children.translated_text: The seed is what is known as <s>Manmatha</s>; the beloved is the power of the eater of oblations.
You yourself, O supreme goddess, are the presiding deity of this mantra.
Its application is proclaimed for attaining the fruits of the four aims of life."

children.text: catuś caturbhir varṇaiś ca catvāry aṅgāni kalpayet
children.translated_text: With four groups of four syllables each, he should form the four limbs.

children.text: dvābhyām astrākhyam aṅgaṃ ca tasyety aṅgāni pañca vai ||
children.translated_text: And with two syllables he should form the limb called astra; thus there are indeed its five limbs.

children.text: nyasyec ca vyāpakatvena tāny aṅgāni karadvaye
children.translated_text: He should place those limbs on the two hands in a pervasive manner.

children.text: tāny aṅgulīṣu pañcātha kecid varṇān svarān api ||
children.translated_text: Then he should place those five on the fingers; some also place the consonants and even the vowels.
And these are stated:
melting, agitation, attraction, subjugation, and likewise causing to flow,
drying, bewildering, kindling, heating, and maddening.
Furthermore:

children.text: namo'ntaṃ hṛdayaṃ cāṅgaiḥ śiraḥ svāhānvitaṃ śikhām
children.translated_text: They place the heart-mantra ending in namaḥ, the head-mantra joined with svāhā, the topknot-mantra

children.text: vaṣaḍyutaṃ ca kavacaṃ huṃyugastraṃ ca phaḍyutam ||
children.translated_text: joined with vaṣaṭ, the armor-mantra, and the astra-mantra joined with huṃ and phaṭ.

children.text: nyasyanti punar aṅguṣṭhau tarjanyau madhyame tathā
children.translated_text: Again they place, in order, the thumbs, the index fingers, the middle fingers,

children.text: anāmike kaniṣṭhe ca kramād aṅgaiś ca pañcabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the ring fingers, and the little fingers with the five limbs.
And again they place all at once the heart and the rest, and similarly the thumb and the rest,

children.text: nyasyanti yugapat sarvāṇy aṅgais taiḥ pañcabhiḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: in order with those five limbs.
They also place the six limbs of that mantra, beginning with the heart.

children.text: hṛdayādiṣu caiteṣāṃ pañcaikaṃ dikṣu ca kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Among these, in the places beginning with the heart, five and one are placed in the directions in order.
The six limbs are also stated in the <s>Sanatkumāra-kalpa</s> of the <s>Saṃmohana-tantra</s>:

children.text: varṇenaikena hṛdayaṃ tribhir eva śiro matam
children.translated_text: "The heart is understood to consist of one syllable, the head of precisely three.

children.text: caturbhiś ca śikhā proktā tathaiva kavacaṃ matam
children.translated_text: The topknot is declared to consist of four, and the armor likewise is understood so.

children.text: netraṃ tathā caturvarṇair astraṃ dvābhyāṃ tathā matam ||
children.translated_text: The eye is likewise made of four syllables, and the astra is understood to be made of two."

children.text: tataś cāpādam ā keśān nyased dorbhyām imaṃ manum
children.translated_text: Then, from the feet up to the hair, he should place this mantra with both hands.

children.text: vārāṃs trīn vyāpakatvena nyasec ca praṇavaṃ sakṛt ||
children.translated_text: He should place it three times in a pervasive manner, and once place the praṇava.
Then, in order, the eighteen syllables of this mantra

children.text: dante lalāṭe bhrūmadhye karṇayor netrayor dvayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should place on the teeth, forehead, between the brows, the two ears, and the two eyes,

children.text: nāsayor vadane kaṇṭhe hṛdi nābhau kaṭidvaye
children.translated_text: on the two nostrils, the mouth, throat, heart, navel, the two sides of the waist,

children.text: guhye jānudvaye caikaṃ nyased ekaṃ ca pādayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: on the secret place, the two knees, placing one syllable on each, and one on the two feet.
Good practitioners place them beginning with the tārā, ending in namaḥ, and furnished with bindu.
Others place them with the śrī-, śakti-, and kāma-bījas, in the order of creation and the other sequences.

children.text: tāraṃ śirasi vinyasya pañca mantrapadāni ca
children.translated_text: Having placed the tārā on the head, he should place the five words of the mantra

children.text: nyasen netradvaye vaktre hṛdguhyāṅghriṣu ca kramāt ||
children.translated_text: in order on the two eyes, the mouth, the heart, the secret place, and the feet.

children.text: dehe ca vyāpakatvena nyaset tāny akhile punaḥ
children.translated_text: And again he should place all those throughout the body in a pervasive manner.

children.text: kecit tāni namo'ntāni nyasyanty ādyākṣaraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: Some place them ending in namaḥ together with their initial syllables.
Likewise, they place three ending in svāhā, mixed successively with the following ones,

children.text: guhyād galān mastakāc ca vyāpayya caraṇāvadhi ||
children.translated_text: pervading from the secret place to the throat and from the head down to the feet.
Here the nyāsa that is concerned with the secret place and so on is for those established in knowledge.
It is to be performed by Vaiṣṇavas on the corresponding syllables of the body composed of one's own syllables.

children.text: ṛṣyādīn saptabhāgāṃś ca nyased asya manoḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: He should place, in order, the seven parts of this mantra beginning with the seer

children.text: mūrdhāsyahṛtsu kucayoḥ punar hṛdi punar hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: on the head, mouth, heart, breasts, then again on the heart and again on the heart.
Then he should display the mudrā called the flute and the mudrā called the forest-garland,
then the lovely ones called <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Kaustubha</s>, and bilva.

children.text: itthaṃ nyastaśarīraḥ san kṛtvā digbandhanaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus made his body one in which nyāsa has been performed, and then having bound the directions,
he should form the hand-tortoise gesture and meditate on <s>Śrī Nanda-nandana</s>.
Now he should remember <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, auspicious and pure, cooled by trees whose branches bend under masses of excellent flowers and new shoots, blooming and
exuding manifest fragrance and honey, and entwined by beautiful creepers charming with newly blossomed clusters.

children.text: athānantaraṃ sitamatiḥ śuddhamanāḥ san vṛndāvanaṃ cintayet
children.translated_text: Thereafter, being pure-minded, he should contemplate <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.
What kind of place is it? It is cooled by trees, made cool by them.

children.text: kīdṛśaiḥ prakaṭam udbhaṭaṃ saurabhaṃ yasya tac ca
children.translated_text: What kind of trees? Those whose fragrance is manifest, that is, intense,
and from which honey has poured forth, that is, dripping honey.
It is utphulla, that is, fully blossomed,

children.text: sac ca uttamaṃ yat prasūnaṃ puṣpaṃ navapallavaṃ ca
children.translated_text: and sat means excellent; the prasūna is a flower, and the new shoot is a navapallava.
A prakara of those two means a mass,
and by that mass their branches are bent.
The short vowel in mādhvika is to be tolerated because it has been composed by a great poet.

children.text: prakaṭasaurabhākulitamattabhṛṅgollasad iti pāṭhas tu sugama eva
children.translated_text: The reading prakaṭa-saurabhākulita-matta-bhṛṅgollasad is itself easy to understand.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ praphullābhir navamañjarībhir lalitā manoharā yā vallaryaḥ agraśākhā latā vā tābhir veṣṭitaiḥ
children.translated_text: Again, what kind of trees? They are entwined by creepers, namely tip-branches or vines, which are charming and beautiful with newly blossomed clusters.
It is śiva, auspicious in form, because it is free from obstruction and because it produces supreme blessedness.
It is filled within with the humming sounds rising from the mouths of moving bees, charming as they taste the nectar of blossoming flowers,

children.text: kapotaśukaśārikāparabhṛtādibhiḥ patribhir virāṇitam itas tato bhujagaśatrunṛtyākulam ||
children.translated_text: and it resounds here and there with birds such as pigeons, parrots, śārikās, and cuckoos; it is crowded with the dancing of the enemy of snakes.
It is constantly served by wandering breezes carrying the restless spray of the waves of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s>, gray with masses of pollen from the interiors of awakened lotuses,
and stirring desire in the women of <s>Vraja</s>, moving about in sportive play.
with coral as its fresh shoots, emeralds as its leaves, clusters of diamonds and pearls as its buds, and many ruby-like fruits,

children.text: sthaviṣṭham akhilartubhiḥ satatasevitaṃ kāmadaṃ tadantar api kalpakāṅghripam udañcitaṃ cintayet ||
children.translated_text: very massive, constantly served by all the seasons, granting desires; within that too he should visualize the lofty wish-fulfilling tree.

children.text: suhemaśikharāvaler uditabhānuvad bhāsvaram adho 'sya kanakasthalīm amṛtaśīkarāsāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Beneath it he should again remember a golden ground, shining like the rising sun from a row of fine golden peaks and showered with drops of nectar,

children.text: pradīptamaṇikuṭṭimāṃ kusumareṇupuñjojjvalāṃ smaret punar atandrito vigataṣaṭtaraṅgāṃ budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: paved with blazing jewels and bright with heaps of flower-pollen; the wise man should remember it without weariness, freed from the six waves of worldly agitation.
Having visualized, on the great <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> set in that jeweled pavement, an eight-petaled, reddish lotus,

children.text: udyadvirocanasarocir amuṣya madhye saṃcintayet sukhaniviṣṭam atho mukundam ||
children.translated_text: then, in its center, he should contemplate <s>Mukunda</s>, comfortably seated and shining with the radiance of the rising sun.
His luster is like Indra's jewel, a mass of crushed collyrium and rain-clouds, and a fresh blue lotus.
He has a very glossy, dark, dense mass of curling hair, and is crowned with the crest-plume of a splendid, charming peacock.
He wears a crest-ornament fashioned from flowers of the heavenly tree, caressed by bees, and his ears are filled with fresh blue lotuses set in his loosened hair.
His forehead flashes beneath restless curls, with a bright <s>gorocanā</s> mark, and he has a quivering line of brows.
His face is lovely like the full disk of the autumn moon, and his eyes are broad like lotus petals.
His mirror-like cheeks are lit by the rays of jewel-sparkling makara earrings, and his handsome nose is high.
His lips are lovelier than vermilion, and his body is illumined by the glow of a gentle smile like the moon, jasmine, and mandāra blossoms.
His attractive conch-like neck shines with a necklace covered by clusters of wild coral flowers.
His shoulders are adorned with a dangling garland of <s>santānaka</s> blossoms, enjoyed by intoxicated, circling bees.
His broad chest is like the expanse of the sky, adorned by constellations of necklaces and by the lovely sun of the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem.
He is beautifully marked with the sign of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, with high shoulders and well-formed arms, rounded and strong down to the knees.
He has a graceful belly, a noble deep navel, and a charming line of hair like a row of female bees.
He is adorned with armlets, bracelets, rings, neck-ornaments, a girdle, anklets, and a belly-band, all fashioned from many jewels.
His slender body is yellowed with divine unguents, and his rounded hips are wrapped in yellow garments.
His beautiful thighs, knees, and shapely calves are well proportioned, and the charm of his raised insteps puts the tortoise's beauty to shame.
His lotus feet are lovely with jewel toe-ornaments and rows of nails that shine like flames from clefts of ruby.
His reddish palms and soles are delightful, marked with fish, goad, conch, banner, barley-grain, lotus, and thunderbolt.
The beauty of his body, formed from the gathered essence of loveliness, defeats the bodily radiance of <s>Manobhava</s>, the god of love.
From his lotus mouth, which fills the holes of the flute, his moving fingers send forth divine melodies.
By those melodies he constantly melts and draws the unbroken succession of all beings; he is an endless ocean of happiness.
He is surrounded by cows whose eyes are absorbed in his lotus face, and whose slow, gentle gait falters under the weight of their udders,
with shoots of grass left bitten at the tips of their teeth, and encircled by creeper-like hanging tails.
He is also surrounded by charming calves whose still, full mouths drip foaming milk after sucking at streaming teats,
and whose pairs of ears are lifted high by the charming deep song set in motion by the flute.
He is surrounded by young bulls and heifers, their hoof-tips restless as they bound in eager clashes of fresh horns and soft heads,
plump, with heavy dewlaps and uplifted tails.
He is surrounded too by great bulls whose lowing shakes the circle of the directions, wearied by the weight of their broad, heavy humps,
their broad nostrils opened wide, their ear-cavities raised and encircled by the nectar of the flute's sound.
He is surrounded by cowherds of similar qualities, character, age, sport, and dress, whose flutes and vīṇās give forth sweet, entrancing tones.
They are intent on songs in low, high, and upper registers, and skilled in graceful dances made by their swaying, creeper-like arms.
He is surrounded by innocent boys wandering about with clusters of swinging little bells tied at their sturdy waists and hip-banks reaching to the thighs,
wearing neck-ornaments made from tiger-claws, and speaking indistinct, charming words.
Then he is surrounded by exceedingly graceful cowherd beauties, slowed by their broad, weighty hips,
whose slender waists are bent by the weight of their heavy breasts, and who bear lines of hair spreading among the three folds of the belly.
Their limbs, feet, and hands have blossomed from the nectar of that very sweet and lovely flute music,
and their creeper-like bodies are adorned with lovely horripilation rising like spreading clusters of buds.
The ocean of their passion swells under the moonlight of his exceedingly beautiful gentle smile,
and their streams of sweat-drops resemble sprays thrown up by the breaking of very tremulous waves.
Their bodies are pierced by showers of sharp arrows of love from his eyes, loosed from the bow of his very graceful, gently curving brows,
so that every vital spot is shattered, their limbs are overwhelmed, and the pain of unbearable trembling spreads through them.
They long to drink the nectar of the splendor of his exceedingly lovely and charming form,
with their languid, rolling lotus eyes, which carry floods of the water of love.
Again and again they are served by a cluster of greedy bees eager for honey dripping from full-blown flowers falling out of their loosened masses of hair.
whose soft voices falter from the intoxicated madness of love, whose girdles sway, whose waistbands loosen and slip, and whose hips shine forth from the edges of their Chinese silk garments;
of those whose graceful lotus feet stumble, and whose directions are filled with the tinkling of jewel anklets struck by a gentle step,
whose petal-like lower lips tremble, whose two lotus-eyes are bud-like and thick with lashes, and whose earrings gleam;

children.text: skhalitasya skhalanayuktasya lalitasya ca pādāmbhojasya mandābhighātena īṣad bhūbhāgaprahāreṇa kvaṇitaḥ kṛtaśabdo maṇimayo yas tulākoṭir nūpuraṃ tenākulaṃ śabdavyāptam āśānāṃ diśāṃ mukhaṃ yābhyas tāsām
children.translated_text: The phrase means: their lovely lotus feet have slipped; by the gentle striking of those feet, that is, by their slight impact on the ground, the jeweled anklet makes a sound, and by it the face of the quarters is filled with sound.

children.text: kuḍmalat mukulāyamānaṃ pakṣmalaṃ ca utkṛṣṭapakṣmayuktam akṣidvayasarasiruhaṃ yāsām ||
children.translated_text: It describes those women whose pair of lotus-eyes is kuḍmalat, bud-like, and pakṣmala, furnished with excellent lashes.
of those whose red lip-shoots grow withered from the heat of the breeze of very long breaths,
whose lotus-hands shine with various offerings, and who are constantly served on every side by their companions;

children.text: drāghiṣṭho 'tidīrghaḥ śvāsanasamīraṇaḥ śvāsavāyus tena abhitāpaḥ santāpas tena pramlānībhavan aruṇoṣṭhapallavo yāsām
children.translated_text: Drāghiṣṭha means very long; the śvasana-samīraṇa is the breath-wind. By its heat, its burning warmth, their red lip-shoots become withered.
his whole body fully worshiped by garlands of open blue lotuses, namely the wide, restless, dark eyes of those women, and serving as the abode of many amusements,
and displaying a charming garland of bee-like eyes, maddened by love, that tastes the honey flowing from the lotus of their enchanting faces.

children.text: vyākośaṃ vikasitaṃ praṇayād unmade udgatamade akṣiṇī eva madhukṛnmālā bhramarapaṅktiḥ
children.translated_text: Vyākośa means opened or blossomed; from love, the eyes are intoxicated, risen in passion, and are themselves a garland of bees, a row of bees.
Bibhrāṇam means bearing it, making it manifest.

children.text: śrīlocanayor itas tato bahudhā nipatanena sarvato darśanān mālety uktam
children.translated_text: Because the beautiful eyes fall here and there in many ways and look everywhere, it is called a garland.

children.text: kīdṛśīm tāsāṃ yan mugdhaṃ manoharam ānanapaṅkajaṃ
children.translated_text: What sort is it? Their face-lotus is mugdha, charming and lovely.
It is disposed to taste the honey-nectar that has streamed forth from that face-lotus.
For that very reason it is captivating.
Outside the cowherd men, cowherd women, and cattle, he should remember, before him, a host of gods,
beginning with <s>Viriñci</s>, the three-eyed one, and <s>Śatamanyu</s>, seeking wealth and intent on hymns of praise.

children.text: idānīṃ krameṇa vittadharmamokṣakāmākhyapuruṣārthacatuṣṭayasya tathā sarvataḥ śreṣṭhasya pañcamapuruṣārtharūpāyā bhakteś ca vāñchāyāḥ pradānāṃ devādīnāṃ dhyānam āha gopeti pañcabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Now, in sequence, he teaches in five verses beginning with gopa the meditation on gods and others who grant the desired aims: wealth, dharma, liberation, desire, the four human goals, and also bhakti, the supreme fifth human goal.
In front of this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that is, facing him.
To his right he should remember a group of sages, firmly desiring dharma and intent on sacred tradition;

children.text: yogīndrān atha pṛṣṭhe mumukṣamāṇān samādhinā sanakādyān ||
children.translated_text: then behind him, in samādhi, the great yogins such as the <s>Sanakas</s>, who desire liberation.
On his right he should also remember a gathering of sages.
It means: one whose desire for dharma is firm.
On his left, then, he should remember the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>, together with their beloved wives,

children.text: sakinnarān apsarasaś ca mukhyāḥ kāmārthino nartanagītavādyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the chief <s>Kinnaras</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, seeking desire by means of dancing, singing, and instrumental music.
He should remember the <s>Yakṣas</s> and the others together with their consorts, that is, along with their wives.
What kind are they? Through dancing and the like they seek kāma, asking for their own respective cherished wishes.

children.text: mukhyāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ urvaśyādyā apsarasaś ca smaret
