children.translated_text: He should also remember the chief <s>Apsarases</s>, the excellent ones such as <s>Urvaśī</s>.
White like a conch, the moon, and jasmine, knowing all āgamas, with a mass of matted hair tawny like a row of lightning flashes,

children.text: tatpādapaṅkajagatām acalāṃ ca bhaktiṃ vāñchantam ujjhitatarānyasamastasaṅgam ||
children.translated_text: desiring firm bhakti directed to his lotus feet, and having utterly abandoned every other attachment;

children.text: tasya śrīkṛṣṇasya pādapaṅkajagatāṃ tadviṣayiṇīm ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is: bhakti that has gone to the lotus feet of that glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that is, bhakti whose object is him.

children.text: ujjhitataro nitarāṃ parityakto 'nyasmin bhaktivyatirikte samaste saṅga āsaktir yena tam
children.translated_text: It describes one by whom every attachment to anything other than bhakti has been completely abandoned.
with delightful mūrchanās occurring in the three grāmas of the seven rāgas, accompanied by many kinds of groups of śrutis,

children.text: saṃprīṇayantam uditābhir amuṃ mahatyā saṃcintayen nabhasi dhātṛsutaṃ munīndram ||
children.translated_text: he should contemplate in the sky the sage-lord, the son of the Creator, pleasing this one with the notes that have arisen from his <s>Mahatī</s>.

children.text: ata eva amuṃ śrīkṛṣṇaṃ mahatyākhyayā kacchapikayā svakīyavīṇayā prīṇayantam
children.translated_text: Thus, he should contemplate him as pleasing glorious <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with the instrument called <s>Mahatī</s>, his own vīṇā.

children.text: kābhiḥ nānāvidhaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadbhedātmako yaḥ śrutigaṇo nādasamūhas tenānvitā ye sapta rāgāḥ niṣādādisvarā meghanādavasantādirāgā vā teṣu vā grāmatrayī tatra grāmāṇāṃ trayāṇāṃ samāhāras tasyāṃ gatāḥ prāptā yā manoharā mūrchanās tābhiḥ
children.translated_text: With what? With delightful mūrchanās: the various groups of śrutis, collections of tones of thirty-six kinds, accompany the seven rāgas, whether the notes beginning with niṣāda or rāgas such as meghanāda and vasanta; within them are the three grāmas, and in that aggregate of the three grāmas the charming mūrchanās have arrived.

children.text: kimbhūtābhiḥ uditābhiḥ svayam eva prākaṭyaṃ prāptābhiḥ
children.translated_text: What sort are they? Uditā means arisen, having become manifest of themselves.
Or the connection may be: arisen from the <s>Mahatī</s>.

children.text: ata eva munīndraṃ munigaṇaśreṣṭhaṃ dhātṛsutaṃ śrīnāradaṃ nabhasi samyak cintayet
children.translated_text: Therefore one should properly contemplate in the sky glorious <s>Nārada</s>, the son of <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the best of the hosts of sages.
In the <s>Śrī Gautamīya-tantra</s>:
Now I shall proclaim the meditation that destroys all sins:
on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, wearing yellow garments and having eyes like lotuses;
auspicious, with red eyes and lips, and with red hands, feet, and nails;
with his chest illuminated by the <s>Kaustubha</s>, adorned with many jewels;
beautiful with a necklace strung with pearls shining in that radiance;
with a crown gleaming from the light of many jewels, and possessing divine splendor;
encircled with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and earrings;
bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> on his chest and adorned with lovely anklets and the rest;
and with waist-cords and rings made variegated by many jewels;
wearing a crest made of peacock feathers and adorned with forest flowers;
ornamented with a forest garland bound with kadamba blossoms;
resembling the pure sky that delights the moon and stars.

children.text: veṇuṃ gṛhītvā hastābhyāṃ mukhe saṃyojya saṃsthitam
children.translated_text: holding a flute with both hands, placing it at his mouth, and standing there,
<s>Hari</s>, singing with divine songs and standing in the midst of the cowherd settlement;
surrounded by a hundred maidens as though fallen from heaven,
endowed with every auspicious mark and shining with beauty;

children.text: śubhaṃ jaganmaṅgalarūpaṃ tasya kaustubhasya dhāmnā tejasā vilasantībhir muktābhir ācchannena saṃveṣṭitena hāreṇa upaśobhitam
children.translated_text: auspicious, having a form that brings blessing to the world, and adorned by a necklace covered and encircled with pearls shining by the radiance of that <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel;
Or the reading is "bound with pearls."
adorned with a waist-cord and rings;

children.text: sacandrābhis tārābhir ānandaṃ sukhakaraṃ yad vimalam ambaraṃ vyoma tatsadṛśam
children.translated_text: like the pure sky, an expanse with moon and stars that brings joy and happiness;
Here, in the place of the moon, the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel is to be understood.
In the place of the stars is the kadamba garland.
In the place of the sky, the glorious surface of his chest is to be supplied.

children.text: svargād iva paribhraṣṭānāṃ paramasundarīṇām ity arthaḥ
children.translated_text: The meaning is: "of supremely beautiful women, as though fallen from heaven."
surrounded by a hundred such maidens, the glorious young cowherd women.
The word "hundred" here denotes an innumerable multitude.

children.text: mohanaṃ sarvagopīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ ca gavām api
children.translated_text: enchanting all the gopīs and all the cows as well,

children.text: lelihyamānaṃ vatsaiś ca dhenubhiś ca samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: being licked all around by calves and by milch cows;
by siddhas, gandharvas, yakṣas, apsarases, and birds,
by gods, asuras, humans, immobile beings, and serpents too,
and by deer and vidyādharas, being gazed upon by those who are greatly astonished;
by <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and the wise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,
by <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and likewise <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
by <s>Dakṣa</s>, by <s>Śaunaka</s> and <s>Atri</s>, and by the siddha <s>Kapila</s>,
and by the chief sages beginning with <s>Sanaka</s>, even those who have gone to <s>Brahmaloka</s>;

children.text: anyair api ca saṃyuktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyāyed aharniśam ||
children.translated_text: one should meditate day and night on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, attended by others also.
Briefly, also in the <s>Śrī Sanatkumāra-kalpa</s>:

May he protect us: he whose splendor is like an opening kalāya flower, whose mass of hair shines with the feathers of the enemy of snakes, whose graceful body is adored as a festival for the eyes of the gopīs, and who is surrounded by groups of cowherds and cows;
that god, the son of <s>Devakī</s>, whose moonlike form rivals his splendid lotus-face, who wears yellow garments, and who has taken away people's composure with the sound of his flute.

children.text: asau anirvacanīyamāhātmyaḥ śrīdevakīnandano devo naḥ asmān avyāt rakṣatu
children.translated_text: May that god, <s>Śrī Devakīnandana</s>, of inexpressible greatness, protect us.

children.text: kalāyasya tatpuṣpasyeva dyutiḥ śyāmā kāntir yasya saḥ
children.translated_text: He is one whose dark beauty is like the splendor of the kalāya flower.

children.text: dhyātvaivaṃ bhagavantaṃ taṃ saṃprārthya ca yathāsukham
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on that Blessed One and prayed to him as one wishes,

children.text: ādau sampūjayet sarvair upacāraiś ca mānasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should first worship him with all mental offerings.
Those offerings that are to be described separately in external worship
should all be imagined in the inner worship according to one's preference.
In the <s>Śrī Nārada-pañcarātra</s>:
Welcome, O Lord of gods; be present nearby, O <s>Keśava</s>.
Accept the mental worship of those who contemplate you as you truly are.

children.text: athopacārair bāhyaiś ca svātmany eva sthitaṃ prabhum
children.translated_text: Then, worshiping with external offerings the Lord who abides in oneself,
one should first establish the conch according to the true tradition.
Having drawn a triangular maṇḍala on the ground in front of oneself to the left,
the wise person should place there the conch with its stand, washed by the astra-mantra.
Into the conch he should put sandal paste, flowers, and unbroken rice with the heart-mantra.

children.text: vyutkrāntair mātṛkārṇais taṃ śiro'ntaiḥ kena pūrayet ||
children.translated_text: He should fill it with water by means of the reversed letters of the mātṛkā, together with the mantras ending in the head-mantra.
With the syllable ma furnished with the bindu, he should worship the fire-disc on its base,
and with the syllable a he should worship the solar disc in the conch.
With the syllable u he should likewise worship the lunar disc in the water.
With the tīrtha-mantra he should invoke the sacred waters, and also the solar disc.
Having also invoked <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> from the lotus of the heart, he should inspect it with the gālinī-mudrā by means of the śikhā-mantra.
Having looked within with the eye-mantra, he should cover it with the armor-mantra.

children.text: kuryān nyāsaṃ jale mūlamantrāṅgānāṃ tato diśaḥ
children.translated_text: He should perform nyāsa in the water of the limbs of the root-mantra, and then, having bound the directions,
he should make it nectar with the astra-mantra, and then with the dhenu-mudrā.
Having protected that water with the cakra-mudrā and covered it with the matsya-mudrā,

children.text: ācchādya saṃspṛśan śaṅkhaṃ japen mūlaṃ tato 'ṣṭaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should touch the conch and then recite the root-mantra eight times.

children.text: taj jalaṃ prokṣaṇīpātre kiṃcit kṣiptvā trir ukṣayet
children.translated_text: Putting a little of that water into the sprinkling vessel, he should sprinkle it three times.
With the remainder of it he should sprinkle the ritual materials and his own body as well.
The little fingers and thumbs of the two hands are joined with each other;
the forefingers, middle fingers, and ring fingers are held together, bent, and arranged.
This mudrā is called gālinī, and it is moved over the conch.
Then, after discarding what remains inside, with water from the vardhanikā vessel

children.text: punar āpūrya kṛṣṇāgre nyased ācārataḥ satām ||
children.translated_text: he should again fill the conch and place it before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, according to the practice of the good.

children.text: gurūn mūrdhni gaṇeśaṃ ca mūlādhāre'bhipūjya tam
children.translated_text: Having worshiped the gurus on his head and <s>Gaṇeśa</s> in the mūlādhāra,
one should worship the pīṭha within oneself according to the pīṭha-nyāsa.

children.text: tato japan kāmabījaṃ tristhānasthaṃ paraṃ mahaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, while reciting the kāma-bīja, one should contemplate the supreme light abiding in the three places,
consisting of the root-mantra and united into one with the bīja.
And, through the five-limbed nyāsa, having conceived that as one's chosen deity made manifest with form,
he should place the pañcāṅga and other nyāsas in him just as in himself.

children.text: kuryur bhagavati prādurbhūte kṛṣṇe ca vaiṣṇavāḥ
children.translated_text: When the Blessed One has become manifest as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, Vaiṣṇavas should perform
those respective nyāsas for the non-difference of the mantra from the Blessed One.
Some place the tattvas and other principles, the unmanifest ones, as stated,
with the mantra-syllables such as svara and haṃsa, on the ornaments of the Lord in order.

children.text: tasmin pīṭhe tam āsīnaṃ bhagavantaṃ vibhāvayan
children.translated_text: Visualizing that Blessed One seated on that pīṭha,

children.text: āsanādyais tu puṣpāntair yathāvidhy arcayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise person should worship him properly with offerings beginning with the seat and ending with flowers.

children.text: tato mukhe'rcayed veṇuṃ vanamālāṃ ca vakṣasi
children.translated_text: Then he should worship the flute at his mouth and the forest-garland on his chest.
Above the right breast he should mark the <s>śrīvatsa</s>, and on the left, in that same place, the <s>kaustubha</s>.
A Vaiṣṇava, anointing this with sandal paste by means of the ring finger,
should draw twelve tilaka marks in the shape of lamp-flames, as before.
Having worshiped him as prescribed with five handfuls of flowers,

children.text: dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ ca naivedyaṃ mukhavāsādi cārpayet ||
children.translated_text: he should offer incense, a lamp, food-offering, mouth-fragrance, and the rest.

children.text: gītādibhiś ca saṃtoṣya kṛṣṇam asmai tato 'khilam
children.translated_text: And having satisfied <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with songs and the like, he should then offer all this to him.

children.text: aśakto bahir arcāyām arpayej japam ācaret ||
children.translated_text: If he is unable to perform external worship, he should offer it inwardly and practice recitation.
In the <s>Vaiṣṇava Tantra</s>:
Thousands of horse sacrifices and hundreds of <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifices
do not equal even a sixteenth part of a single yoga of meditation.
In the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>, in the manifestation of <s>Śrī Vāmana</s>:
By the mere utterance of whose name all calamities perish,

children.text: stotrair vā arhaṇābhir vā kimu dhyānena kathyate ||
children.translated_text: what need be said of hymns, acts of worship, or meditation?
In the <s>Nāradapañcarātra</s>, in the dialogue of the Blessed Lord and <s>Nārada</s>:
This mental sacrifice removes the fear of old age and disease;
it pacifies the flood of all sins and brings about being and non-being, O twice-born one.
Through the yoga of constant practice it releases one from bondage to the body.

children.text: yaś caivaṃ parayā bhaktyā sakṛt kuryān mahāmate
children.translated_text: And whoever performs it once in this way, with supreme devotion, O great-minded sage,

children.text: kramoditena vidhinā tasya tuṣyāmy ahaṃ mune ||
children.translated_text: according to the procedure stated in sequence: with him I am pleased.

children.text: smaraṇadhyānayoḥ pūrvaṃ māhātmyaṃ likhitaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: The greatness of remembrance and meditation that was written previously
should be understood here as greater still, because those two are limbs of inner sacrifice.
Thus, according to one's tradition, according to one's ability, and for as long as the mind is pleased,
one should first perform inner worship and then begin the external worship.
And so it has been said by <s>Nārada</s>:
Having meditated with the sixteen mental services
and having properly performed the worship, one should carry out external worship.

children.text: anujñāṃ dehi bhagavan bahir yoge mama prabho
children.translated_text: O Blessed Lord, O my Lord, grant me permission for the external rite.

children.text: śrīkṛṣṇam ity anujñāpya bahiḥ pūjāṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: Having asked <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> for permission in this way, one should perform the external worship.

children.text: tatra tv anekaśaḥ santi pūjāsthānāni tatra ca
children.translated_text: In that regard there are many places of worship,
and there are many kinds of blessed images, as well as <s>śālagrāma</s> stones.
In the <s>Saṃmohana Tantra</s>:
Worship of <s>Hari</s> should be performed in a <s>śālagrāma</s>, in a mantra, in a yantra, on a prepared altar, in images, and so on,

children.text: hareḥ pūjā tu kartavyā kevale bhūtale na tu ||
children.translated_text: but not on the bare ground alone.
In the Eleventh Book, in the dialogue of <s>Śrīmad Uddhava</s>:

children.text: sūryo 'gnir brāhmaṇā gāvo vaiṣṇavaḥ khaṃ maruj jalam
children.translated_text: The sun, fire, brāhmaṇas, cows, a Vaiṣṇava, space, wind, water,

children.text: bhūr ātmā sarvabhūtāni bhadra pūjāpadāni me ||
children.translated_text: earth, the self, and all beings, O fortunate one, are my places of worship.

children.text: sūrye tu vidyayā trayyā haviṣāgnau yajeta mām
children.translated_text: In the sun one should worship me with the threefold Vedic knowledge; in fire, with oblation;

children.text: ātithyena tu viprāgrye goṣv aṅga yavasādinā ||
children.translated_text: in an eminent brāhmaṇa, with hospitality; in cows, dear one, with grass and the like.
In a Vaiṣṇava, one should worship me by honoring him as a kinsman; in the heart and in space, through steadfast meditation;
in the wind, by understanding it as the chief life-breath; in water, with substances preceded by water.
On the prepared altar one should worship me with the hearts of mantras; in the self, the Self, with enjoyments;
and in all beings, the knower of the field, through equal regard.
In these sacred seats, meditating on my form as joined with conch, discus, mace, and lotus,

children.text: yuktaṃ caturbhujaṃ śāntaṃ dhyāyann arcet samāhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: four-armed and peaceful, one should worship with collected mind.
There also:

children.text: śailī dārumayī lauhī lepyā lekhyā ca saikatī
children.translated_text: Made of stone, made of wood, made of metal, made of clay or paste, painted, and made of sand,
made in the mind and made of gems: the image is held to be eightfold.
The consecrated image, the living temple, is twofold: movable and immovable.
In fixed worship, O <s>Uddhava</s>, dismissal and invocation do not occur.

children.text: asthirāyāṃ vikalpaḥ syāt sthaṇḍile tu bhaved dvayam
children.translated_text: For an unfixed image there may be an option; on a prepared altar both occur.
Bathing is for an image that is not made of paste or clay; elsewhere there is wiping clean.
Because the <s>Gopāla</s> mantra is specified, his blessed image is expected.
Nevertheless, for the satisfaction of Vaiṣṇavas, all blessed images are to be drawn.
In the <s>Śrī Hayaśīrṣa Pañcarātra</s>, in the dialogue of the Blessed <s>Śrī Hayaśīrṣa</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>:
The primal form is <s>Vāsudeva</s>; then he created <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>.

children.text: caturmūrtiḥ paraṃ proktaṃ ekaiko bhidyate tridhā
children.translated_text: The fourfold form is declared supreme; each one is divided into three.
Through the distinctions beginning with <s>Keśava</s>, a set of twelve forms is remembered.
One should place a lotus on the right, and likewise <s>Pāñcajanya</s> above;

children.text: vāmopari gadā yasya cakraṃ cādho vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: for the one whose mace is above on the left and whose discus is arranged below,
this division of the primal form is proclaimed as <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: adharottarabhāvena kṛtam etat tu yatra vai
children.translated_text: Where this is done with the lower and upper positions reversed,
that established image is called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and gives enjoyment and liberation.
For the one whose lotus is below on the left and whose <s>Pāñcajanya</s> is likewise above,

children.text: dakṣiṇordhve gadā yasya cakraṃ cādho vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: whose mace is above on the right and whose discus is arranged below,
this division of the primal form is proclaimed as <s>Mādhava</s>.
For the one whose discus is placed below on the right and whose mace is placed above it,
whose lotus is set above on the left and whose conch is arranged below,
this division of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> is proclaimed as <s>Govinda</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇopari padmaṃ tu gadā cādho vyavasthitā
children.translated_text: The lotus is above on the right, and the mace is arranged below;
this division of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> is named <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇopari śaṅkhaṃ ca cakraṃ cādhaḥ pradarśyate
children.translated_text: The conch is shown above on the right, and the discus is shown below;

children.text: vāmopari tathā padmaṃ gadā cādhaḥ pradarśyate
children.translated_text: likewise, on the left the lotus is shown above and the mace below.
This division of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> has the name <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
The discus is set above on the left, and the conch is shown below;
the left foot reaches the cosmic egg, and the right rests on the back of <s>Śeṣa</s>.
Above on the right is the thousand-spoked discus, and <s>Pāñcajanya</s> is placed below;
one should always fashion <s>Vāmana</s> with a measure of seven tālas.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ dakṣiṇataś cakram adhaḥ padmaṃ vyavasthitam
children.translated_text: Above on the right the discus is arranged, and below the lotus is set.

children.text: padmā padmakarā vāme pārśve yasya vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Padmā</s>, lotus-handed, is stationed at his left side.

children.text: sthito vāpy upaviṣṭo vā sānurāgo vilāsavān
children.translated_text: Whether standing or seated, he is full of affection and graceful charm.
This, indeed, is a variant of <s>Pradyumna</s>, proclaimed as <s>Śrīdhara</s>.
In the upper right is the great discus, and <s>Kaumodakī</s> is placed below it.

children.text: vāmordhve nalinaṃ yasya adhaḥ śaṅkhaṃ virājate
children.translated_text: In whose upper left hand the lotus is, and below it the conch shines;
he should be known as <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>; when installed, he grants all desires.
In the upper right is the lotus, and below it <s>Pāñcajanya</s> likewise;
in the upper left is placed the discus, and <s>Kaumodakī</s> is placed below it.
That image is called <s>Padmanābha</s>; when installed, it bestows liberation.
In the upper right is <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, and below it the lotus;
and in the upper left is <s>Kaumodakī</s>, with the king of weapons placed below.
This is a variant of <s>Aniruddha</s>, remembered as <s>Dāmodara</s>.

children.text: eteṣāṃ tu striyau kārye padmavīṇādhare śubhe ||
children.translated_text: For these, two auspicious female figures should be made, holding a lotus and a vīṇā.
Thus, in order, the twelve beginning with <s>Keśava</s> are the presiding deities of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and the following months.
In the <s>Siddhārthasaṃhitā</s>:
<s>Vāsudeva</s> is regarded as holding a mace, conch, discus, and lotus.

children.text: padmaṃ śaṅkhaṃ tathā cakraṃ gadāṃ vahati keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> bears a lotus, conch, discus, and mace.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ padmaṃ gadāṃ cakraṃ dhatte nārāyaṇaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> always holds a conch, lotus, mace, and discus.

children.text: gadāṃ cakraṃ tathā śaṅkhaṃ padmaṃ vahati mādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s> bears a mace, discus, conch, and lotus.

children.text: cakraṃ padmaṃ tathā śaṅkhaṃ gadāṃ ca puruṣottamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣottama</s> holds a discus, lotus, conch, and mace;

children.text: padmaṃ kaumodakīṃ śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ dhatte'py adhokṣajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Adhokṣaja</s> holds a lotus, <s>Kaumodakī</s>, conch, and discus.
<s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> is remembered as holding a mace, conch, lotus, and discus.

children.text: cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaśaṅkhau govindo dharate bhujaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> bears a discus, mace, lotus, and conch in his arms.

children.text: gadāṃ padmaṃ tathā śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ viṣṇur bibharti yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> bears a mace, lotus, conch, and discus.

children.text: cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ tathā padmaṃ gadāṃ ca madhusūdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madhusūdana</s> holds a discus, conch, lotus, and mace.

children.text: gadāṃ sarojaṃ cakraṃ ca śaṅkhaṃ dhatte'cyutaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s> always holds a mace, lotus, discus, and conch.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ kaumodakīṃ cakram upendraḥ padmam udvahet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Upendra</s> should bear a conch, <s>Kaumodakī</s>, discus, and lotus.
<s>Pradyumna</s> is said to hold a discus, conch, mace, and lotus.

children.text: padmaṃ kaumodakīṃ cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ dhatte trivikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Trivikrama</s> holds a lotus, <s>Kaumodakī</s>, discus, and conch.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ vāmano vahate sadā
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmana</s> always bears a conch, discus, mace, and lotus.

children.text: padmaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ śaṅkhaṃ śrīdharo vahate bhujaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdhara</s> bears a lotus, discus, mace, and conch in his arms.

children.text: cakraṃ padmaṃ gadāṃ śaṅkhaṃ narasiṃho bibharti yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Narasiṃha</s> bears a discus, lotus, mace, and conch.

children.text: padmaṃ sudarśanaṃ śaṅkhaṃ gadāṃ dhatte janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Janārdana</s> holds a lotus, <s>Sudarśana</s>, conch, and mace.
<s>Aniruddha</s> has arms shining with discus, mace, conch, and lotus.

children.text: hṛṣīkeśo gadāṃ cakraṃ padmaṃ śaṅkhaṃ ca dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> should hold a mace, discus, lotus, and conch.

children.text: padmanābho vahet śaṅkhaṃ padmaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Padmanābha</s> should bear a conch, lotus, discus, and mace.

children.text: padmaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ śaṅkhaṃ dhatte dāmodaraḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dāmodara</s> always holds a lotus, discus, mace, and conch.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ sarojaṃ ca gadāṃ vahati yo hariḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> bears a conch, discus, lotus, and mace.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ kaumodakīṃ padmaṃ cakraṃ viṣṇur bibharti yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> bears a conch, <s>Kaumodakī</s>, lotus, and discus.
These images are to be understood according to the order of the lower right hand.
And in the <s>Matsyapurāṇa</s>:
This has been stated in brief, as also the characteristics of images.

children.text: vistareṇa na śaknoti bṛhaspatir api dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even <s>Bṛhaspati</s> cannot describe them in detail, O twice-born ones.
The glorious Vaiṣṇavas devoted to the service of <s>Hari</s>, followers of the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>,
esteem the sacred image highly, because all its limbs are manifest.
One's chosen images should be worshiped with their own respective mantras.
In the form consisting of <s>śālagrāma</s>, however, there is no such restriction.
The image of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is two-armed, cloud-dark, triple-bent, and sweet in form.

children.text: sevyā dhyānānurūpaiś ca mūrtiḥ kṛṣṇasya daivataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be worshiped, together with the deities, in accordance with the meditation.
And the various other glorious images of the avatāras and so on
are to be described later, each according to its own specific form, in the procedure for manifestations.
Here, in the context of daily rites, the procedure for the birth and installation of an image

children.text: vidhir na likhituṃ yogyaḥ sa tu lekhiṣyate'grataḥ ||
children.translated_text: is not suitable to be written; it will be written later.
In the <s>Gautamīyatantra</s>:

children.text: gaṇḍakyāś caiva deśe ca śālagrāmasthalaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: In the region of the <s>Gaṇḍakī</s> there is the great place of <s>śālagrāma</s>.

children.text: pāṣāṇaṃ tadbhavaṃ yat tat śālagrāmam iti smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The stone that arises there is remembered as a <s>śālagrāma</s>.
In the <s>Skandapurāṇa</s>:

children.text: snigdhā kṛṣṇā pāṇḍarā vā pītā nīlā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Smooth, black, white, yellow, and likewise blue,

children.text: vakrā rūkṣā ca raktā ca mahāsthūlā tv alāñchitā ||
children.translated_text: crooked, rough, red, very large, and unmarked;
tawny, mottled, broken, many-disc and single-disc;
large-mouthed, large-disc, or again with an attached disc,
or one with a bound disc, or one with a broken disc and facing downward.
There also:

children.text: snigdhā siddhikarī mantre kṛṣṇā kīrtiṃ dadāti ca
children.translated_text: The smooth one brings success in mantra; the black one gives fame.
The white one burns away sin; the yellow one grants the fruit of a son.
The blue one indicates <s>Lakṣmī</s>; the red one gives disease.
The rough one constantly gives anxiety, and the crooked one gives poverty.

children.text: sthūlā nihanti caivāyur niṣphalā tu alāñchitā
children.translated_text: The large one destroys life, while the unmarked one is fruitless.
A tawny, mottled, broken, many-disc, or single-disc stone,
one large-mouthed, large-disc, or again with an attached disc,

children.text: baddhacakrāthavā yā syād bhagnacakrā tv adhomukhī
children.translated_text: one with a bound disc, or one with a broken disc and facing downward:

children.text: pūjayed yaḥ pramādena duḥkham eva labheta saḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever worships such a one through negligence obtains only suffering.
And in the <s>Agnipurāṇa</s>:
Likewise one with the mouth of a serpent, broken, irregular, or with a bound disc;
one with distorted whorls at the navel, and likewise the <s>Nārasiṃhī</s> type;

children.text: kapilā vibhramāvartā rekhāvartā ca yā śilā
children.translated_text: a tawny stone, one with confused whorls, or one with line-shaped whorls:

children.text: duḥkhadā sā tu vijñeyā sukhadā na kadācana ||
children.translated_text: that should be known as a giver of suffering, and never as a giver of happiness.

children.text: snigdhā śyāmā tathā muktāmāyā vā samacakrikā
children.translated_text: A smooth, dark stone, or one pearl-like, or with even discs...
The forms called <s>Ghoṇī</s> and <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Gambhīrā</s>, and likewise <s>Saṃpuṭā</s>,
the subtle form, the formless one, the one facing forward, and the giver of accomplishment;
that stone which is the size of an āmalaka fruit and is cupped in both hands
is auspicious; such a stone should be worshiped with care.

children.text: iṣṭā tu yasya yā mūrtiḥ sa tāṃ yatnena pūjayet
children.translated_text: Whichever form is dear to a person, he should carefully worship that one.

children.text: pūjite phalam āpnoti ihaloke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: When it is worshiped, he obtains its fruit in this world and in the next.
For it has been said by the Blessed Lord in the <s>Brāhma</s>:
A stone arisen from a <s>śālagrāma</s>, though cut, split, broken, broken at the side, or cleft,
does not bring fault.
And by <s>Śrī Rudra</s> in the <s>Skānda</s>:

children.text: khaṇḍitaṃ truṭitaṃ bhagnaṃ śālagrāme na doṣabhāk
children.translated_text: In a <s>śālagrāma</s> there is no fault if it is cut, torn, or broken.

children.text: iṣṭā tu yasya yā mūrtiḥ sa tāṃ yatnena pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Whichever form is dear to a person, he should carefully worship that one.
Likewise:

children.text: cakraṃ vā kevalaṃ tatra padmena saha saṃyutam
children.translated_text: There may be only a discus there, or one joined together with a lotus;

children.text: kevalā vanamālā vā harir lakṣmyā saha sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or there may be only a forest-garland, or <s>Hari</s> standing together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Among those, the smooth and the rest are regarded as principal, while the red and the rest are regarded as secondary.

children.text: mukhyābhāve tv amukhyā hi pūjyā ity ucyate paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in the absence of the principal ones, the secondary ones too are to be worshiped; so others say.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>, in the dialogue of the Blessed Lord and <s>Brahmā</s>:
I always dwell, O <s>Brahman</s>, in the abode called <s>Śālagrāma</s>.
Hear there the names belonging to me, distinguished by the marks of the chariot-wheel.
When an even discus is seen at the region of the opening, with no interior mark,
that should be known as <s>Vāsudeva</s>, whitish in appearance and very beautiful.

children.text: dve cakre ekalagne tu pūrvabhāgas tu puṣkalaḥ
children.translated_text: When two discuses are joined together as one, and the front part is ample,
it should be known as called <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, reddish in appearance and very beautiful.

children.text: pradyumnaḥ sūkṣmacakras tu pītadīptis tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Pradyumna</s> has a small discus and likewise a yellow radiance;

children.text: śuṣiraṃ chidrabahulaṃ dīrghākāraṃ tu tad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: it should have a cavity, many holes, and an elongated shape.
<s>Aniruddha</s>, however, is dark-blue in appearance, round, and very beautiful;

children.text: rekhātrayaṃ tu tad dvāri pṛṣṭhaṃ padmena lāñchitam ||
children.translated_text: there are three lines at its opening, and the back is marked with a lotus.

children.text: saubhāgyaṃ keśavo dadyāt catuṣkoṇo bhavet tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> should bestow good fortune; he is the one that is quadrangular.
One should know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as dark, with a raised navel-discus.
Furnished with long lines, with a broad cavity on the right,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ mukhaṃ vijānīyāt dvāre ca harirūpiṇam ||
children.translated_text: one should recognize it as having an upward-facing mouth and, at the opening, the form of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: kāmadaṃ mokṣadaṃ caiva arthadaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: It grants desire, grants liberation, and especially grants wealth.
<s>Parameṣṭhin</s> is reddish in appearance and furnished with a lotus and discus.
Likewise it is shaped like a bilva fruit on the back and has a very ample cavity.

children.text: kṛṣṇavarṇas tathā viṣṇuḥ sthūle cakre suśobhanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, dark in color, is beautiful with a large discus.
He is to be worshiped with celibate discipline; otherwise he becomes a giver of obstacles.
And somewhere it is said:
<s>Narasiṃha</s> is tawny, with a broad and beautiful discus.
One whose authority is celibate discipline may worship him; otherwise worship should not be performed.
<s>Narasiṃha</s> has three spots; <s>Kapila</s> has five spots.
He should be worshiped with celibate discipline; otherwise he gives every obstacle.
There are two large discuses in the middle, of the color of molasses, lac, and liquor.
Above the opening there is also a beautiful lotus-shaped line.

children.text: sphuṭitaṃ viṣamaṃ cakraṃ nārasiṃhaṃ tu kāpilam
children.translated_text: The <s>Nārasiṃha</s> that is <s>Kapila</s> has a cracked and irregular discus.

children.text: sampūjya muktim āpnoti saṃgrāme vijayī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Having worshiped it, one attains liberation and becomes victorious in battle.
And in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s> of the <s>Padma</s>:

children.text: yasya dīrghaṃ mukhaṃ pūrvakathitair lakṣaṇair yutam
children.translated_text: The one whose mouth is long and furnished with the previously described marks,

children.text: rekhāś ca keśarākārā nārasiṃho mato hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whose lines are shaped like a mane, is indeed regarded as <s>Nārasiṃha</s>.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>:

children.text: vārāhaṃ śaktiliṅge ca cakre ca viṣame smṛte
children.translated_text: <s>Vārāha</s> is remembered when there is a spear-mark and an irregular discus;
it is large, like a sapphire, auspicious, and marked with three lines.
And in the <s>Padma</s> there itself:
Bent and shaped like a boar, adorned with discus-lines,
that is called <s>Vārāha</s>, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
In the <s>Brāhma</s> itself:
That stone which is long, golden in color, and adorned with three spots
should be known as called <s>Matsya</s>, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
And somewhere it is said:

children.text: matsyarūpaṃ tu deveśaṃ dīrghākāraṃ tu yad bhavet
children.translated_text: If the lord of gods has the form of a fish and an elongated shape,
joined with three spots and shining beautifully with the color of bronze,
in the <s>Brāhma</s> itself:
<s>Kūrma</s> is also raised on the back and filled with round whorls;

children.text: haritaṃ varṇam ādhatte kaustubhena ca cihnitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it takes on a green color and is marked with the <s>Kaustubha</s>.
And in the <s>Padma</s> there itself:

children.text: kūrmākārā ca cakrāṅkā śilā kūrmaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A stone shaped like a tortoise and marked with a discus is proclaimed as <s>Kūrma</s>.
In the <s>Brāhma</s> itself:
<s>Hayagrīva</s> is hook-shaped; lines go near the discus.
It is furnished with many discuses and cloud-dark blue on the back.
And somewhere it is said:
On <s>Hayagrīva</s>, in the hook-shaped form, there are indeed five lines.
In one scattered with many spots, blue forms are seen.
And in the <s>Padma</s> there itself:

children.text: hāyagrīvā yathā lambā rekhāṅkā yā śilā bhavet
children.translated_text: Whichever stone is long like <s>Hayagrīva</s> and marked with lines,
so that one is <s>Hayagrīva</s>; when worshiped, it grants knowledge.
Moreover:

children.text: aśvākṛti mukhaṃ yasya sākṣamālaṃ śiras tathā
children.translated_text: The one whose mouth has the form of a horse and whose head has a rosary,

children.text: padmākṛtir bhaved vāpi hayaśīrṣas tv asau mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or else has the form of a lotus, is considered <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s>.
In the <s>Brāhma</s> itself:

children.text: vaikuṇṭham maṇivarṇābhaṃ cakram ekaṃ tathā dhvajam
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> has the appearance of a jewel, one discus, and likewise a banner.
Above the opening there is also a beautiful lotus-shaped line.

children.text: śrīdharas tu tathā devaś cihnito vanamālayā
children.translated_text: The god <s>Śrīdhara</s>, likewise, is marked with a forest-garland.
He has the shape of a kadamba flower and is adorned with five lines.
<s>Vāmana</s> is proclaimed as round and very short,
resembling the flower of the atasī and beautifully adorned with a spot.
And elsewhere:

children.text: vāmanākhyo bhaved devo hrasvo yaḥ syān mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: The god called <s>Vāmana</s> is the one that is short and of great brilliance.
With a discus above and a discus below, when worshiped, he grants the desired object.
In the <s>Brāhma</s> itself:
Likewise the god <s>Sudarśana</s> is dark-colored and of great splendor;

children.text: vāmapārśve gadācakre rekhe caiva tu dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: on the left side are the mace and discus, and lines indeed on the right.
In the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s> of the <s>Pādma</s>:

children.text: cakrākāreṇa paṅktiḥ sā yatra rekhāmayī bhavet
children.translated_text: Where there is a row in the form of a discus, consisting of lines,

children.text: sa sudarśana ity evaṃ khyātaḥ pūjāphalapradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is famed as <s>Sudarśana</s>, and it bestows the fruit of worship.
In the <s>Brāhma</s>:

children.text: dāmodaras tathā sthūlo madhye cakraṃ pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Dāmodara</s> is thick, with a discus set in the middle;

children.text: dūrvābhaṃ dvārasaṃkīrṇaṃ pītā rekhā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: it is green like dūrvā grass, constricted at the opening, and likewise has a yellow line.
And in that same place in the <s>Pādma</s>:

children.text: uparyadhaś ca cakre dve nātidīrghaṃ mukhe bilam
children.translated_text: There are two discuses, above and below, and a hole at the mouth that is not very long;

children.text: cakre ca rekhā lambaikā sa ca dāmodaraḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in the discus there is one long line: that is remembered as <s>Dāmodara</s>.
And elsewhere:

children.text: sthūlo dāmodaro jñeyaḥ sūkṣmarandhro bhavet tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: One should know as <s>Dāmodara</s> that which is thick and has a small aperture;

children.text: cakre ca madhyadeśasthe pūjitaḥ sukhadaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: when worshipped, with its discus located in the middle region, it always gives happiness.
That called <s>Ananta</s> is of various colors and marked by the coil of a serpent;
that is to be recognized as <s>Ananta</s>, bestowing the fruit of every worship.
And in that same place in the <s>Pādma</s>:
It has an endless discus and is also indicated by many marks;
that is to be recognized as <s>Ananta</s>, bestowing the fruit of every worship.
On the summit is seen a liṅga arising from the <s>śālagrāma</s>;
that whose name is <s>Yogeśvara</s> removes the sin of brahmahatyā.
The reddish one called <s>Padmanābha</s>, furnished with a lotus-canopy,

children.text: tulasyā pūjayen nityaṃ daridras tv īśvaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one should worship daily with tulasī; even a poor man becomes a lord.
One should designate as the one called <s>Hiraṇya</s> a moon-shaped stone with a network of rays,
rich in golden lines and shining with the brilliance of crystal.
Moreover:
The god with the shape of a half-moon is called <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>;

children.text: tam arcya labhate svargaṃ viṣayāṃś ca samīhitān ||
children.translated_text: having worshipped him, one obtains heaven and the desired enjoyments.

children.text: vāmapārśve same cakre kṛṣṇavarṇaḥ sa bindukaḥ
children.translated_text: On the left side there are even discuses; it is black in color and has a dot.
It is known as <s>Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha</s>, bestowing the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.
Likewise the god <s>Trivikrama</s> is dark-colored and of great splendor;

children.text: vāmapārśve tathā cakre rekhā caiva tu dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: on the left side are likewise discuses, and on the right indeed a line.
The stone adorned with a forest-garland turning clockwise,
which is called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, gives wealth, grain, and happiness.
In the <s>Gautamīya</s>:

children.text: bahubhir janmabhiḥ puṇyair yadi kṛṣṇaśilāṃ labhet
children.translated_text: If, through merits accumulated over many births, one obtains a <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-stone,

children.text: goṣpadena tu cihnena janus tena samāpyate ||
children.translated_text: then by the mark of a cow's hoofprint one's birth comes to an end.
Where four lines are seen, running near the side,

children.text: dve cakre madhyadeśe tu sā śilā tu caturmukhā ||
children.translated_text: and two discuses in the middle region, that stone is four-faced.
Moreover, in that same place in the <s>Pādma</s>:

children.text: vajrakīṭodbhavā rekhāḥ paṅktībhūtāś ca yatra vai
children.translated_text: Where there are lines produced by the vajra-worm, arranged in rows,
that <s>śālagrāma</s> stone is called <s>Viṣṇupañjara</s>.
A row of lines coiled like a serpent is <s>Śeṣaka</s>.

children.text: padmākāre ca paṅktī dve madhye lambā ca rekhikā
children.translated_text: When there are two rows in the form of a lotus and a long little line in the middle,

children.text: garuḍaḥ sa tu vijñeyaś catuścakro janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is to be recognized as <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> with four discuses.
Having four discuses, a small opening, and a belly marked with a forest-garland,
the glorious <s>Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa</s> bestows the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.
The <s>śālagrāma</s> stones endowed with these marks are auspicious;

children.text: yāś ca tāsv api sūkṣmāḥ syus tāḥ praśastakarāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and among them, those which are small are remembered as producing excellence.
And likewise, in that same place, in the dialogue of the blessed Lord with <s>Brahmā</s>:

children.text: yathā yathā śilā sūkṣmā mahat puṇyaṃ tathā tathā
children.translated_text: The smaller and smaller the stone is, the greater and greater is the merit;
therefore one should worship it daily for the attainment of dharma, desire, and wealth.

children.text: tatrāpy āmalakītulyā sūkṣmā cātīva yā bhavet
children.translated_text: And among them, O <s>Brahman</s>, the one that is very small, equal to an āmalakī fruit,

children.text: tasyām eva sadā brahman śriyā saha vasāmy aham ||
children.translated_text: in that very one I always dwell together with <s>Śrī</s>.
From touching a <s>śālagrāma</s> stone there is destruction of sins from ten million births;
how much more worship there, which brings about the presence of <s>Hari</s>.
In the <s>Māgha-māhātmya</s> of the <s>Pādma</s>, in that same place:
He who worships <s>Hari</s> in the discus born from a <s>śālagrāma</s> stone,
by him a thousand rājasūya sacrifices have been performed every day.

children.text: yad āmananti vedāntā brahma nirguṇam acyutam
children.translated_text: That imperishable, qualityless brahman which the Vedāntas proclaim
becomes gracious to human beings through worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.
As fire abiding in a great piece of wood becomes manifest when it is churned,

children.text: yathā tathā harir vyāpī śālagrāme prakāśate ||
children.translated_text: so <s>Hari</s>, though all-pervading, becomes manifest in the <s>śālagrāma</s>.
Even those of sinful conduct, unqualified for rites,
who worship the <s>śālagrāma</s>, O Vaiśya, do not go to Yama's abode.

children.text: na tathā ramate lakṣmyāṃ na tathā nijamandire
children.translated_text: He does not delight so much in <s>Lakṣmī</s>, nor so much in his own temple,
as he always delights in the discus of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: agnihotraṃ hutaṃ tena dattā pṛthvī sasāgarā
children.translated_text: By him the agnihotra has been offered, and the earth together with the oceans has been given away,
by whom <s>Hari</s> has been worshipped in the discus born from a <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: kāmaiḥ krodhaiḥ pralobhaiś ca vyāpto yo 'tra narādhamaḥ
children.translated_text: A lowest man here who is overcome by desires, angers, and greeds,
even he goes to the world of <s>Hari</s> through worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: yaḥ pūjayati govindaṃ śālagrāme sadā naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man who always worships <s>Govinda</s> in the <s>śālagrāma</s>

children.text: āhūtasamplavaṃ yāvat na sa pracyavate divaḥ ||
children.translated_text: does not fall from heaven until the final dissolution that has been summoned.

children.text: vinā tīrthair vinā dānair vinā yajñair vinā matim
children.translated_text: Without sacred bathing places, without gifts, without sacrifices, without understanding,
a man, O Vaiśya, goes to liberation through worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.
Hell, residence in the womb, animal birth, and birth as a worm:
not even a sinner goes to these, O Vaiśya, if he worships <s>Acyuta</s> in the <s>śālagrāma</s>.
One who knows the mantra of the initiation rite and offers bali in the discus

children.text: sa yāti vaiṣṇavaṃ dhāma satyaṃ satyaṃ mayoditam ||
children.translated_text: goes to the Vaiṣṇava abode. Truly, truly, this has been spoken by me.

children.text: naivedyair vividhaiḥ puṣpair dhūpair dīpair vilepanaiḥ
children.translated_text: With various food offerings, flowers, incenses, lamps, and unguents,
and with songs, instruments, hymns, and the like, worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone

children.text: kurute mānavo yas tu kalau bhaktiparāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: is performed by the human being who, in the Kali age, is devoted to bhakti.
He delights in the presence of <s>Hari</s> for thousands of crores of kalpas.

children.text: liṅgais tu koṭibhir dṛṣṭair yat phalaṃ pūjitais tu taiḥ
children.translated_text: The fruit that comes from seeing and worshiping crores of <s>liṅgas</s>
is that fruit here, even from a single worship of a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.
Where <s>Keśava</s>, having the form of a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, abides,
there are the gods, asuras, yakṣas, and the fourteen worlds.

children.text: śālagrāmaśilāyāṃ tu yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who performs <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor rite) at a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,

children.text: pitaras tasya tiṣṭhanti tṛptāḥ kalpaśataṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: his ancestors remain satisfied in heaven for a hundred kalpas.
Where there is a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, that <s>tīrtha</s> (holy place) extends for three <s>yojanas</s>.

children.text: yatra dānaṃ japo homaḥ sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: There, giving, <s>japa</s> (recitation), and <s>homa</s> (fire offering) all become multiplied by a crore.
Around a <s>Śālagrāma</s>, within the measure of a <s>krośa</s> on every side,
even a man of Kīkaṭa who dies goes to the mansion of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, O man.
One who gives as the highest gift a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone marked with a discus
has thereby given the circle of the earth, together with its mountains, groves, and forests.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Skanda</s>:
In the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone are the three worlds, with moving and unmoving beings,

children.text: mayā saha mahāsena līnaṃ tiṣṭhati sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: and together with me, O <s>Mahāsena</s>, they always remain absorbed there.

children.text: dṛṣā praṇamitā yena snāpitā pūjitā tathā
children.translated_text: By the one who has seen it, bowed to it, bathed it, and worshiped it,
merit equal to a crore sacrifices and the fruit of a crore cows is obtained.
Even one attached to desire and always devoid of devotional feeling,
if he fully worships a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, O brahmin, becomes connected with <s>Acyuta</s>.
The image of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone destroys crores of killings,

children.text: smṛtaṃ saṃkīrtitaṃ dhyātaṃ pūjitaṃ ca namaskṛtam ||
children.translated_text: when it is remembered, praised aloud, meditated on, worshiped, and bowed to.
On seeing a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, sins depart in many ways,

children.text: siṃhaṃ dṛṣṭvā yathā yānti vane mṛgagaṇā bhayāt ||
children.translated_text: just as herds of deer in the forest flee in fear on seeing a lion.
When a man bows in the worship of a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,

children.text: pāpāni vilayaṃ yānti tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā ||
children.translated_text: his sins dissolve, just as darkness does at sunrise.
Whether attached to desire or angry, if one performs worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,

children.text: bhaktyā vā yadi vābhaktyā kṛtvā muktim avāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: with devotion or even without devotion, he obtains liberation.
There is no fear of <s>Vaivasvata</s>, nor of death and birth,
for one who tells the story of <s>Viṣṇu</s> before a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.
The man who performs worship of a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone with songs, instruments, and hymns,

children.text: kurute mānavo yas tu kalau bhaktiparāyaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: who in the <s>Kali</s> age is wholly devoted to bhakti,
delights in the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> for thousands of crores of kalpas.
When men bow to the <s>Śālagrāma</s>, even without devotional feeling,

children.text: bhayaṃ naiva kariṣyanti madbhaktā ye narā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: those men on earth who are my devotees will have no fear at all.
Those who are extremely proud of the power of being my devotees, and who do not bow to my lord,

children.text: vāsudevaṃ na te jñeyā madbhaktāḥ pāpino hi te ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, should not be known as my devotees; they are indeed sinners.

children.text: śālagrāmaśilāyāṃ tu sadā putra vasāmy aham
children.translated_text: O son, I always dwell in the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: dattaṃ devena tuṣṭena svasthānaṃ mama bhaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This, my own abode, was given by the satisfied god out of devotion to me.

children.text: padmakoṭisahasrais tu pūjite mayi yat phalam
children.translated_text: The fruit that comes when I am worshiped with thousands of crores of lotuses,
that fruit is multiplied by a crore in worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: pūjito 'haṃ na tair martyair namito 'haṃ na tair naraiḥ
children.translated_text: I have not been worshiped by those mortals; I have not been bowed to by those men
by whom worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone has not been performed in the mortal world.
One who performs my worship before a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,
by him I am worshiped continually for twenty-one yugas.
What use are hundreds of <s>liṅgas</s> worshiped, if they are devoid of devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
if the image of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone has not been worshiped, O son?

children.text: anarhaṃ mama naivedyaṃ patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: Even an unfit offering to me, leaf, flower, fruit, or water,
when placed on a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, all goes to purity.

children.text: yo hi māheśvaro bhūtvā vaiṣṇavaliṅgam uttamam
children.translated_text: One who has become a <s>Māheśvara</s> but hates the excellent Vaiṣṇava <s>liṅga</s>

children.text: dveṣṭi vai yāti narakaṃ yāvad indrāś caturdaśa ||
children.translated_text: goes to hell for as long as fourteen <s>Indras</s> reign.
When the image arisen from a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone has been worshiped even once,

children.text: muktiṃ prayānti manujā nūnaṃ sāṅkhyena varjitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: people surely attain liberation, even without <s>sāṅkhya</s> (philosophical discernment).

children.text: malliṅgaiḥ koṭibhir dṛṣṭair yat phalaṃ pūjitais tu taiḥ
children.translated_text: The fruit that comes from seeing and worshiping crores of my <s>liṅgas</s>

children.text: śālagrāmaśilāyāṃ tu ekenāpi hi tad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: comes indeed even from one worship at a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: tasmād bhaktyā ca madbhaktaiḥ prītyarthe mama putraka
children.translated_text: Therefore, with devotion, by my devotees and for the sake of pleasing me, O son,
worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone should always be performed with devotion.
Where <s>Keśava</s>, having the form of a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, abides,
there are the gods, asuras, yakṣas, and the fourteen worlds.
Before a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, ancestors satisfied even once with a <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral offering)

children.text: vasanti pitaras tasya na saṅkhyā tatra vidyate ||
children.translated_text: dwell; no count of that exists there.

children.text: pramāṇam asti sarvasya sukṛtasya hi putraka
children.translated_text: There is a measure for every meritorious deed, O son,
but the fruit of worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone is without measure.
One who gives a stone of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, arisen from <s>Śālagrāma</s>,
to a brahmin devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, has thereby performed many sacrifices.
A stone arisen from <s>Śālagrāma</s> is rare in the human world.

children.text: prāpyate na vinā puṇyaiḥ kalikāle viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is not obtained without merits, especially in the age of <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: sa dhanyaḥ puruṣo loke saphalaṃ tasya jīvitam
children.translated_text: Blessed is that person in the world; fruitful is his life,

children.text: śālagrāmaśilā śuddhā gṛhe yasya ca pūjitā ||
children.translated_text: in whose house a pure <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone is worshiped.
The man who restrains the whole group of his senses and performs worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone

children.text: yaḥ kuryān mānavo bhaktyā puṣpe puṣpe'śvamedhabhāk ||
children.translated_text: with devotion obtains the share of an <s>Aśvamedha</s> for every flower.
Whether at the proper time or at an improper time, worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,

children.text: bhaktyā vā yadi vābhaktyā yaḥ karoti sa puṇyabhāk ||
children.translated_text: if someone performs it with devotion or without devotion, he becomes a possessor of merit.

children.text: dveṣeṇāpi ca lobhena dambhena kapaṭena vā
children.translated_text: Even through hatred, greed, pride, or deceit,
on seeing the god arisen from <s>Śālagrāma</s>, one is released from sin.
Whether impure, of bad conduct, devoid of truth and purity...

children.text: śālagrāmaśilāṃ spṛṣṭvā sadya eva śucir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: By touching the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone, one immediately becomes pure.

children.text: tilaprasthaśataṃ bhaktyā yo dadāti dine dine
children.translated_text: One who, with devotion, gives a hundred prasthas of sesame day after day
obtains that same fruit through worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.

children.text: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ mūlaṃ toyaṃ dūrvākṣataṃ suta
children.translated_text: A leaf, a flower, a fruit, a root, water, dūrvā grass, or unbroken grains, my son,
when offered to the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone, becomes equal to <s>Meru</s>.
Even if one performs it without proper rule, devoid of rite and mantra,
through worship of the cakra one obtains the full fruit taught in scripture.
There also, and elsewhere:

children.text: skandhe kṛtvā tu yo 'dhvānaṃ vahate śailanāyakam
children.translated_text: A person who sets out on the road carrying the lord of stones on his shoulder

children.text: tenoḍhaṃ tu bhavet sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram ||
children.translated_text: has thereby carried the entire three worlds, with all that moves and does not move.

children.text: brahmahatyādikaṃ pāpaṃ yat kiṃcit kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever sin a man commits, such as the killing of a Brahmin,
worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone quickly burns all of that away.

children.text: na pūjanaṃ na mantrāś ca na japo na ca bhāvanā
children.translated_text: There is no formal worship, no mantras, no muttering of prayer, and no visualization,
no hymn of praise and no service-offering required in worship of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.
Wherever the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone is, that place is a tīrtha for three yojanas;

children.text: tatra dānaṃ ca homaś ca sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: there, gifts and oblations become multiplied ten million times.

children.text: śālagrāmaśilāyāṃ tu yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man who performs a śrāddha rite at the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone

children.text: pitaras tasya tiṣṭhanti tṛptāḥ kalpaśataṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: has his ancestors remaining satisfied in heaven for a hundred kalpas.
Within merely a krośa all around the vicinity of a <s>śālagrāma</s>,
even a Kīkaṭa who dies goes to the world of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, O man.
And in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
One who gives in charity the excellent gift of the disk-marked <s>śālagrāma</s> stone
has thereby given the circle of the earth, together with its mountains, forests, and groves.
In the <s>Garuḍa Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: tiṣṭhanti nityaṃ pitaro manuṣyās tīrthāni gaṅgādikapuṣkarāṇi
children.translated_text: The ancestors, human beings, holy places such as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Puṣkara</s>,

children.text: yajñāś ca medhā hy api puṇyaśailāś cakrāṅkitā yasya vasanti gehe ||
children.translated_text: sacrifices, meritorious rites, and holy mountains always dwell in the house of one in whose home disk-marked stones reside.
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Yama</s> and <s>Dhūmrakeśa</s>:

children.text: śālagrāmaśilāyāṃ tu yair naraiḥ pūjito hariḥ
children.translated_text: Those men by whom <s>Hari</s> is worshiped in the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone:

children.text: saṃśodhya teṣāṃ pāpāni muktaye buddhito bhavet ||
children.translated_text: having purified their sins, he becomes disposed toward their liberation.

children.text: kārttike mathurāyāṃ tu sārūpyaṃ diśate hariḥ
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Kārttika</s> at <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Hari</s> grants likeness to himself.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is worshiped in the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone with the ancestors in view,

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ samuddharet tasya pitṝn etān svalokatām ||
children.translated_text: he raises those ancestors of that person up to his own world.
And in the <s>Bṛhannāradīya</s>, at the end of the story of <s>Yajñadhvaja</s>:
Where <s>Keśava</s>, having the form of the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone, abides,
there demons, spirits, vetālas, and the like do not afflict anyone.
Wherever there is a <s>śālagrāma</s> stone, that is a tīrtha, that is an ascetic grove,
because there the blessed <s>Madhusūdana</s> is present.

children.text: śālagrāmaśilās tāś ca yadi dvādaśa pūjitāḥ
children.translated_text: And if those <s>śālagrāma</s> stones, twelve in number, are worshiped,

children.text: śataṃ vā pūjitaṃ bhaktyā tadā syād adhikaṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: or if a hundred are worshiped with devotion, then the fruit is still greater.
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Māgha-māhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of the divine messenger and <s>Vikuṇḍala</s>:
O vaiśya, I shall tell you the merit of the man

children.text: vidhivat pūjitā yena tasya puṇyaṃ vadāmi te ||
children.translated_text: by whom twelve stones arising as <s>śālagrāma</s> stones have been worshiped according to rule.
Whatever merit would arise from twelve crores of liṅgas worshiped with golden lotuses

children.text: yat syād dvādaśakāleṣu dinenaikena tad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: at the twelve times, that arises in a single day.
But one who worships a hundred <s>śālagrāma</s> stones with devotion,

children.text: uṣitvā sa harer loke cakravartīha jāyate ||
children.translated_text: after dwelling in the world of <s>Hari</s>, is born here as a universal emperor.
In the <s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Skanda</s>:
A Vaiṣṇava who daily worships

children.text: arcayed vaiṣṇavo nityaṃ tasya puṇyaṃ nibodha me ||
children.translated_text: twelve stones indeed that have arisen as <s>śālagrāma</s>s: hear from me his merit.
Whatever merit there is from thousands of crores of liṅgas worshiped on the bank of the <s>Jāhnavī</s>,

children.text: kāśīvāse yugāny aṣṭau dinenaikena tad bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and from dwelling in <s>Kāśī</s> for eight ages, that arises in a single day.

children.text: kiṃ punar bahunā yas tu pūjayed vaiṣṇavo naraḥ
children.translated_text: What more need be said? For the Vaiṣṇava man who worships them,

children.text: na hi brahmādayo devāḥ saṃkhyāṃ kurvanti puṇyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: even the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> cannot calculate the amount of his merit.
There also:
The man who declares a price for a <s>śālagrāma</s> stone,

children.text: vikretā cānumantā ca yaḥ parīkṣām udīrayet ||
children.translated_text: the seller, the one who approves, and the one who proposes an appraisal:

children.text: sarve te narakaṃ yānti yāvad āhūtasamplavam
children.translated_text: all these go to hell until the dissolution called Āhūta-saṃplava.
Therefore, O Brahmin, one should completely avoid the buying and selling of the disk-marked stone.
There also:
There is no consecration at all for a <s>śālagrāma</s> stone;

children.text: mahāpūjāṃ tu kṛtvādau pūjayet tāṃ tato budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise person should first perform a great worship and then worship it.
Therefore, among the classes of sacred seats, such as the sun and other images,
the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone itself is the supreme seat of <s>Hari</s>.
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in that same place:

children.text: hṛdi sūrye jale vātha pratimāsthaṇḍileṣu ca
children.translated_text: After fully worshiping <s>Hari</s> in the heart, in the sun, in water, in images, and on prepared ground,

children.text: samabhyarcya hariṃ yānti narās te vaiṣṇavaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: people go to the Vaiṣṇava state.
Or rather, <s>Vāsudeva</s> is always to be worshiped by those who desire liberation
in the <s>śālagrāma</s>, in the stone disk made by the vajra-insect.
For that is the seat of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, destroyer of all sin,
giver of all merit, O vaiśya, and bestower of liberation on everyone.
There also, in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Yama</s> and <s>Dhūmrakeśa</s>:

children.text: pūjā ca vihitā tasya pratimāyāṃ nṛpātmaja
children.translated_text: Worship of him is prescribed in the image, O prince.

children.text: śailī dārumayī lauhī lepyā lekhyā ca saikatā
children.translated_text: The blessed image is remembered as eightfold: made of stone, made of wood, made of metal, made of clay, painted, made of sand,
made in the mind, and made of gems.
But in the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone there is direct service of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>;
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, teacher of the world, is always present there.
In the <s>Skanda Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s>, in the dialogue of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Skanda</s>:

children.text: suvarṇārcā na ratnārcā na śilārcā surottama
children.translated_text: Neither golden worship, nor jewel worship, nor stone-image worship, O best of gods,
equals this: <s>Hari</s> always dwells in the <s>śālagrāma</s> stone.
For this very reason it has been said:

children.text: hatyāṃ hanti yadaṅghrisaṅgatulasī steyaṃ ca toyaṃ pade naivedyaṃ bahumadyapānaduritaṃ gurvaṅganāsaṅgajam
children.translated_text: The <s>tulasī</s> joined to whose feet destroys killing; the water at his feet destroys theft; his <s>naivedya</s> destroys the sin of much wine-drinking and the sin arising from union with the guru's wife;

children.text: śrīśādhīnamatiḥ sthitir harijanais tatsaṅgajaṃ kilbiṣaṃ śālagrāmaśilānṛsiṃhamahimā ko 'py eṣa lokottaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a disposition dependent on <s>Śrīśa</s>, together with the servants of <s>Hari</s>, destroys the sin born from their association. Such is the extraordinary greatness of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> in the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.
Of the ocean of greatness of the Blessed Lord in the form of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,
who, even if sheltered by <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>, is able to count the waves?
In the <s>Padma</s>:
One who eats anything without worshiping the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone
is born, until the end of the kalpa, as a worm in the excrement of caṇḍālas and the like.
And in the <s>Skanda</s>:
Though his body be split by the tips of the peaks of Mount <s>Gaurava</s>,
no inclination arises in him toward worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.
Thus the Blessed Lord, whose nature is the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,

children.text: dvijaiḥ strībhiś ca śūdraiś ca pūjyo bhagavataḥ paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be worshiped by all twice-born men, by women, and by śūdras who are devoted to the Blessed Lord.
Likewise in the <s>Skanda</s>, in the <s>Brahma-Nārada</s> dialogue, in the context of worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone in the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> vow:
Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and also good śūdras
have eligibility with respect to the <s>Śālagrāma</s>; others never do.
Elsewhere in that same text:

children.text: striyo vā yadi vā śūdrā brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyādayaḥ
children.translated_text: Women, or else śūdras, brahmins, kṣatriyas, and the rest,
having worshiped the stone-disc, obtain the eternal abode.

children.text: ato niṣedhakaṃ yad yad vacanaṃ śrūyate sphuṭam
children.translated_text: Therefore whatever prohibitive statement is clearly heard,
the knowers of reality should understand each such statement as applying to non-<s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>.
For example:

children.text: brāhmaṇasyaiva pūjyo 'haṃ śucer apy aśucer api
children.translated_text: I am to be worshiped only by a brahmin, whether pure or even impure;
contact by the hands of women and śūdras is harder to endure even than a thunderbolt.
Through utterance of the <s>praṇava</s> and also through worship of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone,
and through intercourse with a brahmin woman, a śūdra goes to the state of a caṇḍāla.
The <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone should be carefully kept by <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, as among <s>Śālagrāma</s> stones;
and that stone too should always be worshiped, only when furnished with a mark of the <s>Dvārakā</s> disc.
In the <s>Brahma</s>, in that same connection:
The god arisen from <s>Śālagrāma</s> and the god arisen at <s>Dvāravatī</s>--

children.text: ubhayoḥ saṅgamo yatra muktis tatra na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: where there is a conjunction of the two, there is liberation; there is no doubt.
In the <s>Skanda</s>, in the <s>Śrī Brahma-Nārada</s> dialogue:
Where a cakra-marked stone stands
before a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone, O tiger among sages, prosperities increase there.
Elsewhere in that same text:
He who every day worships twelve stones of <s>Śālagrāma</s>,
joined with stones of <s>Dvāravatī</s>, is honored in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.
In the <s>Śrī Prahlāda Saṃhitā</s>:
With one disc it is <s>Sudarśana</s>; with two, it is remembered as <s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: tribhis trivikramo nāma caturbhiś ca janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with three it is named <s>Trivikrama</s>, and with four <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: pañcabhir vāsudevas tu ṣaḍbhiḥ pradyumna ucyate
children.translated_text: With five it is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and with six it is called <s>Pradyumna</s>;
with seven it is <s>Baladeva</s>, and with eight <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
With nine it is <s>Navavyūha</s>, and with ten <s>Daśamūrtika</s>;
with eleven, <s>Aniruddha</s>; with twelve, <s>Dvādaśātmaka</s>;
among others with many discs it is proclaimed as <s>Ananta</s>.
In the <s>Vārāha</s>:

children.text: ye kecic caiva pāṣāṇā viṣṇucakreṇa mudritāḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever stones are marked by the discus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
by merely touching them one is released from all sins.
In the <s>Gāruḍa</s>:
Stones beginning with <s>Sudarśana</s>, when worshiped, bestow all desires.
And in the <s>Skanda</s>:

children.text: bhaktyā vā yadi vābhaktyā cakrāṅkaṃ pūjayen naraḥ
children.translated_text: Whether with devotion or without devotion, if a man worships a disc-marked stone,

children.text: api cet sudurācāro mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even if he is very badly behaved, he is released; of this there is no doubt.
And in the <s>Dvārakā Māhātmya</s>, in the statement of <s>Śrī Brahmā</s> and the others who had come to <s>Dvārakā</s>:

children.text: etad vai cakratīrthaṃ tu yacchilā cakracihnitā
children.translated_text: This indeed is the <s>Cakratīrtha</s>: the stone that is marked with the sign of a disc,
bestowing liberation on sinners in the world, worshiped even in a land of mlecchas.
In the <s>Kapila Pañcarātra</s>:
A stone of <s>Dvāravatī</s> with one disc, very beautiful,
which is called <s>Sudarśana</s>, is the giver of the single fruit of liberation.
With two, <s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s> bestows the fruit of enjoyment and liberation;
and with these, that one in the form of <s>Acyuta</s> grants the fruit of <s>Indra</s>.
Four-armed and four-disc, it bestows the fruit of the four aims of life;
and with five, <s>Vāsudeva</s> removes the fear of birth and death.

children.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ pradyumna evāsau lakṣmīṃ kāntiṃ dadāti saḥ
children.translated_text: With six, that one is <s>Pradyumna</s>; he gives prosperity and beauty;
with seven, he is <s>Balabhadra</s>, increasing the fame of the family line.
With eight, <s>Puruṣottama</s> grants everything desired;

children.text: navacakro nṛsiṃhas tu phalaṃ yacchaty anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: with nine discs, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> gives the unsurpassed fruit.
With ten, he is remembered as <s>Daśāvatāra</s>, the bestower of kingship;
with eleven, <s>Aniruddha</s> grants sovereignty.
With twelve forms, that one gives nirvāṇa and, when well worshiped, happiness.
There also:

children.text: kṛṣṇa mṛtyuprado nityaṃ dhūmraś caiva bhayāvahaḥ
children.translated_text: The black one always gives death, and the smoky one brings fear;

children.text: asvāsthyaṃ karburo dadyān nīlas tu dhanahānidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the mottled one gives illness, while the blue one causes loss of wealth.
A pierced one, when worshiped, certainly gives poverty and sorrows;

children.text: pāṇḍaras tu mahad duḥkhaṃ bhagno bhāryāviyogadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the pale one gives great suffering; the broken one gives separation from one's wife.
The white-colored one gives excellent and exceedingly great happiness

children.text: dadāti śuklavarṇaś ca tasmād enaṃ samarcayet ||
children.translated_text: through sons, grandsons, wealth, and sovereignty; therefore one should worship it.
In the <s>Śrī Prahlāda Saṃhitā</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇā mṛtyupradā nityaṃ kapilā ca bhayāvahā
children.translated_text: A black one always gives death, and a tawny one brings fear;
a mottled one gives sickness and pain; a yellow one destroys wealth.
A smoky-hued one leads to the loss of wealth; a broken one destroys one's wife;

children.text: sacchidrā ca trikoṇā ca tathā viṣamacakrikā
children.translated_text: one that has holes, one that is triangular, and likewise one with uneven discs,

children.text: ardhacandrākṛtir yā ca pūjyās tā na bhavanti hi ||
children.translated_text: and one that has the form of a half-moon--these indeed are not to be worshiped.
In the teaching of <s>Gārgya</s> and <s>Gālava</s>:

children.text: sukhadā samacakrā tu dvādaśī cottamā śubhā
children.translated_text: The evenly disc-marked one gives happiness, and the twelve-disc one is excellent and auspicious;

children.text: vartulā caturasrā ca narāṇāṃ ca sukhapradā ||
children.translated_text: round and square ones also give happiness to men.

children.text: trikoṇā viṣamā caiva chidrā bhagnā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: But the triangular, uneven, pierced, and likewise broken one,

children.text: ardhacandrākṛtir yā tu pūjārhā na bhavet tu sā
children.translated_text: and that which has the shape of a half-moon, is not fit for worship.
When such a one is worshiped, no fruit ever arises there.

children.text: iti śrīgopālabhaṭṭavilikhite śrībhagavadbhaktivilāse ādhiṣṭhāniko nāma pañcamo vilāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth <s>vilāsa</s> (section), called <s>Ādhiṣṭhānika</s>, in the <s>Śrī Bhagavadbhaktivilāsa</s> written by <s>Śrī Gopālabhaṭṭa</s>.
